### A red check's reasons drop Node's own `node:internal` stack frames and the lines the headline already repeats, so the clipped tail keeps more of the assertion's diff (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/build/build-check-report.ts and test/build-check-report.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A red check's output becomes `outputTail` through `clipBuildTail` (src/build/build-check-report.ts): the last 10 meaningful lines, plus a rescued failed-test name line and error-message line. `checkFailureReasons` turns that tail into the reasons a rejection records in `state.lastReview`, the author's next-run note, and the `review_rejected` event. Today the 10-line window spends lines on node:test's own plumbing frames (`at async Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1409:7)`, `at async Test.processPendingSubtests (node:internal/…)`). Those frames are the same in every failure and say nothing about the code under test. In the event log's last 200,000 lines (2026-10-16 18:28Z to 2026-10-20), 20 of 24 `review_rejected` events whose first reason starts `check failed` carried such frames: 50 of their 283 reason lines. Because the window is cut from the end, these frames push out the lines just above the stack, which is where a failed `strictEqual` or `deepStrictEqual` prints its diff. Example: node:test prints `1 !== 0` between `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:` and the stack. In the spec-output fixture of the test "failureHeadline names the failed test even when the stack and assertion dump crowd its name out of the window", that diff line is cut today. Dropping the two internal frames keeps it. Separately, when the headline is `<test name> — <message>`, `checkFailureReasons` removes only a tail line equal to the whole headline. So the `✖ <test name> (510.9ms)` line and the message line both appear again right below the headline, which already says both (seen in the 2026-10-20 `report --role` rejections).

**Approach.**
- src/build/build-check-report.ts:
  - Add `const NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME = /^at\s(?:.*\()?node:internal\//;` with a doc comment: a stack frame inside Node's own runtime (the test runner, the task queue). It matches both `at fn (node:internal/…)` and a bare `at node:internal/…`. It does not match frames in other built-in modules such as `node:fs` or `node:async_hooks`, nor frames in project files.
  - `clipBuildTail`: after the existing blank/banner filter, drop every line `NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME` matches, before taking the 10-line window and the `cut` prefix. If that leaves no lines, use the unfiltered lines, so output made only of internal frames still yields a tail and a headline. When the dropped frame is `at async Test.processPendingSubtests (…) {`, the property dump's opening `{` goes with it; that is accepted. Add one sentence to the doc comment.
  - `checkFailureReasons`, the verified (non-`unverified`) branch: after the headline, drop each tail line the headline already carries, not only the line equal to the whole headline. That means a line equal to the headline; a line that, with its trailing duration removed (the same ` \([\d.]+m?s\)$` replace `failureHeadline` uses), equals the headline or plus ` — ` starts it (the test-name or ⚠ marker line, including node:test's second copy under `✖ failing tests:`); and a line with which the headline ends after a ` — ` (the message line). Every other line keeps its order. The `unverified` branch is unchanged. Update the doc comment.
- No other file changes: `failureHeadline`, `parseFailingTests` (which reads the full output, not the tail), and the callers in src/review/review-precheck.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts and src/baseline/main-baseline.ts read the new tail as is.

**Tests** (test/build-check-report.test.ts):
- Update "failureHeadline names the failed test even when the stack and assertion dump crowd its name out of the window". `tail.length` becomes 11: the rescued name, then a window that now contains the message and `1 !== 0`. Assert `tail.includes("1 !== 0")`, and that no tail line contains `node:internal/`. The headline assertion is unchanged. (A standalone simulation of the change on this fixture gave exactly that 11-line tail.)
- New, "clipBuildTail drops node:internal frames but keeps project and other built-in frames". Use output of: an `AssertionError …` line, `at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///w/dist/test/x.test.js:3:35)`, `at Test.runInAsyncScope (node:async_hooks:226:14)`, `at Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1397:25)`, `at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)`, `actual: 1,`. The tail is those lines without the two `node:internal` frames, in order.
- New, "clipBuildTail keeps an all-internal output rather than returning nothing": two `node:internal` frames in, the same two out.
- New, "a red check's reasons do not repeat the test name or message the headline carries". Pass a tail of `✖ t (1.5ms)`, `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: boom`, `actual: 1,` to `checkFailureReasons`. Expect `["check failed (\`npm run test\`): ✖ t — AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: boom", "actual: 1,"]`.
- The existing "a red check's reasons lead with the headline and drop it from the tail" passes unchanged: it calls `checkFailureReasons` on a hand-built tail, which `clipBuildTail` never filters. So does test/review-precheck.test.ts "gate pre-check names the failing assertion, not the stack frame the tail opens on": its `at TestContext` and `node:async_hooks` frames survive, so `reasons.some((r) => r.startsWith("at "))` still holds.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- No `outputTail` produced by `clipBuildTail` from output that holds any other meaningful line contains a frame `NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME` matches. Frames in project files and in other `node:` modules are kept.
- For the spec-output fixture above, the tail holds `1 !== 0`, and `failureHeadline` still reads `✖ the wake was restored — AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:`.
- A verified red check's reasons hold the headline once. No later reason is the test-name line or the message line the headline already contains.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A merge whose files are dirty in the primary checkout is blocked before its merge check runs, instead of after a full check and three fast-forward attempts (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-git.ts, src/merge/merge-stack.ts, src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, src/merge/merge-batch.ts and their tests. The in-flight entry "A merge blocked by a dirty primary checkout names the files git refused to overwrite…" also edits src/merge/merge-git.ts and adds `overwriteBlockedReason`; this entry prints the same wording, and whichever lands second only rebases)

**Goal.** When the primary checkout is on main, `ffMainToOrWhy` (src/merge/merge-git.ts) fast-forwards it with `git merge --ff-only`. git refuses when the checkout holds uncommitted edits to a file the merge changes, or an untracked file the merge would create. Today tumwater learns this only at the fast-forward, after the expensive step. On 2026-10-19 between 21:26 and 21:39 UTC the event log shows the cost. In the batch path, `mergeStackIn` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) ran a 258 s `build_check` and then failed the fast-forward. The re-stack loop retried twice more, because a re-stack onto an unchanged tip skips the check (`docOnlyRestack`), so the 3 `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: …` warnings came within 0.8 s. The loop then returned `blocked`, and `mergeApproved` (src/merge/merge-batch.ts) emitted `merge_blocked` for every change. Leftover recovery re-merges each such change through its own gate and `tryMerge` (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts), whose in-lock check runs before the same doomed fast-forward. Over those 13 minutes plan, director, feature-2 and bugfix-3 logged `merge_failed merge_blocked` with durations of 152–548 s. A dirty checkout can be seen with one `git status` before any check runs.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-git.ts: add `export async function primaryCheckoutBlockers(root: string, mainBranch: string, tip: string): Promise<{ uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] } | null>`.
  - Return null when `currentBranch(root)` is not `mainBranch`, because the ref-push arm touches no working tree.
  - Otherwise read the paths the merge changes with `gitTry(root, "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-only", mainBranch, tip)`, and the checkout's state with `gitTry(root, "--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")`. `--no-optional-locks` keeps a read-only status from taking `index.lock` under an operator's own git.
  - Split the `-z` output on NUL. Each record is `XY<space>path`. A rename or copy record (X `R` or `C`) is followed by one more record holding the source path; consume it and treat both paths as uncommitted.
  - Put a changed path from a `??` record in `untracked`, and one from any other record in `uncommitted`. Keep the diff's order, and keep only paths in the diff's set.
  - Return null when both lists are empty, or when either git call fails (`gitTry` returns null). This pre-flight never blocks on a read error; the fast-forward still decides.
- The reason text, `the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: a.txt, b.txt; untracked: c.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`. Leave out an empty group, and list at most 5 names per group, then `, +N more`. If `overwriteBlockedReason` already exists in merge-git.ts when you start, call it. Otherwise add it there as `export function overwriteBlockedReason(blockers: { uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] }): string`, with exactly that output, so the sibling entry finds it.
- src/merge/merge-stack.ts `mergeStackIn`: right after `assembleStack` returns and `tip` is known, before `docOnlyRestack`, call `primaryCheckoutBlockers(ctx.root, ctx.mainBranch, tip)`. On non-null, `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, mergeDone.at(-1)!.role, \`merge blocked: ${overwriteBlockedReason(b)}\`)` (the role `ffStackToMain` warns under) and return `{ kind: "blocked" }`. No check runs, and no re-stack follows. Add a sentence to the function's doc comment.
- src/merge/merge-batch.ts: in `mergeApproved`'s `outcome.kind === "blocked"` arm, reword the comment to cover both causes: a race lost on every attempt, or a dirty primary checkout found before the check. The code there is unchanged.
- src/merge/merge-to-main.ts `tryMerge`: after `const target = await headOf(wt, "HEAD")` and before `verifyMerge`, make the same call with `target`. On non-null, warn `merge blocked: <reason>` under `ctx.role` and return `"merge_blocked"`. The in-lock check is skipped. The gate check that ran before the lock is not saved; this entry does not try to save it.
- `ffFailureReason` and `ffMainToOrWhy` stay unchanged. A checkout that turns dirty between the pre-flight and the fast-forward still fails there, as it does today.

**Tests.**
- test/merge-git.test.ts, "primaryCheckoutBlockers names only the dirty paths the merge changes". Use `initializedWorktree()`. In `wt`, commit an edit to a tracked `shared.txt` (committed on main first, then `git reset --hard main` in `wt`) and a new `fresh.txt`. In `root`, overwrite `shared.txt` without committing, write an untracked `fresh.txt` and an untracked `other.txt`. Expect `{ uncommitted: ["shared.txt"], untracked: ["fresh.txt"] }`; `other.txt` is not in the diff. A clean `root` returns null. A `root` checked out on another branch returns null.
- test/merge-git.test.ts, "overwriteBlockedReason caps each group at 5 names": 7 uncommitted names list the first 5, then `, +2 more`, and no `untracked:` group. Skip this case if the sibling entry already landed an equivalent test.
- test/merger-restack.test.ts, "a batch whose files are dirty in the primary checkout is blocked before its check". Use `batchFixture(["alpha", "beta"])`, whose default edit creates `alpha.txt` and `beta.txt`. Write an untracked `alpha.txt` in `root`, then run `runBatch` with `withApprovePi`, as the neighbouring tests do. Expect results `["merge_blocked", "merge_blocked"]` and `batchChecks(root).length === 0`. `warningMessages(root)` holds exactly one `merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (untracked: alpha.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there` and no `fast-forward failed` line. Both refs are kept, and main has not moved.
- The existing tests in test/merge-git.test.ts, test/merge-stack.test.ts, test/merger-restack.test.ts and test/merger.test.ts pass unchanged. Their primary checkouts are clean, so the pre-flight returns null.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a file the merge changes left uncommitted or untracked in a primary checkout that is on main, a batch merge runs no `build_check`, logs one `merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (…) — commit, stash or remove them there`, and keeps every change's ref as `merge_blocked`. A single-change `tryMerge` returns `merge_blocked` with the same warning and runs no in-lock check.
- A dirty path the merge does not change, a primary checkout off main, and a clean checkout all merge exactly as today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The doctor's orphans row names the TUI Health tab's Ctrl+K among the ways to kill the orphans it lists, so an operator reading it in the TUI is pointed at the key on the tab they are looking at (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. The blocked Plain terms series reword comments in src/doctor/ but rename no identifier this entry uses; whichever lands second only rebases — done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** When `checkOrphans` (src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts) finds orphans, its failing detail ends `— nothing reaps these; \`tumwater doctor --kill-orphans\` (or the dashboard Health card's Kill orphans) kills each with its descendants`. Kill orphans part 2/2 (PLANS-DONE.md, done 2026-10-20) added a third way to do the same kill: Ctrl+K pressed twice on the TUI Health tab (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts). - In `checkOrphans`, change the parenthetical in the failing detail to `(or the dashboard Health card's Kill orphans, or the TUI Health tab's Ctrl+K pressed twice)`. ### A merge blocked by a dirty primary checkout names the files git refused to overwrite, instead of cutting git's error off at "would be overwritten by merge:" (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-git.ts and test/merge-git.test.ts. Plain terms code run 18/20 later renames code in src/merge/ but no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases)

**Goal.** When the primary checkout is on main, a merge fast-forwards it with `git merge --ff-only` (`ffMainToOrWhy`, src/merge/merge-git.ts). If the checkout holds uncommitted edits to a file the merge changes, or untracked files the merge would create, git refuses. It lists the files on tab-indented lines below a `… would be overwritten by merge:` header. `ffFailureReason` keeps only the first line of the error, so both callers' warnings (`mergeToMain` in src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, the stacked fast-forward in src/merge/merge-stack.ts) end at that colon. Between 21:26 and 21:39 UTC on 2026-10-19 the event log held 10 such `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: … Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:` warnings, from plan, director, feature-3 and feature-2. None of them said which file to commit or remove. The warning should name the files.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-git.ts: add `export function overwriteBlockers(gitError: string): { uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] }`. It walks the error's lines. A line containing `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:` starts the uncommitted group, and a line containing `untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge:` starts the untracked group. Each following line that starts with a tab adds its trimmed text to the current group. Any other line ends the group. git can print both groups in one error, as `git merge --ff-only` does when one file is dirty and another is untracked.
- `ffFailureReason`: after the main-moved test, compute `overwriteBlockers(errorMessage(err))`. If either group is non-empty, return `fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: a.txt, b.txt; untracked: c.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`. Leave out a group that is empty. Each group lists at most 5 names and then `, +N more`. If both groups are empty, return the first line of the error as today. Update the doc comment: a dirty primary checkout is reported with its files, and any other cause still reports git's first line.
- The `merge blocked: ` prefix and both callers stay unchanged, so the warnings in merge-to-main.ts and merge-stack.ts pick up the new wording with no edits.

**Tests.** In test/merge-git.test.ts, beside "ffMainToOrWhy names main having moved off the ref's base, with its new head":
- "overwriteBlockers reads both of git's would-be-overwritten lists". Input: the error text `git merge --ff-only abc failed (1): error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:\n\tf.txt\n\tg.txt\nPlease commit your changes or stash them before you merge.\nerror: The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge:\n\tnew.txt\nPlease move or remove them before you merge.\nAborting`. Expected: `{ uncommitted: ["f.txt", "g.txt"], untracked: ["new.txt"] }`. An error without either header gives two empty lists.
- "ffMainToOrWhy names the primary checkout's files the fast-forward would overwrite". Use `initializedWorktree()`. Commit `shared.txt` on main in `root`, then `sh(wt, "git", "reset", "--hard", "main")`. In `wt`, change `shared.txt`, add `fresh.txt` and commit. In `root`, overwrite `shared.txt` without committing and write an untracked `fresh.txt`. `ffMainToOrWhy(root, headSha(wt), "main")` returns exactly `fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: shared.txt; untracked: fresh.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`, and main's head has not moved.
- A unit case for the cap: 7 uncommitted names list the first 5, then `, +2 more`. Export the message builder as `overwriteBlockedReason(blockers)` so this case needs no repo.
- The existing `ffMainToOrWhy` tests pass unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A merge blocked by uncommitted or untracked files in the primary checkout logs `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (…) — commit, stash or remove them there`, naming up to 5 files per group.
- Every other fast-forward failure (main moved outside the merge lock, or any other git error) reads exactly as it does today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A tool call's label drops a leading `cd <dir> &&`, so a stalled command's warning names the command and not the worktree path (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/text/phrases.ts and test/phrases.test.ts. Plain terms code run 14/20 edits comments in src/text/phrases.ts but renames no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `describeToolCall` (src/text/phrases.ts) builds the one-line label of a tool call: `<toolName> <detail>`, with the detail squashed to 32 characters. Three places use it: the stall warning (src/pi/pi-stream.ts builds the label, and src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts logs `tool call stalled: <label> — …`), the dashboards' last-tool cell and stall flag (src/ui/progress-data.ts), and transcript rendering (src/ui/transcript.ts). Agents often start a bash command with `cd <their worktree> && …`. The absolute worktree path then fills all 32 characters. In the event log from 2026-10-17 15:58 to 2026-10-19 22:51 UTC, 46 of the 60 `tool call stalled` warnings read exactly `tool call stalled: bash cd /Users/zach/tumwater/.tumwat… — …`, and none of those 46 says which command hung. The label should skip the leading `cd` and show the command that runs after it.

**Approach.**
- src/text/phrases.ts: add a module-private `withoutLeadingCd(command: string): string`. It removes leading segments that match `^\s*cd\s+("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|\S+)\s*(?:&&|;)\s*`, repeatedly, so `cd a && cd b && npm test` becomes `npm test`. Remove a segment only when it ends in `&&` or `;`. A bare `cd dir`, or `cd dir || …`, stays unchanged. If removing would leave the string empty, return the original.
- `describeToolCall`: apply `withoutLeadingCd` only when the candidate came from `args.command` or `args.cmd`, before `squash`. Paths, patterns and urls are unchanged. Add one sentence to the doc comment: a leading `cd <dir> &&` is dropped from a command, because the run's cwd is implied and the path would use up the 32-character budget.
- No caller changes. The stall classifier reads the raw `call.command` (`commandBuffersOutput(call.command || call.label)` in pi-watchdogs.ts and `stalledToolLabel`), not the label, so INV-A2's threshold behavior does not change. A `cd x && sleep 999 | tail` command still classifies as buffered through its raw command.

**Tests.** In test/phrases.test.ts, add the test "describeToolCall drops a leading cd so the label names the command":
- `describeToolCall("bash", { command: "cd /Users/zach/tumwater/.tumwater/worktrees/_slot-10 && npm run test:gate > x.log 2>&1" })` returns `bash npm run test:gate > x.log 2>&1`. A remainder longer than 32 characters is squashed as today: `cd /w && ` followed by 40 `x` gives `bash ` followed by 31 `x` and `…`.
- `cd "/a b" && ls` gives `bash ls`. `cd a; cd b && make` gives `bash make`. `{ cmd: "cd a && ls" }` gives `bash ls`.
- These stay unchanged: `cd /tmp` gives `bash cd /tmp`, and `cd a || exit 1` gives `bash cd a || exit 1`. `{ path: "/x/cd y && z" }` still basenames to `cd y && z`.
- The existing describeToolCall tests and the `tool call stalled` assertions in test/pi.test.ts pass unchanged (none of their commands starts with `cd`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A stalled `cd <worktree> && <cmd>` call logs `tool call stalled: bash <cmd…> — …`. The dashboards' last-tool cell and the transcripts show the same label.
- A command with no leading `cd … &&`/`;` segment gets exactly the label it gets today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 8/20: Rename the runner's run pipeline phases (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 7/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/runner.ts + src/runner/runner-run.ts + test/runner.test.ts + test/runner-2.test.ts through test/runner-5.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The runner's run pipeline (`runPhase`, `runOncePhase`, `runOnceInLeasePhase`, `runWithWorktreePhase`) and the runner's comments and core tests use run wording throughout.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: `tickPhase` → `runPhase`, `runTickPhase` → `runOncePhase` (it pairs with `RoleRunner.runOnce`), `runTickInLeasePhase` → `runOnceInLeasePhase`, `tickWithWorktreePhase` → `runWithWorktreePhase`, and the locals `quietKilledTick`, `tickBase`, `nTick` and `tickOutcome` → run forms. This file has about 150 tick lines; most are comments describing the pipeline, and most of its "run" nouns mean the agent run, so apply the "agent run" rule here with care.
- src/runner/runner.ts: comments ("one full tick of this role" → "one full run of this role"), and uses of `RunOutcome`, `RunUsage`, `runPhase` and `runOncePhase`.

### Kill orphans, part 2/2: the TUI Health pane's Ctrl+K twice kills the orphaned processes, the terminal twin of the dashboard's Kill orphans (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; requires part 1/2 landed for `orphanKillLines` and the `OrphanKillReport` export. A terminal operator who sees the orphans row fail should be able to reap the processes without leaving the TUI.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add a `killOrphans?(root: string): Promise<OrphanKillReport>` seam to the deps beside `runDoctor`, defaulting to `(r) => killOrphans(r)` from src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts, and pass it into the session deps the same way `runDoctor: runDoctorSeam` is passed.

If `session.armedKillOrphans` is false, set `session.killOrphansArmed = true` and flash `press Ctrl+K again to kill the orphaned processes the orphans check lists — any other key keeps them`. If it is true, flash `killing orphaned processes …` and call `session.killOrphans(session.root)`. Write the comment block in the style of the Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N blocks. Ctrl+K is not bound on any view outside the prompt-line editor (src/ui/tui/tui-input.ts), and `promptLineFree` keeps that editor's kill-line binding.

### A run whose end-of-run sweep had to kill processes it left running logs a warning naming the role and the count, so a leaking role shows up in the event feed instead of the sweep's count being discarded (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/process/run-marker.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts, test/run-marker.test.ts and test/pi-process.test.ts. The blocked Plain terms code parts reword src/runner/runner-pi.ts and src/agent/run-agent.ts, but they rename no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** When pi exits, the exit hook in `runAgent` (src/agent/run-agent.ts) calls `sweepRunMarker(runMarker)` (src/process/run-marker.ts). That sends SIGTERM to every process still carrying the run's `TUMWATER_RUN` mark and returns how many it signaled, but the hook throws the number away (`void sweepRunMarker(runMarker).catch(() => {})`). So nobody can tell which role's runs leave servers, watchers or `logs -f` followers running. BUGS.md's open entry about two leaked `logs -f` processes had to be traced by hand. When a run that tumwater did not kill leaves marked processes running, the run should log one warning under its role, giving the run kind and how many processes the sweep signaled. Runs that tumwater kills (abort, deadline, quiet watchdog, blind image read) are excluded: their process group got SIGTERM moments before the sweep scans, so members that are still exiting would be counted and every killed run would raise a false leak.

**Approach.**
- src/process/run-marker.ts: add `export function leftoversSweptMessage(kind: PiRunKind, count: number, killed: boolean): string | undefined`. It returns undefined when `count === 0` or `killed` is true. Otherwise it returns `run sweep: ${plural(count, "process", "processes")} the ${kind} run started ${count === 1 ? "was" : "were"} still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`, using `plural` from src/text/phrases.ts. Import `PiRunKind` as a type from src/pi/pi-event-line.ts. In the doc comment, explain why killed runs are excluded (see Goal).
- src/agent/run-agent.ts:
  - Add an optional `onLeftoversSwept?: (message: string) => void` to `PiRunOptions`. Its doc comment goes beside `onToolCallStalled` and `onAgentWarning`.
  - Put the killed test in one place: declare `const wasKilled = (): boolean => aborted || wd.timedOut || wd.quietKilled || blindRead !== undefined;` right after `let aborted = false;` (below the `startPiWatchdogs` call that sets up `wd`). The `close` handler's `const killed = …` becomes `const killed = wasKilled();`.
  - The `exit` hook becomes `void sweepRunMarker(runMarker).then((n) => { const msg = leftoversSweptMessage(opts.kind, n, wasKilled()); if (msg) opts.onLeftoversSwept?.(msg); }).catch(() => {});`. The sweep is still not awaited, so the run resolves exactly when it did before.
- src/runner/runner-pi.ts (`RunnerPi.runnerPiOpts`): set `onLeftoversSwept: (message) => this.host.warn(message)` beside `onToolCallStalled`. This one site covers the author run, its follow-ups and the gate (review/resolver) runs, because each of them builds its options here. A gate run's warning is filed under the authoring role, the same as its usage.

**Tests.**
- test/run-marker.test.ts, "leftoversSweptMessage words the sweep's count and stays silent for a killed or clean run": `("author", 1, false)` gives `run sweep: 1 process the author run started was still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`. `("gate", 2, false)` contains `2 processes the gate run started were`. `("author", 0, false)` and `("author", 3, true)` give undefined.
- test/pi-process.test.ts, "the end-of-run sweep reaches a detached tool call's cross-group orphan (regression)": pass `onLeftoversSwept: (m) => messages.push(m)` through `runPiFixture(dir, { config, onLeftoversSwept })`. After the existing `waitFor` that the orphan is gone, also `waitFor` `messages.length === 1` (the callback fires after the sweep's scan resolves) and assert that `messages[0]` starts with `run sweep: 1 process the author run started`. `runPiFixture` (test/helpers/pi-run-harness.ts) already passes `kind: "author"`. The existing finally that kills the orphan stays.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A run that ends without being killed and leaves N ≥ 1 marked processes running logs one `warning` event under its role, reading `run sweep: N process(es) the <author|gate> run started … still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`.
- A run that leaves nothing running logs no sweep warning. A run that tumwater aborted or killed (deadline, quiet watchdog, blind read) logs none whatever the sweep counts.
- The run's result, its resolve timing and the sweep's SIGTERM/SIGKILL behavior do not change: `sweepRunMarker`'s signature and body stay as they are, and the existing tests in test/run-marker.test.ts and test/pi-process.test.ts pass.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 7/20: Convert the dashboard and the rest of history (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 6/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/gui/ + src/gui/ + src/history/history.ts + src/history/history-render.ts + test/gui*.test.ts + test/cli-gui.test.ts + test/history*.test.ts + test/cli-history*.test.ts + test/fixtures/history-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The dashboard's browser code, the GUI server's run endpoint and the history command and renderer use run names, including the drawer's run list and the run-detail DOM attribute.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).

- Browser code in src/ui/gui/ (inside String.raw templates, which tsc does not check; grep all of src/ui/gui/ before each rename so names stay unique across the concatenated modules): `drawerTicks` → `drawerRuns`, `drawerTicksAt` → `drawerRunsAt`, `fmtLastTick` → `fmtLastRun`, `chartTicksByRole` → `chartRunsByRole`, `tickWord` → `runWord`, `todayTick` → `todayRun`, the DOM attribute `data-tickdetail` → `data-rundetail` (with its `dataset.tickdetail` reads and the `[data-tickdetail]` selector in gui-client-boot.ts), and uses of `lastTickCell` and `TickResult` → the new names. test/helpers/gui-client-scope.ts reaches browser functions by name; update it.
- src/history/history.ts and history-render.ts: `TickRowCells` → `RunRowCells`, `tickRowCells` → `runRowCells` and `tickRowLine` → `runRowLine` (aliased if src/ui/tui still uses them), and migrate `RunRow`, `readRunRows`, `summarizeRunRows` and the other names part 6/20 introduced.
- Tests: test/gui*.test.ts, test/cli-gui.test.ts, test/history*.test.ts except history-data (part 6/20's), test/cli-history*.test.ts, and test/fixtures/history-fixtures.ts (`repoWithTicks` → `repoWithRuns`).

**Files touched.** src/ui/gui/*.ts, src/gui/*.ts, src/history/history.ts, src/history/history-render.ts, test/helpers/gui-client-scope.ts, and the tests listed above.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -rnE '[Tt]ick[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Tick|TICK_|tickdetail'` over this part's files lists only aliases and serialized names.

### Kill orphans, part 1/2: the dashboard Health card's Kill orphans button runs `doctor --kill-orphans`, so an operator does not need a terminal to reap leaked processes (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts, src/cli.ts, src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts. Move the CLI's wording into it unchanged: `could not scan the process table — <error>; nothing killed`; `killed pid <pid>` plus ` (+N descendant(s))` when there are descendants, then ` <command>`; `could not kill pid <pid>: <reason>`; and `no orphaned processes to kill` when both lists are empty. A second click within the window disarms the slot, shows `showFlash("Killing orphaned processes…")`, posts `/api/kill-orphans`, and then shows `showFlash((d.ok ? "" : "error: ") + d.message)` and calls `fetchDoctor()`.
