### Plain terms code run, part 2/20: Rename RoleRunner's run methods and run-context members (planned 2026-10-16 by user, done 2026-10-20; requires part 1/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/runner.ts + src/runner/runner-run.ts + src/runner/runner-pi.ts + every caller and stub of those members)

**Goal.** Mechanical. `RoleRunner.tick()` becomes `run()`, and every other tick-named member of `RoleRunner`, `RunnerRunContext` and `RunnerPiHost` takes its run name, with all callers, stubs and test overrides moved in the same part. Members cannot carry aliases.

**Approach.**
- Renames (members, so no aliases; rename every use in src/ and test/ here):
  - `RoleRunner`: `tick()` → `run()`, `abortTick()` → `abortRun()`, `handBackTick()` → `handBackRun()`, `tickModel()` → `runModelPair()` (not `runModel`, which is `RunVerdictContext`'s field for the agent run's model), private `runTick` → `runOnce`, `tickContext()` → `runContext()`, `tickPrompt()` → `runPrompt()`, fields `tickAbort` → `runAbort` and `tickPair` → `runPair`, `finishAbortedTick` → `finishAbortedRun`, `finishRecoveryTick` → `finishRecoveryRun`.
  - `RunnerRunContext` (src/runner/runner-run.ts): `tickPrompt` → `runPrompt`, `setTickPair` → `setRunPair`, `resetTickAbort` → `resetRunAbort`, `runTick` → `runOnce`, `finishAbortedTick` → `finishAbortedRun`, `finishRecoveryTick` → `finishRecoveryRun`.
  - `RunnerPiHost` (src/runner/runner-pi.ts): `tickNumber` → `runNumber`.
- Callers: src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts (`tickModel` parameter → `runModelPair`), src/operator/operator-requests.ts, and src/run/run-stage.ts, run-verdict.ts, run-resume.ts and run-timing.ts where they call these members.
- Test overrides and fakes are not type-checked, because they use casts (`as unknown as RoleRunner`) or monkeypatching, so find them by grep, not tsc. Search test/ for `runTick`, `.tick(`, `tick:`, `tickModel`, `handBackTick`, `abortTick` and `stubRunTick`. Known sites: test/runner.test.ts (`(runner as unknown as { runTick … }).runTick = …`), test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts's `fakeRunner(role, tick)` (property `tick` → `run`), test/gate-polls.test.ts and test/gate-event-best-effort.test.ts (`tickModel:`, `handBackTick:`), test/operator-requests.test.ts (`bad.abortTick = …`), test/orchestrator-seams.test.ts, test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts, test/agent-commit-fold.test.ts, test/pi.test.ts, and every test/runner*.test.ts and test/revision.test.ts call of `.tick()`. Also `stubRunTick` → `stubRunOnce`. A missed override fails at runtime, never at compile time.
- Leave node:test mock clocks alone: `t.mock.timers.tick(ms)` and test/inbox.test.ts's `clock.tick(…)` are not runner methods.
- Update comment mentions of exactly these member names in the touched files. Wider comment wording waits for each file's own part.

**Files touched.** src/runner/runner.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts, src/operator/operator-requests.ts, src/run/run-stage.ts, src/run/run-verdict.ts, src/run/run-resume.ts, src/run/run-timing.ts, the test files named above, test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts, test/fixtures/runner-pi-fixtures.ts and test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -rnE '\.(tick|abortTick|handBackTick|tickModel|runTick)\(|\b(stubRunTick|setTickPair|resetTickAbort|tickAbort|tickPair|tickContext)\b|\btick(Model|Prompt)?:\s*(async|\()' src test` prints nothing, apart from `mock.timers.tick` and test/inbox.test.ts's clock helper.
- `RoleRunner` declares `run()`, `abortRun()`, `handBackRun()` and `runModelPair()`, and no tick-named member.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged, including `npm run test:e2e`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's role and Settings writes say when nothing changed, the browser twin of the in-flight `tumwater role <id>` "already"/"not set" entry (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry. The role-config entry edits src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, test/cli-operators.test.ts and docs/cli.md and leaves the GUI alone. The revert entry edits `handleRevert` in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, not this file. Part 2/20 edits the runner. The cancel entry also edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, but in its backlog-drawer Cancel callback, not the cap callback this entry changes, so whichever lands second rebases. Touches src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts, `setRoleModelFields` in src/config/config-write.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts (cap callback), src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts (`saveSetting`), test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui-client-boot.test.ts and test/gui-client-settings.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** The dashboard's per-role writes in src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts always answer as if they wrote something. `handleRoleInterval` and `handleRoleInstances` answer `<base>: … set to …` or `… cleared`. `writeRoleJsonKey`, the shared write for `handleRoleInstructions` and `handleRoleQuietHours`, does the same. `setRoleEnabled` answers `<base>: enabled`/`disabled`, and `handleRoleModel` answers `<base>: model updated`. Each answer is the same when the value was already in place or the key was never set. The existing tests ("handleRoleQuietHours clearing a key the file never set writes nothing", "handleRoleInterval clears a key the file never set without writing …", "handleRoleInstances clears a key the file never set …") prove that such a request leaves tumwater.json byte-identical, yet the flash says `cleared`. `handleRoleCap` and `handleConfigSet` drop `setConfigKey`'s `unchanged` flag, so the drawer flashes `Daily cap set to $2` and Settings flashes `Saved model` for a value that was already there. The CLI already reports these no-ops for `config set`/`config unset` and `role --enable`/`--disable`; the in-flight `role <id>` entry adds the per-role flags. The dashboard should say the same.

**Approach.**
- src/config/config-write.ts `setRoleModelFields`: when no field changed, return `{ ok: true, unchanged: true }`. Capture the flag in a closure variable, as `setConfigKey` does. Widen the return type to `{ ok: true; unchanged?: true } | { ok: false; error: string }`. The TUI caller (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts) only reads `ok`, so leave it as is.
- src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts uses the CLI's wording for a no-op. Every no-op still answers 200 and writes nothing:
  - Clear arms (`handleRoleInterval`, `handleRoleInstances`, `writeRoleJsonKey`): when `unsetConfigKey`'s `oldValue === undefined`, the message is `${base}: ${noun} is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was cleared`. The nouns are `min run interval`, `instances`, and `writeRoleJsonKey`'s existing `noun`. Otherwise keep the `cleared` message.
  - Set arms: when `setConfigKey` returns `unchanged`:
    - `handleRoleInterval`: `${base}: min run interval is already ${value}s, so tumwater.json was not written`.
    - `handleRoleInstances`: `${base}: instances is already ${value}, so tumwater.json was not written`.
    - `writeRoleJsonKey`: `${base}: ${noun} unchanged, so tumwater.json was not written`. This one form fits both the instructions text and a quiet-hours window, so the function gains no parameter.
  - `setRoleEnabled`: on `unchanged`, `${base}: already enabled`/`${base}: already disabled`, matching `cmdRole`'s `${base}: already ${state}`.
  - `handleRoleModel`: on `unchanged`, `${base}: model overrides unchanged, so tumwater.json was not written`.
  - `handleRoleCap` and `handleConfigSet`: add `unchanged: true` to the JSON when `setConfigKey` returned it, and leave the other fields as they are.
  - Each handler's doc comment gains one clause saying a no-op reports itself.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts: the `/api/role-cap` callback returns `Daily cap unchanged` when `d && d.unchanged`; otherwise its current wording stands. The other drawer callbacks already show `d.message`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts `saveSetting`: when `d && d.unchanged`, flash `key + " is already that value — nothing saved"`; otherwise keep its current flashes. `clearSetting` already handles a no-op.
- Leave `handleConfigUnset`, `handleBudget`, the TUI, and the CLI alone.

**Tests.**
- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts: in each never-set-clear test named above, also assert the response's `message` matches `/is not set in tumwater\.json, so nothing was cleared/`. Add assertions that writing the same value twice leaves the bytes identical and the second response says so:
  - interval: `/min run interval is already 300s/`
  - instances: `/instances is already 2/`
  - quiet hours: `/quiet hours unchanged/`
  - `handleRoleModel`, the same triple twice: `/model overrides unchanged/`
  - `handleRoleEnable` on an already-enabled role: `/already enabled/`
  - `handleRoleCap` and `handleConfigSet`, the same value twice: `unchanged === true` on the second response
  - Each first write still answers its current message.
- test/gui-client-boot.test.ts: next to the cap-save case, a `postAction` stub whose `done` gets `{ unchanged: true }` flashes `Daily cap unchanged`.
- test/gui-client-settings.test.ts: next to "saveSetting posts the row's key and value and flashes the outcome", a reply carrying `unchanged: true` flashes `model is already that value — nothing saved`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- POST /api/role-interval `{role:"feature", minRunIntervalSeconds:null}` on a file without that key answers 200 with `feature: min run interval is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was cleared`, and the file bytes do not change.
- Posting the same quiet-hours window twice answers `feature: quiet hours unchanged, so tumwater.json was not written` the second time, and the bytes do not change.
- POST /api/role-enable for an enabled role answers `<base>: already enabled`.
- A second identical /api/role-cap or /api/config-set answers `unchanged: true`, and the drawer or Settings flash says so.
- Changed values, refusals (400s), and their messages are as before.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater revert` names the role whose commit it undid, and drops the "the reverted role may redo the work" line when no role made it (an operator, the harness or a hand-made commit) (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry: the cancel entry edits src/backlog and its GUI/TUI callers, the role-config entry src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, part 2/20 the runner; this one touches src/git/commit-message.ts, src/operator/revert.ts, `cmdRevert` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts, `handleRevert` in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, their tests and docs/cli.md's revert clause) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** After a revert, `cmdRevert` (src/operator/operator-commands.ts) always prints `the reverted role may redo the work, so cancel or edit its PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry if it should not`, and `handleRevert` (src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts) puts the same words in its `message`. That is wrong when no role made the commit. Examples: a `tumwater(operator):` commit such as a `plan --cancel`, `brief` edit or earlier revert; the harness's own `tumwater(tumwater): Revert …` from src/baseline/main-revert.ts; or a hand-made commit. The test "revert succeeds on main, prints the new head, and revers to a clean tree" (test/cli-operators.test.ts) reverts a hand-made "work to undo" commit and asserts the line anyway. When a role did make the commit, the line does not say which one, so the operator has to go back to `git log` to find whose entry to cancel.

**Approach.**
- src/git/commit-message.ts: beside `commitSubject`, export `stampedRole(message: string): string | undefined`. It returns the `<role>` of a first line that matches `SUBJECT_PREFIX` (add a capture group to the regex; `commitSubject` stays as it is), and undefined for an unstamped line.
- src/operator/revert.ts: `revertMergedCommit` reads the target's subject (`git log -1 --format=%s <full>`, as `previewRevert` does) before reverting. Its ok result gains `subject: string`. Export `revertFollowUp(subject: string): string | null`:
  - `stampedRole(subject)` is undefined, `operator` or `tumwater`: return null.
  - Any other role: return `the <role> role may redo the work, so cancel or edit its PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry if it should not`.
- `cmdRevert`: print the follow-up only when it is non-null.
- `handleRevert`: the `message` is `main is now <sha>`, plus ` — <follow-up>` when one exists. Also return `subject` in the JSON.
- No other wording, exit code or refusal changes. The dry-run path is untouched.

**Tests.**
- test/cli-operators.test.ts "revert succeeds on main …": the hand-made commit prints no `may redo` line; assert with `doesNotMatch`. Add one case that commits `tumwater(feature): add x` and reverts it; stdout contains `the feature role may redo the work`.
- test/gui-revert.test.ts: change the `message` regex the same way. Its fixture's commit decides which form applies; check the fixture and assert the matching form.
- test/operator-revert.test.ts (or the commit-message test file): unit-test `stampedRole` (stamped, unstamped, `tumwater(operator):`) and `revertFollowUp` (null for operator/tumwater/unstamped, named for `feature`).
- test/gui-client-history.test.ts only feeds a canned message, so leave it alone.

**Docs.** docs/cli.md's revert clause: if it describes the success output, say the follow-up names the role from the reverted commit's `tumwater(<role>):` stamp and is left out for operator, harness and hand-made commits.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater revert <sha>` of a hand-made commit prints `main is now <sha>` and no `may redo` line, exit 0.
- Reverting a `tumwater(operator): …` commit also prints no `may redo` line.
- Reverting a `tumwater(feature): …` commit prints `the feature role may redo the work, so cancel or edit its PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry if it should not`.
- `POST /api/revert` answers with the same follow-up in `message` (or none), plus `subject`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater plan|bug --cancel <n>` says when a role is working on the cancelled entry and how to stop it, so cancelling an in-flight plan no longer reads as stopping its work (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the pause/resume entry edits src/operator/operator-intent.ts, the revert entry src/operator/revert.ts and operator-commands.ts' revert commands, the part 2/20 rename src/run and the runner; this one touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, their tests and docs/cli.md); done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `plan --list` already marks a claimed entry `[working on it: feature #2]` (`inProgressMark`, src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts), but cancelling that entry says only `cancelled plan in PLANS.md: <title>`. The cancel removes the heading; the orchestrator then drops the runner's claim as `left` (`claimReleaseReason`, src/scheduling/claims.ts, called from src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts), which clears `state.claim` and nothing else — the run in progress goes on implementing, and spending on, the work the operator just retracted. Every cancel surface (CLI, TUI Backlog Ctrl+X, dashboard drawer Cancel) should name the role and the stop command, `tumwater abort --role <runner id>` (`requestAbort`, src/operator/operator-intent.ts).

**Approach.**
- src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, beside `inProgressMark`: export `cancelledClaimNote(runner: string | null): string` — `""` for null, else ``${roleLabel(runner)} is still working on it — its run goes on; `tumwater abort --role ${runner}` stops it``.
- Each surface snapshots `allLiveClaims(root)` (src/runner/runner-state.ts, already imported by backlog-eligibility.ts) BEFORE its cancel call — the orchestrator may release the claim right after the heading leaves — and after a successful cancel looks up `claims.get(entryKey(<removed title>)) ?? null`.
  - `cancelAndAnnounce` (src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts): after the existing `cancelled …` line, `say` the note on its own line when non-empty. `--json` adds `workingOn: "<runner id>"` to the payload only when claimed (the payload is otherwise unchanged).
  - `cancelArmed` (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts): on `cancelled`, the flash becomes `cancelled <kind> #<n>: <title> — <note>` when the note is non-empty; unchanged otherwise.
  - `handleBacklogCancel` (src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts): add `workingNote: <note>` to the `cancelled` 200 JSON only when non-empty. The `entry-cancel` callback in src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts appends `" — " + d.workingNote` to its `Cancelled “…”` flash when present.
- docs/cli.md: the plan/bug row's `--cancel <n> retracts one` clause gains "and names the role still working on it, with the `abort` that stops its run".

**Files.** src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts, test/backlog-write-list.test.ts (or whichever CLI test already covers `plan --cancel`), test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/tui-keys.test.ts, docs/cli.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit: `cancelledClaimNote(null) === ""`; `cancelledClaimNote("feature-2")` contains `feature #2 is still working on it` and ``tumwater abort --role feature-2``.
- CLI: with a claim seeded as the existing "plan --list marks the entry a role is working on" test seeds it (`saveRunnerState(repo, { ...loadRunnerState(repo, "feature-2"), claim: { …, key: entryKey(title), title } })`), `plan --cancel 1` exits 0, the entry is gone from PLANS.md, stdout has the `cancelled plan in PLANS.md:` line and a line containing `tumwater abort --role feature-2`; `--json` carries `workingOn: "feature-2"`. Cancelling an unclaimed entry prints only the `cancelled …` line, and its `--json` has no `workingOn` key.
- GUI: POST /api/backlog-cancel on a claimed entry answers `status: "cancelled"` with a `workingNote` containing `tumwater abort --role feature-2`; on an unclaimed entry the response has no `workingNote`.

### `tumwater resume --role` and `pause --role` say when the role is disabled, so `resume --role selfcheck` no longer promises runs a disabled role never starts (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the config-set entry edits src/config/config-write.ts and src/cli/config-commands.ts, the revert entry src/operator/revert.ts and src/operator/operator-commands.ts' revert commands; this one touches src/operator/operator-intent.ts, test/operator-intent.test.ts and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** On a fresh project (selfcheck ships disabled), `tumwater resume --role selfcheck` after `pause --role selfcheck` prints `role selfcheck resumed — it starts new runs again; tumwater is not running, so it takes effect on the next `tumwater start`` (checked against main's built CLI on 2026-10-20). That is false: a disabled role has no runner, so it starts no runs however its pause stands. `pause --role selfcheck` likewise says `it starts no new runs` as if the pause were what holds it. `tumwater wake` already names disabled targets (`disabledWakeNote`, landed 2026-10-20); the pause/resume confirmations should do the same, with the same fix command.

**Approach.**
- In src/operator/operator-intent.ts, extract from `disabledWakeNote` a small helper `disabledOf(root, roles): string[]` (the `loadConfigCached` read and the `config.roles[baseRoleOf(id)]?.enabled === false` filter; `[]` when the config cannot be read). `disabledWakeNote` calls it; its wording and tests stay as they are.
- `roleResumeMessage(root, role, changed)`: when `changed` and `disabledOf(root, [role])` is non-empty, replace the `it starts new runs again` clause with `it is disabled, so it still starts no runs — enable it with tumwater config set roles.<role>.enabled true`, keeping `${when}`, the team-pause note and `${tail}` as today. The `was not paused` no-op is unchanged.
- `rolePauseMessage(root, role, changed, timed, now)`: when `changed` and the role is disabled, append `; <role> is disabled, so it starts no runs either way — the pause holds once you enable it` after the existing confirmation (before `${tail}` is fine; pick one and assert it). The `is already paused` no-op is unchanged.
- Both functions are shared by the CLI (`cmdPause`/`cmdResume` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts) and the TUI's Ctrl+P (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts), so neither caller changes.
- docs/cli.md "Control the roles" row: one clause saying `pause`/`resume --role` name a disabled role, as the `wake` row does.

**Files.** src/operator/operator-intent.ts, test/operator-intent.test.ts, docs/cli.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**

### `tumwater revert` refuses a root or merge commit, as its `--dry-run` already does, so `tumwater revert <init sha>` no longer deletes the brief and the backlog (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — those edit src/config, src/cli/config-commands.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/operator/operator-intent.ts and the src/tick→src/run move; this one touches src/operator/revert.ts, docs/cli.md and test/operator-revert.test.ts only; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `previewRevert` (src/operator/revert.ts) refuses a commit that does not have exactly one parent (`<short> has <n> parents; revert previews a single-parent commit only`). `revertMergedCommit`, which `cmdRevert` (src/operator/operator-commands.ts) and the dashboard's revert (`gui-operator-commands.ts`) both call, has no such guard. So the preview refuses a commit that the real revert goes on to change. Checked on 2026-10-20 against main's built CLI in a fresh `git init` + `tumwater init hello` repo: `tumwater revert HEAD`, where HEAD is the `tumwater: init` root commit, exits 0, prints `main is now <sha>` and commits `tumwater(operator): Revert <sha>`. That commit deletes README.md (the brief), PLANS.md, BUGS.md, QUESTIONS.md, PRINCIPLES.md and .gitignore, and leaves tumwater.json untracked. It then prints `the reverted role may redo the work`, though no role made that commit. For a merge commit, `git revert --no-commit <merge>` fails without `-m`, and `revertCommitIn` reports this as `reverting <short> conflicted`, which is not what happened. The fix is to refuse both cases the way the preview does. Supporting `-m` is out of scope: harness merges are fast-forwards, and the preview already sets the single-parent-only policy.

**Approach (src/operator/revert.ts).**
- Pull the preview's inline parent count out into one module-private helper, `async function parentRefusal(root: string, full: string): Promise<string | null>`. It runs `runGit(root, ["rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", full])` and counts the words after the first. When the count is not 1 it returns `` `${shortSha(full)} has ${n} parents; tumwater revert undoes a single-parent commit only, so nothing was written` ``. Otherwise it returns null.
- `previewRevert` calls it in place of its inline check: a non-null result → `{ ok: false, error }`. Its try/catch stays as it is.
- `revertMergedCommit` calls it inside the lock, right after `resolveRevertTarget` succeeds and before the dirty-tree check: a non-null result → `{ ok: false, error }`, with nothing staged or committed. Its outer try/catch already turns a git failure into the `did not complete` error.
- Leave `revertCommitIn` and `resolveRevertTarget` alone. The automatic culprit revert in src/baseline/main-revert.ts (INV-L1 in docs/invariants.md) and the dashboard's `handleTick` on-base check call them, and neither should change.
- No CLI or GUI edit is needed. `cmdRevert` passes `result.error` to `fail` and the dashboard's revert handler returns it, so both pick up the refusal. The `--dry-run` text changes from `revert previews …` to the shared wording.

**Docs.** In docs/cli.md's "Steer the project" row, extend `refusing off the base branch, on an unknown or unmerged ref, and on a conflict` to `refusing off the base branch, on an unknown or unmerged ref, on a root or merge commit, and on a conflict`.

**Tests (test/operator-revert.test.ts).** Use the file's existing `makeRepo`/`seedCommit`/`sh`/`headSha` fixtures and its `statusPorcelain` helper.
- `revertMergedCommit(repo, <root sha>)` (root from `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`, after one `seedCommit`) returns `ok: false` with an error matching `/has 0 parents; tumwater revert undoes a single-parent commit only/`. HEAD is unchanged and `statusPorcelain` is empty.
- A merge commit: branch off, `seedCommit` on the branch, check the base branch back out, `git merge --no-ff -m merge <branch>`. `revertMergedCommit(repo, "HEAD")` returns `ok: false` matching `/has 2 parents/`, leaves HEAD at the merge commit, and `statusPorcelain` is empty. `previewRevert(repo, "HEAD")` refuses with the same error.
- The existing "previewRevert refuses an unknown ref and a root commit" test (`/has 0 parents/`) passes unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater revert <root sha>` and `tumwater revert <merge sha>` exit 1 with `tumwater: <short> has <n> parents; tumwater revert undoes a single-parent commit only, so nothing was written`, and leave HEAD and the tracked tree alone.
- `tumwater revert <sha> --dry-run` on either one prints the same error, and the dashboard's revert returns the same text in its `error`.
- A single-parent revert behaves as before: every existing test in test/operator-revert.test.ts and test/cli-operators.test.ts passes unchanged.
- src/baseline/main-revert.ts and `revertCommitIn` are untouched (`git diff --stat` shows neither).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater config set <key> <value>` says `already` and writes nothing when the key already resolves to that value (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the `role <id> --enable`/`--disable` entry makes the same "already" change in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts and calls setConfigKey only when the state differs, so the two do not overlap; this one touches src/config/config-write.ts, src/cli/config-commands.ts, test/config-commands.test.ts and docs/cli.md's `tumwater config` row); done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** On a fresh project, `tumwater config set maxConcurrent 6` exits 0 and prints `set maxConcurrent to 6`, and `config set roles.selfcheck.enabled false` prints `set roles.selfcheck.enabled to false` (checked against main's built CLI on 2026-10-20). Neither changed anything: 6 is the resolved run cap and selfcheck ships disabled. The confirmation reads as if the command did something, so an operator who expected a change learns nothing. `config unset` already reports its no-op (`<key> is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed`); `set` should do the same.

**Approach.**
- **src/config/config-write.ts `setConfigKey`.** Each arm of both `writeConfigMutation` callbacks (the dotted one: `map`, `tier`, `section`, `agent`, role field; and the top-level one) already computes `oldValue` from the loaded, defaults-merged config. Right after that, in each arm, add `if (isDeepStrictEqual(oldValue, value)) return cfg;`. Import `isDeepStrictEqual` from `node:util`. `writeConfigMutation` already treats `mutated === cfg` as "write nothing" (the unset no-op), so the file stays byte-identical. Set a local `unchanged` flag in that branch. Add `unchanged?: true` to the ok result type and return it as `{ ok: true, value, oldValue, unchanged: true }`. The `tier` arm's object-entry `note` cannot apply when unchanged: a string value never deep-equals an object entry. Extend the function's doc comment with one sentence: a value equal to the resolved one is a no-op that writes nothing and returns `unchanged`. The comparison uses the resolved value, not the file's raw text, because the resolved value is what the runtime reads. Setting a key to its default when the file omits it therefore changes no behavior and is reported as already set.
- **src/cli/config-commands.ts `cmdConfig`'s `set` branch.** When `result.unchanged`, print `${k} is already ${JSON.stringify(value)}, so tumwater.json was not written` (with `k = canonicalConfigKey(key ?? "")`) and return before the `note:` lines. Exit code stays 0. The bare-`roles` note is skipped too, because nothing was replaced. Otherwise keep the `set … to …` line unchanged.
- Leave the TUI editors and GUI routes that call `setConfigKey` alone. They ignore the new field, and they now just skip a redundant rewrite.

**Tests (test/config-commands.test.ts).** Add `test("set of the value a key already resolves to says already and writes nothing", …)`:
- With `writeConfig(root, { model: "m1" })`, `cmdConfig(root, ["set", "model", "m1"])` prints exactly `model is already "m1", so tumwater.json was not written\n`, does not exit, and leaves the file bytes unchanged (compare `fs.readFileSync` before and after).
- A dotted role field: `set roles.selfcheck.enabled false` on the same project, where selfcheck is disabled by the catalog default, prints `roles.selfcheck.enabled is already false, …`, and the bytes are unchanged.
- A dotted map key already in the file (e.g. `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.qa`, written first) set to the same number prints `already` and leaves the bytes unchanged.
- A different value still prints `set … to …` and writes.

Leave the existing tests as they are. If one fails because it re-sets a key to its current value and expected a write, report it and change that test's input value, not the new rule.

**Docs.** In docs/cli.md's `tumwater config` row, after the `config set` description, add that a value the key already resolves to is reported as `already` and nothing is written.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On a fresh `tumwater init` project, `tumwater config set maxConcurrent 6` prints `maxConcurrent is already 6, so tumwater.json was not written` and exits 0, and tumwater.json is byte-identical before and after.
- `tumwater config set maxConcurrent 3` still prints `set maxConcurrent to 3` and writes 3.
- A type-invalid or unknown-key `config set` fails exactly as before. The validation arms run before the new comparison, and `perKeyValidator` and the field checks are untouched.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater role <id> --enable`/`--disable` says `already enabled`/`already disabled` and leaves tumwater.json alone when the role is already in that state (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the wake entry edits src/operator/operator-intent.ts, the `start --once --role` entry src/cli/cli-run.ts, the `role <id>` instance-id entry src/roles/role-view.ts and test/role-view.test.ts; this one touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, test/cli-operators.test.ts and docs/cli.md's `tumwater role <id>` row) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** On a fresh project, `tumwater role selfcheck --disable` exits 0 and prints `selfcheck: disabled`, and `tumwater role feature --enable` prints `feature: enabled` (checked against main's built CLI on 2026-10-20). Neither role changed state: selfcheck ships disabled and feature enabled. The line reads as if the command did something, so an operator who mistyped which role they meant, or who expected selfcheck to have been running, learns nothing. A write that changes nothing should say so.

**Approach.** In `cmdRole`'s enable/disable branch (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, the `if (enable || disable)` block), after `requireKnownRole` and the director refusal, and after computing `base`, read the role's resolved state with `loadConfigSafe(root).config` (already imported there). If the config loaded and `config.roles[base]?.enabled === enable`, print `${base}: already ${enable ? "enabled" : "disabled"}` and return without calling `setConfigKey`. Otherwise keep the existing write and the `${base}: enabled|disabled` line. The resolved state comes from the merged config, which seeds every catalog role and every custom role (a custom absent from `roles` is enabled). That makes the check correct whether or not the file holds the key explicitly. When the config does not load (`config` undefined), skip the check and fall through to the write, which still reports `setConfigKey`'s error through `fail`. Exit code stays 0 for the no-op. Extend the comment above the branch with one sentence on the no-op. Do not touch the GUI's enable/disable handlers (src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts): their responses feed the drawer, not a typed confirmation line.

- After `role feature --disable`, a second `role feature --disable` exits 0, matches `/feature: already disabled/`, and leaves the file bytes unchanged. The existing `--enable` that follows still prints `feature: enabled`.
- `role selfcheck --disable` on the fresh project matches `/selfcheck: already disabled/`.
- Adjust the director block: `role director --enable` after the refused disable now prints `director: already enabled`. Keep its `code 0` and `enabled === true` assertions, and add the stdout match.

**Docs.** In docs/cli.md's `tumwater role <id>` row, after the `--enable`/`--disable` clause, add that a role already in the asked-for state is reported as `already enabled`/`already disabled` and the file is not written.

- `tumwater role selfcheck --enable` then prints `selfcheck: enabled` and writes `roles.selfcheck.enabled: true`. Repeating it prints `selfcheck: already enabled`.

### `tumwater role <id>` refuses an instance id the config does not run, so `tumwater role feature-9` no longer shows a made-up role card (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — part 16/16 edits test/ comments only, the wake entry edits src/operator/operator-intent.ts, the `start --once --role` entry edits src/cli/cli-run.ts; this one touches src/roles/role-view.ts and test/role-view.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

With `writeConfig(dir, { roles: { feature: { enabled: true, instances: 2 } } })`, `rolePayload(dir, "feature-4", NO_MODELS)` returns a payload, and `feature-5` throws, because runnerCount is twice the instances.

Add `roles: { feature: { enabled: true, instances: 2 } }` to its `writeConfig`. Run the file and fix any other test that reads an instance id it never configured in the same way, by configuring the instances; do not loosen the guard.

### `tumwater wake` says which of the roles it names are disabled, so a bare `wake` no longer reads as waking `selfcheck` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the config get/set/unset entries edit src/cli/config-commands.ts and src/config, part 16/16 edits test/ comments only; this one touches src/operator/operator-intent.ts, docs/cli.md and test/operator-intent.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On a fresh project, `tumwater wake` prints `wake requested for feature, bugfix, plan, …, selfcheck, …, director — takes effect on the next tumwater start …` (checked against main's built CLI on 2026-10-20), and `wake --role selfcheck` prints `wake requested for selfcheck — …`. `selfcheck` is disabled by default (`roles.selfcheck.enabled` is false), so it has no runner and will not run, whatever the message says. Clearing a disabled role's backoff is deliberate: `requestWake` and `applyWakeMarker`'s `runnerlessTargets` loop do it so that the role starts fresh once it is enabled. Keep the targets as they are and fix only the wording. The confirmation should say which named roles are disabled and won't run until they are enabled.

**Approach.** Do all of it in `requestWake` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts), the one place that builds the confirmation for the CLI (`cmdWake`), the dashboard (`handleWake`), the TUI (`tui-editor-pause.ts`, `tui-pane-backlog.ts`) and backlog filing (`backlog-cli.ts`), so none of them drift.
- Read the config with `loadConfigCached(root).config` (src/config/config.ts). Use the cached read, not `loadConfig`: a broken config must not make a wake throw. When it returns no config, nothing changes.
- A target is disabled when `config.roles[baseRoleOf(id)]?.enabled === false` (`baseRoleOf`, src/roles/runner-ids.ts). An id with no config entry is not called disabled, so the existing tests' `fix` role keeps its current message.
- When one or more targets are disabled, append one clause after the existing message, for the immediate and the scheduled form alike: `; <ids> <is|are> disabled, so the wake only ends <its|their> sleep — <it|they> won't run until you enable <it|them> with tumwater config set roles.<id>.enabled true`. For several ids, write `roles.<id>.enabled` literally, as the template. Join the ids with `, `.

If the existing `applyClause` text differs from that, keep its wording and append only the `; selfcheck is disabled …` clause.

### `tumwater start --once --role <id>` calls a disabled role disabled, not unknown, so `start --once --role selfcheck` names the fix instead of denying the role exists (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the config get/set/unset entries edit src/cli/config-commands.ts and src/config, the wake entry edits src/operator/operator-intent.ts, part 16/16 edits test/ comments only; this one touches src/cli/cli-run.ts, docs/cli.md and test/cli-run-guards.test.ts); done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** On a fresh project, `tumwater start --once --role selfcheck` prints `tumwater: unknown role: selfcheck (valid ids: feature, bugfix, …, director)`, with selfcheck missing from the list (checked against main's built CLI on 2026-10-20). Yet `tumwater role selfcheck` shows the role (`State: disabled, not paused`), and `tumwater report --role selfcheck` accepts it. The refusal is right: a scoped round that booted a disabled role's runner would run nothing. The wording is wrong, though: the role exists and is disabled, and the operator needs the one-line fix. An id that is unknown keeps today's message.

**Approach.** All of it goes in `cmdRun`'s scoped-round parse in src/cli/cli-run.ts, where `parseRoleListFlag(args, runnerIds(config))` validates `--role` today.
- Parse against `knownRoleIds(config)` (src/config/config.ts) instead. It holds every catalog and custom id, enabled or not, plus enabled roles' instance ids. That way a known id gets past the parser, and a typo still fails there with `unknownRoleMessage` and its `did you mean` hint.
- Then check each parsed id against `runnerIds(config)` (src/roles/runner-ids.ts), in the order given. For the first id not among them:
  - When `config.roles[baseRoleOf(id)]?.enabled === false`, fail with `` `<id> is disabled, so a --once round cannot run it — enable it with \`tumwater role <base> --enable\`` ``. Here `<base>` is `baseRoleOf(id)`, and the `tumwater role <id> --enable` command lives in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts.
  - Otherwise fail with `unknownRoleMessage(id, runnerIds(config))`. This branch is defensive: every id in `knownRoleIds` that is not a runner belongs to a disabled role. An instance id beyond the configured count, such as `feature-5` with two instances, is not in `knownRoleIds` at all, so the parser already refuses it.
- Keep the check before booting and after `runStartupCheck`, where it is now. `--role is only valid with --once` keeps its position. Rewrite the comment above the parse so it says that a disabled id is named as disabled rather than read as unknown.

**Docs.** docs/cli.md, in the `tumwater start --once` comment line that reads `# add --role <id>[,<id>...] to scope the round to the listed roles`, append `(enabled roles only)`.

**Tests (test/cli-run-guards.test.ts).**
- Rename and update "run --once --role validates against enabled ids: a disabled built-in reads as unknown" to "run --once --role names a disabled built-in as disabled". It runs `cli(repo, "run", "--once", "--role", "clean")` with `roles.clean.enabled` false and expects exit 1, stderr matching `/clean is disabled, so a --once round cannot run it — enable it with `tumwater role clean --enable`/`, stderr not matching `/unknown role/`, and no events.
- Update "run --once --role rejects a list naming a disabled role before booting" (`clean,readme`, readme disabled) to expect `/readme is disabled/` and still no events.
- New test: `run --once --role cleen` still fails with `/unknown role: cleen \(valid ids: /` and `` /did you mean `clean`/ ``, with no events.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `roles.selfcheck.enabled` false, `tumwater start --once --role selfcheck` exits 1 with `tumwater: selfcheck is disabled, so a --once round cannot run it — enable it with \`tumwater role selfcheck --enable\``, and writes no events.
- An id outside `knownRoleIds(config)` still fails with `unknownRoleMessage`'s text and typo hint. Its valid-ids list is now `knownRoleIds(config)`, so it names disabled roles too (selfcheck included), the same list `tumwater role <typo>` prints.
- An enabled id or list still scopes the round as before. The existing scoped-round tests in test/orchestrator-once.e2e.test.ts and test/cli-run-guards.test.ts pass, apart from the two updated above.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater config get|set|unset` reach one field of the fixed-shape sections, so `config set bootstrap.untilPlansDone 3` and `config get review.model` work (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; touches src/config/config-keys.ts src/config/config-write.ts src/cli/config-commands.ts src/cli/completion.ts docs/config.md and their tests; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater.json` has four top-level sections whose fields are a fixed list in src/config/config-schema.ts: `review` (`REVIEW_KEYS`), `check` (`CHECK_KEYS`), `idleBackoff` (`BACKOFF_KEYS`) and `bootstrap` (`BOOTSTRAP_KEYS`). `parseConfigKey` (src/config/config-keys.ts) refuses every dotted key into them, so on main's build `tumwater config get bootstrap.untilPlansDone`, `config set bootstrap.untilPlansDone 3`, `config get review.model` and `config set idleBackoff.factor 3` each fail with the generic `unknown config key "…" — dotted keys name one entry of a per-role map or one field of a role entry …`. The only way to change one field is to re-type the whole section as JSON (`config set review '{…}'`), which drops any field the operator forgets. `roles.<id>.<field>`, `backends.<id>.<field>` and `model.<tier>` already work this way; this extends the same dotted form to the four sections, nothing else.

**Approach.**
- **src/config/config-keys.ts.** Add `export const DOTTED_SECTION_FIELDS = { review: REVIEW_KEYS, check: CHECK_KEYS, idleBackoff: BACKOFF_KEYS, bootstrap: BOOTSTRAP_KEYS } as const` (imported from config-schema.ts), and a `ParsedConfigKey` variant `{ kind: "section"; section: keyof typeof DOTTED_SECTION_FIELDS; field: string }`. In `parseConfigKey`, before the generic error: when `parts.length === 2` and `first` is a section key, return the `section` kind if `second` is in that section's field list, else `{ kind: "error", error: \`unknown ${first} field "${second}" (valid fields: …)${typoSuffix(second, fields)}\` }` — the wording `unknownRoleFieldError` and the `backends.` arm use. Add the four section names to `DOTTED_KEY_HEADS` so a typo'd head (`bootstarp.untilPlansDone`) gets the did-you-mean. Extend the generic error's examples with `` `review.model x` `` so it names the new form.
- **src/config/config-write.ts `setConfigKey`.** A `section` arm in the `writeConfigMutation` callback, modelled on the `agent` arm: merge the one field into the loaded config's section (`{ ...(record[section] ?? {}), [field]: value }`), keeping every other field. (Every `config set` already writes the whole loaded config, defaults included — on main's build `config set maxConcurrent 3` on a fresh project writes the full `idleBackoff` and `review` sections — so this adds no new spill.) `oldValue` is the loaded field. `validateConfig` inside `writeConfigMutation` owns the value type (`checkObjectSection` arms in src/config/config-validation.ts), so a bad value fails there and the file stays byte-identical. Keep the file's roles section with `preservingFileRoles`, as the `map`/`agent` arms do.
- **`unsetConfigKey`.** A `section` arm modelled on the `agent` arm: a field absent from the file's section is a no-op success; otherwise remove it and write through `withSectionOrDropped(root, cfg, section, next)` so an emptied section leaves the file (unsetting `bootstrap.untilPlansDone` removes `bootstrap`, which ends bootstrap exactly as the README's "remove it from tumwater.json" does).
- **src/cli/config-commands.ts `cmdConfig` get.** A `parsed.kind === "section"` arm reading `(record[section] as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.[field]` from the loaded config, so `get idleBackoff.factor` shows the default when the file is silent. `screenOperableKey` needs no change (no role id to check).
- **src/cli/completion.ts.** Beside the `roles.<id>.<field>` list, add `${section}.${field}` for each `DOTTED_SECTION_FIELDS` entry so `tumwater config set bootstrap.<Tab>` completes.
- **docs/config.md.** The `config get|set|unset` paragraph names the section form (`review.model x`, `bootstrap.untilPlansDone 3`) beside the map and role examples.
- Not in scope: the GUI's `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS`, nested fields below one level (`review.exemptPaths` is set whole as a JSON array), and any other object-valued key (`maxConcurrentPerProvider` is already a dotted map).

**Tests.** In test/config-write.test.ts (setConfigKey/unsetConfigKey) and test/config-unset-key.test.ts or the existing `config get` CLI tests; test/completion.test.ts for the key list.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In an initialized project with `"bootstrap": {"untilPlansDone": 5}`, `tumwater config get bootstrap.untilPlansDone` prints `5`; `config set bootstrap.untilPlansDone 3` exits 0 and the file's `bootstrap` reads `{"untilPlansDone": 3}`; `config unset bootstrap.untilPlansDone` exits 0 and the file holds no `bootstrap` key.
- `config set idleBackoff.factor 3` on a fresh project leaves the file's `idleBackoff` as `{"initialSeconds": 120, "factor": 3, "maxSeconds": 3600}` (the defaults kept, one field changed); `config get idleBackoff.factor` then prints `3`.
- `config set review.model x` keeps every other field the file's `review` held (a test seeds `review.enabled` and `review.afterMerge` and checks both survive).
- `config set idleBackoff.factor abc` exits 1 with validateConfig's message naming `idleBackoff.factor`, and the file is byte-unchanged.
- `config get review.modle` exits 1 with `unknown review field "modle"` listing the valid fields and ending `` did you mean `model`? ``; `config get bootstarp.untilPlansDone` ends `` did you mean `bootstrap`? ``.
- `config get roles.qa.model`, `config set model.strong x`, `config set backends.pi.bin x` and `config set maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.qa 1` behave as before (their existing tests pass unchanged).
- The completion key list contains `bootstrap.untilPlansDone` and `review.model`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater config unset` says what the key now resolves to, and says so plainly when the file never held it, so `config unset maxConcurrent` no longer reads as a change that did not happen (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role, done 2026-10-20; touches src/cli/config-commands.ts test/config-commands.test.ts docs/config.md)

**Goal.** `config unset <key>` removes the file's value, but the key's effective value often stays the same. `tumwater init` writes the defaults into `tumwater.json`, so on a fresh project main's build prints `unset maxConcurrent (was 6)` and then `config get maxConcurrent` prints `6`. `unset idleBackoff` prints `unset idleBackoff (was {"initialSeconds":120,"factor":2,"maxSeconds":3600})` and `get` returns that same object. Both messages say a value went away when nothing changed. Running the same unset again, when the file no longer holds the key, prints `unset maxConcurrent`, which still reads as a removal even though `unsetConfigKey` changed nothing and left the file byte-identical. The confirmation should say what the key resolves to after the unset, and should say clearly when there was nothing to remove.

**Approach (src/cli/config-commands.ts only; `unsetConfigKey` and its `{ ok, oldValue }` contract stay as they are).**
- Move the nested ternary in `cmdConfig`'s `get` arm (the `map`, `tier`, `agent`, `role` and top-level reads of the loaded config) into a module-private `resolvedConfigValue(config: TumwaterConfig, parsed: ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, key: string): unknown` (`ParsedConfigKey` is module-private in config-keys.ts, so name it through `parseConfigKey`), and have `get` call it. `get` keeps its output exactly, including JSON `null` for an absent key. If the planned `section` kind ("`tumwater config get|set|unset` reach one field of the fixed-shape sections") lands first, its `get` arm moves into the helper too.
- In the `unset` arm, keep the `ParsedConfigKey` that `screenOperableKey(root, k)` already returns (`const { parsed } = …`). After a successful `unsetConfigKey`, read `loadConfigSafe(root).config`; when it is defined, set `now = resolvedConfigValue(config, parsed, k)`. When the reload fails, set `now` to undefined, so the message never depends on a reload succeeding. The confirmation then reads:
  - removed, and `now` undefined: `unset <k> (was <old>)`, the same as today;
  - removed, and `now` defined: `unset <k> (was <old>; now resolves to <now>)`;
  - not in the file (`oldValue === undefined`), and `now` defined: `<k> is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed (it resolves to <now>)`;
  - not in the file, and `now` undefined: `<k> is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed`.
  `<old>` and `<now>` are `JSON.stringify` output, as today. The exit code stays 0 in every case: an absent key remains a successful no-op, as `unsetConfigKey`'s doc says.
- The wording says "resolves to" and never "default", because some resolved values do not come from the defaults: a legacy alias (`agentBin`) feeds the `backends.<id>` view, and the role catalog seeds `roles.<id>.minRunIntervalSeconds`.
- Not in scope: the GUI's `/api/config-unset` and the TUI editors, which call `unsetConfigKey` directly and keep their own flashes; `unsetConfigKey` itself; and the whole-config write that rematerializes defaults on every `set` (a later `config set` writes an unset `idleBackoff` back out — leave that alone).

**Tests (test/config-commands.test.ts).** Update the four pinned strings in "unset removes a dotted role field, …" and "unset of a default-carrying key or a default-seeded role field the file never set is a true no-op" to the new no-op wording: `unset roles.qa.model` for the absent field; `maxConcurrent` and `quietHours`; and `roles.qa.minRunIntervalSeconds`, which now reads `… nothing was removed (it resolves to 7200)`. Keep each test's byte-identical file assertions. Add one test that seeds `{ maxConcurrent: 6, idleBackoff: { initialSeconds: 120, factor: 2, maxSeconds: 3600 } }` and asserts that `unset maxConcurrent` prints `unset maxConcurrent (was 6; now resolves to 6)` and that `unset idleBackoff` prints the `was …; now resolves to …` form with both objects. The existing `unset quietHours (was "23:00-07:00")` and `unset roles.qa.model (was "m-qa")` assertions must pass unchanged.

**Docs.** In docs/config.md's `config unset` sentence ("removes one — the inverse of `set`, so a value reverts to its default …"), add that the confirmation names what the key now resolves to and says when the file never held the key.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In a fresh `tumwater init` project, `config unset maxConcurrent` prints `unset maxConcurrent (was 6; now resolves to 6)`. A second `config unset maxConcurrent` prints `maxConcurrent is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed (it resolves to 6)`, exits 0, and leaves the file byte-identical.
- `config unset quietHours` with `"quietHours": "23:00-07:00"` in the file still prints `unset quietHours (was "23:00-07:00")`. With no `quietHours` in the file it prints `quietHours is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed`.
- `config unset roles.qa.minRunIntervalSeconds` on a file that never set it prints `roles.qa.minRunIntervalSeconds is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was removed (it resolves to 7200)`.
- `config get <key>` output is unchanged for every key kind; the existing `get` tests pass unchanged.
- An unknown key, role or role field still fails with the same message (the "unset of an unknown key, role, or role field …" test passes unchanged).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A bare role id given to a `--role` command gets a `did you mean --role <id>?` hint, so `tumwater wake feature` names its fix (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater wake feature`, `pause feature`, `resume feature`, `diff feature`, `logs feature`, `status feature`, `abort feature`, `reset-counters feature` and `retire feature` all fail today with only `unknown argument: feature (valid flags for tumwater wake: --role <id>, …)`: the operator typed the right role in the natural shape and the error does not say the one-token fix. `prompt --role featuer` and `role featuer` already end with `— did you mean \`feature\`?`; this gives the positional slip the same treatment: `unknown argument: feature (valid flags for tumwater wake: …) — did you mean \`--role feature\`?`. A near miss gets the corrected id (`wake featuer` → `` did you mean `--role feature`? ``). The command still fails (exit 1, no side effect). Accepting the positional is not part of this plan: one spelling per command, and a hint fixes the slip without adding a second parse path.

**Approach.** All in `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`:
- `failUnknownArgument(command, arg, specs)` (the generic refusal both `rejectUnknownArgs` and `rejectUnknownDoubleDash` call) picks its suffix as follows. When `specs` includes `ROLE_FLAG` (by identity, `specs.includes(ROLE_FLAG)`), `arg` does not start with `-`, `command !== "role"`, and `suggestClosest(arg, allRoleIds())` (`src/text/suggest.ts`, `src/roles/roles.ts`) returns an id `x`, the suffix is `didYouMean(\`--role ${x}\`)`. Otherwise it keeps today's `typoSuffix(arg, spellings)`. An exact id has distance 0, so `suggestClosest` already returns it, and its first-letter and two-edit rules keep `bogus` from suggesting anything.
- Why `role` is exempt: `cmdRole` (`src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`) peels its own positional id via `peelRolePositional` before `rejectUnknownArgs("role", rest, …)` runs. So in `tumwater role feature bugfix` the stray `bugfix` is a second role and not a missing flag, and the hint would mislead. Leave that path's message unchanged.
- Custom (config-defined) roles get no hint: the parse-time gate has no config. Only built-in ids and `director` (`allRoleIds()`) do. Say so in `failUnknownArgument`'s doc comment.
- Import `allRoleIds` from `../roles/roles.js` and `suggestClosest`/`didYouMean` from `../text/suggest.js`. Check for a circular import: on 2026-10-20 nothing under `src/roles/`, `src/text/` or `src/verdict/` imported from `src/cli/` (`grep -rln 'from "\.\./cli/' src/roles src/text src/verdict`). Re-run that grep before adding the import.
- Update `docs/cli.md` only if it already describes the unknown-argument hint (`grep -n "did you mean" docs/cli.md`). Do not add a new row otherwise.

**Files touched.** `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `test/cli-arg-strictness.test.ts` (or a unit test beside the existing `rejectUnknownArgs` tests: `grep -ln "rejectUnknownArgs" test/`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater wake feature` exits 1, and stderr matches `/unknown argument: feature \(valid flags for tumwater wake: .*\) — did you mean `--role feature`\?/`. It writes no wake marker.
- `tumwater pause featuer` exits 1, stderr ends with `` did you mean `--role feature`? ``, and the team is not paused.
- `tumwater diff bogus` stderr has no `did you mean` (the id is too far, and it is not a flag near miss).
- `tumwater role feature bugfix` stderr has no `--role bugfix` (the `role` exemption).
- `tumwater reset-counters --rol feature` still matches `/unknown argument: --rol/` and still suggests `` `--role` `` (the flag-typo path is unchanged).
- A command whose specs lack `ROLE_FLAG` (`tumwater queue feature`) gets no `--role` hint.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### No error message reads `(got undefined)`: `gotSuffix` names only a value that is present, and `tumwater completion` with no shell or extra words says what is wrong (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight entries touch src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, src/config, src/agent/image-input.ts and src/ comments; this one touches src/text/text.ts, the `completion` case in src/cli.ts, eight call sites that guard `gotSuffix` themselves, test/text.test.ts, test/completion.test.ts, test/gui-revert.test.ts and test/gui-endpoints.test.ts — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Running main's built CLI on 2026-10-20 printed `tumwater: completion takes one shell: bash, zsh, or fish (got undefined)` for a bare `tumwater completion`. For `tumwater completion bash extra` it printed `(got "extra")`, which reads as if `extra` were a bad shell name when the real problem is the word count. `gotSuffix(v)` (src/text/text.ts) is `` ` (got ${JSON.stringify(v)})` ``, and its doc comment leaves undefined values to each caller. Some callers add the guard (`x === undefined ? "" : gotSuffix(x)`) in src/gui/gui-args.ts (three sites), src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts (three), src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts (`questions answer`) and src/agent/role-notes-write.ts. Others don't add it, so a request that leaves out the field gets `(got undefined)`. From reading the code: `handleRevert` (src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts) answers `"sha" must be a hex commit id of 4-64 digits (got undefined)` to a body with no `sha`, and `requireStringField` (src/gui/gui-args.ts) answers `"text" must be a string — … (got undefined)` to a body with no `text`/`prompt`/`window`/model key.

**Approach.**
- `gotSuffix` returns `""` when `v === undefined`. Rewrite its doc comment: drop "Undefined values are the caller's call…" and say instead that a missing value (undefined) appends nothing, because ` (got undefined)` would name a field the request never carried. `null` still prints `(got null)`, since that is a value the request did carry.
- Remove the now-redundant `=== undefined ? "" :` guards at the call sites listed above (find them with `grep -rn 'undefined ? "" : gotSuffix' src`). Messages stay byte-for-byte the same.
- The `completion` case in `src/cli.ts`, past the `--config-keys` branch: with no args, fail `completion needs a shell: bash, zsh, or fish`. With more than one arg, fail `completion takes one shell: bash, zsh, or fish (got N words: <args joined by space>)`. With exactly one unsupported word, keep the current message and its `typoSuffix`. Update the comment above it to match.

**Files touched.** `src/text/text.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `src/gui/gui-args.ts`, `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/agent/role-notes-write.ts`, `test/text.test.ts`, `test/completion.test.ts` (or `test/cli-arg-strictness.test.ts` if the CLI-run tests for completion live there), `test/gui-revert.test.ts`, `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit test: `gotSuffix(undefined) === ""`, `gotSuffix(null) === " (got null)"`, `gotSuffix("x") === ' (got "x")'`.
- `tumwater completion` exits 1 with stderr `tumwater: completion needs a shell: bash, zsh, or fish` and no `got`.
- `tumwater completion bash extra` exits 1, stderr contains `(got 2 words: bash extra)` and no `did you mean`.
- `tumwater completion zs` still ends with `` did you mean `zsh`? ``, and `tumwater completion bash` still prints the bash script.
- A revert POST with body `{}` answers 400, and its error does not match `/got undefined/`. A POST to one `requireStringField` endpoint (for example the brief endpoint) with no `prompt` key answers 400 with no `got undefined`.
- The existing `doesNotMatch(/got undefined/)` assertions in test/gui-endpoints.test.ts still pass, and `grep -rn 'undefined ? "" : gotSuffix' src` prints nothing.
