### Pi built-in image capability, part 2/2: `seamImageInput` answers from the saved `pi --list-models` images column for a pi pair missing from models.json, so a built-in vision model keeps its image prompts (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; "requires part 1/2 landed". Touches src/agent/image-input.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/tick/tick-verdict.ts, src/inbox/inbox-submit.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/status/status-roles.ts, src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, plans/image-input.md, test/image-input.test.ts, test/tick-verdict.test.ts, done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** Part 1/2 saves pi's own images column per `provider/model`. This part has the one resolver read it. A pi pair missing from models.json gets the listing's answer instead of `null`. With that, the preflight keeps an image prompt on a role whose built-in model reads images, and a reroute can target a built-in vision tier. The status, role and submit surfaces say what pi says, and the doctor's `image input` check probes the built-in claim like any other.

**Approach.**
- **src/agent/image-input.ts.**
  - `seamImageInput(seam, providers, probes?, listed?: PiListedModels | null)`. In the pi branch, `base` becomes `piModelImageInput(providers, …)`. When that is null, use `piListedImageInput(listed, seam.provider, seam.model)` instead. models.json wins when it defines the pair. The failed-probe override that follows is unchanged, so it covers a listed claim too: it uses the same `imageProbeKey("pi", …)`.
  - Update the doc comment: "absent from models.json → what `pi --list-models` last said (src/pi/pi-listed-models.ts), else null".
  - Thread a trailing `listed: PiListedModels | null = null` through `imageReroute` (into its `capable` closure), `imageRerouteTarget` and `roleImageInfo`. `roleImageInfo` passes it to both its `seamImageInput` and its `imageReroute` call.
- **Callers.** Each one reads `readPiListedModels(root)` once and passes it on. Every one of these already has `root` (or `ctx.root`):
  - src/runner/runner-run.ts preflight: both the `seamImageInput` call and the `imageReroute` call.
  - src/tick/tick-verdict.ts: the blind-read `imageReroute` call.
  - src/inbox/inbox-submit.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/status/status-roles.ts: their `roleImageInfo` calls.
  - src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts `checkImageInput`: the two `claimed` loops' `seamImageInput(pair, providers)`, the per-role `seamImageInput(rc, providers, probes)` and its `imageReroute`. With this, a listed built-in vision pair is probed and cached like a models.json claim.
- Leave src/agent/run-agent.ts' parser `imageInput` alone. It only acts on `false`, and for a model pi has built in, pi itself reports the non-vision note. Say so in one line of this plan's commit, not in code.
- **plans/image-input.md** "Capability", pi bullet. Replace "Not in models.json at all (pi's built-in catalog) → `null` … already fails such pairs" with: built-in pairs read the images column the doctor last saved from `pi --list-models`, and an unlisted pair reads `null`.
- docs/invariants.md INV-J1 (blind reads) is unaffected: it pins the stop on a blind read, not the capability source.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/image-input.test.ts, new "seamImageInput reads pi's listed images column for a pair models.json does not define". Use the file's `writeModels()` catalog:
  - A pi seam `builtin/vision-x` with `listed = { checkedAt: 0, images: { "builtin/vision-x": true, "builtin/text-x": false } }` reads true.
  - `builtin/text-x` reads false, and an unlisted `builtin/other` reads null.
  - With no `listed`, all three read null, as before.
  - A models.json pair stays on its catalog answer even when `listed` says the opposite.
  - A fresh failed probe for `builtin/vision-x` (`imageProbeKey("pi", "builtin", "vision-x")`) turns it false.
- Same file, new "imageReroute picks a tier whose built-in model pi lists as reading images". The default tier is text-only and the strong tier is `builtin/vision-x`. With the listing, `imageReroute(config, "feature", "primary", models, null, undefined, null, listed)?.tier === "strong"`. Without it, the result is null.
- test/tick-verdict.test.ts, new twin of "a blind read on a text-only tier with a vision reroute target aborts as image-reroute". The strong tier is a pair models.json does not define, listed as reading images with `writePiListedModels(root, { "<pair>": true })` before the verdict. The tick aborts as image-reroute onto strong. Without the listing, the same setup takes the no-target path that "a blind image read fails the tick with an error naming the file and the model" pins. (No test drives the runner-run.ts preflight end to end today, and this part does not add one. The preflight reads the same `seamImageInput`/`imageReroute` the unit tests above cover.)
- The existing image-input, runner, tick-verdict, status, role-view and doctor tests pass unchanged. They write no listing, so every caller reads null and behaves as today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `roles.<id>.model` or `review.model` value that misspells a tier name (`strnog`, `Strong`, `defualt`) is a config error naming the tier, so `tumwater role <id> --model strnog` refuses instead of writing a model id pi cannot resolve (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight entries touch src/ui/status-render.ts and src/doctor; this one touches src/config/config-field-checks.ts, test/config-validation-model.test.ts, test/cli-operators.test.ts, docs/config.md); done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `roles.<id>.model` and `review.model` accept a bare tier name (`small`, `default`, `strong`) as a reference into the top-level `model` map. `checkModelTripleField` (src/config/config-field-checks.ts) matches tier names exactly and case-sensitively, so any other bare string passes as a model id. A typo then goes to pi as a model pattern, and the role runs a model nobody chose. Verified 2026-10-19 in a scratch `tumwater init` project with main's build: `tumwater role feature --model strnog`, `--model Strong`, `--model defualt` and `--model smal` each printed `feature: model set to …` and exited 0. Afterwards `tumwater doctor` only warned `smal names no provider — pi resolves it with its own default, tumwater cannot verify it`. `role --model` writes through `setConfigKey` (src/config/config-write.ts), which validates the candidate config with `validateConfig`, so a new validation problem makes the CLI write, the TUI and dashboard model editors, and a hand edit of tumwater.json all refuse the typo the same way. After this change, a near-miss tier name is a validation problem that names the tier.

**Approach** (src/config/config-field-checks.ts, `checkModelTripleField`):
- In the `modelShape === "tier-name"` path, after the exact `MODEL_TIERS` match returns, add this check. The value is not a tier name, contains no `/`, and the section has no `provider` key (`obj.provider === undefined`; with a legacy provider a bare string is an id under that provider). If `suggestClosest(m, MODEL_TIERS)` (src/text/suggest.ts) returns a tier, push `${prefix}model ${show(m)} is not a tier name or a model id pi can resolve${didYouMean(tier)}`. Import `suggestClosest` and `didYouMean` beside the existing `typoSuffix` import. `suggestClosest` lowercases both sides, so `Strong` suggests `strong`. Its two-edit cap and same-first-letter rule keep real ids (`gpt-5`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`) from matching. The new problem does not depend on `backend`, because no backend has a model id within two edits of a tier name.
- Leave the "selector" and "tier-map" shapes alone: a tier name is already invalid there, and those paths do not change.
- Extend the doc comment of `checkModelTripleField` with one sentence: a bare value within two edits of a tier name (ignoring case) is rejected as a misspelled tier reference.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/config-validation-model.test.ts, in "validateConfig guards the tier-map and tier-name forms of model", add these assertions. `validationError({ roles: { plan: { enabled: true, model: "strnog" } } })` matches `` /roles\.plan\.model "strnog" is not a tier name or a model id pi can resolve — did you mean `strong`\?/ ``. `review: { enabled: true, model: "Default" }` matches the same form with `review.model` and `` `default` ``. `roles.plan.model: "smal"` suggests `` `small` ``. The following stay valid (`assert.doesNotThrow`): `roles.plan.model` set to `"prov/strnog"` (has a `/`), to `"gpt-5"`, and to `"sonnet"`, and `{ provider: "prov", model: "smal" }` in a role section (legacy provider).
- test/cli-operators.test.ts, in "role --provider/--model/--thinking (and --clear-*) write the role's model triple", next to the bogus-thinking check: `cli(repo, "role", "feature", "--model", "strnog")` exits 1, its stderr matches `` /roles\.feature\.model "strnog" is not a tier name .* did you mean `strong`/ ``, and tumwater.json is byte-identical to its content before the call.
- docs/config.md: the `roles.<id>` table's `model` row adds that a value one or two letters off a tier name (in any case) is rejected as a misspelled tier.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 15/16: Reword role-sense "loop" in src/ comments, leaving every iteration-sense "loop" alone (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role, split from the rejected 14/14; requires part 14/16 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches comments in src/ only) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** No comment in src/ says "loop" when it means a role or its worker. Every comment where "loop" means iteration (a `for`/`while` loop, "loop over", "loops through", the poll loop, the event loop, a retry, crash or feedback loop) reads exactly as before.

**Approach.**
- This part exists because the 14/14 review rejected blanket substitution. Judge each hit on its own and change nothing in code, string literals or serialized names.
- Work list: `grep -rnwiE 'loops?' src | grep -E ':[0-9]+:\s*(//|\*|/\*)'` (about 250 lines today, most in src/ui, src/backlog, src/doctor, src/events, src/process, src/paths.ts, src/git, src/agent, src/change and src/pi). Also check trailing `// …` comments on code lines (`grep -rnwiE '//.*\bloops?\b' src`).
- Before editing a hit, classify it by reading the whole sentence:
  - Role sense: the sentence is about a configured role, its runner, its state file, its claim, or "each loop" meaning each role. Reword "loop" to "role", or to "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Fix the grammar ("a loop's" → "a role's", "loops" → "roles").
  - Iteration sense: the sentence is about control flow, polling, retrying or feedback. Leave it byte-for-byte unchanged. Test: if "role" substituted in would make the sentence describe something other than iteration, it is iteration sense.
  - Ambiguous: leave it unchanged, and list it in the commit message.
- Leave alone: legacy readers (the files and regions listed in part 14/16's series rules), quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names, commit subjects, and `customLoop*` names. Rewrap any edited comment past 100 columns.
- Commit message: state the rule you applied. Name only repairs you made, without counts or "all".

**Files touched.** Comments in src/ files from the work list; nothing in test/ (part 16/16).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `git diff main -- src` changes only comment text: no code, string literal or identifier line changes. Check that every changed line is inside a comment.
- In every changed comment, the old "loop" referred to a role or its runner. No removed line has "loop" in an iteration sense (for/while, "loop over/through", poll loop, event loop, retry/crash/feedback loop).
- `grep -rnwiE 'loops?' src | grep -E ':[0-9]+:\s*(//|\*|/\*)'` lists only iteration-sense comments, legacy-reader comments, and the ambiguous ones the commit message names.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Shell completion completes `tumwater doctor` check names, quoting the multi-word ones (`image\ input`, `main\'s\ check`), so `tumwater doctor im<Tab>` finishes a name the operator would otherwise copy from the report (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. It follows the done plan "`tumwater doctor <check>...` runs only the named checks", which left check-name completion out of scope. None of the Planned entries touches these files. This one touches src/cli/completion.ts, test/completion.test.ts, docs/cli.md — done 2026-10-19)

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor <check>...` takes check names as positionals, matched ignoring case against `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` (src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts). `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` offers only doctor's flags there, so the operator has to type a name exactly or copy it from a full report. Many names have spaces (`git binary`, `image input`, `models for each tier`), and `main's check` has an apostrophe, so the names must reach the command line quoted. After this change, every positional word after `doctor` that does not start with `-` completes to the check names. Names come back escaped (`image\ input`, `main\'s\ check`), or raw when the operator opened a quote (`"image in<Tab>`).

**Approach.** All edits are in src/cli/completion.ts. Import `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` from `../doctor/doctor-check-names.js`, a leaf module with no imports.
- **bash/zsh** (`bashScript`). Before the `if [ "$COMP_CWORD" -eq 1 ]` block, add a branch that fires when `"${COMP_WORDS[1]}" = doctor`, `COMP_CWORD -ge 2` and `"$cur" != -*`. Do **not** use `compgen -W`: it re-parses its word list with shell quoting, which drops the apostrophe in `main's check`. This was checked on bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash). The branch body was checked in the same run under bash 3.2 and under zsh with bashcompinit's `emulate sh`, and both printed the outcomes listed here:
  ```
  local word="$cur" quote="" name
  case "$word" in \"*|\'*) quote="${word:0:1}"; word="${word:1}";; esac
  word="${word//\\/}"
  for name in <each DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES entry, double-quoted>; do
    if [[ "$name" == "$word"* ]]; then
      if [ -n "$quote" ]; then COMPREPLY+=("$name"); else COMPREPLY+=("$(printf '%q' "$name")"); fi
    fi
  done
  return 0
  ```
  (In the TS template literal, escape `$`/`\` as the surrounding lines do.) Declare `quote`, `word` and `name` with `local`, as shown. Do not use `${!arr[@]}`, because zsh's bashcompinit fails on it with "bad substitution". Do not use `"${arr[@]// /\\ }"`, because bash 3.2 joins the elements under a non-default IFS. zsh needs no separate code: bashcompinit's `_bash_complete` un-quotes COMPREPLY with `(Q)` and adds the names through `compadd`. Build the list with a small module constant: `DOCTOR_CHECK_WORDS = DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES.map((n) => `"${n}"`).join(" ")`. Give it a doc comment saying the names hold no `"`, `$`, backtick or `\`, so plain double quotes are exact, and that a test pins this.
- **fish** (`fishScript`). Push a function line `function __tumwater_doctor_checks; printf '%s\n' <the same double-quoted names>; end` next to `__tumwater_argc`. Fish double quotes keep `'` literal. Then push `complete -c tumwater -n "__fish_seen_subcommand_from doctor" -a "(__tumwater_doctor_checks)"`. Command-substitution output splits on newlines only, so each multi-word name stays one candidate, and fish escapes the inserted candidate itself.
- **docs/cli.md**. In the `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` clause, after `tier names after `role <id> --model``, add `, and check names after `doctor``. Grep for the clause; do not read the file whole.

**Acceptance criteria** (test/completion.test.ts, through the existing `complete(script, words, cword)` helper; the words are single-quoted there, so pass `"image\\ in"` as a JS string):
- New test "the bash script completes doctor check names, escaping spaces and apostrophes":
  - `["tumwater","doctor","im"]`, cword 2, gives `["image\\ input"]`.
  - `["tumwater","doctor","mai"]` gives `["maintenance\\ allowance","main\\'s\\ check"]`, in list order. Do not type an apostrophe into a test word: the helper wraps each word in single quotes.
  - `["tumwater","doctor","image\\ in"]` gives `["image\\ input"]`.
  - `["tumwater","doctor",""]` gives `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES.length` entries.
  - `["tumwater","doctor","repo","or"]`, cword 3, gives `["orphans"]` (later positionals complete too).
  - `["tumwater","doctor","--pr"]` still gives `["--problems"]`.
  - `["tumwater","status",""]`, cword 2, offers no check name. Assert it does not include `"image\\ input"`.
- The same test asserts every `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` entry matches `/^[a-z0-9' -]+$/i`, which pins the double-quoting assumption.
- A fish assertion (in the existing fish line tests, via `fishScriptLines()`): one line defines `__tumwater_doctor_checks` and contains `"main's check"` and `"image input"`, and one line has `__fish_seen_subcommand_from doctor` together with `-a "(__tumwater_doctor_checks)"`. The existing "the fish script parses under fish when fish is installed" test passes.
- The existing completion tests pass unchanged, including `bash -n` on the script.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Inside a team workspace, the ungated commands (`report`, `backlog`, `questions`, `role`, `bug`/`plan --list`/`--show`) refuse with the owning team root, so `tumwater role <id> --model` can no longer seed a phantom `tumwater.json` in a slot (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry. Touches src/cli/cli-repo-gate.ts, src/cli.ts (the `report` case), src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, plus a new test/cli-team-workspace.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The done plan "Inside a team workspace (`<root>/.tumwater/worktrees/<slot>`), `tumwater init` refuses and every gated command names the owning team root…" covered `init` and the commands that call `requireReadyRepo`. Several commands skip that gate on purpose, because each one degrades to empty output in a directory that was never initialized. Inside a workspace, that degraded output is wrong. Measured 2026-10-19 with main's built CLI in a temp `R/.tumwater/worktrees/_slot-1` git repo:
- `tumwater role feature --model strong` printed `feature: model set to strong`. It created `tumwater.json` in the slot.
- `role feature --notes-file <f>` created `.tumwater/state/notes/feature.md` in the slot.
- `git status` then showed both as untracked files, so a run's commit could pick them up.
- The phantom `.tumwater` also makes `nearestTumwaterRoot(slot)` return the slot itself. After that, `owningTeamRoot` stops recognising the slot as a workspace, and the gated commands' workspace message stops firing there too.
- Run from this plan role's own slot, `tumwater report --failures --since 2d` printed "0 runs, no events" for a team that is busy.

After this change, every command that reads or writes team state answers inside a workspace with the same `teamWorkspaceMessage` the gated commands give.

**Approach.**
- `src/cli/cli-repo-gate.ts`: add `refuseTeamWorkspace(root: string): void`. It does `const owner = owningTeamRoot(root); if (owner !== undefined) fail(teamWorkspaceMessage(owner));`, importing `owningTeamRoot` from `../paths.js` and `teamWorkspaceMessage` from `../gates/readiness.js`. Doc comment: this is the workspace half of `requireReadyRepo` for the commands that deliberately skip the ready-repo gate. Outside a workspace it is a no-op, so those commands keep degrading to empty output in a plain directory.
- Call it in each ungated state-reading command, after that command's argument gate (`rejectUnknownArgs` or its own parse) and before its first file read or write. This keeps the existing order: a malformed call fails with its usage first.
  - `src/cli.ts` `report` case: after the `rejectUnknownArgs("report", …)` call, before `cmdReport`. This covers `--failures` and `--since` too.
  - `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`:
    - `cmdBacklog`: after its `rejectUnknownArgs`.
    - `cmdQuestions`: after its argument scan, before the list, show or answer branches read QUESTIONS.md.
    - `cmdRole`: after its `rejectUnknownArgs`, before the id resolution and every write branch.
  - `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`: at the head of `listAndAnnounce` and `showAndAnnounce`, before they read the backlog file. These are the ungated `bug`/`plan --list` and `--show` forms; every other `bug`/`plan` form already calls `requireReadyRepo`.
- Leave alone: `doctor` (its `checkInit` already prints the workspace message), `completion`, `help` and `version`, which hold no state. Update each touched "No requireReadyRepo gate" comment with a clause saying the workspace refusal still applies.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New `test/cli-team-workspace.test.ts`. It uses `teamWorkspace()` from test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts and `cli` from test/helpers/cli-harness.ts.
  - Test "an ungated command run in a team workspace names the owning team root". Each of these exits 1 with stderr containing `teamWorkspaceMessage(root)`: `report`, `report --failures`, `backlog`, `questions`, `role feature`, `bug --list`, `plan --show 1`.
  - Test "`role <id> --model` in a team workspace refuses and writes nothing". `role feature --model strong` exits 1 with the workspace message. Afterwards the slot holds no `tumwater.json` and no `.tumwater`, and `git status --porcelain` in the slot is empty.
  - Test "the argument gate still runs first in a workspace". `report --days abc` fails naming `--days`, not the workspace.
  - Test "`completion bash` still works in a workspace". It exits 0.
- Existing tests that run `report`, `backlog`, `questions` and `role` in plain temp repos pass unchanged, because none of those repos sits under a `.tumwater/worktrees`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Goal.** Every role-taking command (`logs --role`, `diff --role`, `abort --role`, `history --role`, `prompt --role`, …) answers an unknown role with `unknownRoleMessage` (src/roles/roles.ts): the valid ids plus a did-you-mean. ### Pi built-in image capability, part 1/2: `tumwater doctor` saves the images column of `pi --list-models` to `.tumwater/state/pi-listed-models.json` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role, done 2026-10-19; no dependency on any Planned entry. Part 2/2 reads the file. The in-flight entries touch src/doctor/doctor.ts, src/cli/*, src/config/config-field-checks.ts and src/ comments. This part touches src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, src/paths.ts, a new src/pi/pi-listed-models.ts, test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts and a new test/pi-listed-models.test.ts)

**Goal.** pi's built-in catalog says which models read images. `pi --list-models` prints that in an `images` column (`yes`/`no`). tumwater never keeps it. `seamImageInput` (src/agent/image-input.ts) answers `null` (unknown) for any pi pair missing from models.json, and the runner's attachment preflight (`src/runner/runner-run.ts`, `seamImageInput(cfg, providers) !== true`) treats unknown as blind. So a role on a built-in vision model gets its image prompt rerouted to another tier, or the run errors with "no configured tier can read it". Measured 2026-10-19 on this machine: `pi --list-models` lists `huggingface google/gemma-3-12b-it … images yes`, and main's `piModelImageInput(readPiProviders(piModelsPath()), "huggingface", "google/gemma-3-12b-it")` returns `null`. plans/image-input.md "Capability" chose `null` because "the doctor's tier check already fails such pairs". That stopped being true when the doctor started accepting models from `pi --list-models` (PLANS-DONE.md, 2026-10-19). This part saves the facts. Part 2/2 reads them. `seamImageInput` stays the only capability resolver.

**Approach.**
- **src/paths.ts.** Add `piListedModelsPath(root)` → `path.join(tumwaterDir(root), "state", "pi-listed-models.json")`, beside `imageProbesPath`.
- **src/pi/pi-listed-models.ts** (new). Imports only node built-ins, src/paths.ts, and the JSON file helpers image-probe.ts already uses (`readJsonFile`, `writeJsonAtomic`).
  - `export interface PiListedModels { checkedAt: number; images: Record<string, boolean> }`. Keys are `provider/model`.
  - `export function parsePiModelImages(stdout: string): Record<string, boolean> | null`. Use the same row split and header guard as `parsePiModelList`: the first non-blank row must start `provider model`, else return null. Find the `images` column with `header.indexOf("images")` and return null when it is missing. For each row that has a model, `yes` maps to true and `no` to false. Skip any other value.
  - `export function readPiListedModels(root: string): PiListedModels | null`. Return null for a missing or torn file, or when `images` is not an object.
  - `export function writePiListedModels(root: string, images: Record<string, boolean>, now: number = Date.now()): void`. Write atomically.
  - `export function piListedImageInput(listed: PiListedModels | null | undefined, provider: string | undefined, model: string | undefined): boolean | null`. Return null when an argument is missing or the key is not listed, else the boolean. There is no TTL: every doctor run that lists the models rewrites the file, and an unlisted pair still reads as unknown, as it does today.
- **src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts.**
  - `piListedModels` takes a fourth parameter `root?: string`. After a code-0 run, when `root` is given and `parsePiModelImages(result.stdout)` is not null, call `writePiListedModels(root, images)` inside `try { … } catch {}`, so a failed write never changes the check. The return value stays `parsePiModelList(result.stdout)`.
  - `checkTierModels`' default `listModels` passes `root`. The listing stays lazy: it only runs when a pair is missing from models.json, which is the only case the file is needed. Add one line to `piListedModels`' doc comment saying it records the images column for `seamImageInput`.
  - `parsePiModelList` is unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test/pi-listed-models.test.ts, "parsePiModelImages reads the images column and refuses anything else":
  - On the two-row table from the existing `parsePiModelList` test, it returns `{"huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1": false, "anthropic/claude-x": true}`.
  - It returns null for `'No models matching "x"'`, for `""`, and for a `provider model context` header with no `images` column.
- Same file, "readPiListedModels round-trips writePiListedModels and piListedImageInput answers per pair":
  - write then read returns the same `images` and `checkedAt`.
  - `piListedImageInput` returns true and false for listed pairs, and null for an unlisted pair, an undefined model, and a null `listed`.
  - On a fresh tmp root, before any write, `readPiListedModels` returns null.
- test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, new "piListedModels saves the images column under the root it is given". Use a fake `pi` made with `writeScript` (test/fakes/fake-commands.ts) that prints the two-row table on `--list-models`, on a temp PATH dir:
  - `piListedModels(config, dir, 5000, root)` resolves to the same Set as before, and `readPiListedModels(root)?.images["anthropic/claude-x"] === true`.
  - Without `root`, no file appears at `piListedModelsPath(root)`.
  - A fake that exits 1 writes nothing.
- The existing `parsePiModelList` and `checkTierModels` tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

Note: `PiListedModels` is not exported yet (the unused-export test); part 2/2 exports it when it imports it.

### `tumwater doctor <check>...` runs only the named checks (`tumwater doctor orphans`, `tumwater doctor "image input" --reprobe`), so an operator re-checking one fixed problem waits for that check alone (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight entries touch src/config/config-field-checks.ts, src/cli/completion.ts and src/ comments; this one touches src/doctor/doctor.ts, a new src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/cli-command-args.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `runDoctor` (src/doctor/doctor.ts) evaluates every check eagerly, in one array literal, so `tumwater doctor` always runs all of them. That includes the slow probes: claude auth/version, opencode, `pi --list-models`, the image probes, the process table walk. After the operator fixes one reported problem (kills an orphan, edits a tier model), the only way to confirm the fix is the whole report. Measured 2026-10-19 with main's build: a bare scratch `tumwater init` project took 3.1 s of wall time. `tumwater doctor orphans` exits 1 with `unknown argument: orphans (valid flags for tumwater doctor: --json, --reprobe, --problems)`. After this change, bare positional arguments name checks by the names the report prints. Only those checks run, and the report, the verdict and the exit code cover only them. `--json`, `--problems` and `--reprobe` still apply.

**Approach.**
- **src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts** (new, no imports). Export `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES`, a readonly `as const` tuple of every row name in report order. It includes the two conditional rows, `pi extensions` and `funes` (in that order, after `claude transcripts`). Also export `type DoctorCheckName = (typeof DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES)[number]`. It is a leaf because src/cli.ts loads doctor.ts with a dynamic `import()`, while src/cli/cli-command-args.ts is imported eagerly. Importing doctor.ts from there would pull every check module into each CLI start.
- **src/doctor/doctor.ts.**
  - Import `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` and `DoctorCheckName` from the new leaf module described below.
  - In `runDoctor`, replace the `checks` array literal with a list of lazy steps, `Array<{ name: DoctorCheckName; run: () => CheckOutcome | null | Promise<CheckOutcome | null> }>`. Keep the existing order and every existing comment. Wrap each current expression unchanged in its `run` (for example `run: () => checkOrphans(root, probe)`). `pi extensions` and `funes` return their nullable outcome directly. Then `appendNamedOutcome` has no caller: delete it.
  - Add a fifth parameter, `only?: readonly DoctorCheckName[]`. Walk the steps in order with a `for … of` loop. When `only` is given, skip every step whose name it does not contain. Otherwise `await step.run()`, and push `{ name, ...outcome }` unless the outcome is null. The loop awaits each step in turn, as the literal's inline `await`s do today. The verdict counts fails over the rows the loop produced.
  - `header` and `routing` stay as they are. Extend the doc comment: `only` runs just the named checks, in report order, and a skipped check is never evaluated. A named conditional check that returns null leaves no row.
- **src/cli/cli-command-args.ts.** Add `parseDoctorChecks(positionals: string[]): DoctorCheckName[] | undefined`. It returns `undefined` for an empty list. Otherwise it maps each token to the `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` entry equal to it ignoring case. An unmatched token calls `fail(\`tumwater doctor: unknown check "${token}"${typoSuffix(token, DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES)} (\`tumwater doctor\` lists every check by name)\`)`. Deduplicate the result. Import `typoSuffix` from src/text/suggest.ts and the names from the leaf module.
- **src/cli.ts** `case "doctor"`. Split with `peelPositionals(args)` (doctor has no valued flags, so a bare token is a positional). Run `rejectUnknownArgs` on `rest` and pass `parseDoctorChecks(positionals)` as `runDoctor`'s fifth argument. Leave the TUI and GUI callers (src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) alone: they omit the argument and keep the full report.
- **src/cli/help.ts.** Change the synopsis to `tumwater doctor [<check>...] [--json] [--reprobe] [--problems]`. Add one clause: "naming checks (as the report prints them, any case; quote names with spaces) runs only those, and the verdict and exit code cover only them".
- **docs/cli.md**, Audit row. After `tumwater doctor`'s flags, add `` `tumwater doctor <check>...` `` runs only the named checks. Grep the row; do not read the file whole.
- Shell completion of check names is out of scope. The in-flight completion entry owns src/cli/completion.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/doctor.test.ts, "runDoctor composes the full report — fixed check order, …": also assert that `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES.filter((n) => n !== "funes")` deep-equals `report.checks.map((c) => c.name)`. (funes is absent because the fake PATH has no funes.)
- New test in test/doctor.test.ts, "runDoctor with only runs just the named checks, in report order":
  - On `readyRepo()` with `fakeBins("git", "pi")`, `only: ["orphans", "repo"]` yields check names `["repo", "orphans"]` and verdict `ready to run`.
  - `runDoctor(makeRepo(), "", noProcesses, "never", ["git binary"])` yields one `fail` row named `git binary` and verdict `1 problem`.
  - `only: ["node"]` with a `ProcessProbe` whose `list` and `cwds` count their calls leaves both counts at 0. This proves skipped checks are not evaluated.
- New CLI test in test/doctor.test.ts, "doctor <check>... runs the named checks and rejects an unknown name", on an `initProject` repo:
  - `cli(repo, "doctor", "Orphans", "--json")` exits 0, and its parsed `checks` names deep-equal `["orphans"]`.
  - `cli(repo, "doctor", "image input", "repo")` prints `repo` before `image input` and no `orphans` row.
  - `cli(repo, "doctor", "orphan")` exits 1, and its stderr matches `` /unknown check "orphan" — did you mean `orphans`\?/ ``.
  - `cli(repo, "doctor", "--verbose")` still fails with `unknown argument: --verbose` (the existing test, unchanged).
- The existing doctor tests pass unchanged, including the TUI/GUI doctor-pane tests.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Shell completion completes `history --by` with `role`/`model` and `role <id> --model` with the tier names, so these closed-vocabulary flag values complete like `--thinking` and `--result` do (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight entries touch src/doctor, src/config/config-field-checks.ts and src/ comments; this one touches src/cli/completion.ts, test/completion.test.ts, docs/cli.md; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `completionSpec` (src/cli/completion.ts) takes flag names from the help text, so `tumwater history --b<TAB>` completes `--by`. But no value completes after `--by`, and none completes after `role <id> --model` either, although both take a closed set of words. `--by` takes `HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS` (`role`, `model`; src/history/history-data.ts). `role --model` takes a model id or a tier name from `MODEL_TIERS` (`small`, `default`, `strong`; src/config/config-schema.ts). In `bashScript`, a `$prev` of `--by` or `--model` falls through to the per-command arm, which completes only flags (`$cur` starting with `-`) or subcommands at word 2, so the reply is empty. `fishFlagValue` returns `""` for both flags. Offering the tier names also steers operators away from the misspelled tier references that the Planned tier-name typo entry rejects. After this change, `history --by <TAB>` offers `role model` and `role qa --model <TAB>` offers `small default strong`. `history --model <TAB>` still offers nothing, because its values are run selectors read from the event log.

**Approach** (src/cli/completion.ts):
- Import `HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS` beside the existing `HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES` import. `MODEL_TIERS` is already imported.
- In `bashScript`, after the `--thinking` block, add `if [ "$prev" = "--by" ]` with `compgen -W "${HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS.join(" ")}"`. Then add `if [ "$prev" = "--model" ] && [ "${COMP_WORDS[1]}" = role ]` with `compgen -W "${MODEL_TIERS.join(" ")}"`. Each block ends in `return 0`, like its neighbours.
- Change `fishFlagValue(flag)` to `fishFlagValue(command, flag)` and update its one caller in `fishScript`. `--by` returns `` ` -x -a "role model"` `` (built from `HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS`). `--model` returns `` ` -x -a "<MODEL_TIERS joined>"` `` only when `command === "role"`, and `""` otherwise. Every other flag keeps today's value. fish's `-a` offers candidates without restricting the value, so a full model id still types freely.
- Add a short doc comment on the `--model` branch saying why `history --model` is excluded: its selectors come from the log, not a closed set.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/completion.test.ts, new test "the bash script completes summary groups after --by and tier names after role --model". It covers these cases:
  - `complete(script, ["tumwater", "history", "--by", "m"], 3)` deep-equals `["model"]`.
  - `["tumwater", "history", "--by", ""]` at word 3 deep-equals `["role", "model"]`.
  - `["tumwater", "role", "qa", "--model", "st"]` at word 4 deep-equals `["strong"]`.
  - `["tumwater", "role", "qa", "--model", ""]` at word 4 deep-equals `[...MODEL_TIERS]`.
  - `["tumwater", "history", "--model", ""]` at word 3 deep-equals `[]`.
- Same file, in "the fish script completes values after --role, path flags, --template, and --result, and config keys at word 3":
  - Some `flagLines("by")` line includes both `role` and `model` after `-a`.
  - The `flagLines("model")` line containing `__fish_seen_subcommand_from role` includes `small`, `default` and `strong`.
  - The `flagLines("model")` line containing `__fish_seen_subcommand_from history` contains no `-a`.
- The existing completion tests pass unchanged, including the fish-parses test when fish is installed.
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater completion` paragraph's list of completed values adds "summary groups after `--by`, tier names after `role <id> --model`".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater doctor`'s "models for each tier" check accepts a model pi has built in, by asking `pi --list-models` about a pair that pi's `models.json` does not declare (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight entries touch src/ui/status-render.ts, src/init and src/gates. The blocked plain-terms parts may rename identifiers in src/doctor later, which only means a rebase. Touches src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, docs/backends.md; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** pi ships a built-in model catalog for its providers, and `~/.pi/agent/models.json` holds only the operator's additions. `checkTierModels` (src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts) resolves every declared pair through `readPiProviders(modelsPath)`, which reads models.json alone. So a valid built-in model fails the doctor. Verified 2026-10-19 in a scratch `tumwater init` project with main's build. After `tumwater role plan --model huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1`, `tumwater doctor` printed `fail  models for each tier  huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 does not resolve in pi's definitions (…/models.json) — pi would price it at the provider default's rates and context window`. Yet `pi --list-models` lists that model under `huggingface`: 81 huggingface models, of which models.json declares 4. The fail text's pricing claim is also wrong for a built-in model, because pi prices it from its own catalog. The same false fail hits any built-in provider that is missing from models.json, such as `anthropic/…`, which reads `provider anthropic is not in pi's definitions`. After this change, a pair pi lists counts as resolved. Only a pair that is in neither source fails.

**Approach** (src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts):
- Add a pure `parsePiModelList(stdout: string): Set<string> | null`. It returns null unless the first non-blank line's first two whitespace-separated tokens are `provider` and `model`, which is the header `pi --list-models` prints. Otherwise it returns `provider/model` built from the first two tokens of each later non-blank line. A reply with only the header returns an empty set.
- Add `piListedModels(config: TumwaterConfig, pathEnv: string = envPath(), timeoutMs: number = AUTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<Set<string> | null>`, modeled on `piProviderAuth`. It calls `boundedProbe(resolveAgentBin(config).bin, ["--list-models"], childEnv({ PATH: pathEnv }), timeoutMs, AUTH_CHECK_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)`. It returns null when the probe returned null or a nonzero exit, and `parsePiModelList(stdout)` otherwise. It never throws. Its doc comment says pi lists only the providers it has credentials for.
- `checkTierModels` gains a fifth parameter, `listModels: () => Promise<Set<string> | null>`. Its default is `() => piListedModels(loadConfigSafe(root).config ?? defaultConfig())`. Put it after `env` so the existing four-argument calls still compile. Call it lazily, at most once per check, and only when some pair misses models.json. Cache the promise in a local.
- In the pairs loop, take the `!defs` and `!def` branches only when `(await listed())?.has(\`${provider}/${model}\`)` is false. A listed pair skips `cacheReadUnpriced`, which reads models.json prices only, and goes straight to the provider auth probe, as a resolved pair does today. It also counts toward the `N declared models resolve` ok text.
- Change the two fail texts as follows. Keep today's texts word for word when the listing is null, meaning pi could not be asked; the existing tests pin those texts.
  - When a provider has no models.json entry and no listed model: `provider ${provider} is not in pi's definitions (${modelsPath}) and \`pi --list-models\` lists none of its models — pi lists only providers it has credentials for`.
  - When a model is missing from both sources: `${provider}/${model} is neither in pi's definitions (${modelsPath}) nor listed by \`pi --list-models\``. The pricing clause is dropped, because the listing ran and does not know the model either.
- When models.json is unreadable (`providers` null) and some pair names a provider, check the listing before the early `cannot check — could not read pi's model definitions` warn. If the listing is non-null, run the loop with an empty providers map. If it is null, keep the warn unchanged.
- Out of scope: `seamContextWindow`, `seamFree` and `piModelImageInput` (src/pi/pi-models.ts) still read models.json alone. The fallback checks keep requiring a models.json price of $0. The `names no provider` warn for a bare id stays.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, new test "parsePiModelList reads pi's list-models table and refuses anything else". A header plus two rows (`huggingface  deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1  131.1K  8.2K  yes  no`) yields `{"huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1", …}`. A header alone yields an empty set. `No models matching "x"`, an empty string and arbitrary text yield null.
- Same file, new test "checkTierModels accepts a model pi lists but models.json does not declare". Use the `writeModels()` fixture and the config `{ model: "paid/built-in-x" }` with a listing stub returning `new Set(["paid/built-in-x"])`. The level is `ok`, the detail matches `/1 declared model resolve/` (today's wording, from `resolvedPi`), and the `auth` stub was called with `paid`. Do the same with `{ model: "builtin/some-model" }` (a provider absent from models.json) and a stub listing it. The stub records its calls. Assert that a config whose every pair resolves in models.json never calls it.
- Same file: with the stub returning an empty set, `paid/no-such-model` fails with `/is neither in pi's definitions .* nor listed by `pi --list-models`/`, and `nowhere/mystery` fails with `/lists none of its models/`. The existing test "checkTierModels fails a pair pi cannot resolve and warns on an unready provider" passes `async () => null` as the fifth argument, and its assertions pass unchanged. Every other `checkTierModels(` call in test/ whose fixture holds a pair missing from models.json passes a stub, so no test spawns a real `pi --list-models`. Find them with `grep -n "checkTierModels(" test/*.ts`.
- Same file: with a modelsPath that does not exist and a stub listing the pair, the check is `ok`. With the stub returning null, the outcome is the existing `cannot check` warn.
- docs/backends.md: in the image-input bullet that says the `models for each tier` doctor check flags a pair missing from models.json, say instead that the check also accepts a model pi lists in `pi --list-models`. The image-capability lookup still reads models.json only.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater status` and the TUI's status table name a model every role shares once, under the table, and the name column gives way last on a narrow terminal, so a fresh project's table fits 120 columns (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the blocked plain-terms parts may rename `snap.loops` and rebase over this; touches src/ui/status-render.ts, test/status-render.test.ts, test/status-render-cells.test.ts, docs/backends.md; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A project created with `tumwater init` and no model in `tumwater.json` runs every role on pi's default model. `renderStatusSpans` (src/ui/status-render.ts) appends that model to every name cell, for example `bugfix (huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731:deepinfra:low, pi default)`. The name column then grows to about 85 columns. The name column (index 0) is not in `FLEXIBLE_COLUMNS`, so a 120-column terminal keeps only `role state runs commits output …`. Cost, today, last run, last merged, last result and next run are all clipped away. Verified 2026-10-19: ran `tumwater init "hello"` in a scratch repo, then `status` under `script` with `stty cols 120`. The TUI renders the same `renderStatusSpans` lines, so it loses the same columns. After this change, a model every row shares prints once in a footnote under the table, like the existing `* custom role` footnote. A table whose models still differ shrinks the name column last, so the role label survives and only the model suffix clips.

**Approach** (all in src/ui/status-render.ts, `renderStatusSpans`):
- Split today's `modelSuffix` into `modelInner(s)`, a small local helper returning the text inside the parentheses: `${s.modelTier} · ${s.model}`, `s.modelTier` alone, `${s.model}, pi default`, `s.model` alone, or `""`. Today's precedence stays the same. The suffix becomes `inner ? \` (${inner})\` : ""`.
- Compute `sharedModel` before building `rows`. It is set when `snap.loops.length >= 2` and every row's `modelInner` is the same non-empty string. Otherwise it is `undefined`. When `sharedModel` is set, every name cell drops its model suffix. The name cell keeps the custom asterisk and `fallbackSuffix` (` (over-cap model)`), because those are per-row facts.
- Footnote: when `sharedModel` is set, push `[{ text: \`model (every role): ${sharedModel}\`, tone: "dim" }]` after the closing totals row. It goes before the `* custom role` footnote. The existing final `clipSpans(l, maxWidth)` pass bounds it like every other line.
- Name column last: after the `FLEXIBLE_COLUMNS` loop, while overflow remains, shrink `widths[0]` down to a floor. The floor is `max(displayWidth("role"), max over rows of displayWidth(bare label))`, where the bare label is `roleLabel(s.role)` plus `*` for a custom role. `fmt` already clips each cell to its width with `clipSpans`, so a mixed-model row reads `clean (prov-a/very-long…`. The role label is never cut. Update the `FLEXIBLE_COLUMNS` doc comment and the name-cell comment ("its width derives from row content") to describe the name column giving way last.
- A single row (a scoped `status --role x`) keeps its suffix in the name cell, so a one-role view does not change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/status-render.test.ts, new test "a model every role shares prints once under the table, not on each row". Use `snapshotWith` with three rows, all `{ model: "prov/org/m:route:low", modelFromPi: true }`. No row line matches `/\(prov\//`. Exactly one line equals `model (every role): prov/org/m:route:low, pi default`. A variant with `modelTier: "strong"` on all rows reads `model (every role): strong · <model>`.
- Same file: a snapshot where one row's model differs, or one row has no model, keeps each row's suffix and prints no `model (every role)` line. The three existing name-cell tests ("appends the seam tier…", "appends a lone selector…", "names pi's own default…") use mixed rows and pass unchanged.
- Same file: a shared model plus one row with `fallback` set keeps `(over-cap model)` on that row's name cell.
- test/status-render-cells.test.ts, new test "the name column gives way last: a mixed-model table at 110 columns keeps every role label and every column header". Use two rows with distinct models about 70 characters long. Rendered at `renderStatus(root, snap, 110)` (at 100 the non-name columns alone need about 108, so the test uses 110), every line is at most 110 display columns, the header line contains `next run`, and each row line starts with its role label. The existing "last tick shrinks last…" narrow-width test still passes, since it does not reach the name column.
- docs/backends.md, the paragraph on `pi default`: say that when every role runs that same default, `tumwater status` and the TUI name it once under the table instead of on each row. The dashboard keeps showing it per row.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 14/16: Rename the remaining loop identifiers and retire the old runner names (planned 2026-10-16 by user, replanned 2026-10-19 by the plan role after review rejection; requires part 13/16 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names" and "Guards"; touches every src/ and test/ file with a loop identifier + test/retired-names.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

Replanned 2026-10-19 by the plan role. The single 14/14 sweep was rejected after three review rounds. It rewrote "loop" meaning iteration to "role" in comments, which made them false, and its commit message claimed repairs it had not made. The sweep had about 150 identifier hits and about 250 comment lines in src/, with more in test/, which is too much prose to judge site by site in one run. This part therefore renames **identifiers only**. Comment and test-title wording moves to parts 15/16 (src/) and 16/16 (test/).

**Goal.** No identifier or file name in src/ or test/ uses "loop" for a role or its worker. Every deprecated alias from this series is gone, and test/retired-names.test.ts fails if an old runner identifier comes back.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and identifiers where "loop" means a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields such as the `loop:` key in event fixtures, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope. Name any leftover in the commit message.

### Inside a team workspace (`<root>/.tumwater/worktrees/<slot>`), `tumwater init` refuses and every gated command names the owning team root instead of answering "not initialized — run `tumwater init`" (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry: none names src/gates/, src/init/init.ts or src/paths.ts; runner part 14/16 renames loop identifiers across src and test, src/doctor included, so a shared file such as src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts is a rebase either way; touches src/paths.ts + src/gates/readiness.ts + src/gates/startup-gate.ts + src/init/init.ts + src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts + test/paths.test.ts + test/startup-gate.test.ts + test/init.test.ts + test/doctor-checks.test.ts, done 2026-10-19)

**Goal.** A role's run, an operator's shell, or a `logs -f` left behind in a slot runs with its cwd in a team workspace. That checkout has no `tumwater.json` (the file is untracked) and no `.tumwater`. The CLI's root is `repoToplevel(process.cwd())`, so the root is the workspace. Today this goes wrong in two ways:
- Every gated command (`status`, `logs`, `history`, `stop`, …) fails with `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE`. That message tells the user to run a bare `tumwater init`. Verified 2026-10-19 by running `node ../../../dist/src/cli.js status` and `logs -n 2` from `_slot-6`.
- The bare init works there, because the workspace's README.md carries the brief. `initProject` would then seed `tumwater.json`, PLANS/BUGS/…, and a phantom `.tumwater` inside the workspace, and commit them on the role's branch. That commit could merge to main.

After this change, a command run in a workspace says where the team actually lives, and `init` refuses before any side effect.

**Approach.**
- `src/paths.ts`: add `owningTeamRoot(dir: string): string | undefined`.
  - Call `nearestTumwaterRoot(dir)`. Return that root only when `dir` lies under `worktreesDir(root)`, meaning `path.relative(worktreesDir(root), dir)` is non-empty, not absolute, and does not start with `..`. Otherwise return `undefined`.
  - A normal team root holds its own `.tumwater`, so `nearestTumwaterRoot` returns `dir` itself, which is not under its own worktrees dir. The result is `undefined`, and nothing changes for ordinary projects.
  - Doc comment: a read-only lookup, never used to decide where to write (same caution as `teamRootOf`).
- `src/gates/readiness.ts`: add `teamWorkspaceMessage(teamRoot: string): string`. Wording: ``this is a tumwater workspace of the team at <teamRoot>, not a project — run tumwater from <teamRoot> (`cd <teamRoot>`)``. It sits beside `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE` so the gate, init and doctor share one wording.
- `src/gates/startup-gate.ts` `repoNotReady`: where `tumwater.json` is missing, return `teamWorkspaceMessage(owner)` when `owningTeamRoot(root)` is defined, else `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE` as today. Every `requireReadyRepo` caller and `runStartupCheck` inherit the change; nothing else changes in their order.
- `src/init/init.ts` `initProject`: before the first side effect (next to the existing `findOnPath("git")` check, ahead of the prompt/README validation), throw `new Error(teamWorkspaceMessage(owner))` when `owningTeamRoot(root)` is defined. Also apply this under `dryRun`, so `init --dry-run` in a workspace reports the refusal instead of a would-create list. The CLI's `main().catch` already prints a thrown error and exits 1. `--list-templates` returns before `initProject` and is unaffected.
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` `checkInit`: on a missing config, `failOutcome(teamWorkspaceMessage(owner))` when `owningTeamRoot(root)` is defined, else `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/startup-gate.test.ts`, new test "a team workspace without tumwater.json names the owning team root instead of not-initialized". Set up a temp team root `R` (realpath it, since macOS `/var` → `/private/var`) holding `.tumwater/worktrees/_slot-1`, and git-init that slot with one commit and no `tumwater.json`. Then `repoNotReady(slot)` equals `teamWorkspaceMessage(R)`. A plain repo with no `tumwater.json` outside any `.tumwater` still gets `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE`.
- `test/init.test.ts`, new test "initProject refuses inside a team workspace and writes nothing". Use the same layout, with a README.md carrying the tumwater:prompt markers in the slot. A bare `initProject(slot, "")` rejects with the workspace message. The same holds with `{ dryRun: true }`. Afterwards the slot has no `tumwater.json`, no `.tumwater`, and `git rev-list --count HEAD` is unchanged.
- `test/paths.test.ts` covers `owningTeamRoot`:
  - a workspace returns `R`;
  - `R` itself returns `undefined`;
  - a directory under `R` but outside `.tumwater/worktrees` (e.g. `R/src`) returns `undefined`.
- `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`: `checkInit(slot)` fails with the workspace message, and `checkInit` on a plain uninitialized repo still fails with `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE`.
- Every existing test that pins `NOT_INITIALIZED_MESSAGE` passes unchanged, since none of their temp repos sits under a `.tumwater/worktrees`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard role drawer's Live transcript gets a "Show prompts" toggle, through `GET /api/transcript?…&prompt=1`, the dashboard twin of `tumwater logs --transcript <id> --prompt` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/ui/transcript.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and tests); done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater logs --transcript <id> --prompt` shows a role's live transcript with each agent run's prompt. The dashboard's run History can do the same for a past run ("Show prompts", through `/api/run?…&prompt=1`). The role drawer's "Live transcript" cannot: `handleTranscript` ignores any `prompt` parameter, and `readTranscript` always renders with `createTranscriptRenderer()`, which drops user messages. An operator watching a role in the browser cannot see what it was asked to do.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/transcript.ts.** `readTranscript(root, role, limit = 50, opts: { includePrompts?: boolean } = {})`. Keep a second module-level map, `promptTails`, beside `tails`, and use it when `opts.includePrompts` is true. Its `fresh` callback builds `createTranscriptRenderer({ includePrompts: true })`. A separate map is needed because `withTail` keys its state by file only. Sharing one map would let a prompts reader and a plain reader overwrite each other's renderer. Everything else (`MAX_ENTRIES`, the pending-separator handling, the `take > 0` guard) stays shared. Update the doc comment above `tails` to say there are two caches.
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts.** In `handleTranscript`, pass `{ includePrompts: q.get("prompt") !== null }` to `readTranscript`. This is the same presence test `handleTick` uses for `/api/run`'s `prompt`. Extend the doc comment: "a present `prompt` flag also renders each agent run's prompt, the text `logs --transcript <id> --prompt` prints".
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts.**
  - Add `let transcriptPrompts = false;` next to the other drawer state. `openRole` resets it to false, so each drawer open starts plain.
  - In `openRole`'s static section head, add `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' id='transcriptprompts' data-transcript-prompts>Show prompts</button>` before the "last 200 lines" span.
  - `refreshTranscript` captures `const prompts = transcriptPrompts;` before it fetches. It appends `&prompt=1` to the URL when `prompts` is true. After the await, it returns without painting when `transcriptPrompts !== prompts`, the same way it already drops a response for a role that is no longer open.
  - New `function toggleTranscriptPrompts()`. It flips `transcriptPrompts` and sets `$("transcriptprompts").textContent` to "Hide prompts" or "Show prompts". It then calls `refreshTranscript(true)`, so the repainted panel scrolls to the bottom.
  - In the existing `$("drawer")` click listener, add a branch: a click whose `clickClosest(ev, "button[data-transcript-prompts]")` matches calls `toggleTranscriptPrompts()`.
  - `transcriptHtml` needs no change: prompt lines render as plain text under their run separator.
  - Update the file's header comment, which describes the live transcript.
- **docs/how-it-works.md.** In the dashboard paragraph that mentions the role drawer's live transcript, add one sentence. It says a "Show prompts" button re-reads the transcript through `GET /api/transcript?…&prompt=1` with each agent run's prompt, the text `tumwater logs --transcript <id> --prompt` prints.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/transcript.test.ts: a new test writes a pi log with a user `message_end` ("asked-one") and then an assistant one ("said-one"). `readTranscript(root, "feature")` contains "said-one" but not "asked-one". `readTranscript(root, "feature", 50, { includePrompts: true })` contains both, with "asked-one" first. A plain call made after the prompts call still omits "asked-one", which proves the two caches do not share a renderer.
- test/gui.test.ts, "gui /api/transcript serves rendered lines and validates role/n": its log already has a "tick prompt" user message. Assert that `/api/transcript?role=feature&n=10` has no line containing "tick prompt", and that `…&n=10&prompt=1` has one, placed before "did the thing".
- test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts: a new test opens the `clean` drawer with responses for both `/api/transcript?role=clean&n=200` and `/api/transcript?role=clean&n=200&prompt=1` (different lines). It asserts:
  - the painted transcript shows the plain lines;
  - after `toggleTranscriptPrompts()` and a flush, it shows the prompt lines and the button reads "Hide prompts";
  - a second toggle returns to the plain lines and "Show prompts";
  - reopening the drawer (`toggleRole` twice, or `openRole`) starts plain again.
  Expose `toggleTranscriptPrompts` the same way the harness already exposes `toggleRole`.
- Every existing `/api/transcript` and drawer test passes unchanged. In particular, the plain URL `/api/transcript?role=clean&n=200` is still the one fetched while the toggle is off.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Split `reviewAttempt` in src/review/review.ts into a gate-decision phase and a reviewer-run phase (planned 2026-10-19 by the organize role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/review/review.ts, a new src/review/review-run.ts, test/review*.test.ts only if they import moved names; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Cost today.** `reviewAttempt` (src/review/review.ts, lines 265–790) is one ~525-line async function and makes review.ts the third-largest production module (829 lines). It holds two responsibilities in one closure scope: (1) the deterministic gate that decides before any reviewer exists (already-approved head, conflict-marker / protected-edit / secret-leak / false-fix / backlog-structure rejects, the exempt fast path, the build pre-check or overlapped check, the `afterMerge` and `patchApproved` approvals); (2) the reviewer run itself (resume-vs-fresh session choice, prompt build, run, suite-rerun nudge, verdict-recovery turn, verdict parse, approve/reject bookkeeping). They share only a few closures (`reject`, `keep`, `settleFailedCheck`) and a few locals (`head`, `files`, `overlap`, `knownMainFailures`, `patchApproved`), so the seam is narrow but invisible while it is one function.

**Target structure.**
- review.ts keeps `ReviewContext`, `GateResult`, `reviewAheadOfMain`, the retry loop, `leaseCheckSlot` / `startOverlappedCheck`, and the gate-decision phase of `reviewAttempt` (everything up to and including the `patchApproved` / `afterMerge` early approvals). It builds a small `ReviewRunInput` object (head, files, overlap, knownMainFailures, retry, summary, commitBody, highFriction, and the `reject` / `keep` / `settleFailedCheck` closures) and calls `runReviewer(ctx, state, input)`.
- New src/review/review-run.ts exports `runReviewer` (the model-selector resolution through the approve/reject tail) and may split the nudge / recovery-turn block into one named helper local to that file. Move `withRuns` and `restoreReviewedHead` with it only if the gate phase no longer uses them (grep before moving).
- No behavior change: same event order, same `state` mutations, same return values. This is a pure extraction; the `reject` closure stays defined once in `reviewAttempt` and is passed in.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- review.ts is under ~450 lines and no function in review.ts or review-run.ts exceeds ~300 lines.
- A grep for each moved name over src/, test/ and the markdown docs finds no stale reference.
- `npm run test:gate` passes with no test edits beyond import paths.

**Done as built.** `runReviewer` and `ReviewRunInput` live in src/review/review-run.ts, with `settleUnparsedReview` as its one local helper (the no-verdict failure settlement, rather than the nudge / recovery block). `withRuns`, `restoreReviewedHead`, `REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT` (re-exported from review.ts) and `combineSignals` moved too, since the gate phase needed only the first two as imports. `ReviewRetry` and `CheckOverlap` are exported from review.ts for type use. No test edits were needed.

### The TUI's History run trail shows the run's agent transcript with Ctrl+R, and its prompts on a second press, the terminal twin of `tumwater history <role> <n> --transcript [--prompt]` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight dashboard "Show prompts" plan touches src/gui/ and src/ui/gui/; the logs and history-follow plans touch src/cli/ and src/history/, none of the source files below, and edit other docs/cli.md rows, so whichever lands second just rebases. The blocked plain-terms parts rename identifiers in src/ui/tui/ later, which is only a rebase. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts, done 2026-10-19)

**Goal.** The TUI's History trail (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P) shows a run's event trail and commit stat. It cannot show what the agent did in that run. The CLI can (`tumwater history <role> <n> --transcript [--prompt]`, `cmdTick` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts), and so can the dashboard drill-down (Show transcript). Nothing in src/ui/tui calls `tickTranscriptLines` or `readRunTranscript` (`grep -rn "tickTranscriptLines\|readRunTranscript" src/ui/tui` finds nothing). Add the transcript to the trail, so an operator reading a run in the terminal can see the agent's work without switching to another command.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts (`createHistoryPane`'s closure): add `let trailTranscript: "off" | "plain" | "prompts" = "off"`. Replace the single `trailCache` string assembly with three parts held for the shown run: `trailText` (`renderTickDetail(detail)`), `trailStat` (null until `loadTrailStat` resolves) and `trailTranscriptText` (null when off). Also keep the shown run's `{ role, run, detail }`. Add one `composeTrail()` that sets `trailCache` to `[trailText, trailStat, trailTranscriptText]` with the nulls dropped, joined by `"\n\n"`. That is the same order and separator as `cmdTick`'s text output: detail, then stat, then transcript. `loadTrailStat`'s success branch sets `trailStat` and calls `composeTrail()`, instead of writing `` `${text}\n\n${stat}` `` directly. Its existing `trailGen` guard stays.
- A `loadTranscript()` helper. When `trailTranscript` is off, it sets `trailTranscriptText = null`. Otherwise it calls `tickTranscriptLines(session.root, role, run, detail, { includePrompts: trailTranscript === "prompts" })` (exported from src/tick/tick-detail.ts, synchronous). It sets `trailTranscriptText` to `found.join("\n")` when `found` is non-empty, and to `note` otherwise. Those are `cmdTick`'s two outputs. A throw is caught and flashed (`session.flashError`), and leaves the transcript text null. `loadTrail` calls it after reading the detail, so Ctrl+P steps and scope or filter refreshes keep the chosen transcript level for the newly shown run.
- New key arm in `handleKey`: `key.ctrl && key.name === "r"`. On the History view (`session.view === session.roleIds.length + 4`) with `trailMode` on, it cycles `trailTranscript` off → plain → prompts → off. If the prompt line is free (`promptLineFree(ctx.es)`), it then calls `loadTranscript()`, `composeTrail()` and `session.paneScroll = 0`. It calls `session.requestRender()` and returns true. It does not bump `trailGen`, because the run is unchanged and an in-flight stat still belongs to it. When the History view is not showing or the trail is off, it returns false, so Ctrl+R keeps its other meanings.
- Leaving the trail resets `trailTranscript` to `"off"`: the Ctrl+N toggle-off branch and `reset()` both do this. Ctrl+N back on therefore shows the bare trail, as it does today.
- `state()` returns `trailTranscript`. Add the field, with a doc comment, to the state type in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts beside `trailMode`/`trailIndex`/`trailCache`.
- src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: the Ctrl+R router tries `history.handleKey` after the Pending, Health and Backlog arms. Each arm is view-guarded, so their order does not matter. Update the router's comment.
- src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: the History footer (the `view.kind === "history"` keys) adds `["Ctrl+R", …]` only while `view.trail` is on, next to the existing `Ctrl+P` hint. The label names what the next press shows: `transcript`, then `prompts`, then `hide transcript`. Thread `trailTranscript` into the history `view` union member, the same way `trail` is threaded.
- docs/cli.md: add a TUI keys table row: `Ctrl+R` | History (on a run trail) | cycles the trail's agent transcript, then the transcript with each agent run's prompt, then off (the `history <role> <n> --transcript [--prompt]` text). test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts checks this table against the handlers. docs/how-it-works.md: in the History `Ctrl+N`/`Ctrl+P` paragraph, add one sentence about Ctrl+R.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/tui-keys.test.ts, modeled on "Ctrl+N on the History pane swaps the rows for the newest completed run's trail". The fixture has run 1 of `clean` in the events log and a `.tumwater/log/clean.pi.jsonl`. That pi log holds a `tumwater_run` marker whose `ts` falls inside the run, then an assistant message (fixture shape as in test/gui-server-api.test.ts's transcript tests).
  - After Ctrl+N then Ctrl+R, `state().trailTranscript === "plain"`. `trailCache` equals `renderTickDetail(detail)` + `"\n\n"` + `tickTranscriptLines(root, "clean", 1, detail).found.join("\n")`. This uses a `tickStat` dep stub that never resolves, so no stat part is present.
  - A second Ctrl+R gives `"prompts"`, and `trailCache` ends with the `{ includePrompts: true }` lines. A third gives `"off"`, and `trailCache` is the bare `renderTickDetail` text.
  - Ctrl+N off and back on shows `trailTranscript === "off"`.
- A run whose pi log holds no segment in its window shows `tickTranscriptLines`'s `note` text after Ctrl+R.
- With a resolving `tickStat` stub, the composed cache is detail, then stat, then transcript, whichever finishes first: Ctrl+R before the stat resolves still ends with the transcript once it does.
- Ctrl+R on the History rows (trail off) leaves `state()` unchanged. Ctrl+R on the Pending, Health and Backlog views behaves as before: their existing tests still pass.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: the History footer shows `Ctrl+R` with `transcript` on a trail, and shows no `Ctrl+R` on the rows.
- `npm run test:gate` passes, including test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts.

### `tumwater history -f --json` streams one compact JSON row per line, the scriptable twin of `logs -f --json` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/history/history.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/history-follow.test.ts, done 2026-10-19)

**Goal.** `tumwater history -f` prints a live feed of finished runs, but only as padded table rows: `history -f --json` currently fails as rival shapes ("--json prints one document; -f streams rows"). `logs -f --json` already streams NDJSON (one `sayJsonLine` per event), so a script that wants each finished run's result, model, duration, tokens and cost has to rebuild them from raw `run_start`/`run_end` events itself. Make `history -f --json` print each row as one compact JSON object per line. Each object is the `TickRow` (src/history/history-data.ts) that `history --json` puts in its `{ rows }` array, with `ts`, `tokens` and `costUsd` kept raw. A watcher can then `tumwater history -f --json --result refused,problems | while read -r row; …` without parsing the table.

**Approach (src/history/history.ts).**
- In `cmdHistory`'s `if (follow)` block, delete the `failRivalShapes("history --json", "-f/--follow", …)` line. The `--since` and `--summary` rivals stay. `--by` still needs `--summary`, so `-f --by` fails as before.
- Add a `json: boolean` parameter to `followHistory` and pass `rest.includes("--json")` from the call site.
- In `followHistory`, with `json` set:
  - Print the seed oldest first as `for (const r of ordered) sayJsonLine(r)` instead of the joined `renderRow` block.
  - Print each live row as `sayJsonLine(row)` instead of `say(renderRow(row, widths))`. Skip the `widths` bookkeeping in JSON mode.
  - Leave the `seen` dedupe, the `keep` filter (`--grep`/`--result`/`--model`), the `--role` scope and the `followUntilParentGone` ending exactly as they are.
- Import `sayJsonLine` from `../cli/cli-output.js`.
- An empty seed prints nothing in JSON mode, the same as the table follow. It never prints prose and never prints a `{"rows":[]}` document.
- Update `followHistory`'s doc comment to say that with `--json` each row is one `sayJsonLine` object.
- `--grep` keeps matching against the rendered row text (`tickRowsMatchingGrep`), as it does in the one-shot `history --json`.

**Help and docs.**
- src/cli/help.ts, `history` listing stanza: change `(not with --since, --summary or --json);` to `(not with --since or --summary); with --json, one compact JSON row per line (the --json row shape), like logs -f --json;`. Keep the stanza's line breaks in the existing column style.
- docs/cli.md, the "Watch run history" row: change `(not with \`--since\`, \`--summary\` or \`--json\`)` to `(not with \`--since\` or \`--summary\`; with \`--json\` each row is one compact JSON object per line, like \`logs -f --json\`)`.
- Completion derives from HELP, and `--json` is already a `history` flag, so src/cli/completion.ts needs no change.

**Tests (test/history-follow.test.ts).**
- "history -f fails with its rival shapes": drop `["--json"]` from the rival list. The `--since` and `--summary` asserts stay.
- New test "history -f --json streams one JSON row per line, seed oldest first". Call `follow(["-f", "--json"], seed, [start("clean", 3, 5, "acme/m2"), end("clean", 3, 6, "changed")])`. Split the output on newlines and `JSON.parse` every line. Assert three objects in `role`/`run` order `clean#1`, `feature#2`, `clean#3`. Assert the third has `model === "acme/m2"` and a numeric `ts`.
- New test "history -f --json applies --result to followed rows". Reuse the `more` events from the --role/--result test with `["--result", "merged", "-f", "--json"]`. Assert that the parsed runs include 7 and exclude 6.
