### `tumwater history --model <selector>[,<selector>...]` keeps only the runs that started on the listed models, the row view behind `history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the in-flight part 11/14 renames comments and local names under src/cli/, and src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts and src/cli.ts's `history` case may meet it as a rebase; the status and prompt entries touch `cmdStatus`, src/ui/status-* and src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, not src/history; touches src/history/history.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` (`summarizeTickRowsByModel`, src/history/history-data.ts) counts runs per model, for example how many runs a role spent on the fallback. Nothing lists the runs behind one of its lines. Every `TickRow` carries `model`, the agent-qualified selector its `run_start` named, or null. Today the closest filter is `--grep <model>`, which also keeps rows whose summary or error happens to mention the text. Add `--model <selector>[,<selector>...]`. It keeps the rows whose `model` equals one of the listed selectors exactly, so a line from the `--by model` table can be copied straight into the filter. Out of scope: the dashboard's and the TUI's History views, and value completion for the flag.

**Decided semantics (no open question).**
- A row matches when `row.model` is one of the listed selectors, compared exactly and case-sensitively. A row with a null model never matches. `(unknown)` is only the summary's label for null, so it is not accepted as a selector.
- The value is split on commas, each piece trimmed, empty pieces dropped and duplicates removed, as `--result` does. A missing value, an empty value, or a value made only of commas fails with `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR = "history --model needs a model selector"`.
- An unknown selector is not an error. Models have no closed vocabulary, and an old log holds models the config has since dropped. An unknown selector just keeps no rows.
- The flag composes with `--role`, `-n`, `--since`, `--grep`, `--result`, `--summary`, `--by` and `--json`. It runs on the collected rows after the `--result` filter and before the `--json`, summary and table branches, so all three render the same narrowed set. `-n` still bounds the scanned window, not the printed rows, which is the `--grep` rule.

**Approach.**
- **src/history/history.ts**:
  - Export `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR` beside `HISTORY_RESULT_VALUE_ERROR`, with a doc comment in the same style.
  - In `cmdHistory`, right after the `--result` block, save `const afterResult = rows.length;`. Then read `flagValue(rest, "--model")` and parse it into `models: string[] | null` as described above. When `models` is set, filter with `rows = rows.filter((r) => r.model !== null && models.includes(r.model))`. Add a comment in the file's style naming the exact-match rule and why an unknown selector is not an error.
  - In the empty-state `say(...)` chain, put a new first arm before the `--result` arm: when `models !== null && afterResult > 0`, print `` `no runs on model "${models.join(",")}"` ``. This keeps the existing rule that the message blames the filter that actually emptied the set. `--json` still prints `{"rows":[]}`.
  - Update the `cmdHistory` doc comment's flag list to name `--model`.
- **src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts**: add `export function modelFlagSpec(missingValue: string): FlagSpec`, returning `{ names: ["--model"], value: true, valueName: "<selector>", missingValue }`, beside `resultFlagSpec`/`byFlagSpec`, with a matching doc comment.
- **src/cli.ts** `case "history"`: import `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR` with the other history errors and add `modelFlagSpec(HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR)` to the `rejectUnknownArgs("history", …)` list. The trail form (`history <role> <n>`) is untouched.
- **src/cli/help.ts**: in the `tumwater history` usage line, add `[--model <selector>[,...]]` after the `--result` bracket. In the description, after the `--result` sentence, add: `--model <selector>[,...] keeps only the runs that started on the listed models (the exact selectors --by model prints);`.
- **docs/cli.md** "Watch run history" row: add `[--model <selector>[,...]]` after the `--result` bracket in the synopsis. After the `--result none,refused,problems` clause, add `, `--model` keeps only the runs that started on the listed models, the exact selectors `--summary --by model` prints (`--model acme/m1 --summary` tallies just that model's runs by role)`.

**Files touched.** src/history/history.ts, src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts. Also touch test/cli-help.test.ts or test/cli-doc.test.ts, but only if their help/doc flag-parity checks need the new flag listed.

**Acceptance criteria.** All new tests go in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts and reuse the event fixture from "history --summary --by model tallies runs per model": feature #1 and #3 on `acme/m1`, clean #2 on `acme/m2`, and bugfix #9 with no start.
- "history --model keeps only the runs that started on the listed models":
  - `history --model acme/m1` prints exactly two rows, feature #3 and feature #1, newest first.
  - `history --model acme/m1,acme/m2 --json` gives `rows` with roles `["feature", "clean", "feature"]`.
  - `history --model acme/m1,acme/m1` prints the same as `--model acme/m1`.
  - `history --model acme/M1` prints `no runs on model "acme/M1"` and exits 0, which shows the match is case-sensitive.
  - `history --model m1` prints the same empty-state line, which shows the match is exact, not a substring.
- "history --model composes with --role, --result and --summary":
  - `--model acme/m1 --result merged` keeps only feature #1.
  - `--model acme/m1 --role clean` prints `no runs on model "acme/m1"`.
  - `--model acme/m1 --summary --by model` gives the model column `["acme/m1", "total"]`.
  - `--model acme/m1 --summary` gives one `feature` line plus `total`.
  - `--model nosuch --json` prints `{"rows":[]}`.
- "history --model fails with its own wording when the value is missing or empty": a trailing `history --model`, `history --model ""` and `history --model ","` each exit non-zero, and stderr matches `history --model needs a model selector`.
- "an empty log keeps its own wording under --model": a repo with no events, run with `--model acme/m1`, prints `no runs yet`.
- The existing tests in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts, test/cli-history.test.ts and test/cli-history-views.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A run's trail names the sha its change landed under on main, so a rebased merge's run says which commit `tumwater revert` takes (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the blocked plain-terms parts rename src/tick/ and history-data.ts names later and will rebase over this; the status, prompt and history --model entries touch none of these files; touches src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts src/tick/tick-detail.ts docs/cli.md test/tick-detail-data.test.ts test/tick-detail.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history <role> <n>` (and the dashboard History drill-down and TUI History
pane, which render the same `renderTickDetail` text) shows only the commit the run *pinned*
(`tickCommitSha` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts: the `merge_queued`/`merge_done` event's
`commit`). When the merge rebased, main holds that change under a different sha, so the
pinned sha is not what `tumwater revert` accepts (`revertMergedCommit` in src/operator/revert.ts
refuses a commit that is not on main), and nothing in the trail names the landed one. The
landed sha is already logged: `merged` events carry it (`logEventBestEffort(... type: "merged",
commit ...)` in src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, source = the role). This plan pairs that event into
the run's payload and header. It is also the prerequisite for a later dashboard "Revert this
change" button, which is not part of this plan.

**Approach.**
- src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts: add `mergedSha: string | null` to `TickDetail` (doc it beside
  `merge`), filled in `detailFrom`:
  - result `changed` with `merge === null` (a run that merged directly): the newest `merged`
    event inside `block` whose `commit` is a non-empty string.
  - `merge?.type === "merge_done"` (a queued run whose merge finished): the newest `merged`
    event in `scoped` (already this role's events only) whose `commit` is a non-empty string and
    whose `ts` lies in `[merge.ts - merge.durationMs, merge.ts]`. That is the merge's own
    window, since `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) logs `merge_done` after
    merge-to-main logs `merged`, and `durationMs` runs from the verification's start. If
    `durationMs` is not a finite number, the value is null. This window also covers a
    leftover-recovery run, whose merge sits before its block.
  - Every other case is null: no merge, a failed or pending merge, or a `merged` event that
    rotated out. A no-op fast-forward logs no `merged` event, so it also reads null.
- src/tick/tick-detail.ts `renderTickDetail`: after the ` · commit <short>` segment, append
  ` · merged as <shortSha(mergedSha)>` when `mergedSha !== null && mergedSha !== sha` (when
  they are equal, the commit segment already names it). Leave `tickCommitSha`,
  `tickDetailStat` and `--stat` unchanged: the stat describes what the run changed, per its
  doc comment. `cmdTick --json` and GET /api/run (`handleTick` in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts,
  which spreads the detail) carry the new key without edits. Check that the TUI pane
  (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts) only renders the text.
- docs/cli.md: in the `tumwater history <role> <n>` clause of the "Watch run history" row,
  add that the header names the landed sha (`merged as <sha>`, the one `tumwater revert`
  takes) when a rebased merge put the change on main under a different sha.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/tick-detail-data.test.ts: a new test, built on the fixture style of "a queued tick
  resolves to its merge's verdict and outcome event; a pending merge stays queued", asserts:
  - a queued run with `merged` (commit `landed1`) logged inside its `merge_done`'s
    `durationMs` window reads `mergedSha === "landed1"`;
  - a direct `changed` run with a `merged` event in its block reads that event's commit;
  - a `merge_failed` run, a still-pending queued run, and a `merged` event outside the window
    (e.g. another merge of the same role an hour earlier) all read `null`;
  - another role's `merged` event inside the window is not picked.
- test/tick-detail.test.ts: `renderTickDetail` puts `merged as <short>` in the header when the
  landed sha differs from the pinned one, leaves it out when they are equal or `mergedSha` is
  null, and `cmdTick --json` output includes `mergedSha`.
- Existing tick-detail tests pass with only the new key added to any `deepEqual`'d payload.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

_Built as planned, except the key is named `mergedSha` (not `landedSha`): the terminology guard test rejects the retired name "landed" in identifiers._

### The dashboard's Backlog Search also keeps rows whose entry body matches, through a new `GET /api/backlog-match?grep=<text>`, so it matches what the TUI Backlog pane's `/` and `tumwater backlog --grep` match (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight entries edit status, prompt, history and src/tick, and none touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts's backlog region or the /api/backlog handlers; done 2026-10-19)

**Goal.** The dashboard Backlog card's Search box (`backlogGrep`, `setBacklogGrep` and `renderBacklog` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts) matches only the text a row shows, because `/api/status` carries titles, not bodies. The TUI's `/` (`visibleBacklogIndexes` in src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts) and `tumwater backlog --grep` match the heading or the body through `entryMatches` (src/backlog/backlog.ts). So a dashboard search for a file or symbol named only inside a plan's body finds nothing. This plan closes that gap. Bodies still never ride the 1s status poll.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- One new read-only route, `GET /api/backlog-match?grep=<text>`. It answers `{ plans, bugs, questions, done, fixed, answered }`. Each value is the ascending list of indexes whose entry `entryMatches` the trimmed text. It reads each file through its reader in `BACKLOG_FILE_READERS`, so its indexes are the ones `/api/backlog?file=…&index=N` already addresses. Those are the same indexes the card's rows carry as `data-index`, including the newest-first done/fixed/answered order.
- A missing or blank (after trim) `grep` is a 400 `grep required`, via `badRequest`.
- The Inbox (queued prompts) tab is unchanged: its rows already show the preview, and prompt bodies are out of scope.
- A row shows when its shown text hits, as today, OR when its index is in the body-match list for the current needle. Until the first match response for the needle arrives, only shown-text hits paint. That is today's behavior, so typing never blanks the panel while a request is in flight.

**Approach.**
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts**: add `export function handleBacklogMatch(q, res, root)` beside `handleBacklog`, with a doc comment in the same style. It reads `q.get("grep")`, trims it, and returns 400 when the result is empty. Otherwise it builds the object by iterating `BACKLOG_FILE_READERS` and, for each file, collecting the indexes `i` where `entryMatches(entry, needle)`. Import `entryMatches` from ../backlog/backlog.js. Answer with `sendJson(res, 200, …)`.
- **src/gui/gui-server.ts**: add `"GET /api/backlog-match": (_req, res, target) => handleBacklogMatch(target.searchParams, res, root),` after the `"GET /api/backlog"` route, plus the import.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts**, inside the `backlog:start`/`backlog:end` region:
  - Add `let backlogBodyHits = null;`, shaped `{ needle, plans: [...], bugs, questions, done, fixed, answered }` and holding the last match response.
  - Add `let backlogMatchAt = 0;` for the time of the last match fetch.
  - Add `async function fetchBacklogMatch()`. With an empty `backlogGrep` it sets `backlogBodyHits = null` and returns. Otherwise it captures `const needle = backlogGrep`, sets `backlogMatchAt = Date.now()`, and awaits `getJson("/api/backlog-match?grep=" + encodeURIComponent(needle))`. If `backlogGrep` still equals `needle` when the answer arrives, it stores `{ needle, ...d }` and repaints with `renderBacklog(backlogStatus)` when `backlogStatus` is set. A stale answer for an older needle is dropped. A failed fetch is caught and leaves the shown-text matching in place.
  - `setBacklogGrep` calls `fetchBacklogMatch()` after its repaint.
  - At the top of `renderBacklog`, when `backlogGrep` is set and `Date.now() - backlogMatchAt > 5000`, call `fetchBacklogMatch()` (not awaited). This keeps body hits fresh as the files change, at most once per 5s, much like the History view's `histFetchedAt` throttle.
  - Change the local `hit(text)` to `hit(text, file, i)`. It returns true when `needle` is empty, when the text contains it, or when `backlogBodyHits && backlogBodyHits.needle === backlogGrep` and `(backlogBodyHits[file] || []).includes(i)`.
  - Pass the file and the row's payload index at each call: `"plans"`/`"bugs"`/`"questions"` (the tab key) with the open row's index, `"answered"` with `x.i`, and `"done"`/`"fixed"` (by tab) with `x.i`. The Inbox call keeps one argument.
  - Update the "Search narrows rows by the text each one shows" comment to say that body matches come from /api/backlog-match.
- **docs/cli.md**: in the TUI key table's `/` row, change "the dashboard's Backlog card has a Search box that does the same over each row's shown text" to say the Search box filters by heading or body the same way.

**Files touched.** src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts, docs/cli.md, test/gui.test.ts, test/gui-client-team.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/gui.test.ts, "gui /api/backlog-match lists the indexes whose heading or body matches": seed PLANS.md with three planned entries, only the second of which mentions `zebra`, and only in its body. Seed one BUGS.md open entry whose title says `Zebra`. `GET /api/backlog-match?grep=ZEBRA` answers 200 with `plans: [1]`, `bugs: [0]`, and empty `questions`, `done`, `fixed` and `answered`. `?grep=%20` and a request with no `grep` both answer 400.
- test/gui-client-team.test.ts. The scope helper adds `backlogBodyHits` and `getJson` to `extra` and stubs `getJson` to record paths.
  - "a Backlog Search keeps a row whose body matched on the server": plans `["Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie"]`, `backlogGrep: "zebra"` and `backlogBodyHits: { needle: "zebra", plans: [1], bugs: [], questions: [], done: [], fixed: [], answered: [] }` paint `data-index='1'` only.
  - "body hits for an older needle are ignored": the same fixture with `backlogBodyHits.needle: "zeb"` paints `Nothing matches this search`.
  - "setBacklogGrep asks /api/backlog-match for the trimmed text": `setBacklogGrep("  zebra ")` makes one `getJson` call to `/api/backlog-match?grep=zebra`, and `setBacklogGrep("")` makes none.
- The existing Backlog Search tests in test/gui-client-team.test.ts pass unchanged with `backlogBodyHits: null`. That includes "setBacklogGrep repaints and an empty search restores the tab byte-for-byte".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater status --role <id>[,<id>...]` shows only the listed roles' rows, the status twin of `report --role` and `history --role` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — part 10/14 edits config/roles/init, the questions entry `cmdQuestions` and src/backlog, the Backlog-search entry src/ui/gui; none touches `cmdStatus`, src/ui/status-render.ts or src/ui/status-payload.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `report`, `history`, `wake`, `pause`, `resume`, `abort` and `reset-counters` all take `--role <id>[,<id>...]`, but `tumwater status` does not. `cmdStatus` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts) calls `rejectUnknownArgs("status", args, [JSON_FLAG])`, so `status --role feature` exits 1. A team with 16 roles plus feature/bugfix instances prints a long table, and an operator watching two roles has to scan it all. Let `status --role clean,dedupe` (and `--json`) keep only the listed roles' rows. The header, its badges and the team-wide banners stay the same.

**Approach.**
- `src/status/status-data.ts`: add `export function scopeSnapshotToRoles(snap: StatusSnapshot, roles: readonly string[]): StatusSnapshot`. It returns `{ ...snap, loops: snap.loops.filter(...) }` and keeps a loop when `roles.includes(s.role) || roles.includes(baseRoleOf(s.role))` (`baseRoleOf`, src/roles/runner-ids.ts). So `--role feature` keeps `feature`, `feature-2` and `feature-3`, and `--role feature-2` keeps that one instance. Every other field (budget, inbox, questions, roleInbox, scheduledWakes) is copied unchanged.
- `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdStatus`: add `ROLE_FLAG` (src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts) to the `rejectUnknownArgs` list. Read `const scope = parseRoleListScope(root, args)` (src/cli/cli-args.ts) after `requireReadyRepo`, so ids are checked against `knownRoleIdsCached`: catalog, custom and instance ids. The text path renders `renderStatus(root, scope ? scopeSnapshotToRoles(snap, scope) : snap, width, scope !== null)`. The JSON path calls `statusPayload(root, Date.now(), scope)`.
- `src/ui/status-render.ts`: give `renderStatusSpans` and `renderStatus` a trailing `scoped = false` parameter, and have `renderStatus` pass it through. Only the totals row's today cell changes. Unscoped it stays `usd(snap.budget.spentUsd)`, the team figure the header badge reads. Scoped it is `usd(snap.loops.reduce((sum, s) => sum + dailyCost(s), 0))`, so the total adds up the rows shown. The header badge still shows the team's spend. The other totals cells already sum `snap.loops`/`withMetrics`, so they follow the scope with no change. The TUI caller (src/ui/tui/tui.tsx) is not changed.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts` `statusPayload(root, now = Date.now(), roles: readonly string[] | null = null)`: right after `snapshot(root, undefined, now)`, apply `scopeSnapshotToRoles` when `roles` is non-null. So the payload's `roles` array, and the `teamAlerts` computed from it, follow the scope, while `budget`/`budgetBadge` stay team-wide. The GUI server's existing one-argument calls are not changed.
- An empty match, such as a disabled role in `--role`, is not an error. It renders the header and an empty table with a zero totals row, the existing empty-table path ("totals row shows zeros without breaking alignment").
- `src/cli/help.ts`: change the stanza to `tumwater status [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--json]` and add one sentence: `--role keeps only the listed roles' rows (a base id includes its instances); the header and budget stay team-wide`. `docs/cli.md`, "Check state" row: change `` `tumwater status` `` to `` `tumwater status [--role <id>[,<id>...]]` (only the listed roles' rows, a base role id taking its instances too; works with `--json`) ``. Completion derives from the help stanzas, so it needs no edit.

**Files touched.** src/status/status-data.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/status-render.test.ts, test/status-payload.test.ts (plus test/cli-help.test.ts only if its help-vs-flag check needs the new stanza).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/status-render.test.ts, "a role-scoped status table keeps the listed roles and their instances". Take a snapshot built with `snapshotWith` (test/fixtures/status-fixtures.ts), holding `clean` ($1.25 total), `dedupe` ($0.50) and `feature` plus `feature-2`. Pass it through `scopeSnapshotToRoles(snap, ["feature", "clean"])` and `renderStatus(root, …, undefined, true)`. The output has rows for clean, feature and feature-2, none for dedupe, and the totals row reads `$1.25` plus feature's cost in the total column.
- New test, "a scoped totals row sums today over the shown rows, not the team budget". Set `snap.budget.spentUsd` to 9.99 and give the shown rows today spends summing to $0.40. The scoped totals row contains `$0.40` and not `$9.99`. The same snapshot unscoped still shows `$9.99`.
- New test in test/status-payload.test.ts: `statusPayload(root, now, ["clean"])` on a repo whose state holds clean and dedupe gives a `roles` array with only clean. Its `budget` deep-equals the unscoped payload's `budget`.
- `tumwater status --role nosuch` fails with `unknownRoleMessage`'s wording before rendering. `tumwater status --role ""` fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`. Cover both through the CLI, in the test file the implementer finds already driving `cmdStatus` or `rejectUnknownArgs` (test/cli-help.test.ts or a new test/cli-status.test.ts).
- The existing status-render, status-header and status-payload tests pass unchanged, including "status table ends with a totals row summing tokens and cost".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater prompt --list --role <id>[,<id>...]` lists several roles' inboxes, the inbox twin of `history --role clean,dedupe` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the in-flight part 11/14 edits comments and local names in src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts and test/cli-*.test.ts but not the `--list` role scope, so whichever merges second rebases onto the other's names; the status entry touches `cmdStatus` and src/ui/status-*; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `report`, `history`, `wake`, `pause`, `resume`, `abort`, `reset-counters` (and, once planned work merges, `status`) take `--role <id>[,<id>...]`. `tumwater prompt --list --role` takes only one id: `prompt --list --role qa,readme` fails with `unknownRoleMessage("qa,readme", …)`, because `cmdPrompt` (src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts) checks `parsed.role` as one string. An operator watching two roles' inboxes has to run the command twice or scan every section. Let `--list` (and `--list --json`) take a comma list. The other modes (enqueue, `--cancel`, `--edit`, `--top`) keep their single `--role`, because each writes to one queue.

**Approach.**
- `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts` `cmdPrompt`, list mode only: compute `const listRoles = parseRoleListFlag(args, validIds)` (src/cli/cli-args.ts; `validIds` is already `knownRoleIdsCached(root)` in list mode, which holds the director, catalog, custom and instance ids). It canonicalizes, dedupes, fails an unknown piece with `unknownRoleMessage` and an all-empty value with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`. Skip the existing single-id `validIds.includes(parsed.role)` check in list mode, since `parseRoleListFlag` covers it. Rows: `listRoles === null ? queuedListRows(root, null, validIds) : queuedListRows(root, null, validIds).filter((row) => listRoles.includes(row.role))`. Filtering the list-wide rows keeps the list-wide section order (director first, then `validIds` order) and each section's own 1-based positions, so the positions still match what `--cancel <n> --role <id>` takes. A single id gives the same rows as today's `queuedListRows(root, role, …)`. Match ids exactly: `--role feature` does not pull in `feature-2`'s queue, as today.
- Empty result: one listed id keeps today's `` `${roleLabel(role)}'s inbox is empty` ``. Two or more print `` `every listed inbox is empty (${listRoles.join(", ")})` ``. `--json` still prints `{ prompts: [] }`.
- The non-list modes are unchanged: `prompt --role qa,readme "text"` still fails with `unknownRoleMessage` through the existing `knownRoleIds(loadConfig(root))` check. `parsePromptArgs` (src/cli/cli-command-args.ts) is unchanged, since its `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR` check on a missing value still applies.
- Update the `cmdPrompt` doc comment and the list-mode comment block to say `--list` takes a comma list.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: change the stanza `tumwater prompt --list [--json]` to `tumwater prompt --list [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--json]`. Keep the description, adding `; --role keeps only the listed roles' sections` if it fits the column. `docs/cli.md` "Steer the project" row: after `` `tumwater prompt --list` shows the inbox messages numbered and grouped by role, with how long each has waited (`--json` for scripts) `` add `, and `--role <id>[,<id>...]` keeps only the listed roles' sections, under the same numbers`. Completion derives from the help stanzas, so it needs no edit.

**Files touched.** src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-prompt-queue.test.ts (plus test/cli-help.test.ts or test/cli-doc.test.ts only if their help/doc flag checks need the new stanza).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/cli-prompt-queue.test.ts, "prompt --list --role takes a comma list and keeps each section's numbering". Queue `director task`, two qa prompts and one readme prompt (the `submitPrompt`/`submitRolePrompt` helpers the grouped-listing test uses). `prompt --list --role readme,qa` exits 0. Its output holds the `qa:` section with `1.` and `2.` and the `readme:` section with `1. docs task`, with readme before qa (list-wide order, which follows the catalog, not flag order; the test passes `qa,readme` to show it), and no `director task`. `prompt --list --role qa,qa` prints the same as `--role qa`. `prompt --list --role director,readme --json` gives `prompts` whose `role` values are only `director` and `readme`.
- New test: `prompt --list --role qa,nosuch` exits 1 with `unknownRoleMessage`'s wording for `nosuch`. `prompt --list --role ","` exits 1 with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`. `prompt --list --role qa,readme` on empty queues prints `every listed inbox is empty (qa, readme)`.
- New assertion: `prompt --role qa,readme "text"` still exits 1 with the unknown-role message and queues nothing (`queuedRolePrompts(repo, "qa")` is empty).
- These existing tests pass unchanged: "prompt --list --role with an empty queue names the role, not an error", "prompt --list groups queues by loop and --cancel removes from the named loop's queue", "prompt --list survives a broken tumwater.json; named-role writes still fail loudly", and "prompt --list --json prints one JSON document matching the rendered list".

### The dashboard's Backlog card gets a Search box that narrows the shown tab's rows by text, the browser twin of the TUI Backlog pane's `/` and `tumwater backlog --grep` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry: part 10/14 edits config/roles/init and the questions entry edits src/backlog/question-answer.ts and `cmdQuestions`, and neither touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts or src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Text search on the backlog exists on the terminal: `plan|bug --list --grep`, `tumwater backlog --grep`, `questions --answered --grep`, and the TUI Backlog pane's `/` (`backlogGrep` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts). The dashboard has a Search box on History (`histgrep`, src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts) and on Activity (`feedgrep`, src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts and gui-client-team.ts). Its Backlog card (`#backlogcard`, painted by `renderBacklog` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts) has no search. A long Plans list, such as today's blocked series plus several eligible entries, can only be scanned by eye. Add a Search box to the card that filters every tab's rows on the client as the operator types, the same way the Activity box filters its carried rows.

**Decided scope (no open question).** Matching is case-insensitive substring over the text a row already shows, because the status payload carries no entry bodies. That text is the title plus meta (`splitTitle`) and the hold tag on Plans/Bugs rows, the title and decision on Answered rows, the title on Done/Fixed rows, and the preview plus role id on Inbox rows. Bodies stay searchable from `tumwater backlog --grep` and the TUI's `/`. Tab badges keep their unfiltered counts. A row keeps its original `data-index`, so the drawer, Answer, Release and Move to top still address the right entry. No server endpoint changes.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts**: in `#backlogcard`'s `card-head`, after `#backlogtabs`, add `<label><span class="sr-only">Search</span><input class="field" id="backloggrep" type="search" placeholder="Search backlog…" autocomplete="off"></label>`, the markup the `feedgrep` box uses.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts**:
  - Beside `let backlogTab = recall("backlog") || "";`, which sits outside the marked region, add `let backlogGrep = recall("backlog-grep") || "";`.
  - Inside the `backlog:start`/`backlog:end` region, add `setBacklogGrep(text)`. It sets `backlogGrep = text.trim()`, calls `store("backlog-grep", backlogGrep)`, and repaints with `renderBacklog(backlogStatus)` when `backlogStatus` is set.
  - In `renderBacklog`, add a `const needle = backlogGrep.toLowerCase()` and a local `hit(text)` helper that returns true when `needle` is empty or `text` contains it, compared lowercased. Use it in four places:
    - Inbox: keep only the queued rows where `hit(q.preview + " " + q.role)`. The `paintedFirst` group-head logic still runs over the unfiltered list, so a role's real head never gains a Move to top button.
    - Plans/Bugs/Questions: `rows` becomes empty for a non-hit index, tested on `t.title + " " + t.meta + " " + mark`. When `needle` is set, blocked hits paint flat under the Blocked divider and skip the series collapse, so a matching part is not hidden in a closed series. `heldCount` counts the shown blocked rows only.
    - Answered: test `a.title + " " + (a.decision || "")`.
    - Done/Fixed: test `f.title`.
  - When `needle` is set and the tab shows no rows in any section (open, answered, or finished), paint `<div class='empty'><strong>Nothing matches this search</strong>Clear the search box to see every entry.</div>`. A tab that is empty anyway keeps its own empty state. The New plan / File a bug button and form keep painting.
  - After `backlog:end`, next to the `#backlogtabs` click listener, set `$("backloggrep").value = backlogGrep` once at load. Add an `input` listener that calls `setBacklogGrep(ev.target.value)`. Copy the `feedgrep` comment's reason: the 1s poll must never write the box back.
- **docs/cli.md**: the TUI key table's `/` row ("on Backlog, filter the active entries by heading or body") gains "; the dashboard's Backlog card has a Search box that does the same over each row's shown text".

**Files touched.** src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts, docs/cli.md, test/gui-client-team.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** All tests go in test/gui-client-team.test.ts. Each passes `backlogGrep` through `backlogScope`'s `extra` and adds `setBacklogGrep` to the scope's exported names.
- "the Backlog Search keeps only matching rows under their original indexes": plans `["Alpha budget", "Bravo", "Charlie BUDGET"]` with `backlogGrep: "budget"` paint `data-index='0'` and `data-index='2'` but not `Bravo`. The Plans tab badge still reads 3.
- "a Backlog Search hit inside a collapsed blocked series paints without expanding it": with the series fixture from "the Plans tab shows a blocked series as one row that expands on click" and `backlogGrep: "S2"`, the row `data-index='2'` paints with no `seriestoggle` row, under `Blocked (1)`.
- "the Backlog Search filters the Inbox, Answered and Done sections too": an Inbox preview, an answered decision and a done title that don't match are dropped, and the matching ones stay.
- "a Backlog Search with no match paints its own empty state": `backlogGrep: "zzz"` on a non-empty Plans tab paints `Nothing matches this search`. An empty Bugs tab with the same search keeps `No open bugs`.
- "setBacklogGrep repaints and an empty search restores the tab byte-for-byte": the panel HTML after `setBacklogGrep("")` equals the HTML from a scope that never set a search.

- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater questions --grep <text>` searches the open questions, the open-list twin of `questions --answered --grep` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — part 10/14 edits config/roles/init, the wake entry src/cli wake parsing, the report entry src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts; none touches src/backlog/question-answer.ts or `cmdQuestions`; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Every other backlog listing searches by text with the shared `entryMatches` (`src/backlog/backlog.ts`): `plan|bug --list --grep`, their `--done` forms, `tumwater backlog --grep`, and `questions --answered --grep`. The open-question list is the exception. `tumwater questions --grep x` exits 1 with `--grep needs --answered (it searches the answered questions)` (`cmdQuestions`, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts). The parser already reads `--grep`; only that refusal and the list readers lack the filter. Let the bare list take `--grep` with the same matcher and the same unfiltered numbering, so a printed number still reaches `questions --show <n>` and `questions answer <n>`.

**Approach.**
- **src/backlog/question-answer.ts**: `openQuestionList(root, pattern?: string)` numbers every open entry first (`{ entry, position: i + 1 }`), then keeps those where `entryMatches(entry, pattern)` when a pattern is given. With no pattern its output is unchanged (`numberedList`, or `no open questions`). With a pattern it prints `${position}. ${title}${questionAgeSuffix(title)}${firstBodySuffix(body)}` lines under each entry's unfiltered position, or `no open questions match "<pattern>"` when nothing matches (the wording `answeredQuestionList` uses). `questionListPayload(root, pattern?: string)` filters its mapped entries by the same `entryMatches` after assigning `position`, so `--json` keeps each match's original position. `openQuestionAt` keeps calling it with no pattern.
- **src/cli/question-commands.ts** `sayQuestionList(root, json, pattern?: string)`: pass the pattern to both readers.
- **src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts** `cmdQuestions`: drop the `grep !== undefined && !answeredFlag` refusal. The bare-list branch (`words.length === 0`) calls `sayQuestionList(root, jsonFlag, grep)`. When `grep` is set and `words` is non-empty (the `answer` subcommand), fail `--grep only applies to listing questions`. The `--grep does not apply to --show` refusal stays. The `--grep` missing-value message becomes `--grep needs text (usage: tumwater questions [--answered] --grep <text>)`.
- **src/cli/help.ts**: the `tumwater questions [--json]` stanza becomes `tumwater questions [--grep <text>] [--json]` and gains the clause `--grep keeps the questions whose heading or body contains the text, case-insensitively, numbered as without it`. Shell completion reads its flags from these stanzas (`helpStanzas` in src/cli/completion.ts), so it needs no edit.
- **docs/cli.md**: in the "Answer open questions" row, `tumwater questions` gains `[--grep <text>]` with the same clause, named as the open twin of `--answered --grep`.

**Files touched.** src/backlog/question-answer.ts, src/cli/question-commands.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-questions-list.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/cli-questions-list.test.ts, "questions --grep lists matching open questions under their unfiltered numbers". QUESTIONS.md has three open entries, and the first and third hold `budget` in different case (one in a heading, one in a body). `questions --grep BUDGET` exits 0 and prints exactly lines `1. …` and `3. …`. `--grep budget --json` gives `questions` positions `[1, 3]`. `--grep zzz` prints `no open questions match "zzz"` and exits 0.
- In "questions --answered --grep lists matches under their unfiltered numbers", the `bare` assertion that `questions --grep x` fails with `--grep needs --answered` is replaced: on that fixture (no open entries) it exits 0 and prints `no open questions match "x"`. The `--show … --grep` refusal assertion stays.
- `questions answer 1 --grep x` is refused with `--grep only applies to listing questions` before anything is written. Check this with the --grep before the number (`questions --grep x answer 1 "d"`), since a token after the number is decision prose.

### `tumwater wake --cancel` and `wake --list` take a comma-separated `--role` list, so the scheduled-wake views match plain `wake --role clean,dedupe` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry. The in-flight `abort --role` entry also edits src/operator/operator-commands.ts and test/operator-commands.test.ts, but only `cmdAbort` and its tests, which this entry does not touch; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater wake --role clean,dedupe` (immediate or `--in 45m`) accepts a comma list. `wake --cancel --role clean,dedupe` and `wake --list --role clean,dedupe` do not: `failOnRoleList` (src/operator/operator-commands.ts) rejects them with `wake --cancel and --list take one --role id`. So an operator who scheduled one wake for two roles cannot cancel or list that same pair in one command. Accept the list in both branches. A single id and no `--role` behave exactly as now.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-requests.ts` `cancelScheduledWakes(root, role?: string)` becomes `cancelScheduledWakes(root, roles?: string[])`. `undefined` keeps the current behavior: every pending file is removed. With a list, a file naming none of `roles` is skipped. Otherwise every listed role is dropped from the file's roles: the file is removed if none remain, or rewritten with the rest (same `at` and `notBeforeMs`). The count stays one per file touched. Update the doc comment.
- `src/operator/operator-intent.ts`:
  - `cancelWakes(root, roles?: string[])` passes the list through. Its ` for <role>` suffix becomes ` for ${roles.join(", ")}`.
  - `noWakePending(roles?: string[])` gets the same suffix.
  - `listWakes(root, roles: string[] | undefined, now)` keeps a wake when `w.roles.some((r) => roles.includes(r))`. Entries still carry their full roles list.

### The dashboard's `/api/report` and `/api/failures` take a comma-separated `?role=` list, the server twin of `tumwater report --role clean,dedupe` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — fast merge 14/14 edits the merge path, runner 9/14 status data and scheduling, and the abort and wake entries src/operator; this one touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, test/gui-report.test.ts and test/gui-endpoints.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater report --role clean,dedupe` sums the usage report and failure digest over the listed roles, and the collectors behind it (`collectReport`, `collectReportSince` in src/report/report-data.ts; `collectFailureReport`, `collectFailureReportSince` in src/failure/failure-data.ts) already take `role?: string | readonly string[]`. The dashboard endpoints do not: `reportScope` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) passes the whole `?role=` value to `rejectBadRole` (src/gui/gui-args.ts), so `GET /api/report?role=clean,dedupe` is a 400 `unknown role "clean,dedupe"`. Accept the comma list on both endpoints, in both the days and `sinceMs` shapes. A single id, an absent `?role=`, and the existing 400s behave as now. The client's Role picker (src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts) stays a single-select. It sends one id, which is still valid, so the client does not change.

**Approach.**
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` `reportScope`: its return type becomes `{ roles?: string[]; sinceMs?: number } | null`. When `q.get("role")` is non-null, split it on `,`, trim each piece and drop empty pieces. If no piece remains, call `rejectBadRole(root, res, role)` with the raw value. That keeps today's 400 for `?role=` (`unknown role ""`), and `?role=,` gets the same 400 with its raw value. Otherwise run each piece through `rejectBadRole` and return null on the first miss. The 400 then names the bad piece (`unknown role "bogus"`, with the did-you-mean suffix), not the whole list. Deduplicate in first-seen order. Do not canonicalize legacy ids: the GUI endpoints validate exact ids against `validRoleIds`, and this change keeps that rule. Update the doc comment ("the `?role=` filter" → a comma-separated list, each id validated).
- `handleReport` and `handleFailures`: pass `scope.roles` where they pass `scope.role` today. In both doc comments, `[&role=<id>]` becomes `[&role=<id>[,<id>...]]` and "a present one is the filter" becomes "the listed roles, summed".
- No collector change: a one-element list gives the same output as the bare id (the output `role` field is `bases.join(",")`). The first acceptance test pins that.

**Files touched.** src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, test/gui-report.test.ts, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts.

- In test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, next to the existing `?sinceMs=3600000&role=feature` cases for `serveReport` and `serveFailures`: `?sinceMs=3600000&role=feature,steward` serves the markdown rendered from `collectReportSince(root, 3600000, ["feature", "steward"])` / `collectFailureReportSince(…)` through the same renderers, and `?sinceMs=3600000&role=feature,bogus` is 400.

### `tumwater abort --role` takes a comma-separated list of role ids, so one command stops every in-flight run an operator names (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry except that it reuses the `namedRoleList` helper the in-flight `wake --role`/`reset-counters --role` entry adds to src/operator/operator-commands.ts — it touches only `cmdAbort` there, plus help, docs and test/operator-commands.test.ts — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `abort --role <id>` stops ONE role's in-flight run (`cmdAbort`, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, via `requiredNamedRole`). An operator who has just seen a bad model change, or a broken main, and wants every running feature instance stopped has to run one `abort` per runner. `abort --role feature,feature-2` fails today with `unknown role: feature,feature-2`. Accept the comma list, as `pause --role` already does (and as `wake --role` and `reset-counters --role` will): write one abort marker per listed role. A single id behaves exactly as now.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts` `cmdAbort`:
  - Replace `requiredNamedRole(root, args, "abort")` with `const roles = namedRoleList(root, args) ?? fail("abort requires --role <id> (e.g. \`--role feature\`)");`. Keep that message byte-identical to `requiredNamedRole`'s text for `abort`. `namedRoleList` (from the wake/reset-counters entry) splits on `,`, trims and drops empty pieces, fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR` when none remain, resolves each piece through `namedRole`, and deduplicates in first-seen order. Every piece resolves before anything is written, so one bad id writes no marker. If that entry has not landed when you start, add `namedRoleList` exactly as that entry's Approach specifies, and leave its other changes to it.
  - Then `for (const role of roles) { const result = requestAbort(root, role); if (!result.ok) fail(result.error); say(result.message); }`. `requestAbort` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts) is unchanged: its liveness check fails the first call before any write when no team runs, and each role keeps its own confirmation line, including the director's discarded-prompt note.
  - `requiredNamedRole` stays, because `cmdRetire` still calls it. Reword its doc comment from "abort and retire both need a target" to say retire uses it.
  - Update `cmdAbort`'s doc comment: "kill one loop's in-flight tick" becomes "kill the named roles' in-flight runs (a comma list writes one marker per role)".
- The GUI's POST /api/abort, the TUI's Transcript `Ctrl+A`, and `consumeAbortRequests` (src/operator/operator-requests.ts) do not change: they already work one marker per role.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the usage line becomes `tumwater abort --role <id>[,<id>...]`. Because it outgrows the command column, move the description to the next line, as the `pause` stanza does: "Stop each named role's run in progress (work discarded; the role keeps going)".
- `docs/cli.md`, "Control the roles" row: `tumwater abort --role <id>` becomes `tumwater abort --role <id>[,<id>...]` (a comma list aborts each listed role's run).

**Files touched.** src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/operator-commands.test.ts, and test/help.test.ts if it pins the old `abort` line (grep it for `abort --role`).

After `markLive(root)`, call `cmdAbort(root, ["--role", "coverage, clean,coverage"])`. stdout holds `abort requested for coverage` and `abort requested for clean`, each exactly once. `abortRequestPath(root, "coverage")` and `abortRequestPath(root, "clean")` exist, and `abortRequestPath(root, "dedupe")` does not.

After `markLive(root)`, `cmdAbort(root, ["--role", "coverage,ghost"])` fails with stderr matching `/unknown role: ghost/`, and `abortRequestPath(root, "coverage")` does not exist. `["--role", ","]` fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.

### Fast merge, part 14/14: Roles listed in `review.afterMerge` merge once the gate passes and are reviewed after merging (planned 2026-10-19 by user; requires parts 4c/14 and 6/14 landed; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 7: maintenance roles reviewed after merging"; touches src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/review/review.ts src/merge/merge-verify.ts src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/merge/merge-core.ts tumwater.json docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** clean, dedupe and coverage merge many small code changes, and each one waits for a review before it can merge. For those roles a review after the merge, with the power to revert, keeps the quality bar at a fraction of the wait.

**Approach.**
- Config: `review.afterMerge?: string[]` of base role ids (src/config/config-schema.ts; validated in src/config/config-validation.ts as known role ids, never `director`).
- Verify (src/merge/merge-verify.ts): for a listed role, the deterministic rejects and the gate still run, and the reviewer is skipped, so the change goes on to merge.
- After the merge:
  - Record a post-merge review for the merged commit C in `.tumwater/state/post-review.json`. The verify drain runs it at `VERIFY_TIER` when permits allow, with the usual reviewer prompt over `git diff C^ C`.
  - An approval ends it. `review_verdict` and `review_rejected` carry `afterMerge: true`.
  - A rejection reverts C through part 4b/14's revert task and hands it back through part 4c/14 as a revision with the reviewer's reasons.
  - A revert that conflicts leaves C on main and sends the reasons to the role's inbox (`enqueueRolePrompt`).
- tumwater.json: `"afterMerge": ["clean", "dedupe", "coverage"]`.
- docs/config.md (the `review` row) and docs/how-it-works.md.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/review/review.ts, src/merge/merge-verify.ts, src/merge/merge-drain.ts, src/merge/merge-core.ts.
- Config and docs: tumwater.json, docs/config.md, docs/how-it-works.md.
- Tests: the config validation tests, plus a merge test with a fake reviewer.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A listed role's change merges with no `review_start` before its `merged` event. An `afterMerge` review follows it.
- A rejecting post-merge review puts a revert commit on main and gives the role's runner a revision with the reviewer's reasons.
- An unlisted role is reviewed before merging, as today.
- `npm test` passes.

**What changed.** `review.afterMerge` is validated in src/config/config-validation.ts. The gate (src/review/review.ts) returns `approved` for a listed role once its pre-check passes, with no reviewer run. The merge drain (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) records each merged commit in `post-review.json` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts); src/merge/merge-post-review.ts runs the review and starts the revert through `runMainRevert`, which takes the reviewer's reasons in `MainCulprit.postReview` and an `onFailed` callback that sends them to the role's inbox. src/merge/merge-core.ts needed no change; src/merge/merge-verify.ts only exports `resolveAuthor` for the post-review drain. A post-merge review is queued only when `review.enabled` is on and the merged diff is not exempt (`review.exemptPaths`), matching the pre-merge gate. tumwater.json is not edited by this run (roles never touch it): add `"afterMerge": ["clean", "dedupe", "coverage"]` under `review` there; tumwater.example.json is unchanged. Tests are in test/post-merge-review.test.ts.

### `tumwater start --once --role` takes a comma-separated list of role ids, so one scoped round runs exactly the roles an operator names (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — fast merge 14/14 edits the merge path, runner 9/14 touches src/status/ and src/scheduling/, the TUI History, wake and report entries touch other commands; this one touches src/cli/cli-args.ts, src/cli/cli-run.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/config/config-live.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `start --once --role <id>` scopes a once round to ONE role (`cmdRun`, src/cli/cli-run.ts, via `parseRoleFlag`). A missing or empty value, or no non-empty piece, fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`. Each piece is trimmed, goes through `canonicalRoleId`, and fails with `unknownRoleMessage(piece, ids)` when unknown. The result is deduplicated in first-seen order. `parseRoleListScope(root, args)` becomes `args.includes("--role") ? parseRoleListFlag(args, knownRoleIdsCached(root)) : null`, so it still reads no config without the flag. Update the comment above the parse ("names the one loop" → "names the runners that run"). `onceSummary`, `onceFailures` and the `roles:` banner already take the `roles` array.
- `src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts`: the `roleFilter` option becomes `roleFilter?: readonly string[]`. `const enabled = opts.roleFilter !== undefined ? [...opts.roleFilter] : runnerIds(config);`. Reword its doc comment from "this one role" to "these roles".

Keep the description column aligned. Update any test/help.test.ts regex that pins the old text: grep it for `--role <id>\] \[--gui` and `limits that round`.
- `docs/cli.md`: the `start --once` row's `add --role <id> to scope the round to one role` becomes `add --role <id>[,<id>...] to scope the round to the listed roles`.

### `tumwater report --role` takes a comma-separated list of role ids, so one usage report or failure digest covers every role an operator is comparing (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — fast merge 14/14 edits the merge path, runner 9/14 status data and scheduling, the TUI Ctrl+Y entry src/ui/tui, and the wake entry src/operator plus the wake/reset-counters help lines and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row; none of them is src/report, src/failure/failure-data.ts or the report stanza of src/cli/help.ts, and this edits docs/cli.md's Audit row only; the blocked plain-terms parts reach src/report only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/report/report.ts src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/failure/failure-data.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/report.test.ts test/help.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `history --role` takes a comma list (`parseRoleListScope`, src/cli/cli-args.ts), and the pause/resume/wake work does the same for the operator commands. `report --role` still takes one id: `tumwater report --role clean,dedupe` fails with `unknown role: clean,dedupe`, so an operator comparing the maintenance roles' spend against their output runs one report per role and adds the numbers by hand. Accept the comma list on every report shape: the day report, `--since`, and `--failures` (day and `--since`).

**Approach.**
- `src/report/report.ts` `cmdReport`: replace `parseRoleScope(root, args)` with `parseRoleListScope(root, args)`. It already validates each piece, canonicalizes, deduplicates in first-seen order and fails `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR` on an empty list. Pass `roles ?? undefined` to the four collectors. Update the import and the `--role` comment.
- `src/report/report-fold.ts`:
  - Add an exported `scopeBases(role: string | readonly string[] | undefined): string[] | undefined`. It maps undefined and an empty array to undefined (the team report). Otherwise it maps each id through `baseRoleOf`, deduplicated in first-seen order, so `feature-2,feature` is one base.
  - Widen `roleSum(record, role)` to `roleSum(record, bases: string | readonly string[])`. It sums every key whose `baseRoleOf` is one of the bases. A single string behaves as today.
  - Widen `narrowToRole` the same way. It returns one entry per base with a nonzero `roleSum`, keyed by that base, and keeps the zero-means-absent rule.
  - Widen `scopedByRole(record, base)` to take `readonly string[] | undefined`.
  - Update the three doc comments: "one base role" becomes "the scoped base roles".
- `src/report/report-data.ts`:
  - `collectReport` and `collectReportSince` widen `role?: string` to `role?: string | readonly string[]`. Each computes `const bases = scopeBases(role)` once, and every `base === undefined` test becomes `bases === undefined`. The `roleSum`/`narrowToRole`/`scopedByRole` calls take `bases`.
  - The day branch's work/maintenance split no longer uses `commitTier(base)` on one base. `workCommits` sums `roleSum(fold.commitsByRole, b)` over the bases whose `commitTier(b)` is `"work"`, and `maintenanceCommits` sums those whose tier is `"maintenance"`. With one base this gives the same numbers as today.
  - The output's `role` field stays a string: `bases.join(",")`. The JSON shape does not change, a single-role report keeps the same `role` value, and the render's `role: <id>` header line prints `role: clean,dedupe`. Update the `role?: string` field comments on `ReportData` and `SinceReport` to say this.
  - The callers that pass one string keep compiling unchanged: `reportScope`'s `/api/report` path in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts and `scope` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts. Do not edit them.
- `src/failure/failure-data.ts`:
  - `collectFailureReport`, `collectFailureReportSince` and the shared collector they call take `role?: string | readonly string[]` and compute `bases` through `scopeBases`.
  - `scopeToRole(events, base)` becomes `scopeToRole(events, bases: readonly string[])` and tests membership with `includes`.
  - The memo key uses `bases?.join(",") ?? ""`.
  - The output `role` is `bases.join(",")`, as in the usage report.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the report usage lines become `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. In the three descriptions, "--role <id> scopes … to one role's" becomes "--role <id>[,<id>...] scopes … to the listed roles'". Update the `help.test.ts` regexes that pin the old usage lines (`report --failures [--days N] [--since <duration>] [--role <id>] [--json]` and the `--failures --since` one) in the same change.
- `docs/cli.md`, Audit row: `tumwater report --role <id>` (scopes … to one role's …) becomes `tumwater report --role <id>[,<id>...]` (scopes … to the listed roles' …, summed; the by-role lines keep one entry per listed role).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New case in `test/report.test.ts`, "report --role takes a comma list and sums the listed roles". It uses `writeEvents` with `run_end` events (tokens/cost) for `clean`, `dedupe` and `feature`:
  - `report --role clean,dedupe --json` (day report) has `role` `"clean,dedupe"`. Its days' `runsByRole`/`costByRole` hold exactly the `clean` and `dedupe` keys, and their `tokensOut`/`costUsd` equal the two roles' sum, with `feature` absent.
  - The `--since 6h` form behaves the same: `totals.runs` is the two roles' run count, and the render prints `role: clean,dedupe`.
  - `report --role dedupe,clean,dedupe --json` dedupes, giving `role` `"dedupe,clean"`.
- New case: `report --failures --role clean,dedupe --json` scopes the digest to both roles: `role` is `"clean,dedupe"`, and no row names `feature`.
- New case: `report --role clean,ghost` exits nonzero with `unknown role: ghost`, and `report --role ,` exits nonzero with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.
- The existing single-role cases keep passing unchanged, among them "report --since narrows Revisions by role to the scoped base role" and "report --since folds failed ticks by role and narrows to the scoped base role".
- `tumwater help report` shows `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater wake --role` and `reset-counters --role` take a comma-separated list of role ids, the twin of `pause --role clean,dedupe` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it touches only `targetRoles` and its callers in src/operator/operator-commands.ts, help and docs) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `pause --role` and `resume --role` take a comma list (`pauseTargetRoles`, src/operator/operator-commands.ts), and so do `history`/`logs` (`parseRoleListScope`, src/cli/cli-args.ts). `wake --role` and `reset-counters --role` still take one id: an operator who held `clean,dedupe,organize` and resumed them must wake each one with its own command. `wake --role clean,dedupe` fails today with `unknown role: clean,dedupe`. The writers `requestWake(root, roles, inMs)` and `requestResetCounters(root, roles)` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts) already take a role array. Only the flag parsing is missing.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`:
  - Add `namedRoleList(root, args): string[] | null`. It returns null when `flagValue(args, "--role")` is null. Otherwise it splits the value on `,`, trims each piece and drops empty pieces. When none remain (bare `--role`, `--role ""`, `--role ,`), it calls `fail(ROLE_VALUE_ERROR)`. Each piece resolves through `namedRole(root, ["--role", piece])`, so built-ins skip the config read and an unknown id fails with the existing `unknown role: <id> (valid ids: …)` message. The result is deduplicated in first-seen order. Every piece resolves before the caller writes anything.
  - `pauseTargetRoles` keeps its instance-1 exception (`feature-1` kept verbatim). It is rewritten to share the split/empty/dedupe steps with `namedRoleList`: extract one small private splitter that both call, `rolePieces(args): string[] | null`. Behaviour of pause/resume is unchanged.
  - `targetRoles(root, args)` becomes `namedRoleList(root, args) ?? Object.keys(loadConfig(root).roles)`. This makes `cmdResetCounters` and `cmdWake` (both the immediate and the `--in` scheduled path) accept the list with no other change.
  - `wake --cancel` and `wake --list` keep one role: `cancelWakes`/`listWakes`/`renderWakeList` take `role?: string`, and widening them is not needed for this change. Before the `namedRole` call in each branch, a `--role` value containing `,` fails with `wake --cancel and --list take one --role id`. This replaces the misleading `unknown role: clean,dedupe`.
  - Update the doc comments of `targetRoles`, `cmdResetCounters` and `cmdWake` to name the comma list.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the usage lines become `tumwater reset-counters [--role <id>[,<id>...]]` and `tumwater wake [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--in <dur> | --cancel | --list [--json]]`. Keep the description column aligned, with the `pause` stanza as the model.
- `docs/cli.md`, "Control the roles" row: `tumwater reset-counters [--role <id>]` becomes `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. The `tumwater wake` clause gains `wake --role clean,dedupe` wakes each listed role, the same as one command per role.
- The TUI, the GUI endpoints (`/api/wake`, `/api/reset-counters`) and the intent writers do not change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New case in `test/operator-commands.test.ts`, "cmdWake and cmdResetCounters --role take a comma list":
  - Seed `clean` and `dedupe` with backoff and counters, and leave `organize` as is.
  - `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean, dedupe,clean"])` prints `wake requested for clean, dedupe`, clears both backoffs and leaves `organize`'s state unchanged. `wakeRequestPath`'s `roles` reads `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
  - `cmdResetCounters(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe"])` prints `counters reset for clean, dedupe`, zeroes both, and `resetRequestPath`'s `roles` reads `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
- New case: `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe", "--in", "45m"])` writes one scheduled-wake file whose `roles` is `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
- New case "wake and reset-counters: a comma list with an unknown id writes no marker":
  - `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean,ghost"])` fails with `unknown role: ghost`. Neither `wakeRequestPath` nor `clean`'s state changes.
  - `cmdResetCounters` behaves the same way.
  - `["--role", ","]` fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.
- New case: `cmdWake(root, ["--cancel", "--role", "clean,dedupe"])` and `["--list", "--role", "clean,dedupe"]` fail with `wake --cancel and --list take one --role id`.
- These cases keep passing unchanged:
  - in `test/cli-operators-team.test.ts`: "reset-counters --role targets one loop; unknown or missing role fails without side effects" and "wake --role targets one loop; …";
  - in `test/operator-commands.test.ts`: "cmdPause and cmdResume --role take a comma list" and "a comma list with an unknown id writes no marker".
- `tumwater help wake` shows `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI History pane's `Ctrl+Y` cycles role summary → model summary → rows, the terminal twin of `tumwater history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the dashboard By-model entry edits src/gui and src/ui/gui, the pause/resume entry src/operator, the help lines and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row, fast-merge part 14/14 src/config, src/review and src/merge, and runner part 8/14 src/orchestrator, none of which is src/ui/tui; it shares docs/cli.md's "Watch run history" row with the dashboard By-model entry (a rebase: edit whichever wording is on main); the blocked plain-terms series renames identifiers in src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` tallies runs per model (`summarizeTickRowsByModel` in src/history/history-data.ts, rendered by `renderModelSummary` in src/history/history-render.ts). The TUI History pane's `Ctrl+Y`, though, only flips between the run rows and the per-role table (`renderSummary`). So an operator watching a mixed-provider team in the terminal cannot see what each model merged or cost. This plan makes `Ctrl+Y` a three-step cycle: rows → per-role summary → per-model summary → rows. The model table is folded over the same rows the pane's window, role, result and search already selected. Out of scope: the dashboard (its own Planned entry), and any new key.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`:
  - Session state: `let historySummary = false;` becomes `let historySummary: HistorySummaryGroup | null = null;`. Here `type HistorySummaryGroup = (typeof HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS)[number]`, imported from src/history/history-data.ts (`["role", "model"]`). Export the type from there if it is not already exported. `null` means the row list. Update the comment above it.
  - `historyPaneCache`'s `summary: boolean` parameter becomes `summary: HistorySummaryGroup | null`. The body becomes: `"role"` with rows present → `renderSummary(summarizeTickRows(filtered))`; `"model"` with rows present → `renderModelSummary(summarizeTickRowsByModel(filtered))`; otherwise `historyPaneText(filtered)`. Keep the non-empty guard and its comment. Import both new helpers alongside the existing ones.
  - The `Ctrl+Y` arm: replace `historySummary = !historySummary` with the cycle `null → "role" → "model" → null`. Write it inline as `historySummary = historySummary === null ? "role" : historySummary === "role" ? "model" : null;`. Keep the `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` guard, `recompute()` and `requestRender()`. Update the comment to name the three steps.
  - `state()` returns `historySummary` unchanged by name, now with the new type.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`: in the state interface, `historySummary: boolean` becomes `historySummary: "role" | "model" | null`, or the imported `HistorySummaryGroup | null`. Update the doc comment to name the cycle. `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` and `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx` pass the value through unchanged and need no edit beyond what the compiler asks.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`: the history view kind's `summary?: boolean` becomes `summary?: "role" | "model" | null`. The hint token `["Ctrl+Y", view.summary ? "rows" : "summary"]` names the next step: `!view.summary` → `"summary"`, `"role"` → `"by model"`, `"model"` → `"rows"`.
- `docs/cli.md`:
  - TUI-keys table, `Ctrl+Y` row: "on History, toggle the per-role Summary table" becomes "on History, cycle the per-role Summary table, the per-model table (`history --summary --by model`), and the run rows".
  - "Watch run history" row: the clause "the TUI's History pane shows the same per-role summary with `Ctrl+Y`" also names the per-model table, as the second `Ctrl+Y` press.
  - `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` compares only the set of Ctrl letters, so it needs no change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/tui-keys.test.ts`:
  - The existing case "Ctrl+Y toggles the History pane between the run rows and the per-role Summary table" is renamed to say "cycles", and its assertions are updated: `historySummary` is `null` on entry and `"role"` after one `Ctrl+Y`, with the same per-role table assertions. The fixture gains `run_start` events with `model: "m-a"` for feature #1 and `model: "m-b"` for qa #1. A second `Ctrl+Y` gives `"model"`, and the pane's first line matches `/model/`, `/runs/` and `/cost/`. The pane has lines starting `m-a` and `m-b` and a `total` line, and no `#1`. A third `Ctrl+Y` gives `null` and restores `feature #1`.
  - A `run_end` with no `run_start` shows as `(unknown)` in the model table.
  - The budget-mode-inert and Activity-vs-History `Ctrl+Y` cases keep passing, with their `true`/`false` expectations updated to `"role"`/`null`.
- `test/tui-frame.test.ts`: the hint assertions cover all three states: `summary: null` → `Ctrl+Y summary`, `"role"` → `Ctrl+Y by model`, `"model"` → `Ctrl+Y rows`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard History view gains a "By model" summary mode, the twin of `tumwater history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — none of them names src/gui, src/ui/gui, src/history or the history row of docs/cli.md; the blocked plain-terms parts that rename symbols in src/history mean a rebase at most; touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts docs/cli.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` (`summarizeTickRowsByModel`, src/history/history-data.ts) tallies runs per model, but its plan scoped the dashboard out. So the History view's Summary toggle can only group by role, and an operator watching a mixed-provider team in the browser cannot see what each model merged or cost. This plan adds a third mode, "By model", next to Table and Summary. It shows one row per model with the same columns, `(unknown)` for the null bucket, then the total. Out of scope: the TUI History pane (`Ctrl+Y` keeps the per-role table).

**Approach.**
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts`, `handleHistory`: in both arms (the `sinceMs` window and the `n` count), when `summary` is present, add an additive `modelSummary: summarizeTickRowsByModel(<the served rows>)` beside `summary`. Use the same rows that `summary` folds: `matched` in the window arm, the grep-filtered `rows` in the count arm. Import `summarizeTickRowsByModel` from src/history/history-data.ts. Without `summary` the response keeps today's shape, with no `modelSummary` key. Extend the doc comment's `summary` sentence to say that it also adds `modelSummary`, `{ models, total }`, the `history --summary --by model` tally of the same rows. Do not add a new query parameter: one fetch carries both, so switching modes never refetches, as Summary already doesn't.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts`:
  - State: add `let histModelSummary = null;` beside `histSummary`. The mode restore becomes `const m = recall("hist-mode"); let histMode = m === "summary" || m === "models" ? m : "table";`.
  - `HIST_MODES` becomes `[["table", "Table"], ["summary", "Summary"], ["models", "By model"]]`. The toolbar's `histsum` segment and its click handler (`store("hist-mode", histMode)`) need no other change.
  - `fetchHistory`: beside the `histSummary = …` line, set `histModelSummary = d && d.modelSummary && Array.isArray(d.modelSummary.models) ? d.modelSummary : null;`. A server too old to send it leaves the value null.
  - Inside the `// history-summary:start` … `:end` block, factor the table out of `histSummaryHtml` into `summaryTableHtml(header, entries)`. Here `entries` is `[{ label, row, total }]`. The function keeps the existing cells, the `hist-total` class on the total row, and the `<th>` header text, with the first `<th>` replaced by `header`. `histSummaryHtml(summary)` maps roles to `{ label: roleLabel(r.role), row: r }` and appends `{ label: "total", row: summary.total, total: true }`, so its HTML stays the same for the same input. Add `histModelSummaryHtml(summary)`, which maps `summary.models` to `{ label: r.model === null ? "(unknown)" : r.model, row: r }`, then the total, under the header `Model`. Labels go through `esc`, as today.
  - `renderHistory`: hide `histfilter` when `histMode !== "table"`. Pick the body as follows: in `"summary"` mode with `histSummary` and rows present, `histSummaryHtml`; in `"models"` mode with `histModelSummary` and rows present, `histModelSummaryHtml`; otherwise the table. The fallback is the same one an empty or too-old response gets today. Update the comment there to name both modes.
- `docs/cli.md`, the "Watch run history" row: after "the TUI's History pane shows the same per-role summary with `Ctrl+Y`", add "; the dashboard's History view has Summary and By model modes for the two groupings".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`, new case "handleHistory ?summary also folds the served rows per model". Seed `run_start` events carrying `model` (two models) with their `run_end`s, plus one `run_end` with no start. Assert that `modelSummary` deep-equals `summarizeTickRowsByModel(rows)` of the served rows, in both the `?n=50&summary=1` and the `?sinceMs=3600000&summary=1` arm. Assert that the null bucket is last with `model: null`, and that `?n=50` without the flag has no `modelSummary` key. The existing "handleHistory ?summary folds the served rows into an additive per-role summary" case passes unchanged.
- `test/gui-client-history.test.ts`:
  - The `HIST_MODES` regex assertion is updated to the three-mode literal.
  - A new case loads the `history-summary` block via `clientScope` (as the existing `histSummaryHtml` case does). It asserts that `histModelSummaryHtml` renders a `Model` header, one row per model, `(unknown)` for `model: null`, an escaped `<` in a model id, and a `hist-total` row.
  - The existing `histSummaryHtml` case passes unchanged.
  - The "fetchHistory rides the server summary…" pattern is extended (or copied) with `recall("hist-mode")` returning `"models"` and a response carrying `modelSummary`. It asserts that `histMode` restores as `"models"` and that the fetched `modelSummary` is kept.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 8/14: Convert the orchestrator and its tests (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 7/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/orchestrator/ + test/orchestrator*.test.ts + test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The orchestrator and its unit and e2e tests use `RoleRunner`, `RunnerState` and runner/role wording.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, orchestrator-poll.ts, orchestrator-scheduling.ts, orchestrator-launch.ts and retention.ts: migrate `LoopRunner` → `RoleRunner`, `loopEnabled` → `runnerEnabled`, `loopIds` → `runnerIds`, `saveLoopState` → `saveRunnerState` and `LoopState` → `RunnerState`, and convert comments ("the LoopRunners above" → "the RoleRunners above"). The poll loop stays the poll loop.
- Tests: every test/orchestrator*.test.ts and test/orchestrator*.e2e.test.ts (`loadLoopState` alone is about 170 lines here), plus test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts. Rename test locals per the series rules; test/orchestrator-2.e2e.test.ts's `loopOrder` → `roleOrder`.
- Locals such as `dryTicks` and `dryFailedAt` carry role-id and tick words, which belong to later series; leave them.

- `grep -rnwiE 'loops?'` over the same files lists only the poll loop and other kept senses.
