### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's model (`model`) with Ctrl+A, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Model` field and `tumwater config set model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the plan-rerun entry edits src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling, src/orchestrator and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, the queue-order entry src/roles and src/prompt, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; the in-flight run-cap (Ctrl+N), worktree-slots (Ctrl+W) and provider-caps (Ctrl+P) entries — plus the landed quiet-hours (Ctrl+S) editor — also edit src/ui/tui and share src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx and tui-frame.ts with this one — each adds one editor module, one held flag, one state field and one frame branch — and share docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table as different rows, a rebase either way; when those concurrency entries have landed, this plan's `onArrow` no-editor condition and its new `heldEditorFlash` clause include their `concurrency`/`slots`/`providerCaps` flags, as noted below; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-model.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-model.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts)

**Goal.** The team's model — the top-level `model` key, a selector string or a map by tier (`small`/`default`/`strong`), validated by `checkModelTripleField` (`src/config/config-field-checks.ts`) and the `checkSelectorHalves`/per-entry `checkSelectorValue` block in `validateConfig` (`src/config/config-validation.ts`; the scalar shape message is `model must be a model id or a map by tier (small, default, strong)`, verified at `config-field-checks.ts`) — is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Model`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose field renders an object as compact JSON through `settingsFieldValue`) and `tumwater config set model '{"strong":"..."}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: no `tui-editor-model.ts` exists and no TUI editor writes the top-level `model` (the `model` occurrences under `src/ui/tui` are the History pane's per-run model cell in `tui-history.ts` and "model-written text" comments in `tui-frame.ts`/`tui.tsx`). The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`) and its quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`, `createQuietEditor`), and its run cap, worktree slots and provider caps once the in-flight Ctrl+N/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+P entries land. `model` is the most fundamental of the dashboard Settings rows still without a TUI twin (the others are `provider`, `fallback`, `notify` and `backends`), so add it beside the rest. `Ctrl+A` is free on the Activity view: the answer editor's `Ctrl+A` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-answer.ts`) is guarded to a selected open backlog question, the pause editor's per-loop abort `Ctrl+A` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`, guarded by `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length`) is a role's Transcript, and `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`), so the new arm must enter only on `ctx.view === 0` and return false everywhere else. `Ctrl+M` is deliberately not used: ink's key bridge maps `key.return` before `key.ctrl` (`src/ui/tui/tui-keymap.ts`), so Ctrl+M arrives as the `return` key and cannot be told from Enter.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-model.ts** (new) — `createModelEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring the team half of `createQuietEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts) but with no role scope: a private `modelMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitModelMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.model` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "a"`: enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (a role's Transcript keeps `Ctrl+A` for abort, Backlog keeps it for answer), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("model")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `modelMode` and `session.held.model`, pre-fill from one fresh `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.model` — a string as-is, an object as `JSON.stringify(...)`, `""` when unset — place the cursor at the end, and flash `edit the team's model (model, a model id or a JSON map by tier like {"strong":"..."}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "model")` and, on `ok`, flashes `team model cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "model", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `team model set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a bare `huggingface/...` becomes the literal selector string, while `{"strong":"..."}` becomes the map), and `validateConfig` owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitModelMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitModelMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the quiet and budget editors do; import no `baseRoleOf` (the team key owns no role).
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `model: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+A team-model editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"model"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. Extend the guard body with the two clauses the existing per-editor entries use: first, beside `h.quiet && entering !== "quiet"`, add `if (h.model && entering !== "model") return session.busyFlash("model edit");`, which covers entering any other editor while the model editor holds the line; second, beside the existing `entering === "instructions"` clause, add an `entering === "model"` clause that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions` is set (naming that editor's subject, the same nested-ternary wording those clauses use). The second clause is required, not redundant: the guard body has no generic `h.budget && entering !== "budget"` early clause, so entering a value the bottom clauses do not list while the budget editor holds the shared line would otherwise let the new editor overwrite it. If the in-flight Ctrl+N/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+P concurrency entries have landed, add their `concurrency`/`slots`/`providerCaps` flags to this plan's `entering === "model"` subject list exactly as they extend each other's, and add their flags to this plan's `onArrow` list below.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `modelMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createModelEditor` and add `createModelEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createBudgetEditor(session)`; return `modelMode: session.held.model` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.model` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.budget`), adding `!session.held.concurrency`/`!session.held.slots`/`!session.held.providerCaps` there too if those in-flight entries have landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `modelMode: s.modelMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `modelMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "model", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.modelMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.modelMode) keys = [["Enter", "save the model"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+A", "model"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table gains a `| Ctrl+A | Activity | edit the team's model (`model`, a model id or a JSON map by tier like `{"strong":"..."}`; empty clears it) |` row, one row per (key, view), distinct from the Transcript `Ctrl+A` (abort an in-flight run) and Backlog `Ctrl+A` (answer the selected question) inside the existing `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+V` and backlog rows.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-model.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+A opens with the footer `model ›` and the line pre-filled from `tumwater.json`'s `model` (the bare string when it is a string, compact JSON when it is a map, empty when unset); Enter on a selector string writes that string to `tumwater.json` and flashes `team model set to <text>`; Enter on a JSON tier map writes the object; Enter on the number `42` flashes the validator's `model must be a model id or a map by tier (small, default, strong)` message, leaves the editor open with the text kept and the file byte-identical; Enter on an empty line unsets the key (it disappears from the file) and flashes `team model cleared`, leaving the file bytes unchanged when it was already absent; Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with another editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+A flashes the busy message and leaves it open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+A on Activity opens the model editor (`session.held.model`, and `session.held.budget` stays false); on a role's Transcript, Ctrl+A still aborts that role's run (the existing per-loop control, unaffected because the new arm returns false off view 0); and the existing "Ctrl+E is inert in the prompt-line modes and off the report views only moves the label" test stays green unchanged (this plan binds Ctrl+A, not Ctrl+E).
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, modelMode: true })` reading `model ›` and the hint branch's `save the model`; and the Activity hint line naming `Ctrl+A model`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+A opens the editor; the footer reads `model › `, the line pre-fills the file's `model` (a bare string as-is, a map as compact JSON, empty when unset) and the open flash names `model`, the model-id-or-tier-map shape and the empty-clears rule. On a role's Transcript, Ctrl+A still aborts the in-flight run; on Backlog with a question selected, Ctrl+A still opens the answer editor.
- Enter with a selector string or a JSON tier map writes `model` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `team model set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `team model cleared`; a number (e.g. `42`) flashes the validator's `model must be a model id or a map by tier (small, default, strong)` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line, and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, modelMode: true })` reads `model › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s model branch names `save the model`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+A model`.
- `test/tui-keys.test.ts`'s existing Ctrl+E report-window test is unchanged and still passes (this plan does not bind Ctrl+E).
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+A | Activity` row naming the team model and `model`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm test` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 4/14: Rename the status model's role phase and rank (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/status-model.ts + src/ui/tone.ts + src/ui/badges.ts + test/status-model.test.ts + test/badges.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The shared display model names what it describes, a role's row: `rolePhase`, `roleRank`, `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortRolesByState`, `roleRowCells` and `roleWakeMarker`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/ui/status-model.ts: `loopPhase` → `rolePhase`, `loopRank` → `roleRank`, `LOOP_RANK_RULES` → `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortLoopsByState` → `sortRolesByState`, `LoopSortRow` → `RoleSortRow`, `loopRowCells` → `roleRowCells`. Each export used outside this part keeps an alias: `loopPhase` is named in src/merge/, src/runner/, src/tick/, src/ui/ and src/ui/gui/; `LOOP_RANK_RULES` is interpolated by src/ui/gui/gui-client-model.ts.
- src/ui/badges.ts: `loopWakeMarker` → `roleWakeMarker` (alias; src/ui/status-render.ts uses it). src/ui/tone.ts: migrate its `loopRank` import and comments.
- test/status-model.test.ts (about 130 `loopPhase` calls and 69 `freshLoopState` calls) and test/badges.test.ts: migrate to the new names, including `freshRunnerState`, and convert comments and test titles.
- The browser twin of the rank (`loopRank` inside gui-client-model.ts's template) is part 7/14's; only the server export's name changes here.

**Files touched.** src/ui/status-model.ts, src/ui/tone.ts, src/ui/badges.ts, test/status-model.test.ts, test/badges.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `rolePhase`, `roleRank`, `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortRolesByState`, `roleRowCells` and `roleWakeMarker` are the declared names; old names exist only as deprecated aliases, and only while another file still uses them.
- `grep -nE '[Ll]oop[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Loop|LOOP_|\bloops?\b'` over this part's five files lists only aliases and kept senses.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

**Note.** Also migrated this part's use of part 2/14's earlier rename inside status-model.ts: its nine `LoopState` type references became `RunnerState` (the deprecated `LoopState` alias still has live users in src/runner, e.g. `freshlyWoken(s: LoopState)`). Comment cross-references to the GUI page's browser twin (`sortLoops`, `loopRank`, the loop-list) were reworded to neutral phrasing; gui-client-model.ts and the other GUI files are untouched (parts 7-9 own them).

### The TUI's Transcript view edits the viewed role's model override (`roles.<base>.model`) with Ctrl+X, the terminal twin of `tumwater role <id> --model` and the dashboard role drawer's Model overrides editor (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 3/14 moves src/runner and its tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight TUI editors (run cap Ctrl+N, worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, notify Ctrl+E, backends Ctrl+X) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-role-model.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A role's model override (`roles.<base>.model`, resolved per tier by `configForRole` in `src/config/config-views.ts` and printed by `tumwater role <id>` as its `Model:` line, `src/roles/role-render.ts`) is writable from two surfaces: the CLI (`tumwater role <id> --model <id>` / `--clear-model`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`) and the dashboard role drawer's Model overrides editor (`POST /api/role-model` → `handleRoleModel`, `src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts`), both through `setRoleModelFields(root, base, { model })` (`src/config/config-write.ts`), whose `checkModelTripleField` (shape `"tier-name"`, `src/config/config-field-checks.ts`) accepts a non-empty model id or a bare tier name (`small`/`default`/`strong`) and owns the `roles.<id>.model …` rejection messages. The TUI cannot: no `tui-editor-role-model.ts` exists and `grep -rn model src/ui/tui` finds no per-role write (the `model` hits are the History pane's per-run cell and the team-wide editors). The Transcript view already edits the sibling per-role holds — daily cap Ctrl+B, quiet hours Ctrl+O, min run interval Ctrl+S, standing instructions Ctrl+L, notes Ctrl+E, counters Ctrl+V — so add the last per-role override beside them. `Ctrl+X` is free on the Transcript view: the transcript pane consumes it only in notes mode (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts`'s `noteMode` arm, which clears notes), the backlog cancel and Health retire arms are guarded to their own views, and the editors run before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`), so the new arm enters only when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length && !ctx.noteMode` and returns false everywhere else. (`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+L`/`Ctrl+E`/`Ctrl+X` are the in-flight team editors' keys on Activity; the view guards keep them disjoint.)

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts** (new) — `createRoleModelEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring `createIntervalEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-interval.ts`): a private `roleModelMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitRoleModelMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.roleModel` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "x"`. Enter only when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length && !ctx.noteMode` (notes mode keeps Ctrl+X for clear-notes; every other view falls through unchanged), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("roleModel")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, pin `lockedRole = ctx.roleIds[ctx.view - 1]!` so a roster shift cannot redirect the write, set `roleModelMode` and `session.held.roleModel`, pre-fill from `rawRoleField(session.root, baseRoleOf(lockedRole), "model")` (a string as-is, `""` when unset — the FILE's own override, so clearing a role that only has the catalog's tier never looks like an operator override), place the cursor at the end, and flash `edit ${lockedRole}'s model override (a model id or tier name like strong; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `setRoleModelFields(session.root, baseRoleOf(lockedRole), { model: "" })` and, on `ok`, flashes `${lockedRole}: model override cleared`; otherwise `setRoleModelFields(session.root, baseRoleOf(lockedRole), { model: session.input.trim() })` and, on `ok`, flashes `${lockedRole}: model override set to ${text}`; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitRoleModelMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitRoleModelMode }`. Import `setRoleModelFields` from `../../config/config-write.js`, `baseRoleOf` from `../../roles/runner-ids.js`, and `rawRoleField` from `../../roles/role-view.js` — the shared write the CLI's `--model` and the dashboard's `handleRoleModel` use, not a hand-rolled `setConfigKey`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `roleModel: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Transcript view's Ctrl+X role-model editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"roleModel"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. Add, beside the sibling early clauses, `if (h.roleModel && entering !== "roleModel") return session.busyFlash("role model edit");`, and add an `entering === "roleModel"` clause at the bottom that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the interval/instructions clauses use; the early clause above does not cover `budget` because `budget` has no early `!== entering` clause). If the in-flight `model`/`fallback`/`notify`/`backends` flags have landed, name them in the same clause.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `roleModelMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState`; import `createRoleModelEditor` and add `createRoleModelEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createIntervalEditor(session)`; return `roleModelMode: session.held.roleModel` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.roleModel` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.interval`), adding any in-flight flags present there too.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `roleModelMode: s.roleModelMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `roleModelMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "role model", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.roleModelMode`, placed with the existing interval/instructions prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.roleModelMode) keys = [["Enter", "save role model"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside those branches; and the `view.kind === "transcript"` key list gains `["Ctrl+X", "role model"]` beside the other per-role editors.
- **docs/cli.md** — in the `## TUI keys` table add a distinct `Ctrl+X | Transcript | edit the viewed role's model override (roles.<base>.model, a model id or tier name; empty clears it)` row (the Health retire, Backlog cancel, Inbox cancel and notes-clear rows stay as they are), and in the `tumwater role <id>`/Configure sentence extend the TUI clause that already names the Transcript Ctrl+O/Ctrl+L editors with the Ctrl+X model editor.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-role-model.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default (only) role's Transcript: Ctrl+X opens with the footer `role model ›` and the line empty when `tumwater.json` leaves `roles.<role>.model` unset, and pre-filled when it holds one; Enter on a model id persists it to `roles.<role>.model` and flashes `model override set to <text>`; re-entering pre-fills the just-saved value; Enter on a tier name (`strong`) writes that literal; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key and flashes `model override cleared`, leaving the file bytes unchanged when it was already absent; a draft prompt typed before opening is restored byte-for-byte on Esc and on Ctrl+T; with the budget editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+X flashes the busy message and leaves the budget editor open. The instance→base mapping is pinned at the unit level rather than by the fixture (see `test/tui-keys.test.ts`).
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+X on a role's Transcript opens `session.state().roleModelMode`; with the notes view up (`Ctrl+N` once), Ctrl+X still clears notes (two presses) and does not set `roleModelMode`; on Backlog Ctrl+X still arms/starts the entry cancel; on Health it still opens the retire editor. If the test's `ctx.roleIds` can hold an instance id, pin that an instance id writes its base role's key.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, roleModelMode: true })` reading `role model › ` and the hint branch's `save role model`; and the Transcript hint line naming `Ctrl+X role model`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On a role's Transcript view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+X opens the editor; the footer reads `role model › `, the line pre-fills the FILE's `roles.<base>.model` (empty when unset) and the open flash names the role and the model-id/tier shape. In the notes view Ctrl+X keeps clearing notes, and on Backlog/Health it keeps its existing meaning (the new arm returns false off a Transcript and in notes mode).
- Enter writes `roles.<base>.model` through `setRoleModelFields` and flashes `model override set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the override and flashes `model override cleared`; clearing an override the file never set leaves the file byte-identical.

### The TUI's Transcript view edits the viewed role's parallel-runner count (`roles.feature.instances` / `roles.bugfix.instances`) with Ctrl+G, the terminal twin of `tumwater role <id> --instances` and the dashboard role drawer's instance-count editor (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 3/14 moves src/runner and its tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight TUI editors (run cap Ctrl+N, worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, notify Ctrl+E, backends Ctrl+X, role model Ctrl+X) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instances.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-instances.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A role's parallel-runner count (`roles.<base>.instances`, resolved to the `feature-2`…`feature-N` loop ids) is writable from two surfaces: the CLI (`tumwater role <id> --instances <n>` / `--clear-instances`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, through `writeRoleConfigKey` → `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey`) and the dashboard role drawer's instance-count editor (`POST /api/role-instances` → `handleRoleInstances`, `src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts`), both through the shared `setConfigKey` dotted path so `validateConfig` owns the value's truth: `INSTANCE_COUNT` (`src/config/config-validation.ts`) requires an integer 1–8, and `INSTANCE_ROLES` (`src/roles/runner-ids.ts`, `feature` and `bugfix`) rejects an instances key under any other role. The TUI cannot: no `tui-editor-instances.ts` exists and `grep -rn instances src/ui/tui` finds no instance write. The Transcript view already edits the sibling per-role holds — daily cap Ctrl+B, quiet hours Ctrl+O, min run interval Ctrl+S, standing instructions Ctrl+L, notes Ctrl+E, counters Ctrl+V (and, once the in-flight entry lands, model Ctrl+X) — so add the parallel-runner count, the last per-role hold `tumwater role` and the drawer both write. `Ctrl+G` is free on a role's Transcript: the only pane arms for it are the Activity scope cycle (view 0), the History scope cycle (the History view) and the report scope cycle (`src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` routes Ctrl+G by view; `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts`'s arm is `promptLineFree`-guarded), and the prompt-line editors run before every pane arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`), so the new arm consumes Ctrl+G only when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` and returns false everywhere else; the report scope cycle stays reachable from Activity, History, Usage and Failures. `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` scans the code for handled Ctrl letters against docs/cli.md's table, and `Ctrl+G` is already documented, so no key-set change is needed — only the row's description gains the Transcript meaning.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instances.ts** (new) — `createInstancesEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring `createIntervalEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-interval.ts`): a private `instancesMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), and an `exitInstancesMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.instances`, clears the pinned role, and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`. `handleKey` opens on `key.ctrl && key.name === "g"` when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` (toggle out when already open; every other view returns false unchanged). On open: run `session.heldEditorFlash("instances")` and, when it names another editor, flash it and return true; otherwise run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, pin `lockedRole = ctx.roleIds[ctx.view - 1]!` so a roster shift cannot redirect the write, set `instancesMode` and `session.held.instances = true`, pre-fill `session.input` from `rawRoleField(session.root, baseRoleOf(lockedRole), "instances")` (`typeof existing === "number" ? String(existing) : ""` — the FILE's own entry, so a role that never set the key pre-fills empty), place the cursor at the end, and flash `` `edit ${lockedRole}'s parallel-runner count (an integer 1-8; feature and bugfix only; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel` ``. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm writes `roles.${baseRoleOf(lockedRole)}.instances`: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, cfgKey)` and, on `ok`, exits and flashes `${lockedRole}: instances cleared`; otherwise call `setConfigKey(session.root, cfgKey, session.input.trim())` (the same raw text the CLI passes) and, on `ok`, exit and flash `${lockedRole}: instances set to <value>`; on `{ok:false}` flash the returned error and STAY open, leaving the file untouched. There is no own range or role check: exactly as `handleRoleInstances` and the CLI document, `validateConfig`'s `INSTANCE_COUNT` and `INSTANCE_ROLES` own the bound and the feature/bugfix restriction, so `0`, `9`, `1.5`, `abc` and a non-instance role all surface that error and stay open (the clear path is a no-op success on a role the file never set). Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitInstancesMode }`. Import `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, `baseRoleOf` from `../../roles/runner-ids.js`, `rawRoleField` from `../../roles/role-view.js`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `instances: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface (documented as the Transcript view's Ctrl+G instance-count editor) and initialize it `false`; add `"instances"` to the `entering` union of `heldEditorFlash`. Add a sibling early clause `if (h.instances && entering !== "instances") return session.busyFlash("role instances");`, and a bottom `if (entering === "instances" && h.budget) return session.busyFlash("budget edit");` — `budget` is the only editor with no early `!== entering` clause, so the early clauses of every other editor catch entering them; if the in-flight editor flags have landed, name them in the same early clause set.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `instancesMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState`; import `createInstancesEditor` and add `createInstancesEditor(session)` to the `editors` array beside `createIntervalEditor(session)`; return `instancesMode: session.held.instances` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.instances` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition (beside `!session.held.interval`) so Up/Down cannot recall prompt history into the held field.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `instancesMode: s.instancesMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `instancesMode?: boolean` to the inline `mode` types of `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "instances", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.instancesMode`, beside the interval/instructions prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.instancesMode) keys = [["Enter", "save instances"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]`; and the `view.kind === "transcript"` key list gains `["Ctrl+G", "instances"]` beside the per-role holds.
- **docs/cli.md** — extend the `## TUI keys` table's `Ctrl+G` row so its `Where` cell names Transcript and its action text says that on a role's Transcript it edits the viewed role's parallel-runner count (`roles.<base>.instances`, an integer 1–8; only `feature` and `bugfix`; empty clears it), and extend the `tumwater role <id>` sentence's TUI clause (the one naming the Transcript Ctrl+O/Ctrl+L editors) with the Ctrl+G instance editor.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-instances.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with the existing fixtures (`makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` in `test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`) on a role's Transcript: Ctrl+G opens with the footer `instances ›` and the line pre-filled from the FILE (`roles.<role>.instances`) when set, empty when not; Enter on `3` persists `3` to `roles.<role>.instances` and flashes `instances set to 3`; re-entering pre-fills `3`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key and flashes `instances cleared`, leaving the file byte-identical when the key was already absent (compare file bytes before/after, as the sibling editor tests do); Enter on `0` and on `9` flashes the `validateConfig` error and stays open (the draft keeps the typed text); on a non-instance role's Transcript the same write is refused and stays open; a draft prompt typed before opening is restored byte-for-byte on Esc and on Ctrl+T; with the budget editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+G flashes the busy message and leaves the budget editor open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+G on a role's Transcript sets `state().instancesMode` and leaves `state().activityRole`/`state().historyRole` untouched; Ctrl+G on Activity still cycles `activityRole`; Ctrl+G on History still cycles `historyRole`; Ctrl+G on Usage/Failures still cycles the report scope; and if the fixture roster can carry an instance id, pin that an instance id writes its base role's key.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, instancesMode: true })` reading `instances › `, the `hintLine` `save instances` branch, and the Transcript hint naming `Ctrl+G`/`instances`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On a role's Transcript with a free prompt line, Ctrl+G opens the editor; the footer reads `instances › `, the line pre-fills the FILE's `roles.<base>.instances` (empty when unset), and the open flash names the role and the 1–8/feature-bugfix shape. On Activity, History, Usage and Failures Ctrl+G keeps its existing scope-cycle meaning (the new arm returns false off a role's Transcript).
- Enter writes `roles.<base>.instances` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `instances set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key via `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `instances cleared`; clearing a key the file never set leaves the file byte-identical. An instance id (e.g. `feature-2`) writes and pre-fills `roles.feature.instances` through `baseRoleOf`.
- `0`, `9`, `1.5`, `abc` and a non-instance role (e.g. `clean`) each flash the `validateConfig` message and stay open, leaving the file unchanged; the editor does not re-implement the bound or the role restriction.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line (e.g. the budget editor on Ctrl+B), and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into the field.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, instancesMode: true })` reads `instances › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s instances branch names `save instances`; the Transcript hint names `Ctrl+G instances`; docs/cli.md's `Ctrl+G` row names the Transcript role-instance meaning and `roles.<base>.instances`.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's fallback (`fallback`) with Ctrl+L, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Fallback (free at the spend cap)` field and `tumwater config set fallback` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the runner part 2/14 edits src/runner, src/roles/runner-ids.ts and their tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight run-cap (Ctrl+N) and provider-caps (Ctrl+P) entries and the waiting model (Ctrl+A) entry edit src/ui/tui and share src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts and docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table with this one — each adds one editor module, one held flag, one state field and one frame branch, a rebase either way; if the Ctrl+A model editor has landed, add its `model` flag to this plan's `heldEditorFlash` subject list and `onArrow` condition and add this plan's `fallback` flag to its `entering === "model"` clause, as noted below; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-fallback.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instructions.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-fallback.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts test/tui-instructions.test.ts)

**Goal.** The team's fallback model — the top-level `fallback` key, a model selector string, an ordered step list, or a map by tier (`FallbackStep[] | Partial<Record<ModelTier, FallbackChain>>`, `src/config/config-schema.ts`) that a role switches to after a failure and that is also the free model the budget gate falls back to — is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Fallback (free at the spend cap)`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose field renders an array or object as compact JSON through `settingsFieldValue`) and from `tumwater config set fallback`, but the TUI has no editor for it: no `tui-editor-fallback.ts` exists and `grep -rn fallback src/ui/tui` finds no editor or write (the `fallback` hits under `src/ui/tui` are unrelated prose and the transcript/history panes). The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`), its quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`), its model (`Ctrl+A`, the waiting entry), and — once the in-flight Ctrl+N/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+P entries land — its run cap, worktree slots and provider caps, so add `fallback` beside them, the key that says where a role's work goes when its model fails or the cap is reached. `Ctrl+L` is free on the Activity view: the instructions editor's `Ctrl+L` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instructions.ts`) enters only on a role's Transcript (`ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length`) and returns false everywhere else, and no pane or key arm in `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`/`tui-keys.ts` binds `Ctrl+L`, so on Activity the key currently falls through to `applyKey` (ignored). `Ctrl+L` is therefore a re-used key (Transcript = instructions) and the instructions editor's "bound on no other TUI view" comment must gain "except the Activity view's fallback editor".

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-fallback.ts** (new) — `createFallbackEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring the team half of `createQuietEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts`) with no role scope: a private `fallbackMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitFallbackMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.fallback` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "l"`. Enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (the instructions editor keeps `Ctrl+L` on a role's Transcript; every other view falls through unchanged), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("fallback")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `fallbackMode` and `session.held.fallback`, pre-fill from one fresh `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.fallback` — a string as-is, an array or object as `JSON.stringify(...)`, `""` when unset — place the cursor at the end, and flash `edit the team's fallback model (fallback, a model id or a JSON map by tier; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "fallback")` and, on `ok`, flashes `team fallback cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "fallback", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `team fallback set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a bare `omlx/...` becomes the literal selector string, while `["omlx/..."]` becomes the step list and `{"strong":{...}}` the tier map), and `validateConfig` owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitFallbackMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitFallbackMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the quiet and budget editors do; import no `baseRoleOf` (the team key owns no role).
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `fallback: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+L team-fallback editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"fallback"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. Extend the guard body with the two clauses the existing per-editor entries use: first, beside `h.quiet && entering !== "quiet"`, add `if (h.fallback && entering !== "fallback") return session.busyFlash("fallback edit");` (covers entering any other editor while the fallback editor holds the line); second, beside the existing `entering === "instructions"` clause, add an `entering === "fallback"` clause that returns the busy flash when `h.budget` is set (the guard body has no generic `h.budget` early clause, so a value the bottom clauses do not list while the budget editor holds the shared line would otherwise overwrite it). If the waiting Ctrl+A model editor has landed, add its `h.model` to this clause's subject list and add `!session.held.model` handling to the model editor's `entering === "model"` clause for `h.fallback`, exactly as this plan lists `h.budget`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `fallbackMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createFallbackEditor` and add `createFallbackEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createBudgetEditor(session)`; return `fallbackMode: session.held.fallback` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.fallback` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.budget`), adding `!session.held.model` there too if the waiting Ctrl+A model editor has landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `fallbackMode: s.fallbackMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `fallbackMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "fallback", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.fallbackMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.fallbackMode) keys = [["Enter", "save the fallback"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+L", "fallback"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instructions.ts** — the Ctrl+L arm's doc comment ("bound on no other TUI view") gains that Ctrl+L also enters the Activity view's fallback editor; no behavior change, the view guard already keeps the two apart.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table's `Ctrl+L | Transcript` row becomes `Ctrl+L | Activity, Transcript`, naming the team fallback on Activity (`fallback`, a model id or a JSON map by tier; an empty line clears it) and the standing-instructions replace on a Transcript, inside the existing row.

**Tests.**

The pause editor's three Activity-view arms (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+R in `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`) and the shared `/` search editor's arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts`) each gained `!session.held.fallback` in their own held-flag guard lists, so none of them opens or fires over the fallback editor on the shared prompt line — a second guard direction beside `heldEditorFlash` — and `onArrow`'s no-editor condition in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` gained `!session.held.fallback` too, keeping Up/Down from recalling prompt history into its text. `tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes with the table's `Ctrl+L | Activity, Transcript` row.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's agent backends (`backends`) with Ctrl+X, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Agent backends (JSON)` field and `tumwater config set backends` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 2/14 moves src/runner, src/roles/runner-ids.ts and their tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight TUI editors (worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, notify Ctrl+E) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-backends.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-backends.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team's agent-backends section — the top-level `backends` key, a map from the reserved backend ids (`pi`, `claude`) to their per-backend `bin`/`args` (and claude's `configDir`) entries (`backends?: Record<string, AgentConfig>`, `src/config/config-schema.ts`; each entry validated by `checkObjectSection(r, "backends", …)` in `validateConfig`, `src/config/config-validation.ts`) — is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Agent backends (JSON)`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose `settingsFieldValue` renders the object as compact JSON) and `tumwater config set backends '{"pi":{"bin":"…"}}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: no `tui-editor-backends.ts` exists and `grep -rn backends src/ui/tui` finds no editor (only the plain-terms rename comments of the blocked series). The Activity view (view 0) already edits every other dashboard Settings row — the daily cap (`Ctrl+B`), provider caps (`Ctrl+P`), run cap (`Ctrl+N`), quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`), and, once the in-flight entries land, slots, model, fallback and notify — so `backends` is the last row without a terminal twin; add it beside them. `Ctrl+X` is free on Activity: `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`); the panes' `Ctrl+X` router (`src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`) sends the key to the Transcript notes-clear arm (guarded by `noteMode`), the Queued cancel arm and the Backlog cancel arm, all of which are guarded to their own views, and the retire editor's `Ctrl+X` arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-retire.ts`, mnemonic “**x** remove”) is guarded to the Health view (`ctx.view === ctx.roleIds.length + 7`), so on Activity no arm consumes it today. Mnemonic: the section names the backend **eX**ecutables (each entry's `bin`/`args`).

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-backends.ts** (new) — `createBackendsEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createProviderCapsEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts`): a private `backendsMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitBackendsMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.backends` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "x"`: toggle out when `backendsMode`, return false when `ctx.view !== 0` (the Transcript/Inbox/Backlog/Health `Ctrl+X` arms keep their meaning), otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("backends")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `backendsMode` and `session.held.backends`, pre-fill `session.input` with the compact JSON of the section the file actually holds and `""` when it holds none — read from the raw file (`parseJsonConfig`) rather than the merged config, because init/saveConfig write an empty `{}` section even when the operator never set it, so the merged view can't tell "unset" from a set-but-empty section (an empty section also pre-fills empty, matching "empty clears" on save); the dashboard's merged `GET /api/config` source is where the provider-caps editor reads from, but its `backends` always defaults to `{}`, so the raw read is what gives the pinned "empty when unset", place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's agent backends (backends, a JSON object like {"pi":{"bin":"/path/to/pi"}}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "backends")` and, on `ok`, flashes `agent backends cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "backends", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `agent backends set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a compact object becomes the section, while `pi` collapses to the literal string) and, because the key is the whole section, its top-level arm runs `collapseAgentAliases` so a legacy `agentBin`/`piArgs` can never sit beside the new `backends.pi` spelling; `validateConfig` owns the value's truth through `checkObjectSection`, rejecting a non-object with `backends must be an object (got …)` and a non-object entry with `backends.<id> must be an object with optional bin and args (got …)`; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitBackendsMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitBackendsMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and provider-caps editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `backends: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+X agent-backends editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"backends"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. In the guard body add, beside the sibling early clauses, `if (h.backends && entering !== "backends") return session.busyFlash("agent backends");`, and add an `entering === "backends"` clause at the bottom that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions`/`h.providerCaps`/`h.concurrency` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use; the early clause above only covers flags with their own `!== entering` clause, so the bottom clause is what holds `h.budget` out). If the in-flight `slots`/`model`/`fallback`/`notify` flags have landed, name them in the same two places the sibling entries already do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `backendsMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `providerCapsMode`; import `createBackendsEditor` and add `createBackendsEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createProviderCapsEditor(session)` (it must sit before `createRetireEditor(session)` so the Activity view reaches it, and the retire arm still gets `Ctrl+X` on Health because this arm returns false off view 0); return `backendsMode: session.held.backends` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.backends` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.providerCaps`), adding any in-flight flags that are present there too.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `backendsMode: s.backendsMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `backendsMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "agent backends", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.backendsMode`, placed with the existing provider-caps/budget prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.backendsMode) keys = [["Enter", "save agent backends"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside those branches; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+X", "agent backends"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]` and `["Ctrl+P", "provider caps"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — in the `## TUI keys` table, add `Activity` to the `Ctrl+X` rows' Where columns (the cancel rows for Backlog/Inbox and the Health retire row are keyed by view, so add a distinct `Ctrl+X | Activity | edit the team's agent backends (backends, a JSON object of per-backend bin/args such as {"pi":{"bin":"/path/to/pi"}}; empty clears it)` row rather than folding it into another view's row), and in the Configure row extend the `backends` clause that already names the dashboard Agent backends row with the Activity `Ctrl+X` editor.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-backends.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+X opens with the footer `agent backends ›` and the line empty when `tumwater.json` leaves the key unset, and pre-filled with compact JSON when it holds `backends`; Enter on a valid object (`{"pi":{"bin":"/opt/pi"}}`) writes it and flashes `agent backends set to <text>`; Enter on a non-object (`pi`) or a bad entry (`{"pi":5}`) flashes the validator's `backends …` message and stays open with the text kept and `tumwater.json` byte-identical; Enter on an empty line removes the key (it disappears from the file) and flashes `agent backends cleared`, leaving the file unchanged when it was already absent; a file with a legacy `agentBin` and a saved `backends.pi.bin` round-trips to the single `backends.pi.bin` spelling (no `agentBin` left); Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with the budget editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+X flashes the busy message and leaves the budget editor open. With `makeTuiRepo` seeding a legacy `agentBin`, open, confirm the pre-fill, type a new object and Enter, then assert `agentBin` is gone from the file.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+X on Activity opens the backends editor (`session.state().backendsMode`), while Ctrl+X on a role's Transcript notes view still clears notes and on the Health view still opens the retire editor, so the new arm does not swallow those keys.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, backendsMode: true })` reading `agent backends ›` and the hint branch's `save agent backends`; and the Activity hint line naming `Ctrl+X agent backends`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+X opens the editor; the footer reads `agent backends › `, the line pre-fills compact JSON from a set `backends` (empty when unset) and the open flash names `backends` and the JSON-object shape. On Transcript/Inbox/Backlog/Health, Ctrl+X keeps its existing meaning (the new arm returns false off view 0).
- Enter with a JSON object writes `backends` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `agent backends set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `agent backends cleared`; a non-object or a non-object entry flashes the validator's `backends …` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Saving over a file that carries the legacy `agentBin`/`piArgs` leaves exactly one spelling (`backends.pi.bin`/`.args`), thanks to the whole-section arm's `collapseAgentAliases`. A successful save rewrites the whole default-expanded config through `setConfigKey` → `writeConfigMutation`, so it is not byte-identical even for a no-op open/Enter on an already single-spelling object — the file is reformatted; byte-identity is only asserted for a rejected save (the `{ok:false}` path leaves the file untouched).
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line (e.g. the budget editor on Ctrl+B), and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, backendsMode: true })` reads `agent backends › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s backends branch names `save agent backends`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+X agent backends`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+X | Activity` row naming the agent backends and `backends`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm test` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 3/14: Rename RoleRunner and the run pipeline context (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 2/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/ + test/runner*.test.ts + test/revision.test.ts + test/leftover.test.ts + test/model-fallback.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `LoopRunner` becomes `RoleRunner` and `LoopTickContext` becomes `RunnerRunContext`; the rest of src/runner/ and its tests read "runner" and "role" instead of "loop".

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/runner/runner.ts: `class LoopRunner` → `class RoleRunner`, with the two-line aliases `/** @deprecated Use RoleRunner. */` + `export const LoopRunner = RoleRunner;` and `/** @deprecated Use RoleRunner. */` + `export type LoopRunner = RoleRunner;` (26 src and 18 test files name it). Its comments ("this role loop", "the loop's …") follow the series rules.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: `LoopTickContext` → `RunnerRunContext` (used only by runner.ts and runner-run.ts, so no alias). It takes its final name here; the tick-named members inside it are Plain terms code run's.
- Comments in src/runner/leftover.ts, model-fallback.ts, revision.ts, runner-fallback.ts and runner-recovery.ts.
- Tests: test/runner.test.ts, test/runner-2.test.ts through test/runner-5.test.ts, and test/runner-{counters,fallback,interrupted,leftover-recovery,merge-conflicts,prompt-requeue,quiet-watchdog,recovery,red-main,refusal,transient-retry}.test.ts, test/revision.test.ts, test/leftover.test.ts, test/model-fallback.test.ts: migrate `makeLoopRunner`, `LoopRunner`, `LoopState`, `freshLoopState`, `loadLoopState`, `saveLoopState` and `LoopPi` to the new names, and convert comments and test titles.

**Files touched.** All of src/runner/ except runner-state.ts and runner-pi.ts (done in part 2/14), plus the test files listed above. Two part-2/14 files are touched despite that line: runner-pi.ts loses its now-dead `LoopPi` deprecated re-export (no code user remains, so test/exports.test.ts would fail; only comment mentions of `LoopPi` survive), and runner-state.ts's `freshlyWoken` doc has its two "the loop" comment senses fixed to "the runner" so the `loops?` acceptance grep lists only kept senses. No identifier or behavior in either file changes.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `RoleRunner` and `RunnerRunContext` are the declared names; `LoopRunner` exists only as the deprecated alias pair in src/runner/runner.ts.
- `grep -rnwiE 'loops?' src/runner test/runner*.test.ts test/revision.test.ts test/leftover.test.ts test/model-fallback.test.ts` lists only kept senses: JavaScript, poll, event, retry or crash loops.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's notify hook (`notify`) with Ctrl+E, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Notify hook` field and `tumwater config set notify` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 2/14 moves src/runner and test/runner*, and the in-flight TUI editors (run cap Ctrl+N, worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-notify.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-notify.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team's `notify` key (an optional string, the shell command the orchestrator runs when a notable event fires; absent or empty means off — `notify?: string` in `src/config/config-schema.ts`, validated by the `if ("notify" in r && typeof r.notify !== "string")` block in `validateConfig`, `src/config/config-validation.ts`) is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Notify hook`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, which also gives it a Send test) and `tumwater config set notify`, and testable from the TUI's Health view (`Ctrl+N`, `createHealthPane` in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts`) — but the TUI cannot edit it: `grep -rn notify src/ui/tui` finds only that Health test. The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`), per-provider caps (`Ctrl+P`, `createProviderCapsEditor`), quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`, `createQuietEditor`) and, once the in-flight entries land, its run cap, slots, model and fallback. Add the notify hook beside them. `Ctrl+E` is free for the editor subsystem on Activity: `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`), the `createReportPane` Ctrl+E arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts`) is therefore only reached when no editor consumed the key, and off its Usage/Failures views it merely advances a report window that draws nothing there; every other `Ctrl+E` editor arm requires a view or selection Activity never has (`ctx.briefMode`, `noteMode`, `entryEditFor`, `queuedEditFor`).

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-notify.ts** (new) — `createNotifyEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createProviderCapsEditor`: a private `notifyMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitNotifyMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.notify` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "e"`: toggle out when `notifyMode`, return false when `ctx.view !== 0` (every other view keeps its own Ctrl+E — the Usage/Failures window, the Health reclaim, the notes/Brief file replace), otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("notify")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `notifyMode` and `session.held.notify`, pre-fill `session.input` with `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.notify ?? ""`, place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's notify hook (notify, the shell command run on notable events; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "notify")` and, on `ok`, flashes `notify hook cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "notify", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `notify hook set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a bare `notify-me` stays the literal string, while a typed `42` or `{"a":1}` becomes a non-string) and `validateConfig`'s notify block owns the value's truth, rejecting a non-string with `notify must be a string (the shell command to run on notable events, empty string disables; got …)`; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitNotifyMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitNotifyMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and provider-caps editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `notify: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+E notify-hook editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"notify"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. In the guard body add, beside the sibling early clauses, `if (h.notify && entering !== "notify") return session.busyFlash("notify hook");`, and add an `entering === "notify"` clause at the bottom that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions`/`h.providerCaps` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use; the early clause above only covers flags with their own `!== entering` clause, so the bottom clause is what holds `h.budget` out, exactly as the fallback entry words its `entering === "fallback"` clause). If the in-flight `concurrency`/`slots`/`model`/`fallback` flags have landed, name them in the same two places the sibling entries already do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `notifyMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `providerCapsMode`; import `createNotifyEditor` and add `createNotifyEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createProviderCapsEditor(session)`; return `notifyMode: session.held.notify` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.notify` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.providerCaps`), adding any in-flight flags that are present there too.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `notifyMode: s.notifyMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `notifyMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "notify hook", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.notifyMode`, placed with the existing provider-caps/budget prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.notifyMode) keys = [["Enter", "save the notify hook"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside those branches; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+E", "notify hook"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.

**Tests.**

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+E opens the editor; the footer reads `notify hook › `, the line pre-fills the file's `notify` string (empty when unset) and the open flash names `notify` and the empty-clears rule. On Usage/Failures/Health/Transcript/Brief, Ctrl+E keeps its existing meaning (the new arm returns false off view 0).
- Enter with a command writes `notify` as that string through `setConfigKey` and flashes `notify hook set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `notify hook cleared`; a number or object (`42`, `{"a":1}`) flashes the validator's `notify must be a string` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line (e.g. the budget editor on Ctrl+B), and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
