### `tumwater prompt --top <n>` moves the Nth queued prompt to the head of its role's inbox, the last inbox-management verb beside `--list`, `--cancel <n>` and `--edit <n>` (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; the twin of the landed `tumwater plan|bug --top <n>` and the TUI Backlog pane's Ctrl+V move-to-top — an inbox drains oldest-first (`dequeueRolePromptEntry` takes `queuedFiles(root, role).find(deliverablePredicate(now))`), so an urgent directive cannot jump a deep queue and a `--at` prompt cannot be re-prioritized once due — and independent of the in-flight "Split the TUI pane monolith" plan (no `src/ui/tui` file) and of the in-flight image-attach plan, which it meets only at `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts` and `docs/cli.md`, a rebase either way; touches src/inbox/inbox-top.ts (new), src/inbox/inbox.ts, src/cli/cli-command-args.ts, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, docs/cli.md, test/inbox-top.test.ts (new), test/cli-prompt-queue.test.ts, test/cli-prompt-strictness.test.ts, src/cli/help.ts, src/events/event-labels.ts and test/cli-command-args.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)
**Goal.** A queued prompt's order is its queue-file name (`queueFileName(stamp, seq, pid)`), and dequeue picks the oldest deliverable file, so the only way to make one prompt next is to give it the smallest stamp in its role's inbox. Today the operator can `--list`, `--cancel <n>` and `--edit <n>` but cannot reorder: an urgent prompt sent while a role is busy lands last, and a prompt scheduled with `--at` that has become due cannot be pulled forward. Add `--top <n>` (a new mode, like `--cancel`), reusing the list-wide position resolution: it moves the Nth prompt of the resolved role's queue to the front by renaming its file to a stamp one below the queue's minimum, carries its image attachments to the new stem (the `movePromptImages`/`stripVanishedImageReferences` pair `PendingPrompt.requeueUnfulfilled` uses), preserves its `--at` marker so a deferred prompt still is not deliverable early, and logs a `prompt_topped` event. `--list`, the dashboards' Inbox tab, the TUI Queued pane and `peekRolePrompt` all read `queuedFiles`, so they show the new order with no change of their own.

**Approach.**
- `src/inbox/inbox-top.ts` (new): `export type TopOutcome = { status: "topped"; preview: string } | { status: "gone" }` and `export function movePromptToTop(root: string, role: string, position: number): TopOutcome`. Resolve `file = queuedFileAtPosition(root, role, position)` (its out-of-range throw is the shared wording), fail `prompt ${position} is already first` when `position === 1` (the `moveEntryToTop` precedent), then `const text = readTextIfExists(file); if (text === null) return { status: "gone" };` (the cancel/edit race policy). Compute `stamp = (min of queueFileStamp(basename) over queuedFiles(root, role), or Date.now() when none parses) - 1` and `newFile = join(dirname(file), queueFileName(stamp, 0, ".md"))`, decrementing `stamp` while `existsSync(newFile)` (so a concurrent writer's name is never overwritten; the pid in `queueFileName` keeps two concurrent tops' names apart). `const moved = movePromptImages(file, newFile, text)`, `warnEventBestEffort(root, role, …)` when `moved.problem !== null`, `const carried = stripVanishedImageReferences(moved.text).text`, `writeTextAtomic(newFile, carried)`, `removeQueueFile(file)`, `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: role, type: "prompt_topped", preview: promptPreview(carried) })`, and return `{ status: "topped", preview: promptPreview(carried) }`. The not-before marker rides in `text`, so the renamed file keeps it byte-for-byte.
- `src/inbox/inbox.ts`: its doc comment names inbox-top.ts (no re-export — importers reach `movePromptToTop` through inbox-top.ts directly, matching how inbox-cancel/inbox-edit are described but not re-exported).
- `src/cli/cli-command-args.ts`: add `{ names: ["--top"], value: true, valueName: "<n>" }` to `PROMPT_FLAG_SPECS`; read `topFlag` beside `cancelFlag`/`editFlag`; extend the mutual-exclusion checks (`--list`/`--cancel`/`--edit` each refuse `--top`); add `topFlag >= 0` to `refuseQueueOnlyFlag`'s mode predicate; and add a `--top` branch before the enqueue branch that runs `parsePositionFlag("--top", args[topFlag + 1], "--top 2")`, `failStrayArg(args, "with --top there is no prompt text", topFlag, topFlag + 1, ...roleClaim)`, and returns `{ mode: "top", role, position: n }`. Widen the `PromptArgs` union with that member and the module's doc comment with `--top <n>`.
- `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts`: handle `parsed.mode === "top"` with the same list-wide resolution the cancel branch uses — no `--role`: `movePromptToTop(root, failQueueMiss(resolveListedQueue(root, listWideScope(root), parsed.position), parsed.position).role, parsed.position)`; with `--role`: the role-scoped call. Render through one small helper: `${preview}` for the resolved outcome and `gone` → ``prompt ${position} is no longer in the inbox — ${roleLabel(role)} already took it``, naming the role only when unscoped (the `sayPromptOutcome` contract). Name `--top` in the module doc comment's mode list.
- `src/events/events.ts`: add `| "prompt_topped" // a queued prompt was moved to the front of its role's inbox (tumwater prompt --top)`. `src/events/event-format.ts`: add `case "prompt_topped": return \`inbox message moved to the front: ${textOr(e.preview)}\`;` beside the `prompt_edited` case, and `src/events/event-labels.ts` labels it `message moved to front`. No notify-allowlist change, so docs/config.md's table is untouched.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the "Steer the project" row, after the `--cancel <n>` clause, add `` `tumwater prompt --top <n>` moves the Nth entry as `--list` shows them to the front of its role's inbox, so the role dequeues it next (a `--at` deferral still holds until its time); it takes `--role <id>` when several roles share that number ``. `src/cli/help.ts`: add `--top` to `FREEFORM_VALUED_FLAGS.prompt` and a `tumwater prompt --top <n>` help stanza after the `--cancel` one (help.ts does not derive its prompt usage from `PROMPT_FLAG_SPECS`, so the stanza and the flag list are added by hand).
- `test/cli-command-args.test.ts`: the unknown-flag error's valid-flags wording gains `--top <n>` after `--edit <n>`.
- Anchors are symbol-level; no line numbers.

**Files touched.** `src/inbox/inbox-top.ts` (new), `src/inbox/inbox.ts`, `src/cli/cli-command-args.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts`, `src/events/events.ts`, `src/events/event-format.ts`, `src/events/event-labels.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/inbox-top.test.ts` (new), `test/cli-prompt-queue.test.ts`, `test/cli-prompt-strictness.test.ts`, `test/cli-command-args.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New `test/inbox-top.test.ts` (a temp root with `enqueueRolePrompt` for a role, as `test/inbox-edit.test.ts` builds one): with three queued prompts, `movePromptToTop(root, role, 3)` leaves `queuedFiles(root, role)[0]` the moved file and `dequeueRolePrompt(root, role)` returns the moved text first; the file's text (and a `tumwater:not-before …` marker when present) is byte-identical. `movePromptToTop(root, role, 1)` throws `/already first/`; a removed file returns `{ status: "gone" }`.
- The same file pins the attachment carry: write a sibling `<stem>.png` beside the third queue file and an `[image attached: <absolute path>]` line in its text; after `--top` the referenced path exists and its basename starts with the new file's stem, and `removeSameStemSiblings(root, role, newFile)` removes it (no same-stem leak under the old stem).
- The same file pins the deferral: a prompt enqueued with a future `notBeforeMs` still leaves `inboxSize(root, role)` 0 and `dequeueRolePrompt(root, role)` null after `movePromptToTop`, and ordering among the deliverable ones places it first.
- `test/cli-prompt-queue.test.ts` (or `test/prompt-commands.test.ts`): `tumwater prompt --top 2` makes `tumwater prompt --list` print the moved entry's text as line 1 of its role's section; a bad position, a list-wide ambiguity and a list-wide miss report the same wordings `--cancel` does; the unscoped success line names the role.
- `test/cli-prompt-strictness.test.ts`: `--top` with `--list`, `--cancel`, or `--edit` fails as mutually exclusive; `--top 1 --file x`, `--top 1 --at 1h`, `--top 1 --attach p.png` fail with the `only queues a prompt` wording; `--top 1 extra text` fails as stray text.
- `tumwater logs --type prompt_topped` (or the event feed) holds one `prompt_topped` entry per successful move, with the preview.
- `npm run test` passes.

### OpenCode backend, part 1/7: The claude-only branches outside the backend seam become per-backend traits, with no behavior change (planned 2026-10-17 by user; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "Groundwork: the claude-only branches become backend traits"; touches src/agent/backend-traits.ts (new) src/config/config-validation.ts src/prompt/dialect.ts src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts src/ui/progress-data.ts src/pi/pi-models.ts src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts src/agent/image-input.ts and their tests — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The OpenCode backend (parts 2–7) should not need another sweep through config, prompts, watchdogs, pricing and doctor.

- Today about a dozen places outside src/agent/agent-backend.ts test `agent === "claude"`.
- What most of them really ask is a capability:
  - whether the backend streams tool output;
  - which prompt dialect it speaks;
  - which passthrough flags it reserves;
  - whether its model jobs need pi's models.json;
  - how its model ids are labeled;
  - how its free-ness is judged.

This part names those capabilities per backend id and makes each of those places read them. pi and claude behave exactly as before.

**Approach.**
- Add src/agent/backend-traits.ts (`// vocabulary: plain`).
  - It is pure and imports nothing from the runtime registry, so the config, prompt and UI layers can read it. That is the same reason `AGENT_DEFAULT_MODELS` lives in src/config/model-selector.ts.
  - An id with no entry reads as pi, because src/agent/run-agent.ts runs an unregistered id on pi.
  - It provides:
    - `streamsToolOutput(agent)`: true for pi, false for claude.
    - `usesPiModels(agent)`: whether the backend's model jobs resolve through pi's models.json. True for pi only.
    - `reservedPassthroughFlag(agent, flag)`: the reason string config validation prints for a reserved `backends.<id>.args` flag, or undefined. It wraps claude's `HARNESS_CLAUDE_FLAGS` and pi's `HARNESS_PI_FLAGS` and keeps today's reason strings.
    - `modelLabel(agent, provider, model)`: `provider/model` for pi, and claude's bare model (or "claude backend" when there is none). These are today's two inline label lambdas in src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts and src/agent/image-input.ts.
- src/config/config-validation.ts: the `backends.<id>.args` check calls `reservedPassthroughFlag` instead of its `id === "claude" ? … : id === "pi" ? …` chain.
- src/prompt/dialect.ts: `dialectFor` reads a table keyed by backend id (`pi`, `claude`). An unknown id gets pi's dialect.
- src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts (`deps.agent === "claude"`) and src/ui/progress-data.ts (the open-call stall check) test `!streamsToolOutput(agent)` instead.
- src/pi/pi-models.ts `seamFree`: one `switch` arm per backend.
  - The pi arm is `pairFree`; the claude arm is today's subscription rule; the default arm is false.
  - Part 6/7 then adds an arm and changes nothing else. The signature is unchanged.
- src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts:
  - `needsDefinitions` becomes `pairs.some((p) => usesPiModels(p.agent ?? "pi"))`.
  - The fallback-chain probe's `isClaude` (`pair.provider === "claude"`) becomes "the provider names a backend other than pi" (`isAgentId(pair.provider) && pair.provider !== "pi"`). A non-pi step then never asks pi for a base URL.
  - The image rows ask the registered backend's `imageInput` hook when it has one (claude today), instead of testing the id.
- src/agent/image-input.ts: the seam label uses `modelLabel`.
- **Out of scope:** the claude subscription machinery stays as it is:
  - claude-account
  - src/gates/budget-gates.ts's `seamIsClaude` / `pairIsClaude`
  - the window holds
  - src/loop/loop-pi.ts's `authoringBudgetCap`
  - src/status/status-budget.ts
  - the billing row in src/roles/role-view.ts

  These belong to claude's account; they are not shared capabilities.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/backend-traits.ts (new), src/config/config-validation.ts, src/prompt/dialect.ts, src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts, src/ui/progress-data.ts, src/pi/pi-models.ts, src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, src/agent/image-input.ts.
- Tests: test/backend-traits.test.ts (new), test/prompt-dialect.test.ts, test/pi-watchdogs.test.ts, test/progress.test.ts, test/pi-models.test.ts, test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, test/config-validation.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/backend-traits.test.ts checks each trait:
  - pi streams tool output, uses pi's models and labels `provider/model`.
  - claude does neither and labels its bare model.
  - An id with no entry reads as pi.
  - `reservedPassthroughFlag` returns today's validation reason for a reserved pi flag and a reserved claude flag, and undefined for an unreserved one.
- None of the places listed in the design's table tests a backend id by its literal any more. The claude subscription places listed under Out of scope still do.
- Every existing test passes unchanged, and `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater restart` applies a pending self-redeploy from the terminal, waiving the cooldown — the CLI twin of the dashboard update alert's refresh button (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; the only caller of `requestRestart` today is `handleRestart` (POST `/api/restart`) in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, whose own doc comment says it is "the same marker-writing core a CLI surface would call", and `tumwater help` lists no `restart`; independent of every Planned entry — the in-flight `prompt --top`/image-attach plans and the pane split touch no src/operator or src/cli marker file, and only docs/cli.md is shared, a one-clause edit, so either lands first; touches src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/cli-marker-commands.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/how-it-works.md, test/help.test.ts and test/cli-operators.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** When tumwater is building itself, a stale running build shows `Update available`; `autoRestart` applies it at most once every 12 hours, and the dashboard's update alert has a refresh button that waives that cooldown and starts the pending update now (`docs/how-it-works.md` "Updates"). That button is `handleRestart` (`src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts`), which calls `requestRestart(root)` (`src/operator/operator-intent.ts`) to write the `.tumwater` restart marker the orchestrator consumes through `consumeRestartRequest` (`src/operator/operator-requests.ts`), which calls `redeployer.forceRestart()`. No CLI command reaches that core: `tumwater help` has no `restart` stanza, `src/cli.ts`'s switch has no case, and `markerCommandCores` (`src/cli/cli-marker-commands.ts`) lists neither — so a terminal-only operator must open the dashboard or wait out the cooldown. Add `tumwater restart`: a marker command that calls `requestRestart` and prints its message verbatim (or fails with its error, `no update is waiting — tumwater is current with main`, when the running build is not stale), matching the dashboard button. It takes no flags (the body is ignored there too; `--role` is meaningless), and with no team running the marker is written harmlessly for the next run's first poll, exactly as the GUI handler's twin test pins.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`: import `requestRestart` beside `requestAbort` from `./operator-intent.js`; add `export async function cmdRestart(root: string, _args: string[]): Promise<void>` with the `cmdAbort` shape — `const result = requestRestart(root); if (!result.ok) fail(result.error); say(result.message);` — and a doc comment naming the dashboard twin and the waived-cooldown wording.
- `src/cli/cli-marker-commands.ts`: add `cmdRestart` to the import; add `"restart"` to the `MarkerCommand` union; add `restart: cmdRestart` to `markerCommandCores`; add `restart: []` to `perCommandFlags` (no flags — `rejectUnknownArgs(command, args, [])` then rejects any stray one, so `tumwater restart extra` and `--role` both fail before a marker is written); update the header and `runMarkerCommand` comments that say "the six marker commands" to seven and name `restart`.
- `src/cli.ts`: add `case "restart":` to the existing marker fall-through (`reset-counters` … `reclaim`), and update its "six marker commands" comment to seven so the case labels stay exactly `MarkerCommand`'s members.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: insert a `  tumwater restart` stanza by `reclaim`/`abort` in the control block, reading that it applies a pending self-redeploy now and waives the restart cooldown (the dashboard's update-alert button; a passing check on main, a successful compile, and in-flight runs finishing still apply). `helpStanzas` derives the topic from that usage line, so `tumwater help restart` works with no other help edit.
- `docs/cli.md`: name `tumwater restart` in the "Control the roles" row beside `tumwater reclaim`/`tumwater abort`. `docs/how-it-works.md` "Updates": after the refresh-button sentence, add "or run `tumwater restart`", so the terminal and browser routes are stated together.
- Anchors are symbol-level; no line numbers.

**Files touched.** `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`, `src/cli/cli-marker-commands.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md`, `test/help.test.ts`, `test/cli-operators.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New tests in `test/cli-operators.test.ts`, modelled on the `abort`/`reclaim` sections there (whose `writeOrchestratorMarker` seeds live team info) and on `seedTeam` in `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts` (which writes `orchestratorStatePath` JSON as `{ pid: process.pid, build: { sha, builtAt, stale, aheadCommits } }`):
  - With a live team whose published build is stale, `tumwater restart` exits 0, stdout matches `/restart requested/` and `/cooldown is waived/`, and `restartRequestPath(root)` exists with a numeric `at` — the same file `consumeRestartRequest` consumes and `handleRestart` writes.
  - With `stale: false`, it exits 1 with stderr matching `/no update is waiting/` and writes no marker; with no orchestrator info at all it exits 0, writes the marker, and stdout matches `/tumwater is not running/`.
  - `tumwater restart extra` and `tumwater restart --role feature` fail (unknown arg) and leave `restartRequestPath` absent.
- `test/help.test.ts`'s `ALL_COMMANDS` oracle gains `"restart"` (its sync test then requires the help stanza), so `helpTopic("restart")` resolves. `test/cli-doc.test.ts` passes with the new `docs/cli.md` mention (no new long flag).
- `npm run test` passes.

### The TUI's prompt line attaches an image path to the next director prompt with Ctrl+V, the terminal twin of `tumwater prompt --attach <path>` and the dashboard composer's drop/paste (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; the last prompt capability the TUI's prompt line lacks — `tumwater prompt --attach` and the dashboard composer both attach images, and the core `submitRolePrompt(root, role, text, images, notBeforeMs)` already takes a `PromptImageInput[]` — and independent of the in-flight "Split the TUI pane monolith" plan and of the two in-flight Ctrl+V plans, whose keys live in the Transcript and Backlog views while this editor is bound to the Activity view and lives in new src/ui/tui/tui-editor-attach.ts, which none of them touch; it shares the tui-frame.ts hint/prefix branches with the reset plan, a rebase either way; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-attach.ts (new), src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, src/inbox/inbox-attachments.ts, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, docs/cli.md, test/tui-attach.test.ts (new), test/tui-frame.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Images reach a queued prompt only through the browser composer's drop/paste (POST `/api/prompt`, which passes its `images` to `submitPrompt` in src/inbox/inbox-submit.ts) or the CLI's `tumwater prompt --attach <path>` (which reads and validates the paths through `readPromptImages` in src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts). The TUI's prompt line cannot attach one: both submit sites pass `undefined` for images (`submitPrompt(session.root, prompt, undefined, …)` in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` and `submitRolePromptAndWake(session.root, role, parsed.value, undefined, …)` in `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-prompt.ts`), so a terminal-only operator must leave the TUI. Add an image-attach editor on the prompt line: on the Activity view, `Ctrl+V` opens a path editor on the prompt line, `Enter` validates and reads that one image through the same rules `--attach` uses, stores it as a pending attachment, and flashes its name (or the image-input reroute notice); pressing `Enter` on the director prompt then sends it with the stored images through the existing `submitPrompt` images argument. The pending list clears on a successful send and on an empty-path Enter, survives a failed send, and `Esc` only closes the editor.

**Approach.**
- `src/inbox/inbox-attachments.ts`: add `export function readPromptImageFiles(paths: readonly string[]): PromptImageInput[]` — the throwing core of the CLI's reader. It applies the same cheap path-only rules `attachPathsProblem` in prompt-commands.ts applies today (the exported `promptImagesCountProblem`, `promptImageExtensionProblem`, and `promptImageSizeProblem`, plus the regular-file `fs.statSync` check so a FIFO cannot block the TUI), reads each surviving file whole, and re-checks with `promptImagesProblem`; each failure is a thrown `Error` with the existing wording instead of a `fail()`. `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts`'s `readPromptImages` becomes `try { return readPromptImageFiles(paths) } catch (err) { return fail(errorMessage(err)) }`, and its now-duplicate `attachPathsProblem` is deleted, so the CLI and the TUI validate from one home.

Add Ctrl+R to release the selected plan or bug through the same non-exiting `tryReleaseEntry`, committing with `commitBacklogEdit` and waking its loop with `requestWake` — the same two calls the dashboard release makes.

1. `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` imports: beside `tryCancelEntry` in the `../../backlog/backlog-write.js` import add `tryReleaseEntry` and `OPERATOR_FILE_KINDS`; add `import { requestWake } from "../../operator/operator-intent.js"` (the module `tui-editor-pause.ts` already imports it).

Refusals mirror Ctrl+X: a `done`/`fixed`/`answered` row → `a done plan, fixed bug or answered question is read-only`; a `question` → `only a plan or open bug can be released here`; any `hold` other than `"refused"` or `"waiting-for-failure"` → `that ${kind} carries no Refused or Waiting for the next failure note` (the `hold` field `browsableBacklogEntries` already carries). Otherwise the first press sets `releaseArmed` and flashes `press Ctrl+R again to release ${kind} #${position} — any other key keeps it`; a matching second press calls `tryReleaseEntry(root, kind, position, armedRelease.title)` — on `released` it calls `commitBacklogEdit(outcome.file, \`Release ${kind}: ${outcome.title}\`)` then `requestWake(root, [OPERATOR_FILE_KINDS[kind].role])`, clears the selection and scroll and flashes `released ${kind} #${position}: ${outcome.title}`; `gone`/`moved` clear the selection and flash `that ${kind} was already removed or moved — nothing released`; `not_refused` flashes the no-note message. ### Split the TUI pane monolith `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` into per-pane modules beside a shared pane session (planned 2026-10-17 by the organize role; the largest source file — one `createTuiPanes` closure at ~1006 lines, 5.3× the repo's 188-line src median — the sibling of the landed "split tui-editors" reorganize, which shrank that same-shaped factory to a 240-line aggregator beside per-editor modules; touches src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, new src/ui/tui/tui-pane-*.ts with tui-pane-ctx.ts and tui-pane-session.ts, and test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` is the repository's largest source file — one `createTuiPanes` closure, ~1006 lines (5.3× the 188-line median over src), holding every pane's session state and the whole pane half of the key dispatch in a single `handleKey` whose ~380-line body switches by view index. That is exactly the shape of the `tui-editors.ts` monolith the team already split: its 1121-line closure became a 240-line aggregator plus per-editor modules beside a shared session (`tui-editor-session.ts`, the `TuiEditorModule` contract in `tui-editor-ctx.ts`), and the same confusion remains here — a change to one pane's keys or state must be threaded through the one shared closure amid every other pane's state and arms. Split it the same way: per-pane modules each own the state and the handler arms of the views they serve, a shared pane-session object holds the cross-pane state and the route, and `createTuiPanes` becomes a thin aggregator. No behavior change: the view-index layout, the Ctrl-key assignments, and the key-routing order are preserved exactly.

**Approach.**
- Follow the landed `tui-editors` split as the template: a shared session module, a per-module contract, per-pane factory modules, and an aggregator that builds them and routes keys in today's order.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-ctx.ts`: the per-keypress read `createTuiKeys` passes to every pane arm — the editor flags `promptLineFree` rests on (`es.*` from the editors), `view`, `roleIds`, and `TuiEditorCtx` — the analog of the `ctx` argument in `TuiEditorModule.handleKey`. `interface TuiPaneModule` here, the analog of `TuiEditorModule`: `handleKey(key, ctx, session): boolean` (true on consume), `enter(session): boolean` (the pane's half of `cycleView`'s Ctrl+T cache/render, run in the aggregator's view order), and `state(session)` (the pane's slice of the render state the frame merges).
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts`: the cross-pane state and seams every pane arm shares — the `view` index, `paneScroll`, `eventBudget`/`entryBudget`, the active pane's `paneCache` slot, the second-Ctrl+X targets `armed`/`cancelArmed` and `notesClearArmed`, the `TuiPanesDeps` seams (root, now, flat, flashMessage, flashError, commitBacklogEdit, the collectors), and the shared cycle tables/helpers (`nextInCycle`, `cycleLabel`, `SESSION_WINDOW_TAIL`, `HISTORY_WINDOWS`, `REPORT_WINDOWS`, `HISTORY_RESULTS`, `scopeCycle`). This is the analog of `tui-editor-session.ts` (which holds the shared prompt line and the held-editor registry): it makes the cross-pane sharing explicit at the module boundary instead of implicit in one closure, and keeps `paneScroll`/`armed`/`view` single-homed so the panes cannot drift.
- Per-pane factory modules, each owning the views, state, and arms listed (view indices follow `cycleView`: 0 activity, 1..N per-loop transcript, N+1 project status, N+2 usage, N+3 failures, N+4 history, N+5 pending, N+6 queued, N+7 health, N+8 brief):
  - `tui-pane-activity.ts` — view 0; `activityScroll`, `activityRole`, `activityGrep`, `applyActivitySearch`; the Ctrl+G activity-scope arm and the PgUp/PgDn tail-paging arm.
  - `tui-pane-transcript.ts` — views 1..roleIds.length; `noteMode`, `noteCache`, `changeMode`, `changeCache`; the Ctrl+N transcript→notebook→change arm and the notebook/change PgUp/PgDn arm.
  - `tui-pane-backlog.ts` — view N+1; `selectedEntry`, `entryScroll`, `cancelArmed`; `clearBacklogSelection`; the entry up/down, PgUp/PgDn body, Ctrl+X cancel, and answer/title-edit arms.
  - `tui-pane-report.ts` — views N+2 (usage) and N+3 (failures); `reportWindow` and the report side of `scopeRole`; `usagePaneCache`/`failuresPaneCache`; the Ctrl+E window and Ctrl+G scope arms and the Markdown-pane PgUp/PgDn arm.
  - `tui-pane-history.ts` — view N+4; `historyWindow`, `historyResult`, `historyRole`, `historyGrep`, `trailMode`, `trailCache`, `trailGen`, `loadTrailStat`, `refreshTrail`, `applyHistorySearch`, `historyPaneCache`; the Ctrl+S window, Ctrl+O result, Ctrl+G scope, the `/` search arm, the Ctrl+N trail arm, and the trail/history PgUp/PgDn arm.
  - `tui-pane-pending.ts` — view N+5; the merge-queue read plus the `collectPending` fire-and-forget body now inline in `cycleView`.
  - `tui-pane-queued.ts` — view N+6; `queuedRows`, `selectedQueued`, `refreshQueued`; the up/down select, Esc-to-list, and Ctrl+X cancel arms.
  - `tui-pane-health.ts` — view N+7; `healthProblems`, `lastDoctorReport`; the `runDoctor` fire-and-forget body.
  - `tui-pane-brief.ts` — view N+8; the `readBrief`/`renderBrief` body.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` becomes the thin aggregator: `createTuiPanes(deps)` still builds the session and the per-pane modules, and keeps `beginKey`, `editorCtx` (re-reads the shared state), `cycleView` (routes each view's `enter` in today's view order, keeping the stale-resolution guards), `handleKey` (routes each key to the matching pane module in today's dispatch order — editor-exclusion/`promptLineFree` first, then the pane arms), `syncRoster` (the roster shift/clamp and the per-pane scope drops), `setLineBudgets`, and `state` (merges each module's slice in view order). Export names and `TuiPanesDeps` are unchanged, so `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` and `tui-editors.ts` keep their call sites.
- `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts`: its code scan today loops `tui-editor-*.ts` plus `tui-keys.ts` and `tui-panes.ts` for Ctrl keys; extend it to also loop `tui-pane-*.ts` (the analog of its existing editor scan), or it fails once the Ctrl arms leave `tui-panes.ts`. Its three assertions and `docs/cli.md` table are otherwise unchanged.
- Update every doc comment that cites `tui-panes.ts` as holding the pane arms; the historical mention in `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`'s Done entry describes the 2026-10-16 part 2/2 and is left as history.

**Files touched.** All new files live in `src/ui/tui/` beside `tui-panes.ts`. New: `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-ctx.ts`, `tui-pane-session.ts`, `tui-pane-activity.ts`, `tui-pane-transcript.ts`, `tui-pane-backlog.ts`, `tui-pane-report.ts`, `tui-pane-history.ts`, `tui-pane-pending.ts`, `tui-pane-queued.ts`, `tui-pane-health.ts`, `tui-pane-brief.ts`. Rewritten: `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`. Tests: `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` (extend the scan list); the pane-key/pane-state suites (`tui-keys.test.ts`, `tui-notebook.test.ts`, `tui-reload.test.ts`, `tui-backlog.test.ts`, `tui-history.test.ts`, `tui-prompt-history.test.ts`, `tui-operator-keys.test.ts`) pass unchanged — they reach the panes only through `tui-keys.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `npm run test` passes.
- `git diff -M --stat` shows `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` shrunken to a thin aggregator and eleven new `tui-pane-*.ts` modules; no identifier renamed and no Ctrl assignment or routing order changed (`git diff src/ui/tui` shows moved lines only).
- `git grep -n 'tui-panes' src test docs` lists only the new shell's imports, `tui-keys.ts`'s call site, `tui-editors.ts`'s type import, `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts`'s scan list, and the historical `test/backlog-structure.test.ts` Done mention — no path still points at a pane arm that moved out.
- `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes with the extended scan, its assertions unchanged.

### `tumwater doctor` warns when a queued prompt has waited more than a day for a role that is not dequeuing it (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every other Planned entry — it adds one warn-only check beside `checkStaleQueuedMerges` in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, one row in `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, and reads the inbox through the existing `queuedListRows`/`listWideScope` traversal rather than adding a reader; the only file it shares with the in-flight `Backlog items opened` plan is docs/cli.md, a one-clause edit, so either lands first and the other rebases; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts and test/doctor.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A prompt queued for a role (`tumwater prompt --role <id>`, the dashboard composer, the TUI, a `--at` delay whose time has now passed) is dequeued at that role's next run. A role that is paused, disabled, or failing never reaches that run, so the prompt waits indefinitely and only the Inbox views (`tumwater prompt --list`, the dashboard Inbox tab, the TUI Inbox pane) show its age — and only when the operator looks. `tumwater doctor` already warns when a merge sits in the queue too long (`checkStaleQueuedMerges`), when a question waits 7 days, and when a bug waits 3 days, but says nothing about a stranded prompt. Add a warn-only `checkStalePrompts` naming the oldest due-but-undelivered prompt, its role, and the deliver-or-drop commands.

**Approach.**
1. `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, placed after `checkStaleQueuedMerges`:
   - Add `const STALE_PROMPT_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` with a doc comment: an opinionated default with no knob, like `MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS`; a day is long enough that a healthy role's next run would have dequeued it, and short enough that a paused or disabled role's stranded prompt shows up.
   - Add `export function checkStalePrompts(root: string, now: number): CheckOutcome`, reading the one shared list traversal `tumwater prompt --list`, the TUI Queued pane and the dashboard Inbox use: `queuedListRows(root, null, listWideScope(root))` (both exported from `src/inbox/inbox.ts`). Each row carries `role`, `position`, `queuedAtMs`, and `notBeforeMs`.
   - Keep only rows that are (a) deliverable now — `deliverableAt(p.notBeforeMs, now)` from `src/inbox/prompt-not-before.ts`, so a `--at 7d` prompt still counting down is never stale — and (b) stamped (`p.queuedAtMs !== null`) more than `STALE_PROMPT_MS` ago.
   - Empty → `okOutcome("no queued prompt has waited more than 1 day for a role to dequeue it")`. Otherwise `warnOutcome` naming the oldest in full and the rest through the module's existing `andMore` helper: `` `inbox prompt for ${roleLabel(first.role)} #${first.position} has waited ${humanSeconds(secondsSince(first.queuedAtMs, now))} — the role is not dequeuing it (paused, disabled, or failing); resume or enable it, or drop the prompt with \`tumwater prompt --cancel ${first.position} --role ${first.role}\`` `` plus the `andMore` suffix. `roleLabel`, `humanSeconds`, and `secondsSince` are already imported in this module.
   - A warn, never a fail, matching the `checkStaleQueuedMerges`/`checkStaleQuestions`/`checkStaleBugs` precedent.
   - Extend the module header's opening sentence so it names the queued-merge and queued-prompt checks too (the header today claims only backlog-document readers, which `checkStaleQueuedMerges` already exceeds).
2. `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: add `{ name: "stale prompts", ...checkStalePrompts(root, Date.now()) }` immediately after the `stale merge-queue entries` row, so the two "queued too long" rows sit together.
3. `docs/cli.md`: in the `tumwater doctor` row's enumeration, add the new warn — "a prompt queued for a role that has not dequeued it within a day" — beside the other waited-too-long items.

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, `test/doctor.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New tests in `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, modelled on its `checkStaleQueuedMerges` suite (same `tmpdir`/config fixture style, the `andMore` "and 1 more:" assertion): seed the inbox through `enqueueRolePrompt` and rename each returned queue file to an old 13-digit stamp (`${oldStamp}-000000-1.md`, the filename `queueFileStamp` parses into `queuedAtMs`) under a root whose `tumwater.json` lists the roles.
  - An empty inbox, one queued exactly 24 h ago (the threshold, not past it), and one whose `notBeforeMs` is in the future while its stamp is 25 h old all read `ok`.
  - One prompt for a role queued 25 h ago reads `warn`; the detail names the role label, `#<position>`, the age from `humanSeconds`, and the `tumwater prompt --cancel <position> --role <role>` fix. A second, older stale prompt on another role adds `and 1 more: <role> #<position>`.
- `test/doctor.test.ts`'s pinned check-name list gains `"stale prompts"` immediately after `"stale merge-queue entries"`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater history --summary` tallies each role's run time beside its tokens and cost, and the GUI Summary table shows the column (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every Planned and blocked entry — it touches only src/history, src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, one clause in docs/cli.md and one in src/cli/help.ts; the blocked plain-terms run series edits src/history only in its later parts, and no in-flight plan edits these files; touches src/history/history-data.ts, src/history/history-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/history-data.test.ts, test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts and test/gui-client-history.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary` and the dashboard History Summary table tally each role's runs by outcome class, output tokens, and cost — but not how much wall-clock those runs consumed. `TickRow.durationMs` already carries each completed run's span (paired from the tick's `run_start` by `tickSpanMs`, null only when rotation lost the start), and the failure digest already prices loss in agent-hours, so the number is on hand; the per-role summary is the one tally that omits it. Add a `time` column: the sum of each role's run spans among the summarized rows (and the total), so an operator reads how much agent wall-clock the team actually spent beside the tokens and cost it burned.

**Approach.**
1. `src/history/history-data.ts`:
   - `HistorySummaryRow` gains `durationMs?: number` — the sum of the summarized rows' `durationMs` (the zero-means-absent convention, like the report's optional fields: absent when the loop's rows all carried a null span, so an untimed window keeps today's exact JSON shape). Document it beside `tokens`/`costUsd`.
   - `summarizeTickRows`: inside the existing `for (const t of [entry, total])` loop, after the token/cost adds, add `if (row.durationMs !== null) t.durationMs = (t.durationMs ?? 0) + row.durationMs;`. `blank()` stays as it is (no key until a span contributes), so `summarizeTickRows([])` and every existing fixture whose rows carry `durationMs: null` return the exact object they do today.
2. `src/history/history-render.ts`:
   - Add `"time"` to `cols` after `"cost"`, so the table reads runs, changes, none, problems, tokens, cost, time, last change.
   - In `cell`, `c === "time" ? (r.durationMs === undefined ? "—" : humanSeconds(r.durationMs / 1000))`. Import `humanSeconds` from `../text/datetime.js` (the module already imports `formatTimestamp` from there; `shortSpanPhrase` is seconds/minutes only, and a per-role sum can reach hours).
   - Update `renderSummary`'s doc comment, which names the columns.
3. `src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts`, `histSummaryHtml` (inside the `history-summary` region): add a `Time` `<th>` after `Cost` and a time cell after the cost cell, `r.durationMs === undefined ? "—" : esc(fmtSpan(Number(r.durationMs)))` — the page's existing row formatter, in scope via the `format` region. Update the function's comment enumerating the column set.
4. Docs, same change: `docs/cli.md`'s `history` row `--summary` clause becomes "tallying its tokens, cost and run time"; `src/cli/help.ts`'s `--summary` description gains "and its run time" to its tally list.
5. `HistorySummaryRow` is shared, so `tumwater history --summary --json` and `/api/history?summary` gain the optional `durationMs` key only when a role's rows carried timed spans — an additive script-interface change; the docs' list of summary keys needs no edit because the zero-absent rule leaves the common shape untouched.

**Files touched.** `src/history/history-data.ts`, `src/history/history-render.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/history-data.test.ts`, `test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts`, `test/gui-client-history.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/history-data.test.ts`, beside `summarizeTickRows sums tokens and cost per loop and into the total`: rows with `durationMs` 60_000 and 120_000 for one role and 30_000 for another give that role `durationMs: 180000`, the other `30000`, and the total `210000`; a row with `durationMs: null` adds nothing. A `summarizeTickRows` over rows whose `durationMs` are all null leaves `durationMs` absent on every role and the total (assert `"durationMs" in summary.total === false`), pinning the zero-absent shape; the existing deepEqual cases keep their expected objects unchanged.
- `test/history-data.test.ts`'s `renderSummary` test asserts the header contains `tokens`, `cost` and `time` in that order, and that a `HistorySummaryRow` with `durationMs: 3_600_000` renders `1h` in its row while a row without the field renders `—`.
- `test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts`'s `history --summary tallies each loop's outcomes over the rows the table would print` expected header gains the `time` column (with the widths `renderSummary` actually computes), its data rows gain the time cell, and its `--result problems` regex gains that cell. Its `--json` total assertion gains `durationMs` only when the seeded rows carry spans.
- `test/gui-client-history.test.ts`'s `histSummaryHtml paints one row per loop plus the total…` header loop gains `"Time"`, and a fixture row with a timed span asserts its `fmtSpan` cell (`60m` for an hour — the page's formatter favors minutes under two hours, so the plan's `1h` expectation applies to the CLI's `humanSeconds`, not the GUI's `fmtSpan`) while one without the field asserts `—`.
- `test/cli-run.test.ts`'s `windowSummary counts every tick once…` header regex gains `time` (an assert on the same summary column set the plan's file list omitted).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Each day's newly filed plans and bugs are counted as `Backlog items opened` — window totals on the day report's totals line and a stacked GUI Usage chart beside `Backlog items done` (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the plain-terms series and of the in-flight `Commits by role` GUI chart, which shares `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts` but adds a different builder and render-chain slot; the in-flight plain-terms part 11f rewrites comments in `src/backlog/backlog.ts` while this adds one function there, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/backlog/backlog.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts, docs/cli.md, test/report-data.test.ts, test/report.test.ts and test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The day report and the dashboard show what the team finished each day (`featuresDone`/`bugsFixed`, folded from the `## Done`/`## Fixed` completion stamps and drawn as the stacked `Backlog items done` GUI chart), but never what was filed each day, so an operator cannot read net progress (opened vs done) — only the current open-backlog count in the status header. Every backlog entry already carries a filing stamp in its heading: `planned DATE` for plans, `reported DATE`/`found by <role> DATE` for bugs, parsed by `filingDate` (`src/backlog/backlog.ts`) for `plan|bug --list`'s age suffix. Collect those stamps per day into two new day fields, print their window totals on the day report's totals line, and draw a stacked `Backlog items opened` chart beside `Backlog items done`.

**Approach.** One theme, three sites; no event-log or `/api` change (the fields ride the `/api/report` JSON the Usage view already renders).

1. `src/backlog/backlog.ts`: add `sectionFilingDates(root, fileName, sectionTitle): string[]`, the filing-stamp twin of `sectionCompletionDates` beside it — same stat-cached `dateCache` and `cachedTextByStat` shape, same `entryDates(md, sectionTitle, dateRe)` call, but with the module's private `STAMP_DATE_RE` (`(?:planned|reported|found by)\b[^)]*?\b(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})`) as the date regex, a distinct cache key (e.g. `` `${file}\u0000${sectionTitle}\u0000planned` ``), and a doc comment naming it the per-day filing twin of the completion read. Reusing `entryDates` keeps entry detection symmetric with `featuresDone`/`bugsFixed` (a `- ` epitaph still needs its `commit` reference), so an entry counted as done and one counted as opened use the same start/detection rule.
2. `src/report/report-data.ts`:
   - Add two optional `ReportDay` fields beside `featuresDone`/`bugsFixed`: `plansAdded?: number` (PLANS.md `## Planned` + `## Done` filing dates) and `bugsFiled?: number` (BUGS.md `## Open` + `## Fixed` filing dates), documented as zero-means-absent like the newer optional fields, so a day with none carries no key and the existing exact-shape assertions stay green.
   - Extend the `countOn` helper's `field` union to all four field names and make its increment create the key on first count: `day[field] = (day[field] ?? 0) + 1` (`featuresDone`/`bugsFixed` are still initialized to 0 in the day factory, so their behavior is unchanged).
   - Inside the existing `if (role === undefined)` backlog block (role scope leaves day-granular file tallies at zero), fold the filing dates: `sectionFilingDates(root, "PLANS.md", "Planned")` and `("PLANS.md", "Done")` through `countOn(d, "plansAdded")`; `sectionFilingDates(root, "BUGS.md", "Open")` and `("BUGS.md", "Fixed")` through `countOn(d, "bugsFiled")`.
   - Add `plansAdded?`/`bugsFiled?` to `ReportTotals`, folded with local accumulators over the series and set only when > 0 (`...(plansAdded > 0 ? { plansAdded } : {})`), exactly as `notionalCostUsd`/`mergeFailed` are.
3. `src/report/report-render.ts`, `renderReportMarkdown`: extend the totals-line `tail` after `N features done · M bugs fixed`, gated on the window having any, so a window with no filing stamps renders exactly as before: `+ ((t.plansAdded ?? 0) + (t.bugsFiled ?? 0) > 0 ? ` · ${t.plansAdded ?? 0} plans added · ${t.bugsFiled ?? 0} bugs filed` : "")`. `renderSinceReportMarkdown` passes no tail (its totals already omit the day-granular backlog cells), so it is unchanged.
4. `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`, `report-chart` region and `usage` render chain:
   - Add `chartBacklogItemsOpened(data)` beside `chartBacklogItems`, the same `reportSvg(data.series, (d) => [...], countAxis, true)` two-series shape: `{ value: Number(d.plansAdded) || 0, color: "#6366f1", title: d.date + ": " + plural(Number(d.plansAdded) || 0, "plan") + " added" }` and `{ value: Number(d.bugsFiled) || 0, color: "#ef4444", title: d.date + ": " + plural(Number(d.bugsFiled) || 0, "bug") + " filed" }` — the same two colors as `chartBacklogItems`, so opened and done read as a pair.
   - Add `seriesHasBacklogAdded(data)` mirroring `seriesHasBacklogItems`: `data.series.some((d) => Number(d.plansAdded) > 0 || Number(d.bugsFiled) > 0)`.
   - In the `usage` render chain, insert `(seriesHasBacklogAdded(d) ? block("Backlog items opened", chartBacklogItemsOpened(d), "per day · plans added + bugs filed") : "")` immediately before the existing `block("Backlog items done", …)` term. A role-scoped series zeroes the tallies, so the gate hides it there, mirroring `Backlog items done`.
5. `docs/cli.md`: in the `tumwater report` row, name the new totals cells (the workflow/maintenance split clause becomes "the work/maintenance split, the window's newly filed plans and bugs").

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/report-data.test.ts`, `test/report.test.ts`, `test/gui-client-report.test.ts`.

- New test in `test/report-data.test.ts`, modelled on ``collectReport counts features done and bugs fixed from backlog history``: with `d1 = dayKey(at(4))`, `d2 = dayKey(at(3))`, `d3 = dayKey(at(2))`, write a PLANS.md whose `## Planned` holds `### Open plan (planned <d1>)` and whose `## Done` holds `### Closed plan (planned <d2>, done <d3>)`, and a BUGS.md whose `## Open` holds `### Open bug (found by qa loop <d1>)` and whose `## Fixed` holds `### Fixed bug (reported <d2>, fixed <d3>)`. ### The GUI Usage view charts each day's `Commits by role` as a stacked per-role element, the per-role split of the `Merged commits` total (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the in-flight `Merged by role` chart and of the plain-terms comment parts 11b/11 and 11e/11 — a different builder, seed line and render-chain slot in the same file, so all three land in any order; touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

Add one stacked `Commits by role` chart beside `Merged commits`, the dashboard twin of the CLI line.

This is not the same series as the in-flight `Merged by role` chart: `commitsByRole` counts `merged` events (`merge-stack.ts` emits one per change in a stacked fast-forward, `src/merge/merge-stack.ts`) while `mergedByRole` counts `merge_done` events (one per merge run, `src/merge/merge-slot.ts`), so the two charts answer different questions — which commits, versus which merge outcomes — and both are worth a tile.

**Approach.** All changes are in the `report-chart` region of `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts` and the `usage` view's render chain in the same file; no server or `report-data.ts` change — `commitsByRole` already rides the `/api/report` JSON the view renders.

   `for (const role of Object.keys(d.commitsByRole || {})) if (!Object.hasOwn(byRole, role)) byRole[role] = 0;`.

   keyed by loop id (`feature-2`) while `commitsByRole` is base-role keyed (`feature`), so a
   role that merged only through an instance would otherwise get no colour or legend entry.

   `chartCommitsByRole(data)` built through `roleStackChart`:
   `return roleStackChart(data, "commitsByRole", (n) => plural(n, "commit"), countAxis, true);`
   with a comment naming it the day's merged commits per base role, the per-role split of the
   `Merged commits` total it sits beside (same `roleStackChart` shape, palette, legend order
   and integer count axis as the other role charts).
3. In the `usage` view's render chain, insert
   `block("Commits by role", chartCommitsByRole(d)) +`
   immediately after the existing `block("Merged commits", chartCommits(d)) +` term. No
   `seriesHasAny` gate: the collector pre-fills the map on every day (a commit-free day
   carries an empty map), and the sibling total charts render unconditionally, so the block
   matches them.

### The dashboard composer recalls recently sent prompts with Up and Down, restoring the draft you were typing — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The composer keeps one unsent draft per target (`drafts`), but a sent prompt is gone:
re-sending a nudge means retyping it. The TUI's prompt line recalls recent prompts
(`tui-prompt-history.ts`); give the dashboard composer the same recall — Up steps back through
the prompts you have sent, Down steps forward and restores the draft you were typing.

**Approach.** All changes are inside the `gui-client-composer` blob in
`src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts`, beside the existing `drafts`/`promptInput`/keydown/submit
code; no server or page change.

1. Beside `drafts` add the recall state: `const promptHistory = [];` (oldest first, the text of
   each successfully sent prompt), `let recallIndex = null;` (null means the live draft, an
   index means browsing `promptHistory`), `let recallDraft = "";` (the live draft saved when
   browsing starts), and `const PROMPT_HISTORY_MAX = 50;`.
2. Add one helper, `recallSentPrompt(step)` where `step` is `-1` for Up and `1` for Down, that
   returns true when it changed the box. Up with `recallIndex === null` saves
   `recallDraft = promptInput.value` and moves to the newest entry; otherwise it steps one older
   while it can. Down at the newest restores `recallDraft` and resets `recallIndex` to null.
   Down while already live is a no-op. On a change it sets `promptInput.value` to the entry (or
   `recallDraft`), then calls `autosize()`, `updateCount()` and
   `promptInput.setSelectionRange(value.length, value.length)` so the recalled text is ready to
   send. Doc it as the composer's mirror of the TUI's `recallPromptHistory`.
3. In the existing `promptInput.addEventListener("keydown", …)`, add an `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`
   arm: when `!ev.isComposing` and (scouting already browsing, or the current value has no
   newline — `recallIndex !== null || !promptInput.value.includes("\n")`), call
   `recallSentPrompt(ev.key === "ArrowUp" ? -1 : 1)` and `ev.preventDefault()` when it returns
   true. The newline guard applies to the live draft only: a recalled multi-line entry keeps
   its Up/Down recallable (Down always walks back to the saved draft), while an untouched
   multi-line draft keeps the textarea's own Up/Down line movement, like the TUI keeps its
   arrows for other panes.
4. Record a send in the existing submit handler's success path (the code after the
   `try`/`finally` that is reached only when the server accepted the prompt, where the input is
   cleared): push the trimmed `text` unless it equals `promptHistory`'s last entry, drop the
   oldest entry past `PROMPT_HISTORY_MAX`, and reset `recallIndex = null; recallDraft = "";`.
   On `setTarget`, hand the saved draft to the old target's slot when a switch happens
   mid-recall (`drafts[promptTarget] = recallIndex !== null ? recallDraft : promptInput.value`,
   the TUI's `settlePromptRecall` swap) and reset `recallIndex`/`recallDraft`, so a target swap
   never saves the recalled entry over the unsent draft or discards it; `draftForDirector`
   resets the same two after routing through `setTarget`, so a prefilled answer is never left
   mid-recall.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts`, `test/gui-client-composer.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-client-composer.test.ts`: a new test "the composer recalls sent prompts with Up and
  Down and restores the live draft", modelled on the existing submit test. Submit `first`, then
  `second` (the `s.fire(s.form(), "submit", SUBMIT)` + `await s.flush()` pattern), type
  `draft in progress`, then fire `keydown` `ArrowUp`: the box reads `second`; a second `ArrowUp`
  reads `first`; a third stays `first` (the oldest end); `ArrowDown` reads `second`; a second
  `ArrowDown` restores `draft in progress`; a third is a no-op. `preventDefault` was called on
  each recall. With the value `line one\nline two`, `ArrowUp` leaves it unchanged and does not
  call `preventDefault`. Submitting the same text twice in a row adds one history entry (one
  `ArrowUp` reaches it, the next stays).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Each day's red full-suite merge checks are counted in the `tumwater report` day report (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the plain-terms series and of the in-flight problems-only Health view plan; the report half of a red-check signal whose GUI chart is left to a later plan, as the project did for `Merge check median`; touches src/build/build-check-events.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The day report shows `**Merge check median:**` — how long the passing full-suite
merge checks took — but not how often that check went red. A flaky or broken suite is the
team's biggest merge bottleneck: a red merge check keeps its pin and retries, so it usually
produces no `merge_failed` and no `Merge failures by role` row, and the median happily reports
a fast pass on a day when half the checks failed first. Count each day's failed full-suite
`build_check` events (the merge, batch and baseline scopes `isPassingFullCheck` already
counts) and print them as a `**Red merge checks:**` line beside the medians, so a spike shows
a flaky or broken suite without reading the failure digest.

**Approach.**

1. `src/build/build-check-events.ts`: add `export function isRedFullCheck(ev: HarnessEvent): boolean`
   right after `isPassingFullCheck` (line 23). Body:
   `ev.type === "build_check" && ev.status === "failed" && ["merge", "batch", "baseline"].includes(String(ev.scope))`.
   Doc it as the red sibling of `isPassingFullCheck`: the same three scopes and the failed
   status; a `skipped` check made no verdict about the tree, and a merge-scope timeout is
   already remapped to `failed` by `runScopedBuildCheck` (`MERGE_SCOPES`), so `failed` alone is
   the rule. The two predicates are mutually exclusive on `status`, so the fold branch below
   never sees the other's events.
2. `src/report/report-data.ts`:
   - `UsageFold` (starts line 37): add `checkFailures: number;` beside `checkDurationsMs`, with
     a doc comment: a count of failed full-suite build_check events (`isRedFullCheck`), so a day
     whose checks went red before passing is visible beside its passing-check median.
   - `foldUsageEvent` (line 121): after the `isPassingFullCheck(ev)` branch that pushes
     `checkDurationsMs`, add `else if (isRedFullCheck(ev)) { target.checkFailures++; }` with a
     one-line comment, and import `isRedFullCheck` beside `isPassingFullCheck`.
   - `DayFold` (line 199): add `checkFailures: number;` beside `checkDurationsMs`.
   - `dayFoldFor` (line 308): initialize `checkFailures: 0,` beside `checkDurationsMs: []`.
   - `collectReportSince`'s `acc` initializer (line ~603): initialize `checkFailures: 0,`
     beside `checkDurationsMs: []` (the field is part of `UsageFold`, so the shape must satisfy
     it).
   - `ReportDay` (line ~420): add
     `/** Failed full-suite build_check events that day (isRedFullCheck); absent when the day has none (zero means absent). */ checkFailures?: number;`
     beside `checkMedianMs`.
   - The day assembly's team branch (beside
     `if (fold.checkDurationsMs.length > 0) day.checkMedianMs = …`, line ~731): add
     `if (fold.checkFailures > 0) day.checkFailures = fold.checkFailures;`. Leave the
     role-scoped branch alone — checks belong to the merge slot, so a scoped series carries
     none, exactly like `checkMedianMs`.
3. `src/report/report-render.ts`: in the team branch of `renderReportMarkdown`, right after the
   `**Merge check median:**` push (line ~293), push a `**Red merge checks:**` line when any day
   has `checkFailures`, each day rendered `${monthDay(d.date)} ×${d.checkFailures}` and joined
   with ` · `. Zero-absent: no line when no day carries the field.
4. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater report` parenthetical (line 47), extend the
   merge-check clause to say the team report also names each day's count of red full-suite
   merge checks beside the merge check median.

**Files touched.** `src/build/build-check-events.ts`, `src/report/report-data.ts`,
`src/report/report-render.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/build-check-events.test.ts`,
`test/report-data.test.ts`, `test/report.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

### Plain terms code merge, part 11a/11: Rewrite the merge family in the pipeline modules' comments (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; split 2026-10-17 by the plan role from part 11/11, siblings parts 11b/11, 11c/11 and 11d/11; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches comments in src/merge/ src/events/ src/review/ src/verdict/ src/git/ src/tick/ src/failure/ src/change/ src/build/ src/process/ and src/loop/) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

### Split the TUI prompt-line editor monolith `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` into per-editor modules beside a shared prompt-line session (planned 2026-10-17 by the organize role; the natural second half of the landed "split the TUI key-handling monolith" series — part 1/2 made `tui-editors` the prompt-line editors and part 2/2 split the pane state into `tui-panes`, both merged 2026-10-16, so the single largest source file left is this one factory closure. Independent of every other Planned entry. It touches only `src/ui/tui/` and the existing `test/tui-*.test.ts` suites; the in-flight Health tab plan edits `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`/`tui-panes.ts` and `src/ui/gui/`, not `tui-editors.ts`, so the two do not overlap) — done 2026-10-17

**Why.** `tui-editors.ts` is 1121 lines, the largest source file in the repo at ~5.8× the ~193-line median, and it is one factory closure, `createTuiEditors`, that owns the one shared prompt line (`input`/`cursor`/`promptHistory`) plus eight mutually-exclusive modal editors — budget Ctrl+B, per-role prompt Ctrl+R, defer Ctrl+L, pause Ctrl+F/stop/wake, the inbox row's in-place editor Ctrl+E, the backlog answer editor Ctrl+A, the backlog new-entry/title editor Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N, and the `/` search editor — each with its own saved-draft pair, exit helper, and handleKey arms, all tangled in one ~700-line `handleKey`. A reviewer cannot hold one editor's behavior (its key, its pre-fill, its Enter/Esc guards) without the whole file. Part 2/2 of the monolith split already cut the pane side; this is the same split applied to the editor side, so each modal editor has one module boundary. This is a restructure only; it changes no behavior.

**Goal.** `createTuiEditors` becomes a thin aggregator. The shared mutable prompt line moves into one small session module, and each modal editor becomes its own module owning its mode flag, saved-draft pair, exit helper, and the handleKey arms for its keys. The mutually-exclusive invariants the file currently states "hold here once, at the module boundary" move into the session module, which exposes the shared `input`/`cursor`/`promptHistory`, `restorePromptFrom`, `settleDraft`, `busyFlash`, `heldEditorFlash`, and the exit-all routine.

**Approach.** Restructure only, no behavior change. Move code verbatim wherever possible; `test/tui-*.test.ts` (tui-budget, tui-role-prompt, tui-keys, tui-frame, tui-input, tui-prompt-history, tui-reload, tui-notebook, tui-operator-keys, tui-history, tui-backlog) is the regression net. Suggested target modules, all under `src/ui/tui/`:
- **`tui-editor-session.ts`** — the shared prompt line. Owns `input`, `cursor`, `promptHistory` and the shared helpers `restorePromptFrom`, `settleDraft`, `busyFlash`, `heldEditorFlash` and `exitAll` (which today just calls every per-editor exit helper in order). Exposes a plain mutable session object and the shared deps (`root`, `now`, `flat`, `flashMessage`, `flashError`, `commitBacklogEdit`) so the editor modules take only the session + the per-key `TuiEditorCtx`, not the whole `TuiEditorsDeps`.
- **`tui-editor-budget.ts`** and **`tui-editor-defer.ts`** — the budget Ctrl+B and defer Ctrl+L editors; each owns its mode flag, its saved-pair, `exitBudgetMode`/`exitDeferMode`, and the arms for its key (including its `heldEditorFlash(entering)` guard clause, which keeps the shared guard priority in the session module).
- **`tui-editor-prompt.ts`** — the per-role prompt Ctrl+R editor with its own saved pair and exit helper.
- **`tui-editor-pause.ts`** — the pause/stop/wake editor Ctrl+F (team) and per-loop pause/wake, owning `pauseEditMode`/`pauseEditRole`/`pauseEditWake`/`pauseEditStop`, its save pair, and the parse/dispatch leaves (`parsePauseInput`, `parseRolePauseInput`, `parseStopInInput`, `parseRoleWakeInput`, `parseBudgetInput` sits with budget).
- **`tui-editor-queued.ts`** — the inbox row's in-place editor Ctrl+E, owning `queuedEditFor` + pair and the `readQueuedPromptBody`/`editQueuedFile` arms.
- **`tui-editor-answer.ts`** — the backlog answer editor Ctrl+A, owning `answerFor` + pair and the `tryAnswerQuestion` arm.
- **`tui-editor-entry.ts`** — the backlog new-entry/title editor Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N, owning `entryEditFor` + pair, its plan↔bug flip, the `fileEntryWithBody`/`commitBacklogEdit` arms, and the position math that counts `plan`/`bug` labels.
- **`tui-editor-search.ts`** — the `/` search editor, owning `searchMode`, `searchFor`, its pair, and the `applyHistorySearch`/`applyActivitySearch` arms.
- **`tui-editors.ts`** shrinks to the aggregator: build the session, register the editors, and expose the unchanged `TuiEditors` surface. Its `handleKey` routes each key to the editors in today's priority order (each module returns true when it consumed the key and false to fall through, so the mutually-exclusive/busy-guard ordering is preserved exactly); `state()` returns `{ input, cursor, budgetMode, rolePromptFor, deferMode, defer, pauseEditMode, pauseEditRole, pauseEditWake, pauseEditStop, queuedEditFor, searchMode, answerFor, entryEditFor }` exactly as today; `onArrow`/`apply`/`exitAll`/`sync` move with the session or stay as the aggregator's thin tail. `TuiEditors`, `TuiEditorCtx`, `TuiEditorsDeps` and every `TuiEditorState` field name and type stay unchanged.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` (shrinks) and the new `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-*.ts` modules above. `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` (which scans the editor source for the Ctrl keys the docs table must name) got its hardcoded file list extended to the new per-editor modules; the rest of `test/tui-*.test.ts` (which covers these editors through the `TuiKeys` surface) passes unmodified.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `TuiEditors`, `TuiEditorCtx`, `TuiEditorsDeps`, and every `TuiEditorState` field name and type are unchanged; `createTuiKeys` in `tui-keys.ts` and `tui.tsx`/`tui-app.tsx` pass unmodified.
- Every editor consumes and leaves the prompt line exactly as today: the same keys open it, the same Esc/repeat-key exits it, the same saved draft is restored byte-for-byte, and the busy-guard flash wording and priority are unchanged.
- No behavior change: `npm run test` passes, with `test/tui-*.test.ts` unmodified (apart from the `tui-keys-doc` scan list) as the regression net.

### `tumwater doctor --problems` prints only the warn and fail rows (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor` now prints well over 50 rows and a routing table. On a healthy team
almost every row is `ok`, so the one `warn` that explains a slow or stuck team is easy to miss.
Add `--problems` so the operator sees only what needs attention: the header, the warn and fail
rows, one line counting the hidden ok rows, and the verdict. The checks that run, the exit-code
contract, and the default output stay as they are. This is independent of the plain-terms
series. Its only overlap with the in-flight merge rename part 10/11 is the few lines of the
`doctor` case in `src/cli.ts`.

**Approach.**
1. `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`: add `export const PROBLEMS_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--problems"] };`
   beside `REPROBE_FLAG`. Give it a doc comment in the same style: a value-less flag accepted by
   `doctor`.
2. `src/doctor/doctor-render.ts`:
   - Pull the check-row loop out of `renderDoctor` into a private
     `checkLines(checks: DoctorReport["checks"]): string[]`. It keeps the current name-column
     rule: the width is the longest name, at least 12. `renderDoctor`'s output must stay
     byte-for-byte the same; the existing `renderDoctor` tests in `test/doctor.test.ts` pin
     this.
   - Add `export function problemsOnly(report: DoctorReport): DoctorReport`. It returns
     `{ ...report, checks: report.checks.filter((c) => c.level !== "ok") }`, keeping header,
     routing, and verdict unchanged. `--problems --json` prints this.
   - Add `export function renderDoctorProblems(report: DoctorReport): string`, which takes the
     full report. It prints the header, then `checkLines` over the non-ok checks (their width is
     computed over the shown rows only), then the line
     `<n> ok checks hidden — run tumwater doctor for the full report` (singular `check` when
     n is 1, using `plural` from `src/text/phrases.ts`; the line is left out when n
     is 0), then the verdict. It never prints the routing table. A report with no warn or fail
     rows prints the header, the hidden-count line, and `ready to run`.
3. `src/cli.ts`, `case "doctor"`: add `PROBLEMS_FLAG` to the `rejectUnknownArgs` list. With
   `--problems`, call `sayJsonOrRender(args, args.includes("--json") ? problemsOnly(report) : report, renderDoctorProblems)`.
   `sayJsonOrRender` in `src/cli/cli-output.ts` takes one payload, so the JSON branch gets the
   filtered report and the render gets the full one. Without the flag the call is unchanged.
   The exit-code line keeps reading the full `report`.
4. `src/cli/help.ts`: change the usage line to `tumwater doctor [--json] [--reprobe] [--problems]`
   and add one sentence to the stanza: `--problems prints only the warn and fail rows (and how
   many ok rows it hid), the same verdict and exit code; with --json the checks array holds
   only those rows`. Shell completion reads its words from this usage line through
   `usageWords` in `src/cli/completion.ts`, so it needs no edit.
5. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` parenthetical, add `--problems` after the
   `--json` clause with the same meaning.

**Files touched.** `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-render.ts`, `src/cli.ts`,
`src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/doctor.test.ts`.

### `tumwater doctor` says how long merges waited over the last 24 h, from enqueue to merged on main (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater report` now shows each day's median merge wait, and `tumwater doctor` says how
long passing merge checks took over the last 24 h. But doctor, the pre-flight an operator runs
when the team feels slow, says nothing about how long finished work waited to reach main. Its
"stale merge-queue entries" row only warns about one entry stuck for 6 hours. Add a 24 h
merge-wait phrase to that row. It is information only and adds no new warning threshold.
Independent of the plain-terms series: it touches only `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, its test,
and docs/cli.md.

**Approach.**
1. `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`: add an exported
   `mergeWaitPhrase(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): string | undefined` beside
   `checkStaleQueuedMerges`, modelled on `checkDurationPhrase` in `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`.
   - It takes `merge_done` events only, mapped through `finiteNumber(ev.queuedMs, 0)` and kept
     when > 0. A merge logged before `queuedMs` existed is skipped, the same rule as
     `foldUsageEvent` in `src/report/report-data.ts`. A `merge_failed` is not a wait that
     ended on main.
   - It sorts the values and takes the lower median, `values[Math.floor((n - 1) / 2)]`, and the
     longest.
   - It returns `merges in the last 24h waited <median> median, <longest> longest (<plural(n,
     "merge")>)`, with spans from `shortSpanPhrase` and `plural` from `src/text/phrases.ts`.
     It returns undefined when no event qualifies.
   - Its doc comment says the wait runs from the entry's last enqueue to its outcome and
     includes the merge check.
2. `checkStaleQueuedMerges(root, now)`: read
   `readEventsSince(root, MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS).events`, already imported in this file, and keep
   `ev.ts >= now - MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS`. `MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 3600_000` is a new module
   constant. Pass the result to `mergeWaitPhrase`. When it returns a phrase, append
   ` · <phrase>` to the detail of both the ok and the warn outcome. Wrap the read in try/catch.
   On an error, omit the phrase and keep the outcome otherwise unchanged, so an unreadable event
   log never changes this row's level. Leave the level rules, the row name in
   `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, and every existing detail text as they are.
3. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` description, after "the declared check
   and how long its passing merge checks took over the last 24 h", add "how long merges waited
   from enqueue to merged on main over the last 24 h (median and longest)".

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts` has a new test, "mergeWaitPhrase reports the lower median and
  longest of merge_done waits". Given `merge_done` events with `queuedMs` 60_000, 180_000 and
  600_000, it asserts the result equals
  `merges in the last 24h waited ${shortSpanPhrase(180_000)} median, ${shortSpanPhrase(600_000)} longest (3 merges)`.
  With two values it asserts the lower one is the median. It also checks that `merge_failed`
  events, `merge_done` events without `queuedMs` or with 0, and other event types give
  `undefined`.
- Another new test, "checkStaleQueuedMerges appends the last 24h merge wait to its detail",
  writes events with `logEvent` into a `queueRoot()`: two `merge_done` events with `queuedMs`
  within the window and one with `ts` 48 h ago. It asserts that the ok detail ends with
  ` · merges in the last 24h waited … (2 merges)`, so the 48 h-old one is excluded. It also
  asserts that a stale entry's warn detail carries the same suffix and stays `warn`.
- The existing `checkStaleQueuedMerges` tests pass unchanged. With no `merge_done` in the
  window, the detail has no ` · merges` suffix.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `plan|bug --list --done` and `questions --answered` take `--grep <text>` to find an old finished entry by its text (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** PLANS.md ## Done, BUGS.md ## Fixed, and QUESTIONS.md ## Answered keep every finished
entry, and they grow by several a day. The CLI shows only the newest N, and `-n` widens the
list without searching it. So "did we already do X?" or "how was that bug fixed?" means
scrolling hundreds of titles or grepping the raw file. Add a `--grep <text>` filter to the three
finished-entry lists, matching like `history --grep` and `logs --grep` do (case-insensitive
substring). Each match keeps its number from the unfiltered newest-first list, so the
number printed beside a match is the one `--show <n> --done` / `--show <n> --answered` takes.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: in the arg loop, accept `--grep <text>` once
   (`rejectRepeatFlag`; take `args[++i]`, and when it is missing or empty, fail with
   `--grep needs text (usage: tumwater <command> --list --done --grep <text>)`). After the
   loop, fail with `--grep needs --done (it searches the finished entries)` when `--grep` is
   given without `--done`, beside the existing `-n needs --done` check. In the `done`
   branch: number `all` first (`{ entry, position: i + 1 }`). Then, when a pattern is set,
   keep only the entries whose `` `${title}\n${body}` `` lowercased includes the lowercased
   pattern. Then apply the limit (`count ?? 10`) to the matches. `older` counts matches left
   out, not all entries. Prose lines print `${position}. ${title}`, not `i + 1`.
   With a pattern and no match, print `no ${what} match "<text>"`. With a pattern, the
   header reads `${what} in ${fileName} matching "<text>", newest first:`. The trailing
   hint keeps its form but names the match count (`-n ${matches.length} shows more`).
   `--json` entries gain `position` (the unfiltered number) with or without a pattern,
   and `older` counts matches left out. Without `--grep`, every prose line and key the
   command prints today is unchanged. Update the function's doc comment.
2. `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`: give `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst` an optional
   `pattern?: string` and have it return each kept entry with its unfiltered newest-first
   `position`, filtered by the same title+body case-insensitive substring rule.
   `answeredQuestionList(root, count, pattern?)` prints `${position}. …` and, with a pattern,
   the header `answered questions in QUESTIONS.md matching "<text>", newest first:`, or
   `no answered questions match "<text>"` when none do.
   `answeredQuestionPayload(root, count, pattern?)` gives each question its `position`.
   `answeredQuestionAt` is unchanged.
   Put the one matcher in `src/backlog/backlog.ts` as an exported
   `entryMatches(entry: BacklogEntry, pattern: string): boolean`, used by both files.
3. `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdQuestions`: accept `--grep <text>` under the same
   `!numbered` guard as `-n` (once; a missing or empty value fails like step 1's). Add
   `--grep` to the unknown-argument error's flag list and to the `rejectEqualsForm`
   specs. Fail with `--grep needs --answered (it searches the answered questions)` when
   `--grep` is given without `--answered`, and refuse it beside `--show`. Pass the pattern
   to `answeredQuestionList`/`answeredQuestionPayload`.
4. `src/cli/help.ts`: add `[--grep <text>]` to the `bug --list --done`, `plan --list --done`,
   and `questions --answered` stanzas, with one line saying it keeps the entries whose
   heading or body contains the text, case-insensitively, numbered as without it.
   `docs/cli.md`: name `--grep` in the Steer row's `--list --done` clause and the Answer
   row's `--answered` clause.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`,
`src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`,
`docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`: a new test beside "plan --list --done lists the newest
  done plans, and bug --list --done an empty Fixed". From a ## Done holding entries whose
  bodies (not only titles) carry a word in mixed case: `plan --list --done --grep <word>`
  prints only the matching entries, each under its unfiltered number. The `--show <n> --done`
