### `tumwater doctor` warns when a recently Fixed bug's quoted test has failed again since its fix and no Open bug names that test (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts and test/doctor.test.ts; no src/merge, src/tick, src/backlog or src/ui edit)

**Goal.** BUGS.md's ## Fixed section holds flake bugs whose headings quote the test name. Two of today's are `"runGit SIGKILLs a git that ignores SIGTERM, taking its grandchild with it"` (fixed 2026-10-16) and `"a later wake request leaves a pending scheduled wake standing"` (fixed 2026-10-14). When such a test fails again, nothing links the failure to the Fixed record. The open `startParentDeathWatch` bug was filed by hand, after its 10-01 and 10-09 Fixed entries, when an operator session happened to read improve's red merge check. `checkWaitingBugs` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts) already does this matching for Open bugs that carry a Waiting note: `quotedTestName` on the heading, then `failureMentions` over the event log since the day after the note. This plan applies the same matching to the newest Fixed records. It adds one doctor row, `regressed fixes`, which warns when a Fixed record's quoted test has failed since the day after its fix and no Open bug quotes the same test. Like every backlog check, it is a warn, never a fail, and doctor writes nothing to BUGS.md.

**Approach.** All logic is in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
- Extract the inline day-after computation in `checkWaitingBugs` (the `new Date(Number(date.slice(0, 4)), Number(date.slice(5, 7)) - 1, Number(date.slice(8, 10)) + 1).getTime()` expression) into an unexported `dayAfterMs(date: string): number` (local midnight after a `YYYY-MM-DD`). `checkWaitingBugs` calls it, and its behaviour is unchanged.
- Add an exported `checkRegressedFixes(root: string): CheckOutcome`:
  - Read BUGS.md with `readDocChecked(…, "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify")`, as `checkFixClaims` does.
  - Take `fixedEntries(doc).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)`, the same newest-10 window `checkFixClaims` uses and for the same reason: older records drift.
  - For each record, `name = quotedTestName(entry.title)` and `date = lastDate(entry.title, /(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/)` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts; the last date in the heading is the fix date in both heading shapes, `— fixed 2026-10-14` and `(fixed 2026-10-16)`). Skip a record whose `name` or `date` is null, or whose `dayAfterMs(date)` is NaN.
  - Skip a record when an Open bug's heading quotes the same test: `openBugEntries(root).some((e) => quotedTestName(e.title) === name)`. The regression is then already filed. This is why the open startParentDeathWatch bug stops the Fixed 10-09 record from warning.
  - When any record is left, read events once with `readEventsSince(root, Math.max(0, Date.now() - <earliest since>))`, exactly as `checkWaitingBugs` does. Keep the records where `failureMentions(events, name, since)` is non-empty, and remember each one's newest mention.
  - None left: `okOutcome("no recently Fixed bug's quoted test has failed since its fix")`.
  - Otherwise, warn on the first in file order (newest-first), with `andMore` over the rest (`#`-less, `"${truncate(title, FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX)}"`): `BUGS.md Fixed record "<title truncated to FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX>" quotes a test that failed again after its <date> fix (<formatTimestamp(ts)>: <truncate(text, REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX)>)<more> — file it as a new bug with \`tumwater bug\`, quoting the test name and citing the Fixed record`.
- Update the comment on `checkWaitingBugs`/`failureMentions` only where it says the matching serves Waiting bugs alone. Give `checkRegressedFixes` its own doc comment in the style of its neighbours.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import `checkRegressedFixes` and add `{ name: "regressed fixes", ...checkRegressedFixes(root) }` directly after the `"waiting bugs"` row.
- Out of scope: auto-filing or reopening the bug (doctor stays read-only), Fixed records older than the newest 10, one-line compressed records (`fixedEntries` returns `###` entries), and any team alert or dashboard change (dashboards already show doctor rows).

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, a fixture like `recurrenceRoot` writes a BUGS.md with an empty `## Open` and a `## Fixed` entry `### \`test/x.test.ts\` "${FLAKY_TEST}" flaked (found by bugfix <5 days ago>) — fixed <N days ago>`, and logs a `warning` event `${FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX}<failure>`:
  - N = 2 with failure `✖ ${FLAKY_TEST}`: `checkRegressedFixes` is `warn`, and the detail contains `failed again after its`, the failure text, and `tumwater bug`;
  - N = 0 (same-day failure): ok;
  - N = 2 with an unrelated failure: ok;
  - N = 2 with an Open entry whose heading quotes the same `FLAKY_TEST`: ok;
  - a Fixed heading with no quoted span of 12 or more characters, or with no date: ok;
  - no BUGS.md: ok with `no BUGS.md — nothing to verify`;
  - two regressed Fixed records: the warn names the first and carries the `andMore` count.
- The existing `checkWaitingBugs` tests pass unchanged after the `dayAfterMs` extraction.
- test/doctor.test.ts's row-name list gains `"regressed fixes"` right after `"waiting bugs"`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Staging asks a bugfix run that adds a Progress note to an open bug, but leaves no Waiting for the next failure note under it, to write that note (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/tick/stage-check.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and test/stage-check.test.ts; no src/merge, src/backlog, src/ui or src/doctor edit)

**Goal.** Step 2 of bugfix's find text (src/roles/role-catalog.ts, the `bugfix` entry) says that when a bug cannot be reproduced, the run records a Progress note, writes `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE` (src/roles/role-guidance.ts) as its own line under the heading, and ends. The note's hold then stops later bugfix runs from re-investigating without new evidence. Runs skip the second half. The open BUGS.md entry for the `startParentDeathWatch` flake gained four `**Progress 2026-10-16 (bugfix…)**` notes on one day. The fourth was a BUGS.md-only "no repro, no code change" run. None of them wrote the Waiting note, so the bug stayed eligible and each run spent a tick, a review and a landing. This plan adds a staging finding (the same one fix-up turn the other findings get, src/tick/tick-stage.ts) for a bugfix run whose diff adds a Progress note to an entry that stays under `## Open` with no Waiting note. The finding is advisory: the change commits and queues either way, and the gate does not run it (like `planDependencyFinding`).

**Approach.** All code is in `src/tick/stage-check.ts`:
- Add a pure, exported `waitingNoteFinding(head: string, base: string): string | undefined`. `head` is the edited BUGS.md and `base` is its text at the merge-base.
  - Parse both with `parseEntryDetails(text, "Open")` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts, already imported). Pair entries by `entryKey(title)` (src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts). Skip a head entry with no base entry: a newly filed bug is not a re-investigation.
  - Count the entry's Progress lines: lines whose trimmed text matches `/^-\s+\*\*Progress\b/`. That is the form today's open entry uses (`- **Progress 2026-10-16 (bugfix, second):** …`).
  - A head entry counts when its Progress count is greater than its base entry's, `waitingNote(body)` is null, and `refusalNote(body)` is null (both from src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts).
  - Return undefined when no entry counts. Otherwise name the first in file order, with `moreSuffix(<number of other counting entries>)` (src/text/phrases.ts, already imported) appended: `BUGS.md bug "<title>" gained a Progress note but stays open with no Waiting for the next failure note — if this run could not reproduce it, add ${WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE} as its own line under the heading so later runs wait for new evidence (bugfix's step 2); if it did reproduce, leave the entry as it is`. Quote `<title>` in full, as `heldMovedFinding` does.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the PLANS.md block, add: when `baseRoleOf(role) === "bugfix"` (src/roles/loop-ids.ts, so `bugfix-2` counts) and `files.includes("BUGS.md")`, read the head with `readTextOrNull` and the base with `fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), "BUGS.md").catch(() => undefined)`, exactly as the PLANS.md block does. Push the finding when it is defined. Every other role is unaffected. A run that moves the bug to `## Fixed` gives no finding, because the entry is no longer under Open in head.
- Update the module header comment: like `planDependencyFinding`, `waitingNoteFinding` is staging-only and bugfix-only.
- docs/how-it-works.md, in the hold-note bullet that begins "A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce": add one sentence. A bugfix run that adds a Progress note to an open bug without writing the note is asked to write it in its staging fix-up turn.
- Out of scope: role ids other than bugfix (selfcheck lifts notes, it does not write them); any gate or in-lock check; changing bugfix's find text.

**Files touched.** src/tick/stage-check.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit tests of `waitingNoteFinding` in test/stage-check.test.ts, over a two-entry `## Open` base where entry A has one Progress line:
  - head adds a second Progress line to A and no Waiting note: the finding names A's title and contains `Waiting for the next failure`;
  - the same head plus a `**Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: x**` line under A: undefined;
  - the same head plus a `**Refused …**` line under A: undefined;
  - head identical to base, or editing A's Symptom line only: undefined;
  - head moving A to `## Fixed` with a new Progress line: undefined;
  - a newly filed entry C carrying a Progress line: undefined;
  - Progress lines added to both A and B: the finding names A and carries the `moreSuffix` count.
- A `stageCheckFindings` test built with `repoWith` (as the "a duplicated ## Done heading" test is): BUGS.md on main has an Open entry with one Progress line, and the worktree adds a second. With role `"bugfix"` and with `"bugfix-2"`, the findings include the Waiting-note finding. With role `"feature"`, they do not.
- The existing stage-check and tick-stage tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` warns when a bug held by a Waiting for the next failure note has failed again, naming the failure and the release command (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md and test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce is held by a `**Waiting for the next failure …**` note until it fails again (docs/how-it-works.md). Two things lift the hold: whoever records a new occurrence deletes the note, or an operator runs `tumwater bug --release <n>`. In practice only selfcheck records occurrences, and selfcheck is opt-in (`roles.selfcheck.enabled`). On a default team, a waiting test can flake again in the gate or the merge check, and the event log records the failure. But nothing connects that failure to the held bug, so the bug stays parked with exactly the evidence it was waiting for. Doctor's `waiting bugs` row (`checkWaitingBugs`) already names each held bug and its release command, and today it always reports ok. This plan makes it warn when a held bug's test has failed in a gate or merge check since the day after its note was written. The warning names the failure and the release command. Doctor stays read-only: it writes nothing to BUGS.md.

**Approach.** All of the change is in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
- Add a pure, exported `quotedTestName(title: string): string | null`. It returns the first span between straight double quotes in a bug heading that is at least 12 characters long (`/"([^"]{12,})"/`), or null. Today's open bug heading quotes its test name this way (`… "startParentDeathWatch takes a SIGKILLed supervisor's grandchild down with it" …`). The test-runner failure line that `failureHeadline` (src/build/build-check-report.ts) puts into flake warnings and rejection reasons carries the same text verbatim, after `✖ `. The 12-character floor stops a short quoted word from matching unrelated failures.
- Add a pure, exported `waitingNoteDate(note: string): string | null`. It returns the first `YYYY-MM-DD` in `waitingNote(entry.body)`'s text, or null.
- Add a pure, exported `failureMentions(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], name: string, sinceMs: number): { ts: number; text: string }[]`. It collects every event with numeric `ts >= sinceMs` that falls under either rule:
  - a `warning` whose string `message` includes `name`. This covers the gate's `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`, the merge check's `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`, and the `merge check failed (kept for one retry): …` warning in src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts.
  - a `review_rejected` event whose `stringList(e.reasons)` (src/files/json-object.ts) has an entry that includes `name`. For this event, `text` is the first such reason.

  Results come back in event order.
- In `checkWaitingBugs`, for each held bug (a waiting note and no refusal note, as today), take `quotedTestName(entry.title)` and `waitingNoteDate(note)`. When both are non-null, compute `since` as local midnight starting the day after the note date. The note carries only a date, so a same-day failure cannot be told apart from the failure the note was written about, and the day after is the conservative cutoff. Read events once per check with `readEventsSince(root, Date.now() - firstSince)` from src/events/event-window.ts, using the earliest `since` across held bugs. Skip the read entirely when no held bug yields both values. A bug with any `failureMentions` has recurred.
- When any held bug recurred, return `warnOutcome`:
  - Text: `BUGS.md bug #<n> "<title>" failed again since its Waiting for the next failure note (<formatTimestamp(ts) of the newest mention>: <truncate(text, REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX)>)<more> — record the occurrence under the entry and release it with \`tumwater bug --release <n>\``.
  - `<more>` uses `andMore` over the other recurred bugs.
  - `formatTimestamp` comes from src/text/datetime.ts.
- With no recurrence, keep today's ok text unchanged.
- Update the function's doc comment: it is now ok, or warn when a held bug's quoted test failed again. A warn is never a fail.
- Docs:
  - docs/how-it-works.md, in the hold-note bullet that begins "A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce": add one sentence saying `tumwater doctor` warns when the held bug's quoted test has failed again in a gate or merge check since the day after the note.
  - docs/cli.md, in the Audit row's waiting-bugs clause (grep `open bugs held by a Waiting`): add "and warning when one has failed again since".
- Out of scope: lifting the note automatically (that is a harness write to BUGS.md, and the note is a human or role decision); matching bugs whose heading quotes no test name; the dashboard and TUI.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `quotedTestName('`test/x.test.ts` "startParentDeathWatch takes a grandchild down" flaked')` returns the quoted name. A heading with no quotes, or only a quoted span shorter than 12 characters, returns null.
- `waitingNoteDate("Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: x")` is `"2026-10-16"`. A note with no date gives null.
- `failureMentions` over synthetic events returns:
  - a gate flake warning, a merge flake warning and a `review_rejected` whose reasons include the name, all at or after `sinceMs`;
  - nothing for an event before `sinceMs`, a warning that does not include the name, or a `review_rejected` with no matching reason.
- `checkWaitingBugs` fixtures in test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, built with `logEvent` the way test/doctor-checks.test.ts's `checkFlakyChecks` tests are:
  - Recurrence: one held bug quotes a test name, its note is dated two days before today (`daysAgoStamp(2)`), and a `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` warning naming the test is logged now. The check returns `level: "warn"`, and the detail contains `failed again`, the warning's text and `tumwater bug --release 1`.
  - Same-day: the same fixture with the note dated today (`daysAgoStamp(0)`) stays ok with today's text.
  - Unrelated: the same fixture with a flake warning that does not include the name stays ok.
- The existing `checkWaitingBugs` and `checkStaleBugs` tests still pass, with no change to their expected text.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's entry drawer offers "Release this entry" on a bug held by a Waiting for the next failure note, as `tumwater bug --release <n>` already does (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts (doc comment), src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests; no src/backlog, src/merge, src/tick or src/ui/tui edit) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A bug carrying a **Waiting for the next failure** note is held from bugfix until someone lifts it. `tumwater bug --release <n>` lifts it, and so does the dashboard's `POST /api/backlog-release`: `tryReleaseEntry` in `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts` goes through `liftRefusal`, which drops a Refused note or, failing that, the waiting note. But the entry drawer never shows the button for a waiting bug. `refreshEntry` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` renders "Release this entry" only when `d.refused` is true, and `handleBacklog` in `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` sends `{ title, body, refused }` with no waiting flag. An operator who sees a waiting bug in the dashboard has to switch to a terminal. Show the button for waiting entries too.

**Approach.**
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` (the `GET /api/backlog?file=&index=` handler that sends `refused: refusalNote(entry.body) !== null`): also send `waiting: waitingNote(entry.body) !== null`. `waitingNote` is already exported from `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts` next to `refusalNote`. Keep `refused` and its meaning as they are. Questions entries get `waiting: false` the same way they get `refused: false`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` `refreshEntry`: render the existing `entry-release` button when `d.refused || d.waiting`. Keep the same markup, label, and position. Use one click, with no arming, as for refused entries.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts` `entry-release` handler: change the `not_refused` toast from "That entry carries no Refused note — refreshed" to "That entry carries no Refused or Waiting note — refreshed". The `not_refused` status name stays as it is, so no payload key is renamed.
- `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts` `handleBacklogRelease` doc comment: say that an entry with neither a Refused nor a Waiting-for-the-next-failure note answers `not_refused`. That is what `liftRefusal` already does, so this is a comment-only change.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Steer row, where `--release <n>` is described, add that the dashboard's plan/bug drawer offers the same release on a refused or waiting entry. Grep for existing wording about the drawer's Release first, and extend it if it is there.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts` "the entry drawer offers Release this entry only on a refused entry" (rename it to "…only on a refused or waiting entry") also covers a fixture `{ title: "Wait", body: "**Waiting for the next failure …**", refused: false, waiting: true }`, which shows `data-act='entry-release'`. An entry with both flags false still shows no `entry-release`.
- `test/gui.test.ts`'s `/api/backlog` assertions include `waiting: false` in their `deepEqual` payloads. A bug fixture carrying a `**Waiting for the next failure` note line (the `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX` in `src/roles/role-guidance.ts`) reads back `waiting: true` and `refused: false`. Add that fixture beside the existing refused bug, or as a new test in `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`.
- `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`: either extend "handleBacklogRelease lifts the Refused note, …" or add a sibling test. Posting a release for a BUGS.md entry that carries only a waiting note answers `status: "released"`, removes the note line from the file, and writes the wake request. This pins the server half the drawer now relies on.
- `test/gui-client-boot.test.ts`: if any test asserts the `not_refused` toast text, it now matches the new wording.
- `npm run test` passes. `test/comment-width.test.ts` stays green on the edited doc comment.
- Out of scope: the TUI (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`), any change to how the note is written or lifted, auto-expiry, and a distinct button label for waiting entries.

### A red merge check whose failure matches a recorded flake keeps its pin once instead of being rejected on main's cached green (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts, src/loop/loop-state.ts, src/tick/tick-apply.ts and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The review gate already skips a failure it has recorded as flaky. In `src/review/review-precheck.ts`, a red whose headline passes `isKnownFlake` (`src/review/known-flakes.ts`) keeps the commit and the pin and counts no strike (BUGS.md 2026-10-06). The merge side has no such check. When the in-lock merge check goes red twice on one patch (`MERGE_CHECK_FAILURE_LIMIT`), or a batch bisect narrows a red to one change (`src/merge/merge-batch.ts`), `attributeRedCheck` in `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts` asks `mainTipVerdict` for main's verdict. That verdict usually comes from the per-SHA cache, which an earlier merge seeded green, so the change is rejected. This applies even when the failing test is one the gate or the merge retry recorded as a flake within the last 24 h. The merge-check flake record (done 2026-10-16) now feeds that memory from merge retries too, so the merge side can use it. One excuse per headline per pin bounds the retry: a change that really breaks a flaky test is still rejected, after at most one extra round of retries.

**Approach.**
- `src/loop/loop-state.ts`: add `mergeFlakeExcused?: string` to `LoopState`, next to `mergeCheckFailures`. Its doc comment says it holds the normalized failure headline (`normalizeClusterKey`) that `attributeRedCheck` last excused as a known flake for this role's pinned change. It is cleared when the change merges or is rejected. In the heal function that heals `mergeCheckFailures`, delete `mergeFlakeExcused` when it is not a string.
- `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`: on the line `if (changeGone) s.mergeCheckFailures = undefined;`, also clear `s.mergeFlakeExcused`, so each new change starts with its one excuse available.
- `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `attributeRedCheck`: after the unverified-tree branch and before `mainTipVerdict`, compute `headline = failureHeadline(red.outcome.outputTail) ?? describeCheck(red.check)`. This is the expression `mergeCheckRed` and review-precheck.ts already use. Also compute `key = normalizeClusterKey(headline)` (import from `src/failure/failure-cluster.ts`). When `isKnownFlake(ctx.root, headline)` is true and `state.mergeFlakeExcused !== key`, do the following:
  - set `state.mergeFlakeExcused = key`;
  - set `state.lastError` to the template `` `${label} failed: known-flaky failure, merge kept: ${headline}` ``;
  - call `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, role, detail)`, where `detail` is the template `` `${label}: known-flaky failure, merge kept: ${headline}` ``;
  - call `saveLoopState`;
  - return `"merge_blocked"`.

  That is the return the unverified branch already uses: the ref stays and recovery merges it again. Otherwise, continue to main's verdict unchanged. Extend the function's doc comment with the known-flake branch, its once-per-headline limit and the reason (this plan, BUGS.md 2026-10-06).
- Same file, `mergeCheckRed`: today it logs `merge check failed (kept for one retry): …` whenever `keepPinOrAttribute` returns `"merge_blocked"`. With this plan, that result can also come from the attribution callback's flake excuse, which logs its own warning. Track whether the callback ran with a local `let attributed = false` set inside the callback, and log the kept-for-retry warning and store the strike headline only when `!attributed`.
- Leave unchanged: the gate side, `mainTipVerdict`'s cache use (a forced fresh run on the merge side would be a separate plan), and the batch caller in merge-batch.ts. It already passes the returned result through `emit`, and `"merge_blocked"` is an outcome it already handles from the unverified branch.
- The file is `// vocabulary: plain`: say "merge", never "landing", in new lines.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `src/loop/loop-state.ts`, `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`, `test/attribute-red-check.test.ts`, `test/streak-gate.test.ts`, `test/loop-state.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/attribute-red-check.test.ts`, a new test named "attributeRedCheck keeps the ref once for a known-flake red, then attributes a repeat". Use the "rejects deterministically when main's own tip is green" fixture (a green fake npm) with a unique marker. Seed one warning event for the role whose message is `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX + "✖ the flaky test"`. Run the red with `outputTail: ["✖ the flaky test (1.2ms)", "expected 2 to be 3"]`.
  - The first call returns `"merge_blocked"`. The pin ref still exists, `state.lastReview` is unchanged (no reject), `state.lastError` contains `known-flaky failure, merge kept` and `the flaky test`, and `loadLoopState(root, ROLE).mergeFlakeExcused` is set.
  - A second call with the same state returns `"rejected"` and deletes the pin.
- The same file: a red whose headline matches no flake warning still returns `"rejected"` on a green main. The existing first test covers this, since it seeds no flake warning. It must still pass unchanged.
- A test in `test/streak-gate.test.ts`, which already drives `applyMergeOutcome` (`src/tick/tick-apply.ts`): `mergeFlakeExcused` is cleared on `"changed"` and on `"rejected"` and kept on `"merge_blocked"`.
- `test/loop-state.test.ts`: a saved state with a non-string `mergeFlakeExcused` loads with the field absent.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/vocabulary.test.ts` and `test/comment-width.test.ts`.

**Note.** The seeded flake warning in the new test is the full headline `✖ the flaky test — expected 2 to be 3` (what `failureHeadline` yields for that outputTail), not `✖ the flaky test` alone: the key is the normalized whole headline.

### Plain terms code merge, part 5/11: Rename the merger core and batch and stack identifiers (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 4/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/merge/merge-core.ts merge-batch.ts merge-stack.ts and the merger tests)

**Goal.** The merger (the old lander), the batch verify-and-merge and the stack take merge, merger, verify and approved names in identifiers, comments, test names and fixtures. A mechanical rename of about 450 lines with no behavior change.

**Approach.**
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `lander` → `merger`, `vet` → `verify`, `vetted` → `approved`, and a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`;
  - comments, test names, temp-dir prefixes (`"lander-rec-"`, `"lander-rereview-rej-"` → `"merger-…"`) and assertion messages follow the same rule;
  - comment lines wrap at 100 columns.
- **merge-core.ts:**
  - `LanderContext` → `MergerContext`. merge-to-main.ts already has `MergeContext`, a different shape. Keep both, and start each doc comment by saying which one it is.
  - `LandRequest` → `MergeRequest`, `LandingScopeContext` → `MergeScopeContext`, `RETRIABLE_LANDING_RESULTS` → `RETRIABLE_MERGE_RESULTS`, `landApprovedChange` → `mergeApprovedChange`, `landApprovedChangeIn` → `mergeApprovedChangeIn`.
- **merge-batch.ts:** `landVetted` → `mergeApproved`, `vetRequest` → `verifyRequest`, `vetRequestIn` → `verifyRequestIn`, `VetVerdict` → `VerifyVerdict`, `landOne` → `mergeOne`, `landedCount` → `mergeDoneCount`, and the parameter `vetted` → `approved`.
- **merge-stack.ts:** `landStack` → `mergeStack`, `landStackIn` → `mergeStackIn`, local `landed` → `mergeDone`.
- **Fixtures and tests:** `vetAndLand` → `verifyAndMerge`, `vetThenMerge` → `verifyThenMerge`, `landerCtx` → `mergerCtx`, and `landWt` → `mergeWt`. If `mergeWt` is already bound in the same scope, use `mergeWorktree`.
- **Earlier callers move now:** `VetVerdict`, `vetRequest`, `landVetted` and `landApprovedChange` in part 4/11's files, and `LandRequest` and `LanderContext` in part 2/11's files.
- **Aliases.** None were kept: every caller of the renamed names (including those outside part 5/11's own files) moved in this part, so no `@deprecated` alias exists for `vetRequest`, `landVetted`, `LanderContext`, `RETRIABLE_LANDING_RESULTS`, `landStack` or `vetAndLand`.
- **Leave alone:**
  - user-visible strings and expected-output literals;
  - event type names;
  - the `_land-<role>` legacy worktree name;
  - PLANS.md and BUGS.md titles quoted in comments, kept verbatim (test/plan-citations.test.ts).
- Skip any name that an earlier series already renamed.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-core.ts`, `merge-batch.ts`, `merge-stack.ts`; `test/fixtures/merger-fixtures.ts`; `test/merger.test.ts`, `test/merger-bisect.test.ts`, `test/merger-errors.test.ts`, `test/merger-restack.test.ts`, `test/merge-stack.test.ts`; earlier-caller lines in the part 2/11 and 4/11 modules.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `MergerContext`, `MergeRequest`, `mergeApproved`, `verifyRequest`, `VerifyVerdict`, `mergeStack` and the other new names are exported. Each old name is either gone or a `@deprecated` alias of it.
- `MergeContext` (merge-to-main.ts) and `MergerContext` (merge-core.ts) both exist, and each doc comment names its role.
- After this part, no file under `src/merge/` has an identifier, comment or test name with a retired merge word, except aliases, `runLandingPi`/`foldLandingUsage`/`AbortableLanding`/`applyMergeOutcome` (parts 6, 7 and 9), quoted backlog titles and legacy-layout names.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` names open bugs held by a "Waiting for the next failure" note, and stops calling them stale (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md and test/doctor-backlog.test.ts)

**Goal.** The "Waiting for the next failure" hold (done 2026-10-16) parks an open bug until it fails again, but doctor does not know about it. `checkStaleBugs` (`src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`) skips only Refused bugs, so a bug held on purpose still warns "has waited N d for a fix — no role is fixing it: check that the bugfix role is enabled and not failing". That advice is wrong for a held bug. No doctor row lists which bugs are waiting or how to release one, so the only sign is the `[blocked: waiting for the next failure]` mark in the backlog listings. This plan makes `checkStaleBugs` skip waiting bugs and adds one doctor row, `waiting bugs`, that names them.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: next to `refusalNote`, export `waitingNote(body: string): string | null`. It applies the same rule to `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX` (already imported for `entryHoldAgainst`): it takes the first trimmed line that starts with the prefix and strips the leading `**` and the first closing `**`. Factor the shared body into a private `noteText(body, prefix)` that both functions call, so `refusalNote`'s behavior stays the same.
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
  - `checkStaleBugs`: skip an entry when `waitingNote(entry.body) !== null`, the same way it skips refused entries. Update its doc comment to say that a waiting bug is skipped too and that `checkWaitingBugs` names it.
  - New `export function checkWaitingBugs(root: string): CheckOutcome`, shaped like `checkStaleBugs`. Read BUGS.md with `readDocChecked(…, "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify")`. Walk `openBugEntries(root)` in order and keep `{ position: index + 1, title, note }` for each entry whose `waitingNote` is non-null and whose `refusalNote` is null; a Refused bug belongs to `checkRefusedEntries`. When none match, return `okOutcome("no open bug is waiting for its next failure")`. Otherwise return an **ok** outcome, never a warn: the hold is deliberate, and doctor only reports it. The detail is `` BUGS.md bug #<n> "<title>" is held until it fails again (<note, truncated to REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX>)<andMore> — selfcheck lifts the note when it records a new occurrence; release it now with `tumwater bug --release <n>` ``. Truncate titles with `FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX` and render the rest with `andMore` as `` #<n> "<title>" ``, as `checkStaleBugs` does. Give the function a doc comment in the style of its neighbors.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import `checkWaitingBugs` and register `{ name: "waiting bugs", ...checkWaitingBugs(root) }` right after the `stale bugs` row.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the `Audit` row's `tumwater doctor` list, after "open bugs unfixed 3 days or more after their filing stamp", add ", open bugs held by a Waiting for the next failure note (not counted as unfixed; released with `tumwater bug --release <n>`)".
- Out of scope: the dashboard drawer's Release button for a waiting bug, warning when a hold gets old, and any change to how the note is written or lifted.

**Files touched.** src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts (and test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts for `waitingNote`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `waitingNote("x\n  **Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: the message names the pid**\n")` returns `"Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: the message names the pid"`. A body that mentions the words only mid-line returns null. The existing `refusalNote` tests pass unchanged.
- `checkStaleBugs` reads ok for a BUGS.md whose only Open entry is stamped 9 days ago and carries a `**Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: …**` line. Its existing tests stay green.
- `checkWaitingBugs`:
  - Returns level `ok` with detail starting `BUGS.md bug #2 "` for an Open section that holds a plain bug and then a waiting one. The detail includes the note text and `tumwater bug --release 2`.
  - With two waiting bugs, names the first and the second through `(and 1 more: #… "`.
  - Returns exactly `{ level: "ok", detail: "no open bug is waiting for its next failure" }` when no Open entry carries the note, including when the note appears only under `## Fixed` or only on an entry that is also Refused.
  - Returns `{ level: "ok", detail: "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify" }` when BUGS.md is absent.
- `tumwater doctor`'s report has a `waiting bugs` row: grep `"waiting bugs"` in src/doctor/doctor.ts. Any test that pins doctor's row names or count, found by grepping test/ for `"stale bugs"`, is updated to include it.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms code merge, part 4/11: Rename the merge pipeline and drain and verify identifiers (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts merge-drain.ts merge-verify.ts, their tests and test/comment-width.test.ts) (done 2026-10-16)

*Replanned 2026-10-16 by plan after two rejected rounds: the earlier attempts rewrapped comments so that overflow words started a new line with a stray `/**` (e.g. `/** no` in test/fixtures/merge-fixtures.ts's `reviewers` doc), and test/comment-width.test.ts checks only width, so it could not catch that. This plan now adds that check first and states how to rewrap.*

**Goal.** The pipeline, the merge-queue drain and the verify stage take merge, verify and approved names in identifiers, comments and test names. Two names that would collide take explicit alternatives. A mechanical rename of about 480 lines with no behavior change, plus a guard that keeps rewrapped doc comments well formed.

**Approach.**
- **Comment guard first.** In `test/comment-width.test.ts`, extend `commentOffenders` so a line whose trimmed text starts with `/*` while `inBlock` is already true is also an offender. Mark it in `offendersInFile`'s output as `(nested)`, next to `(cols)`; return a `kind: "cols" | "nested"` field from `commentOffenders` to do that. Update the comment above `commentOffenders` and the first test's name ("every comment line in src/ and test/ fits in 100 columns and opens no block inside a block"). Add a case to `commentOffenders flags over-wide comment lines only`, or a sibling test, with a `/** a` line followed by `/** b` that asserts the second is flagged `nested`, and a closed `/** a */` followed by `/** b */` that is not flagged.

### A merge check that fails and then passes on its kept-pin retry is recorded as a flake, so the gate's known-flake memory, doctor's `flaky checks` and the tick prompt's flake note count it (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/review/known-flakes.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts, src/merge/merge-core.ts, src/loop/loop-state.ts and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Two retries exist for load flakes. One is the gate pre-check's immediate re-run (`src/review/review-precheck.ts`). It logs `gate check failed then passed on retry — flaky: <headline>` (`FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`), and every flake consumer reads that line through `flakeWarningKeys` in `src/review/known-flakes.ts`:
- the gate's own `isKnownFlake` excuse;
- doctor's `checkFlakyChecks`;
- the tick prompt's `flakeCounts` note.

The other is the in-lock merge check's kept pin (`mergeCheckRed` in `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`). On the first red it logs `merge check failed (kept for one retry): <reason>` and keeps the pin, and recovery merges it again. When that retry passes, nothing is logged, so the failure is never recorded as a flake. BUGS.md's open supervisor entry is an example: improve's 07:29 merge check failed `startParentDeathWatch takes a SIGKILLed supervisor's grandchild down with it`, and the retry merged green at 07:40. None of the three consumers counts that red. So when the same test next fails a gate pre-check, `isKnownFlake` does not excuse it, and the gate asks main's verdict and may reject an unrelated change (the BUGS.md 2026-10-06 class). This plan records a merge-check flake in the same form the gate uses.

**Approach.**
- `src/loop/loop-state.ts`: widen `LoopState.mergeCheckFailures` to `{ patchId: string; count: number; headline?: string }`. Extend the doc comment: `headline` is the failing test's headline, set only by a red merge check (never by a cross-check block). In the existing `healRecord` call for `mergeCheckFailures`, delete `headline` when it is not a string.
- `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `mergeCheckRed`: when `keepPinOrAttribute` returns `"merge_blocked"` and `ctx.state.mergeCheckFailures` is set, store `headline = failureHeadline(red.outcome.outputTail) ?? describeCheck(red.check)`. That is the expression review-precheck.ts uses for its flake warning; import both helpers from `src/build/build-check-report.ts`. The unverified-tree branch (host sleep) returns before the tally and stores nothing. `mergeBlocked` stores no headline. Its `tallyCheckFailure` writes a fresh `{ patchId, count }` record, which drops any earlier headline, so a cross-check block is never counted as a flake.
- Add an exported `noteMergeRetryPassed(ctx: LanderContext, role: string): void` to the same module. If `ctx.state.mergeCheckFailures?.headline` is set, it calls `warnEventBestEffort` for `role` with the message `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX + headline`. Give it a doc comment naming this plan's reason.
- `src/merge/merge-core.ts`: in the `if (result === "changed")` branch that deletes the pin ref, call `noteMergeRetryPassed(ctx, req.role)` before returning. `applyMergeOutcome` in `src/tick/tick-apply.ts` clears `mergeCheckFailures` on `changed` afterwards, so the record is read once, while it still belongs to this pin.
- `src/review/known-flakes.ts`: export `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX = "merge check failed then passed on retry — flaky: "` beside `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`. Change `flakeWarningKeys` to match either prefix: take the first prefix found in the message and slice past it. Update the module and `checkFlakyChecks` doc comments (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) to name both sources. Keep `isKnownFlake`, `flakeKeys` and `flakeCounts` signatures unchanged.

**Files touched.** `src/review/known-flakes.ts`, `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `src/merge/merge-core.ts`, `src/loop/loop-state.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` (comment only), `test/known-flakes.test.ts`, `test/merger.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/known-flakes.test.ts`: a new test, "flakeKeys and flakeCounts read merge-check flake warnings too". It builds one warning with each prefix for the same normalized headline and asserts `flakeCounts` returns that key with count 2 and `flakeKeys` contains it. The existing tests still pass.
- `test/merger.test.ts`: a new test, "a red merge check that passes on its kept-pin retry logs a merge-check flake warning". Start from the fixture of "a kept-for-re-land red landing check logs a warning naming the failing test" (pinnedFixture, advanceMain, noteGreenBaseline). The first check command prints `✖ the flaky test (1.2ms)` and exits 1, and `landApprovedChange` returns `"merge_blocked"`. Assert `state.mergeCheckFailures?.headline` contains `the flaky test`. Then set a passing check command and call `landApprovedChange` again with the same request. Assert:
  - it returns `"changed"`;
  - exactly one warning starts with `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` and contains `the flaky test`;
  - `isKnownFlake(root, "✖ the flaky test (3.4ms)")` is true.
- The same file: a fix-claim-blocked first attempt followed by a green merge logs no `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` warning. Extend "a fix-claim-blocked landing retries once, then rejects with the block reason", or add a short sibling test. A merge that was never red logs none either, which the existing green merge tests show when one asserts on warnings. If none does, add that assertion to one of them.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/vocabulary.test.ts`. The new source lines say "merge", not "landing", because `merge-check-failures.ts` is `// vocabulary: plain`.

### `tumwater questions --show <n>` prints one open question in full, so an operator reads its context, options and recommendation at the terminal before answering (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/question-answer.ts, `cmdQuestions` in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, the `questions` stanza of src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md's "Answer open questions" row and test/cli-questions-list.test.ts) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** A role that posts a question writes its context, the options and its recommendation in the body. The prose `tumwater questions` list prints only each question's heading, age and first body line (`openQuestionList` in `src/backlog/question-answer.ts` uses `firstBodySuffix`). `plan --show <n>` and `bug --show <n>` already print one entry in full (`showAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`), but questions have no such reader. Today the operator either opens QUESTIONS.md or starts the bare `questions answer <n>` editor just to read a question. Add `tumwater questions --show <n> [--json]`, the read half of `questions answer <n>`.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`: add `export function openQuestionAt(root: string, n: number)`. It returns the Nth (1-based) entry of `questionListPayload(root).questions` (`{ position, title, body, since?, ageDays? }`), or `null` when `n` is past the end. Reusing the payload keeps the JSON shape identical to one `questions --json` entry. Add a second export, `renderShownQuestion(q: { title: string; body: string })`. It returns `title` alone when `body` is empty, and otherwise `` `${title}\n\n${body}` ``, the same shape as `renderShownEntry` in `backlog-cli.ts`. That function is private, so write a local copy rather than exporting it from a file the Plain terms series edits.
- `cmdQuestions` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`: in the arg loop, beside the `--answered` branch, add `if (!numbered && arg === "--show")`. It calls `rejectRepeatFlag(show !== undefined, "--show")` and then `show = parsePositionFlag("--show", args[++i], "--show 2")`; import `parsePositionFlag` from `./cli-args.js`. The `--show` branch consumes its number, so `numbered` stays false and a later `--json` is still read as the flag. Add `--show` to the unknown-argument message's flag list. Pass `{ names: ["--show"], value: true, valueName: "<n>" }` in the `rejectEqualsForm` specs, so `--show=2` is refused with the separate-token hint. After the loop and the `-n` check, and before the `answeredFlag` branch, handle `show !== undefined`:
  - fail `--show prints one open question; it takes no subcommand` when `words.length > 0`;
  - fail `--show and --answered cannot be combined` when `answeredFlag`;
  - fail `--file only applies to questions answer <n>` when `file !== undefined`.

  Next, call `openQuestionAt(root, show)`. On `null`, fail `` `no open question at position ${show} (${count} in QUESTIONS.md)` ``, taking `count` from `questionListPayload(root).questions.length`; the wording mirrors `locateEntry`'s. Otherwise `sayJson(q)` under `--json`, or else `say(renderShownQuestion(q))`, then return. The command stays without a `requireReadyRepo` gate, like the list: when QUESTIONS.md is missing, the reader returns no questions and the out-of-range failure says `0 in QUESTIONS.md`.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: add a `tumwater questions --show <n> [--json]` stanza after the `--answered` one: "Print the Nth open question in full (heading, blank line, body), the numbering `questions` lists and `questions answer <n>` takes; --json prints {position, title, body, since, ageDays}". Shell completion reads its flags from `helpStanzas`, so it picks up `--show` with no other edit. Confirm this with `tumwater completion zsh`.
- `docs/cli.md` "Answer open questions" row: add one clause naming `tumwater questions --show <n>` (`--json` for scripts).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Add one test to `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`. It uses a QUESTIONS.md with two open questions, the second with a multi-line body. `questions --show 2` prints the second question's heading, a blank line, and every body line. `questions --show 2 --json` and `questions --json --show 2` both print `{position: 2, title, body, since, ageDays}`, and that object deep-equals `questions --json`'s second entry.
- A second test covers the refusals. Each of these exits non-zero with the message named above: `--show 3` with two open questions (`no open question at position 3 (2 in QUESTIONS.md)`), `--show 0`, `--show` with no value, `--show 1 --show 2`, `--show=1`, `--show 1 --answered`, `--show 1 --file x`, and `answer --show 1`. In the last case, `answer` comes first as a word, so the `words.length > 0` check is the one that refuses it.
- Bare `tumwater questions` and `questions --answered` keep their current output; their existing tests pass unchanged.
- `tumwater help questions` shows the new stanza, and `tumwater completion zsh` output contains `--show` for `questions`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### An open bug that cannot be reproduced is held by a "Waiting for the next failure" note until it recurs, so bugfix stops spending runs on it (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/roles/role-guidance.ts, src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Bugfix can't reproduce the supervisor SIGKILL-grandchild flake in BUGS.md `## Open`. It spent four runs on 2026-10-16 adding Progress notes, and each ended with "the entry stays open until the next flake reads out". Nothing tells bugfix to stop. The entry stays eligible, so every wake brings another strong-model run that has no new evidence. This plan adds one more hold note, like Refused, Needs review and Needs replan. When bugfix has made a failure explain itself but can't reproduce it, it writes the note. The bug is then held until whoever records a new occurrence deletes the note.

**Approach.**
- `src/roles/role-guidance.ts`: next to `NEEDS_REPLAN_PREFIX` / `NEEDS_REPLAN_NOTE`, add `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX = "**Waiting for the next failure "` and `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE = "${WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX}<YYYY-MM-DD> by bugfix: <what the next failure's message will show>**"`, with a doc comment in the style of the Needs-replan pair.
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`:
  - Widen `EntryHold` with `"waiting-for-failure"`.
  - In `entryHoldAgainst`, return it after the Needs-replan check when `hasNoteLine(entry.body, WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX)` (the same line-prefix rule as the other notes, so a mention in prose never holds).
  - `holdMark` renders it as ` [blocked: waiting for the next failure]`.
  - Generalize `withoutRefusalNotes` into a private `withoutNoteLines(lines, prefix)` with the same blank-line collapsing. Keep `withoutRefusalNotes` as the Refused-prefix wrapper, because `src/verdict/refusal.ts` must keep lifting only Refused notes. Export `withoutWaitingNotes` as the Waiting-prefix wrapper.
  - Update the module header comment's list of holds.
  - `eligibleEntries`, `backlogHolds` and the backlog index pick the new hold up through `entryHoldAgainst` with no change of their own. Because of that, a bug whose only open entry is held makes `eligibleEntries(root, "bugfix")` empty, and bugfix sleeps as it does for a Refused bug.
- `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`:
  - `liftRefusal` lifts a Refused note. When the entry has none, it lifts a Waiting-for-the-next-failure note instead (via `withoutWaitingNotes`). So `tumwater bug --release <n>` and the dashboard's `tryReleaseEntry` also release a waiting bug.
  - `releaseEntry`'s failure reads `carries no Refused or Waiting for the next failure note`.
  - `ReleaseEntryOutcome`'s `not_refused` status keeps its name (it is a payload value).
- `src/roles/role-catalog.ts`:
  - Bugfix `find`, step 2: append one sentence. When the bug cannot be reproduced and this run made its failure message name the cause next time (or found it already does), record a Progress note, write `${WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE}` as its own line under the heading, and end the run. Do not keep investigating without new evidence. Step 1's "Skip entries the index marks `[blocked: …]`" already covers skipping a waiting bug, so it needs no new words.
  - Selfcheck `find`, step 4: when the matching Open entry carries a Waiting-for-the-next-failure note and the cluster failed again after the note's date, add the new occurrence under the entry (time, merged commit, failure message) and delete the note line, instead of filing a duplicate.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: next to the existing hold-note description (grep `Needs replan` / `needs-replan`), state what writes the new note, what it holds, and the two ways it lifts: deleting the line when recording an occurrence, or `bug --release`. `docs/cli.md`: in the `--release <n>` clause, write "lifts a Refused or Waiting for the next failure note".
- Out of scope: the dashboard drawer's Release button, which today renders only for `d.refused`. Doctor's blocked-entry listing. Any automatic expiry. Each can be its own plan later.

**Files touched.** src/roles/role-guidance.ts, src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md, test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts, test/backlog-write-cancel.test.ts (it holds the `releaseEntry`/`tryReleaseEntry` cases), test/role-guidance.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `entryHold` returns `"waiting-for-failure"` for an Open bug whose body has a line starting `**Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: …**` (indented or not). It returns null when the same words appear mid-line in prose. A Refused note on the same entry still reads `"refused"`.
- `holdMark("waiting-for-failure")` is ` [blocked: waiting for the next failure]`. A fixture BUGS.md whose only Open entry carries the note yields `eligibleEntries(root, "bugfix")` empty.
- `releaseEntry(root, "bug", 1)` on that fixture removes the note line, collapsing the blank line around it the way the Refused case does, and the entry becomes eligible. On an entry with neither note it fails with the new wording. `withoutBlockedPlanRefusals` still lifts only Refused notes: an existing refusal.ts test stays green unchanged.
- The bugfix find text contains `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE`'s text, and the selfcheck find text names the note and says to delete it when recording a recurrence (role-guidance or role-catalog test).
- `npm run test` passes.

### A series part whose heading words its prerequisite as "blocked by part i/n" (or "after", "follows", "depends on") instead of a requires clause gets a doctor warning (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, and src/tick/stage-check.ts only when its `planDependencyFinding` already exists) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The claim allocator reads one dependency form only: `requires <ref> landed` in a heading's parenthetical. BUGS.md "The plan loop is never told the one prerequisite form the claim allocator reads" (2026-10-14) shows the cost of any other wording. A part headed `(planned …; blocked by part 1/2 above, …)` was handed out six times while part 1/2 was still in flight. The fix there was prompt guidance (`src/roles/role-guidance.ts`). No deterministic check exists. `planDependencyProblems` (`src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`) only inspects headings that already have a `requires` clause, so a misworded heading passes `checkPlanDependencies` (`src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`) as clean. This plan adds a `misworded` problem kind: a heading names a still-Planned part through a dependency verb, and no requires clause holds that part.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `planDependencyProblems`: widen the return type with `misworded: Array<{ title: string; ref: string }>`.
  - Scope: for each planned entry that has its own `seriesPart`, read the same meta text `requiresClause` reads (`trailingParenthetical`, falling back to `openParenthetical`). Run a module-level constant `MISWORDED_DEPENDENCY_RE = /\b(?:blocked by|blocked on|after|follows|depends on|waits on|waits for|once)\s+(?:the\s+)?(parts?\s+[0-9]+[a-z]?\/[0-9]+)/gi` over it.
  - Parsing: feed each capture to `parseRef(capture, own.series)`.
  - What counts: a ref is misworded when its `partKey` is in `plannedPartKeys(planned)` (the prerequisite is still Planned, so the hold matters now) and is not among the keys of `requiredParts(entry.title)` (no requires clause already holds it). Push `{ title, ref: "<series> <part>/<of>" }`.
  - Out of scope on purpose: a ref to a Done part, such as "follows the landed part 1/2", already in Done headings. It holds nothing and needs nothing. Headings with no series part are also skipped.
  - Docs: extend the function's doc comment with the new kind, and give the regex constant a one-line doc saying why it exists (the 2026-10-14 bug). Any source line in this `// vocabulary: plain` module that contains the word `landed` ends with `// vocabulary-ok: PLANS.md heading syntax`.
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `checkPlanDependencies`: destructure `misworded`. Report it after `unparsed` in the same first-then-`andMore` shape, and add `[misworded.length, "misworded dependency(ies)"]` to the `others(...)` lists of the cycle, dangling and unparsed branches. Wording: `` PLANS.md plan "<title>" names <ref> as a prerequisite without a `requires … landed` clause — the claim allocator ignores that wording and hands the part out now; write it as `requires part i/n landed` ``. Update the ok message to `every planned plan's requires clause names a known part, with no cycle or misworded dependency`.
- `src/tick/stage-check.ts`, staging. This step applies only if `planDependencyFinding` exists when this plan is picked up. That function comes from PLANS.md "A staged PLANS.md edit that breaks a requires clause gets a staging finding", which is now Done, so expect it to exist.
  - When it exists, add `misworded` as its fourth kind, after unparsed. It counts as new when the base has no item with the same `title` and `ref`. Use the doctor wording above, with ` — fix it before this change commits` appended. Add one test case in `test/stage-check.test.ts`.
  - When it does not exist, leave stage-check.ts alone and say so in the commit's RISK line. The in-flight plan will then destructure only the fields it knows, which the widened return type does not break.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`; conditionally `src/tick/stage-check.ts` and `test/stage-check.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, the existing "planDependencyProblems finds dangling refs, unparsed clauses and cycles" assertion `ok` is updated to include `misworded: []`. A new test, "planDependencyProblems flags a still-planned prerequisite named without a requires clause", checks:
  - `[S, part 1/2: a, S, part 2/2: b (planned 2026-10-14 by plan; blocked by part 1/2 above)]` yields `misworded` `[{ title: <part 2/2's title>, ref: "S 1/2" }]`;
  - the same part 2/2 with `S, part 1/2` only in the done titles yields `[]`;
  - `S, part 2/2: b (requires part 1/2 landed; after part 1/2)` yields `[]`;
  - a non-series `Plain plan (after part 1/2)` yields `[]`.
- In `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, a new test, "checkPlanDependencies warns on a misworded dependency", uses `plansWith` with the two-part misworded pair. It asserts a `warn` whose detail contains `names S 1/2 as a prerequisite`. The existing checkPlanDependencies tests still pass.
- No heading under PLANS.md `## Planned` on main at implementation time trips the new kind. Verify with `node dist/cli.js doctor` in the worktree or a one-off check, and report what was run.

### A staged PLANS.md edit that breaks a requires clause gets a staging finding (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/tick/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts and docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The claim allocator decides when a series part is free from the heading's `requires <Series> i/n landed` clause. If a plan, director or steward run writes one of these clauses wrong, the allocator gets it wrong. A ref to a part no heading carries (dangling) leaves the dependent part claimable at once. A clause that parses to no refs (unparsed) holds nothing. A dependency cycle blocks every part on it forever. `checkPlanDependencies` (`src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`) reports these problems, but only after the edit has merged and only when someone runs `tumwater doctor`. By then a feature instance may already have claimed the part too early, which is the waste behind BUGS.md's 2026-10-14 "six wasted claims" entry. The pre-queue self-check (`stageCheckFindings`, `src/tick/stage-check.ts`) runs while the authoring session can still take one fix-up turn (`requestStageFix` in `src/tick/tick-stage.ts`). This plan makes it report any dependency problem that the run's own PLANS.md edit adds, so the author fixes the heading before the change commits. Problems already on main are not this run's fault and stay doctor's to report.

**Approach.**
- `src/tick/stage-check.ts`: add and export a pure `planDependencyFinding(head: string, base: string): string | undefined`. For each text, parse `parseEntryDetails(text, "Planned")` and the titles of `parseEntryDetails(text, "Done")` (both from `src/backlog/backlog-md.ts`), then run `planDependencyProblems` (`src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`) on them. A problem is new when the base does not have it:
  - a cycle is new when head's `cycle` is non-null and base's `cycle` is null;
  - a dangling item is new when the base has no item with the same `title` and `ref`;
  - an unparsed title is new when it is not among the base's unparsed titles.
  Return a finding for the most serious new problem, in the order cycle, then dangling, then unparsed. When more new problems follow it, append ` (+N more)` with `moreSuffix` from `src/text/phrases.ts`, which the module already imports. Return undefined when nothing is new. The wording is:
  - cycle: `` PLANS.md's requires clauses now form a cycle: <A 1/2 → B 2/2 → A 1/2> — every part on it stays blocked forever; edit one heading's `requires … landed` clause to break it ``
  - dangling: `PLANS.md plan "<title>" requires <ref>, which no PLANS.md heading carries — the claim allocator ignores the clause and hands the plan out now; fix the series name or part number to match the prerequisite's heading`
  - unparsed: `` PLANS.md plan "<title>" has a `requires … landed` clause that names no part the claim allocator can read — it holds nothing; write each ref as `<Series> i/n` or `part i/n` after a `<Series>, part i/n:` heading prefix ``

  The module is opted in with `// vocabulary: plain`. Wherever one of these literals contains `landed`, end the line with the `// vocabulary-ok: PLANS.md heading syntax` comment that `checkPlanDependencies` uses. Write the doc comment in the module's style and say why only new problems count.
- `stageCheckFindings` in the same file: right after the `backlogStructureReason` finding, when `files` includes `"PLANS.md"`, read head with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, "PLANS.md")) ?? ""` (from `src/files/files.ts`; add the `node:path` import). Read base with `fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), "PLANS.md")` (`src/git/git.ts`, where `changeBaseRev` is already imported). Push `planDependencyFinding(head, base)` when it is defined. Wrap the git read in `.catch(() => undefined)`, the way the other checks are wrapped, so a git hiccup gives no finding. This is a staging-only check: do not add it to the review gate or the in-lock landing re-check, because the doctor warning is the backstop for anything that gets past the fix-up turn.
- Add a sentence to the module's top doc comment saying this check is staging-only.
- `docs/invariants.md`: if a section's **Binds.** line names `src/tick/stage-check.ts` and states which findings staging reports, add this guarantee there, pinned to the new test. If no section does, leave the register alone.

**Files touched.** `src/tick/stage-check.ts`, `test/stage-check.test.ts`, possibly `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/stage-check.test.ts`, "planDependencyFinding reports only the requires-clause problems an edit adds". A base PLANS.md text with `## Planned` holding `### S, part 1/2: a` and `### S, part 2/2: b (requires part 1/2 landed)`, then `## Done`. The test checks:
  - head equal to base gives undefined;
  - head where part 2/2's clause reads `requires part 3/2 landed` gives a finding that names that title and `S 3/2`;
  - head where part 1/2's heading gains `(requires part 2/2 landed)` gives a finding that starts with the cycle wording and names `S 1/2` and `S 2/2`;
  - head whose new `### Other plan (requires nothing landed)` clause parses to no refs gives the unparsed finding naming `Other plan`;
  - a base that already has the dangling clause, with a head that keeps it and changes only a body line, gives undefined.
- New test, "a staged PLANS.md edit adding a dangling requires clause yields the dependency finding". It uses `repoWith` with the base above. It writes the dangling head into the worktree, and `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "plan")` returns a finding containing `which no PLANS.md heading carries`. The existing "a clean change yields no findings" test still passes.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/vocabulary.test.ts`.

### An assigned series part names the later parts waiting on it (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts and their tests; it adds code next to "An assigned series part names the Done entries of the parts it requires", so whichever lands second rebases onto the other) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A feature instance assigned a series part such as "Plain terms code merge, part 1/11" gets an `<assigned-entry>` note (`buildAssignmentNote`, `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`) that tells it to "Implement or fix only that entry". It is not told which later parts are waiting on this one, and each of those later parts already plans its own share of the work. If the implementer cannot see where its part ends, it may do a later part's work early, which leaves that part with nothing to do and makes the diff bigger than its plan. Or it may change a name that a later part's plan relies on. Those parts are in PLANS.md's `## Planned`, which the charter says never to read wholesale. This plan adds a short `<waiting-parts>` note that lists, by title and line range, the planned parts that require this one. The implementer then knows where its part ends and what the later parts expect it to leave in place.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: add and export `waitingPartRanges(root: string, title: string): EligibleEntry[]`. Read `plannedPlanEntries(root)` and `actionableEntryRangesFor(root, "PLANS.md", "Planned")`, pairing them by index the way `eligibleEntries` does. Find the index of the planned entry whose `entryKey(e.title)` equals `entryKey(title)`. If there is none, or the entry has no `seriesPart`, return `[]`. Otherwise return `{ key, title, start, end }` for each index that the existing `plansWaitingOn(planned, index)` returns, in its ascending (file) order. Skip an index that has no range. `plansWaitingOn` is transitive, so a part that waits through a chain is listed too, and every one of those parts is work this part must leave alone. A missing PLANS.md gives `[]`, because both readers already treat a missing file as empty. Write the doc comment in the module's style.
- `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`: add a pure `buildWaitingPartsNote(entries: readonly { title: string; start: number; end: number }[]): string` after `buildMainRedNote`, at the end of the file, so it does not sit beside the in-flight `buildLandedPrerequisitesNote`. Leave `buildAssignmentNote` alone. The note is:
  ```
  <waiting-parts>
  Later parts of your series wait for yours to land, and each one plans its own share of the work: do none of it here, and keep in place the names and files they say your part leaves behind. Read one by its range when you need to know what it expects:
  - "<title>" (PLANS.md lines <start>-<end>)
  </waiting-parts>
  ```
  List at most 5 entries. After the fifth, add one more line, `- …and N more`, as a literal (`moreSuffix` in `src/text/phrases.ts` renders ` (+N more)`, which does not fit a list line). Give it a doc comment saying why it is a pure function, the same as its neighbours.
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, in `assembleTickPrompt`: right after the `if (claim && userPrompt === null) { … }` block, add a separate `if (claim && userPrompt === null && claim.file === "PLANS.md")` block. That block keeps this change out of the lines the in-flight landed-prerequisites plan edits. It computes `waitingPartRanges(root, claim.title)`, and when the result is non-empty it adds `buildWaitingPartsNote(...)` to the prompt with `appendPromptNote`. A BUGS.md claim, an unclaimed tick, and a tick running a dequeued user request get no note. `tumwater role <id>`'s preview calls the same `assembleTickPrompt`, so its next-prompt view shows the note without a change of its own.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`, `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/gate-prompts.test.ts`, `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, next to "plansWaitingOn follows requires clauses transitively and stops on a cycle", new test "waitingPartRanges names the planned parts that wait on an entry, with their ranges". A temp root's PLANS.md has `## Planned`, which holds `### S, part 1/3: a`, `### Unrelated plan`, `### S, part 2/3: b (requires part 1/3 landed)` and `### S, part 3/3: c (requires part 2/3 landed)`, and then `## Done`. The test checks:
  - For part 1/3's title, the result is part 2/3, then part 3/3, and each range matches that entry's real heading line and last body line.
  - Part 3/3's title gives `[]`.
  - `Unrelated plan` (no series part) gives `[]`.
  - A title not in Planned gives `[]`.
  - A root with no PLANS.md gives `[]`.
- `test/gate-prompts.test.ts`, new test "buildWaitingPartsNote lists each part's title and range and caps at five":
  - With one entry, the note starts with `<waiting-parts>`, holds `"S, part 2/3: b" (PLANS.md lines 10-20)`, and ends with `</waiting-parts>`.
  - With 7 entries, it lists 5 and ends its list with `- …and 2 more`.
- `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`, next to "the assignment names the claimed entry's paths missing from the checkout", new test "a feature instance's claimed series part names the parts waiting on it". It writes the PLANS.md above and calls `promptFor(dir, "feature", { state: { claim: { file: "PLANS.md", key: "s, part 1/3: a", title: "S, part 1/3: a", at: 1, source: "assigned" } } })`. The prompt holds `<assigned-entry>` and `<waiting-parts>`, which names both later titles with their ranges. A claim on part 3/3 gives no `<waiting-parts>`. A BUGS.md claim gives no `<waiting-parts>` either.
- `npm run test` passes.

### An assigned series part names the Done entries of the parts it requires (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts and their tests; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A series part such as "Plain terms code team, part 6/6" builds on what its prerequisites did. The heading lists those prerequisites in a `requires part 5/6 landed` clause. When the claim allocator hands a feature instance that part, its prompt gets the `<assigned-entry>` note (`buildAssignmentNote`, `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`) with only the part's own title and line range. The prerequisites' Done entries record which files and names they actually changed. Those entries sit somewhere in PLANS.md's `## Done`, which runs to thousands of lines, and the charter says never to read PLANS.md wholesale. So the implementer either greps for them blind or works from the plan's assumptions about code the earlier part may have changed. This plan adds a short `<landed-prerequisites>` note that gives each landed prerequisite's Done heading and line range, so the implementer can read exactly that range.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: add and export
  `landedPrerequisiteRanges(root: string, title: string): EligibleEntry[]`. For each ref in `requiredParts(title)`, in order, it finds the first entry of `actionableEntryRangesFor(root, "PLANS.md", "Done")` whose `seriesPart(e.title)` has the same `partKey` as the ref (series compared case-insensitively, the part token verbatim, through the module's existing `partKey`). Done is newest-first, so the first match is the most recent landing. It returns `{ key: entryKey(e.title), title: e.title, start, end }` for each match. A ref with no Done match is skipped, so a prerequisite still in Planned, or one that was renamed, adds nothing. A title with no parseable requires clause returns `[]`. A missing PLANS.md returns `[]`, because `actionableEntryRangesFor` already reads a missing file as no ranges. Write the doc comment in the module's style.
- `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`: add a pure `buildLandedPrerequisitesNote(entries: readonly { title: string; start: number; end: number }[]): string`. Put it next to `buildHeldEntriesNote`, and leave `buildAssignmentNote` alone; "The assigned entry names its paths missing from the checkout" (now landed) changed that function's signature. The note is:
  ```
  <landed-prerequisites>
  Your assigned entry builds on parts that already landed. Each one's Done entry records what it actually changed; read one by its range when your entry depends on its details, rather than searching PLANS.md:
  - "<title>" (PLANS.md lines <start>-<end>)
  </landed-prerequisites>
  ```
  List at most 5 entries. After the fifth, add one more line, `- …and N more`, built with the existing `moreSuffix` from `src/text/phrases.ts` if its wording fits, else a literal. Give it a doc comment saying why it is a pure function, the same as its neighbours.
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, in the `if (claim && userPrompt === null)` block after the assignment-note append: when `claim.file === "PLANS.md"`, compute `landedPrerequisiteRanges(root, claim.title)`. When the result is non-empty, add `buildLandedPrerequisitesNote(...)` to the prompt with `appendPromptNote`. A BUGS.md claim gets no such note. Neither does a tick that runs a dequeued user request, because that block is already skipped.

**Landing note.** The tag is `<merged-prerequisites>` and the prose says "already merged", not `<landed-prerequisites>`: `test/vocabulary.test.ts` bans "landed" in `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`. The `- …and N more` line is a literal, since `moreSuffix` words it ` (+N more)`.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts`, `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/gate-prompts.test.ts`, `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

A temp root's PLANS.md has `## Planned`, holding `### S, part 3/3: c (requires parts 1/3–2/3 landed)`, and `## Done`, holding (newest first) `### s, part 2/3: b (done 2026-10-16)`, `### S, part 1/3: a (done 2026-10-15)` and an older duplicate `### S, part 1/3: a-old (done 2026-10-01)`. The test checks:
  - The result is part 2/3, then part 1/3 `a`, not `a-old`. Each range matches the entry's real heading line and last body line.
  - A title with no requires clause gives `[]`.
  - A title requiring `part 9/9 landed` (no Done match) gives `[]`.
  - A root with no PLANS.md gives `[]`.
- `test/gate-prompts.test.ts`, new test "buildLandedPrerequisitesNote lists each entry's title and range and caps at five":
  - With one entry, the note starts with `<landed-prerequisites>`, holds `"S, part 1/3: a" (PLANS.md lines 10-20)`, and ends with `</landed-prerequisites>`.
  - With 7 entries, it lists 5 and names the 2 left out.

It writes the PLANS.md above and calls `promptFor(dir, "feature-2", { state: { claim: { file: "PLANS.md", key: …, title: <part 3/3 heading>, at: 1, source: "assigned" } } })`. ### The repeated-failure pause, part 2/2: Status, the dashboard and the role view show instance 1 paused under its own key (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; requires part 1/2 landed; touches src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/status-model.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/cli/cli-run.ts and their tests)

**Goal.** Part 1/2 makes the scheduler treat a runner as paused through `loopPaused` (`src/roles/loop-ids.ts`): its own id, its base role's id, or for instance 1 the `feature-1` key. The display surfaces still test `pausedRoles.includes(role)`. A breaker-paused instance 1 (marker `feature-1`) therefore shows as idle on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and `tumwater role feature`. A `feature-2` row under a whole-role `pause --role feature` already shows that way today. Have every surface read the scheduler's own answer.

**Approach.**
- `src/status/status-data.ts`: add `pausedLoops: string[]` to the status snapshot type, beside `pausedRoles`. Its doc comment: "the loop ids the scheduler treats as paused by the per-role marker". Build it where `pausedRoles: pausedRoles(root)` is built: `loopIds(config).filter((id) => loopPaused(set, id))` over one read of the marker, using the snapshot's config. Keep `pausedRoles` as the raw marker; it is what `resume --role` takes.
- `src/ui/status-model.ts`: the row's paused test `snap.pausedRoles.includes(s.role)` becomes `snap.pausedLoops.includes(s.role)`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts` (both `(d.pausedRoles || []).includes(l.role)` reads) and `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` (its one read): read `(d.pausedLoops || [])`.
- `src/roles/role-view.ts`: `paused: pausedRoles(root).includes(role)` becomes `loopPaused(new Set(pausedRoles(root)), role)`.
- `src/cli/cli-run.ts`, the once-mode skip reason: `pausedRoles(root).includes(role)` becomes `loopPaused(new Set(pausedRoles(root)), role)`.
- Grep `src/` for other `pausedRoles(root).includes(` and `pausedRoles.includes(` reads of a loop's paused state. Switch each to `loopPaused`, except the TUI `p` toggle in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`: it decides what to write, so it keeps reading the raw marker.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/status-model.test.ts`, new test: a snapshot with `pausedRoles: ["feature-1"]`, `pausedLoops: ["feature"]` and runners `feature` and `feature-2` gives the `feature` row the paused cell and leaves `feature-2` not paused. The paused cell is the same text a `pausedRoles: ["feature"]` single-instance snapshot renders.
- A status-data test (grep `test/` for the one that asserts `pausedRoles` on the snapshot), new case: with feature at 2 instances and the marker holding `feature`, `pausedLoops` holds both `feature` and `feature-2`. With the marker holding `feature-1`, it holds only `feature`.
- A role-view test (grep `test/` for `paused:` on the role view): `feature` with the marker holding `feature-1` reports `paused: true`.
- Existing status, dashboard and role-view tests pass with `pausedLoops` added to their fixtures where the type requires it.
- `npm run test` passes.
