### `tumwater retire --role <id>` accepts a role id that is no longer configured while its branch or merge ref remains (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; done 2026-10-16; independent of the waiting series — touches src/operator/retire.ts, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/retire.test.ts, and src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts plus test/doctor-checks.test.ts only when `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` is already on main)

**Goal.** Lowering `roles.feature.instances` from 4 to 2 leaves `tumwater/feature-3` and `tumwater/feature-4` behind. The same happens to a custom role removed from `tumwater.json`. `tumwater retire --role feature-4` rejects these ids as `unknown role: feature-4`. The reason is that `cmdRetire` resolves its target through `requiredNamedRole` → `namedRole` (`src/operator/operator-commands.ts`), which accepts only `allRoleIds()` plus `knownRoleIds(loadConfig(root))`, and `knownRoleIds` adds only the configured `loopIds` instances. Retire exists to clean up the leftovers of a loop that no longer runs, so it should accept any well-formed id that still has a leftover branch or merge ref. `retireRole`'s rails need no change: `loopEnabled` is false for such an id, so the "still enabled" rail stays quiet, and the unmerged-commits, dirty, unusable-worktree, and mid-run rails apply as they do today.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/retire.ts`: add `export async function hasRetirableLeftovers(root: string, role: string): Promise<boolean>`, with a doc comment saying it is the id gate for ids no config names. It returns true only when all of these hold:
  - `CUSTOM_NAME_RE.test(role)` (`src/config/config-schema.ts`). That is the custom-role name pattern, and it also matches instance ids such as `feature-4`. It keeps `..` and `/` out of the `worktreePath`/`branchName` paths collectRetire builds.
  - `role !== DIRECTOR_ROLE` (`src/roles/roles.ts`).
  - Either `await branchExists(root, branchName(role))` is true or `await refSha(root, landingRefName(role)) !== null`. Both helpers are already imported there.
  
  This function is read-only.
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`: add `async function retireTargetRole(root: string, args: string[]): Promise<string>` and use it in `cmdRetire` in place of `requiredNamedRole(root, args, "retire")`. Leave `namedRole`, `requiredNamedRole`, and their other callers (abort, resume, wake, reset-counters) unchanged. Behavior, in this order:
  - `flagValue(args, "--role")` is `null` → fail with the same `retire requires --role <id> (e.g. \`--role feature\`)` text `requiredNamedRole` prints. Reuse `requiredNamedRole`'s message by calling it on this path, not by copying the string.
  - Empty value → `fail(ROLE_VALUE_ERROR)` (from `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`), as `parseRoleFlag` does.
  - `allRoleIds().includes(role)` → return it. This keeps today's broken-config path: collectRetire then throws "cannot read tumwater.json".
  - Else load `ids = knownRoleIds(loadConfig(root))`. On a load error, `fail(errorMessage(err))` as `namedRole` does. When `ids.includes(role)`, return it.
  - Else, when `await hasRetirableLeftovers(root, role)` is true, return it.
  - Else `fail(unknownRoleMessage(role, ids))` (`src/roles/roles.ts`). This is the same message as today, so `retire --role bogus` keeps printing `unknown role: bogus`.
  - Update the `cmdRetire` comment that says the config exists only to validate the id so it also mentions the leftover-branch gate.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: in the `tumwater retire --role <id>` stanza, replace the last line `changing nothing` with these three lines, using the same 35-column indent:
  ```
  changing nothing; an id no longer configured (`feature-4`
  after lowering `instances`, a removed custom role) is
  accepted while its branch or merge ref remains
  ```
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Control-the-roles row, change the `tumwater retire --role <id> [--dry-run]` parenthetical's clause "use after setting `enabled: false` for that role" to "use after setting `enabled: false` for that role, lowering `instances`, or removing a custom role — an id no longer in `tumwater.json` is accepted while its `tumwater/<id>` branch or merge ref remains". Leave the rest of the row alone.
- Doctor follow-through. Do this only when `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` exists in `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` at implementation time. It is the in-flight "`tumwater doctor` names disabled roles that still keep a branch" entry, and its "unknown" part says retire rejects ids outside `knownRoleIds`, which stops being true after this change. Change its split so an id is retirable when `knownRoleIds(config).includes(id) || CUSTOM_NAME_RE.test(id)`. Every other id stays in the unknown part, with that part's wording unchanged. The check already has the branch, so it does not call `hasRetirableLeftovers`. In `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, the test "checkLeftoverRoleBranches names disabled roles' branches and unknown ones, skipping enabled roles and the director" changes in three ways:
  - Its `tumwater/ghost` case now expects `ghost` among the retirable ids.
  - Its unknown-branch assertion uses `tumwater/old.role` (the `.` fails `CUSTOM_NAME_RE`).
  - Its `tumwater/feature-2` case expects `feature-2` among the retirable ids after `writeConfig(root, {})`.
  
  When `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` is not on main, skip this step entirely. The doctor entry is then implemented against the new `retireTargetRole`, and its implementer reads this plan's Done entry.

**Files touched.** src/operator/retire.ts, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/retire.test.ts, plus src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts and test/doctor-checks.test.ts when the doctor follow-through applies.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/retire.test.ts`, "retire accepts a leftover instance id above the configured instances and removes its branch". Use `initializedRepo()`. Write `roles.feature` with `instances: 2` the way the "retire refuses an enabled work instance id, not just its bare base role (part 5b/7)" test does. Create the branch with `sh(root, "git", "branch", branchName("feature-4"))`. Then `cli(root, "retire", "--role", "feature-4", "--json")` exits 0, `removed` includes `"branch"`, and `branchHead(root, branchName("feature-4"))` is `null` afterwards.
- Same file: `retire --role feature-4 --dry-run` on that fixture, before the removal, exits 0 and prints `would remove the branch (tumwater/feature-4)`.
- Same file: a leftover id whose branch holds a commit not on main is still refused with `/unmerged commit/` and keeps its branch. Make the commit with `git commit --allow-empty` on the branch via a worktree or `git commit-tree` + `git update-ref`, so main's checkout is untouched.
- The test "retire validates its arguments like the other operator commands" still passes unchanged (`unknown role: bogus` when no `tumwater/bogus` branch exists). Add one assertion there: `retire --role ../x` fails with `/unknown role/` even after `git update-ref refs/heads/tumwater/x HEAD`. That covers the `CUSTOM_NAME_RE` gate keeping a path-like id out.
- Unit test of `hasRetirableLeftovers`: false for `director` even with a `tumwater/director` branch, false for an id with no branch and no landing ref, and true for an id with only a landing ref (`setRef(root, landingRefName("gone"), mainSha(root))`).
- `tumwater help retire` output contains `accepted while its branch or merge ref remains`. Extend the "tumwater help retire shows the command's usage stanza" test with that match.
- When the doctor follow-through applied, its updated test passes as described above.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms state, part 3/5: Add the startup migration hook and move the land queue to merge-queue (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 2/5 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "State and git"; touches src/orchestrator/ src/paths.ts src/landing/ src/loop/leftover.ts src/tick/tick-stage.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/events/ test/) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** tumwater gets one reusable registry of idempotent startup-migration steps. The orchestrator runs it before its first per-runner state read, and a CLI reader can run it safely too. Its first step moves `.tumwater/land-queue/` to `.tumwater/merge-queue/`. Queue entries carry `run` instead of `tick`, and older entries still read.

**Approach.**
- New module src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts holds the registry:
  - `interface StartupMigration { name: string; run(root: string): Promise<string[]> }`. A step returns one short note per thing it moved, and nothing when there was nothing to do. Each step must be idempotent and must tolerate a concurrent run: a source that vanished mid-step is skipped, not an error.
  - `registerStartupMigration(step)` appends to the registry; a duplicate `name` throws.
  - `runStartupMigrations(root)` runs the registered steps in registration order.
    - A step that moved something logs one `state_migrated` event (`source: TUMWATER_SOURCE`, `step`, `moved`, `detail`).
    - A step that throws logs one warning, the remaining steps still run, and the failed step retries at the next start.
    - A second call moves and logs nothing.
  - `runStartupMigrationsIfIdle(root)` is the CLI-reader form. It runs the same steps only when no orchestrator is alive for `root` (`orchestratorAlive`, src/fleet/orchestrator-info.ts), so a CLI process never moves files under a running fleet, which may still be the old build. A live fleet has already migrated at its own start.
- New module src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts is the one place that fixes step order. It imports `registerStartupMigration`, calls it once per step at top level in order, and re-exports `runStartupMigrations`/`runStartupMigrationsIfIdle`. Callers import from this file, so the steps are registered before anything can run. This also avoids an import cycle: startup-migrations.ts never imports the steps. A step's implementation may live in the module that owns the data. Later parts, and the Plain terms role ids series, add a step by appending one `registerStartupMigration(...)` call at the end of this file.
- Call `runStartupMigrations` once, from `runOrchestrator` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts), awaited before the `LoopRunner`s are constructed. Each `LoopRunner` constructor's `loadLoopState` is the first per-runner state read, and the merge pipeline's first queue read comes later. In-process callers, tests and `--once` rounds included, get the same call.
- No CLI command in this series calls the Idle form: the observers read both layouts (below). It exists so the role ids series can migrate from a CLI read path when no fleet is running.
- Add `state_migrated` to the `HarnessEvent` union, an event-format.ts case (`state migrated — <detail>`) and the label map, in its server and browser forms, with a routine tone.
- First step, `mergeQueueDir`:
  - Move every `*.json` in `legacyLandQueueDir(root)` into `landQueueDir(root)` with `fs.renameSync`, keeping the basename, because the queue order lives in the filename.
  - If the basename already exists in the new directory, leave the file in place and note it.
  - Remove the old directory once it is empty.
  - Leave the files' contents as they are.
- src/paths.ts: `landQueueDir` returns `.tumwater/merge-queue`. Plain terms code merge renames the function. Add `legacyLandQueueDir`, which returns `.tumwater/land-queue`.
- src/landing/landing-queue.ts:
  - `LandingEntry.run` replaces `tick`.
  - `isLandingEntry`/`readEntry` accept an entry that carries `tick` instead and map it to `run`.
  - `queueFiles` lists the new directory plus any files still in the legacy one, sorted by basename. `tumwater queue`, `status`, doctor and the dashboard, running in another process before the new orchestrator's first start, therefore show the full queue.
  - `dropLanding` removes by full path, so either directory works.
  - If the vocabulary guard flags a legacy path literal, end its line with `// vocabulary-ok: legacy path read from old layouts`.
- Callers (tsc): `stageTickMerge` (tick-stage.ts), `recoverLeftover` (leftover.ts), landing-vetting.ts, landing-drain.ts, landing-queue-render.ts and status-data.ts. In status-data.ts the `--json`/API key is already `run`. The in-memory `LandRequest.tick` stays; Plain terms code run renames it.
- **Self-hosting:** safe in one part.
  - The old orchestrator enqueues into `land-queue/` until it exits.
  - The new one moves those entries before its first read.
  - Observers on the new build read both directories.
  - The old build never reads `merge-queue/`.
  - A crash mid-migration leaves each file whole in one directory or the other, both are read, and the next start finishes the move.

**Files touched.** src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts (new), src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts (new), src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/paths.ts, src/landing/landing-queue.ts, src/landing/landing-vetting.ts, src/landing/landing-drain.ts, src/landing/landing-queue-render.ts, src/loop/leftover.ts, src/tick/tick-stage.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, the label-map module(s); test/startup-migrations.test.ts (new), test/landing-queue.test.ts, test/landing-slot.test.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, test/cli-queue.test.ts and the others tsc lists (~48 typed sites).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Fixture: a repo whose `.tumwater/land-queue/` holds two entries with `tick` and a torn file. `runStartupMigrations` moves all three into `merge-queue/`, removes `land-queue/` and logs one `state_migrated`. `readLandingQueue` then returns the two entries in their original order with `run` set, and counts the torn file as unreadable. A second call changes nothing and logs nothing.
- `runStartupMigrationsIfIdle` moves nothing while a live orchestrator info file names a running pid, and migrates when none does. Registering a duplicate step name throws.
- Before any migration, `readLandingQueue` on the old layout returns both entries with `run` set.
- After `runOrchestrator` starts on the old-layout fixture, the queued entries are vetted and dropped as before.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Fallback chain, part 6/7: `claudeWindowReserve` leaves part of each subscription window unused by the team (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 5/7 landed; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "Reserve"; touches src/config/ src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/events/ docs/backends.md and their tests)

**Goal.** The team and you share one claude.ai account. A team that uses up the weekly window by Tuesday leaves your own Claude Code sessions on extra usage, or locked out, until it resets.

This part adds an optional reserve: `"claudeWindowReserve": { "seven_day": 0.8 }`. At or past that utilization, subscription Claude counts as used up for the team until the window resets. The team then moves down its chain (part 1/7), or waits if it has nowhere to go. It also lets the team leave the subscription before a run crosses into overage. The director is exempt: it runs your own prompts. Absent by default.

**Approach.**
- Config: an optional top-level `claudeWindowReserve: Record<string, number>`, mapping a window type to a fraction with 0 < f ≤ 1. Add it to the config schema, validation, the editable/known key lists and the example config.
- `claudeWindowUsedUp(account, now, reserve?)` also returns a non-reset window whose `utilization >= reserve[type]`, with that window's `resetsAt`. It returns a `reason: "rejected" | "reserve"` beside it.
- `claudeWindowObservation` (src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts) holds on a reserve crossing too, so subscription Claude jobs with no fallback wait. The observation carries `reserve: true`. Scheduling must not hold the director on it: the director hold the BUGS.md 2026-10-16 fix adds applies to a rejected window only.
- The budget gate passes the live config's reserve. Part 2/7's director view ignores it.
- A later Claude model in a chain (an `extraUsage` step, part 5/7) would spend the reserved quota before it reaches extra usage. Past the reserve it is usable only once a current reading shows `isUsingOverage`.
- A new `claude_window_reserved` event `{ windowType, utilization, reserve, resetsAt }` is logged once per window, with the same once-per-`type:resetsAt` memory as `pollClaudeWindowWarning`. src/events/event-format.ts renders it.
- docs/backends.md: the key, an example, and the note that the team learns its utilization one run late (readings come only from runs).

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/config/config-keys.ts, src/config/config-editable-keys.ts, src/config/config-example.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md, tumwater.example.json.
- Tests: test/claude-account.test.ts, test/fleet-polls.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/config-validation*.test.ts, and test/event-format-fleet.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `seven_day` utilization 0.85 and reserve 0.8:
  - Subscription Claude role jobs move to the fallback.
  - The director stays on Claude.
  - `claude_window_reserved` is logged once.
- At 0.75 nothing moves.
- At 0.85 with `fallback: [{ model: "claude/claude-sonnet-5-5", maxDailyCostUsd: 10 }, LOCAL]` and no reading showing `isUsingOverage`, the default tier resolves to LOCAL, not the extra-usage step. With `isUsingOverage` reported, it resolves to the extra-usage step.
- With no fallback, non-director Claude roles wait until `resetsAt` while the director still runs.
- Validation rejects 0, 1.5, and a non-number.
- Absent, every existing test passes unchanged, and `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` names disabled roles that still keep a branch, pointing at `tumwater retire --role <id>` (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** Disabling a role in `tumwater.json` (or lowering `roles.feature.instances`) stops its runs, but its `tumwater/<id>` branch stays, along with any worktree, landing ref, and paused marker. `tumwater retire --role <id>` (`retireRole` in `src/operator/retire.ts`) removes them, but nothing tells the operator which roles need it. This repo shows the gap: `git for-each-ref refs/heads` lists `tumwater/telemetry` while telemetry is opt-in. The "workspaces" row (`checkWorktreePool`) reports legacy checkout directories and stale pins only. It never looks at branches. Add a doctor row, "leftover role branches", that names each such role and the command that removes its leftovers.

**Approach.**
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`: add `export async function checkLeftoverRoleBranches(root: string, config?: TumwaterConfig | null): Promise<CheckOutcome>`, documented like `checkWorkInstances`. Behavior:
  - No config: return `okOutcome("no readable tumwater.json — nothing to verify")`, the `checkWorkInstances` wording. `checkInit` reports the config itself.
  - List branches with `listBranches(root)` from `src/git/git.ts`. Keep the ones that start with the prefix `branchName("")` (`src/paths.ts`, which is `tumwater/`) and strip the prefix to get an id. Drop an empty id, an id containing `/`, `DIRECTOR_ROLE`, and every id where `loopEnabled(config, id)` (`src/roles/loop-ids.ts`) is true. The director has its own `tumwater/director` branch and is never in `config.roles`, so it is always skipped.
  - Split what remains. An id that `knownRoleIds(config)` (`src/config/config.ts`) includes is retirable, because `cmdRetire`'s `namedRole` accepts exactly those ids. Every other id is unknown. Examples: a removed custom role, or an instance id such as `feature-4` above the configured instance count. `knownRoleIds` adds only `loopIds(config)` instances, so retire rejects those ids as an unknown role.
  - When both lists are empty, return `okOutcome("no branches left by disabled roles")`.
  - Otherwise return `warnOutcome` whose detail joins these parts with `"; "`. The retirable part (when non-empty) is `` `${ids.join(", ")} ${agree(n, "is", "are")} disabled but still ${agree(n, "has", "have")} a branch — \`tumwater retire --role <id>\` removes each (\`--dry-run\` previews)` ``. The unknown part (when non-empty) is `` `${branches.join(", ")} ${agree(n, "names", "name")} no role retire accepts — delete with \`git branch -D\` once its commits are not needed` ``, where the list shows the full branch names (`tumwater/ghost`). Both lists keep `listBranches` order, which is refname order. `agree` comes from `src/text/phrases.ts`.
  - The check is read-only, like every doctor check. It only lists refs.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: add `{ name: "leftover role branches", ...(await checkLeftoverRoleBranches(root, config)) }` to the `checks` array, directly after `"parallel instances"`.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` parenthetical, after the clause "waits for a workspace that call for a larger `worktreeSlots`", add ", disabled roles that still keep a `tumwater/<id>` branch (removed with `tumwater retire --role <id>`)". Do not touch any other clause.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, "checkLeftoverRoleBranches names disabled roles' branches and unknown ones, skipping enabled roles and the director". ### Fallback chain, part 5/7: A chain's first Claude model stops at the end of the subscription window, and a Claude model listed after it spends extra usage within its caps (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 4/7 landed; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "Config" and "Overage"; touches src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/config/config-fallbacks.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts docs/backends.md and their tests)

**Goal.** This account allows extra usage (`overageStatus: "allowed"` in every recorded `rate_limit_event`). So today a used-up window does not stop Claude: runs continue on paid extra usage, and their whole cost counts toward the team cap, until `maxDailyCostUsd` moves Claude model jobs to the over-cap model. That spend has no place in the chain and no cap of its own.

You decided on 2026-10-16 (plans/fallback-chain.md D1) that position in the chain decides it:

- The **first** Claude model in a tier's chain runs on the subscription only. The tier's primary counts, including a tier default from `agent: "claude"`. It is unavailable once the window is used up: rejected, or a current reading shows `isUsingOverage`.
- Any Claude model listed **after** it in the same chain may spend extra usage, within its own step cap and the team cap.
- So `"model"` Sonnet with `"fallback": [{ "model": "claude/claude-sonnet-5-5", "maxDailyCostUsd": 10 }, "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b"]` means: Sonnet on the subscription, then up to $10 of Sonnet extra usage, then local.

This is a behavior change for accounts that allow extra usage. Without a later Claude model in the chain, the team moves down its chain at the end of the window instead of spending extra usage up to the cap.

**Approach.**
- The fix in BUGS.md 2026-10-16, "After a Claude subscription window that ran into paid overage resets …", must be in, so that a reset window is not in overage. If that entry is still under `## Open`, fix it first here with its test, and move it to `## Fixed`.
- `claudeWindowUsedUp` (src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts) also counts a window whose current reading has `isUsingOverage` as used up, and returns its `resetsAt`. The hold's observation keeps the rejected-only rule: overage never holds.
- src/config/config-fallbacks.ts: `tierOwnChain` marks each Claude step `extraUsage: true` when a Claude model comes earlier in the same chain. The tier's primary (`withModelOverrides(config, tier, {})` routed to `claude`) counts as earlier.
  - A step borrowed from another tier keeps the mark from the chain that declares it.
  - No config key is added: the mark comes from position alone.
- src/gates/budget-gates.ts, the usable predicate for Claude steps:
  - **Unmarked (first) Claude step:** today's subscription rule, with "used up" now including overage. On API billing it is priced as before.
  - **`extraUsage` step on a subscription account:** usable when all of these hold:
    - the newest non-reset window's `overageStatus` is not `rejected`;
    - no window is `rejected`;
    - `!reached`;
    - its pair spend (`dayCostByPair`, part 4/7) is under its step cap;
    - its breaker is serving.
  - **`extraUsage` step on API billing:** an ordinary priced step.
- It runs the ordinary `claude` command. Its pair spend is that model's real spend, so the step cap caps extra usage directly.
  - The run that crossed into overage on the first step also counts its whole cost there (`runCostIsReal`), which is conservative.
  - The keep predicate for a subscription Claude primary uses the same "used up" rule. So an account in overage moves the primary to its chain on the next poll even below the cap.
- The run that crosses into overage finishes in overage, because tumwater cannot stop the CLI mid-run. The next poll moves on.
- docs/backends.md: the position rule, the example above, the crossing run, and the behavior change.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, src/pi/pi-models.ts (only if the bug fix is done here), src/config/config-fallbacks.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md.
- Tests: test/claude-account.test.ts, test/config-views.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, and test/orchestrator-fallback.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Marking by `tierOwnChain`:
  - With a Claude primary, every Claude step in the chain is `extraUsage`.
  - With a pi primary and `["claude/claude-sonnet-5-5", "claude/claude-sonnet-5-5", LOCAL]`, the first Claude step is unmarked and the second is marked.
  - A borrowed step keeps its mark.
- With `agent: "claude"`, `fallback: [{ model: "claude/claude-sonnet-5-5", maxDailyCostUsd: 10 }, LOCAL]`, a current window reporting `isUsingOverage`, and spend under the cap:
  - The default tier resolves to the Sonnet extra-usage step.
  - Once that pair's real spend reaches $10 it resolves to LOCAL.
  - At the team cap it resolves to LOCAL.
- The same account with `fallback: [LOCAL]` resolves the subscription Claude tiers to LOCAL on the next poll.
- A `rejected` window (no overage allowed) skips the extra-usage step and resolves to LOCAL.
- Once the window's `resetsAt` passes, the tiers return to their subscription primary, and `npm test` passes.

### The dashboard's entry drawer can move a plan or bug to the top of its section: a "Move to top" button does what `tumwater plan|bug --top <n>` does (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/invariants.md and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Feature and bugfix claim entries in file order, so an entry's position in `## Planned` / `## Open` is its priority. `tumwater plan|bug --top <n>` (`moveEntryToTop` in `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`, `topAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`) reorders an entry from a terminal. The dashboard's entry drawer can already cancel, edit, and release an entry, but it cannot reorder one. Add a "Move to top" drawer button on every plan and bug entry except the first. It posts to a new `POST /api/backlog-top`, which moves the entry with the same splice and commits `tumwater(operator): Prioritize <kind>: <title>`. Today no `backlog-top` route exists in `src/gui/gui-server.ts`, and nothing under `src/gui` calls `moveEntryToTop`. This plan leaves the TUI alone.

**Approach.** Follow the release landing (`tryReleaseEntry` / `handleBacklogRelease` / `entry-release`) step for step.
- `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`:
  - Factor the splice in `moveEntryToTop` (everything from `const first = findEntry(...)` up to the `writeTextAtomic` call) into a private `spliceEntryToTop(lines: string[], sectionTitle: string, entry: ActionableEntryRange): void`. Both `moveEntryToTop` and the new function call it, so their bytes cannot drift. `moveEntryToTop` keeps its `n === 1` fail and its out-of-range wording.
  - Add `export type MoveEntryOutcome = { status: "moved_to_top"; file: string; title: string } | { status: "gone" } | { status: "moved"; title: string } | { status: "already_first"; title: string }`.
  - Add `export function tryMoveEntryToTop(root, kind, n, expectedTitle): MoveEntryOutcome`, shaped like `tryReleaseEntry`: inside `withStateLock(primaryWorktreeLockPath(root), …)` it finds the entry with `findEntry`. A missing position gives `gone`. A different title gives `moved`. Position 1 gives `already_first` and writes nothing. Otherwise it calls `spliceEntryToTop`, writes the file, and returns `moved_to_top`.
- `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts`: add `handleBacklogTop(req, res, root)`, modeled on `handleBacklogRelease`. It takes the same body and uses `checkedBacklogKind` and `checkedEntryPositionAndTitle`. A `moved_to_top` outcome is committed through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit(root, outcome.file, stampedSubject("operator", \`Prioritize ${kind}: ${outcome.title}\`))`, with the same `// vocabulary-ok` comment, and answers `200 { ok: true, status: "moved_to_top", file, title, committed }`. It calls no `requestWake`, because reordering makes no entry newly eligible, which matches `topAndAnnounce`. `already_first` answers `200 { ok: true, status: "already_first", title }`, and `gone`/`moved` answer `okGone(res)`. Add backlog-top to the header comment and to the `checkedEntryPositionAndTitle` doc's endpoint list. Re-export it from `src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts`, and route `"POST /api/backlog-top"` in `src/gui/gui-server.ts` beside `"POST /api/backlog-release"`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` (`refreshEntry`): in the plans/bugs branch, add `(index > 0 ? "<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-act='entry-top' data-arg='" + esc(file + ":" + index) + "'>Move to top</button>" : "")` after the Release button. `index` is the drawer's 0-based index, so this hides the button on the first entry.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts` (`runAct`): add an `entry-top` arm beside `entry-release`. It uses the same `entryTitleAt`, kind, and position mapping and posts to `/api/backlog-top`. Its flash callback calls `closeDrawer()`. On `moved_to_top` it returns `"Moved “" + splitTitle(title).title + "” to the top of " + (BUGS.md|PLANS.md) + " — " + (bugfix|feature) + " takes it next" + uncommittedTail(d)`. On `already_first` it returns `"That entry is already first — refreshed"`, and otherwise `"That entry was removed or moved — refreshed"`. The drawer closes because the entry's index has changed.
- `docs/invariants.md` INV-B5: after the release clause, add "your reorder (`--top` and the dashboard's Move to top, `handleBacklogTop`) commits `Prioritize <kind>: <title>` and wakes no role". Add `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts` (`handleBacklogTop`) to **Binds**. `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts` is already listed in **Pinned by**.

**Files touched.** src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/invariants.md, test/backlog-write-top.test.ts, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts, test/gui-client-boot.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The existing `test/backlog-write-top.test.ts` tests (such as "moveEntryToTop moves the last entry first and leaves ## Done untouched" and "moveEntryToTop moves a middle entry above the first") pass unchanged.
- Unit (`test/backlog-write-top.test.ts`, modeled on "tryReleaseEntry leaves the bytes releaseEntry leaves and refuses without writing" in `test/backlog-write-cancel.test.ts`): seed two repos with `withDone`. `moveEntryToTop(a, "plan", 3)` and `tryMoveEntryToTop(b, "plan", 3, "c")` leave byte-identical PLANS.md, and the latter returns `{ status: "moved_to_top", file: "PLANS.md", title: "c" }`. On a fresh seed, `tryMoveEntryToTop` with a wrong title returns `{ status: "moved", title: … }`, position 9 returns `{ status: "gone" }`, and position 1 returns `{ status: "already_first", title: "a" }`. Each of those three leaves the file unchanged.
- Endpoint (`test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`, modeled on "handleBacklogRelease lifts the Refused note, wakes the kind's role, and answers gone, not_refused, and 400s without writing"): a plan at position 2 answers `{ ok: true, status: "moved_to_top", file: "PLANS.md", title: "p2", committed: false }`, and p2's heading now precedes p1's. The same for a bug. Position 1 answers `already_first`, and a stale title answers `{ ok: true, status: "gone" }`. `wakeRequestPath(root)` does not exist after any of these. The four bad bodies used by the release test answer 400 without writing.

In `test/gui-client-boot.test.ts`, a test like "entry-release posts the release at once for plans and bugs" shows `runAct("entry-top", "plans:1")` and `runAct("entry-top", "bugs:0")` posting `["/api/backlog-top", { kind: "plan", position: 2, title: "B" }]` and `["/api/backlog-top", { kind: "bug", position: 1, title: "C" }]`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms state, part 1/5: Rename LoopState ticks to runs (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires Plain terms event log 9/9 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "State and git"; touches src/loop/ src/tick/ src/verdict/ src/cli/cli-run.ts src/scheduling/ src/ui/ test/)

**Goal.** Mechanical. The per-role state file `.tumwater/state/<id>.json` stores its run counter as `runs`. A file the old build wrote, with `ticks`, loads unchanged and is saved back as `runs`. The JSON key equals the TypeScript property, with no alias.

**Approach.**
- src/loop/loop-state.ts:
  - `LoopState.runs` replaces `ticks`, including in `freshLoopState`, `zeroCounters` and `loadLoopState`'s heal.
  - Add a `LEGACY_STATE_KEYS` table (old key → new key).
  - `loadLoopState` applies the table to the parsed object before the spread onto the fresh state. Copy the old key's value to the new key when the new key is absent, then delete the old key in every case, so a file holding both keeps the new value and `saveLoopState` writes only new keys.
  - This part adds `ticks → runs`.
  - If the vocabulary guard flags a legacy key literal, end its line with `// vocabulary-ok: legacy state key read from old files`.
- Every reader goes through `loadLoopState`: `loopStateForPoll` (status-polls.ts), retire.ts and `LoopRunner`'s constructor. Nothing else needs a fallback.
- Consumers: tsc lists ~28 src sites in ~11 files, among them:
  - loop.ts and loop-tick.ts (`s.ticks + 1`);
  - tick-stage.ts and refusal.ts (the trailer's number);
  - cli-run.ts's `ticksBefore`/`ticksThisRound`;
  - once-round.ts;
  - scheduling.ts and tick-verdict.ts;
  - status-payload.ts, where the `--json` key is already `runs` from Plain terms scripting and only the right-hand side changes;
  - status-render.ts.

  Keep other identifiers that contain "tick" (`ticksBefore`, `ticksRun`, `tickNumber`); Plain terms code run renames them.
- Tests: ~221 typed sites in ~39 files, mostly `.ticks` on a `LoopState` and `ticks:` in `LoopState` literals. JSON state fixtures written straight to `state/<id>.json` keep `ticks` and now exercise the loader. Add loader cases to test/loop-state.test.ts.
- **Self-hosting:** safe in one part. The old build saves `ticks` until it exits, and the new build's loader maps it before any use. The old build never loads a file the new build saved, because the CLI and the orchestrator share one dist. The exception is a standalone dashboard still on the old build, which shows 0 runs until it restarts (display only).

**Files touched.** src/loop/loop-state.ts, src/loop/loop.ts, src/loop/loop-tick.ts, src/tick/tick-stage.ts, src/tick/tick-verdict.ts, src/verdict/refusal.ts, src/cli/cli-run.ts, src/scheduling/once-round.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts; test/loop-state.test.ts and the ~39 test files tsc lists.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `{ "role": "qa", "ticks": 7 }` loads as `runs: 7`, and the next save writes `runs` with no `ticks` key.
- A file holding both `ticks: 3` and `runs: 9` loads `runs: 9` and drops `ticks`.
- The next run of a role whose state the old build wrote is numbered from the old counter: run 8 after `ticks: 7`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's Settings view can send a test notification: a "Send test" button on the Notify hook row runs what `tumwater notify --test` runs (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/cli/notify-command.ts, src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/invariants.md and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The Settings view (`renderSettings` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`) lets an operator set the `notify` hook, but they can only check that it works from a terminal, with `tumwater notify --test` (`cmdNotify` in `src/cli/notify-command.ts`). Add a "Send test" button to the Notify hook row. It posts to a new `POST /api/notify-test`, which runs the saved hook once with the same synthetic event, waits under the same `NOTIFY_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS` bound, and flashes the same outcome line the CLI prints. Today no notify route exists in `src/gui/gui-server.ts`, and nothing under `src/gui` or `src/ui/gui` calls `runNotifyHook`. This plan leaves the TUI alone.

**Approach.**
- `src/cli/notify-command.ts`:
  - Give `runNotifyHook` a fourth parameter, `stdio: "inherit" | "ignore" = "inherit"`, and pass it to `spawn`. The CLI keeps inheriting stdio. The dashboard passes `"ignore"`, so a hook's output never lands in the server's terminal or logs. The existing call `runNotifyHook("sleep 30", {}, 150)` in the tests still type-checks.
  - Extract the outcome into `export type NotifyTestOutcome = { status: "not_configured" } | { status: "ran"; passed: boolean; message: string }` and `export async function testNotifyHook(root: string, stdio: "inherit" | "ignore" = "inherit"): Promise<NotifyTestOutcome>`. It reads `loadConfig(root).notify`. An unset or empty hook gives `not_configured`. Otherwise it runs the hook with `notifyCommandEnv(NOTIFY_TEST_TYPE, NOTIFY_TEST_SOURCE, NOTIFY_TEST_MESSAGE)` and builds the line `cmdNotify` prints today: `notify hook did not finish within 10s and was killed`, `notify hook exited 0`, or `notify hook exited with code N` plus `notifyExitGloss(N)`. `passed` is true only on exit 0.
  - `cmdNotify` becomes the CLI wrapper: usage check, then the `running the notify hook …` line, then `testNotifyHook(root)`. On `not_configured` it calls the same `fail(...)` as now. Otherwise it calls `say(outcome.message)` and sets `process.exitCode = 1` when the hook did not pass. Its output and exit codes stay as they are.
- `src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts`: add `handleNotifyTest(req, res, root)`, which ignores its body the way `handleRestart` does (`readPostBody(req, res, "{}")`). On `not_configured` it answers `409 { error: "notify is not configured (set \`notify\` in tumwater.json)" }`, the CLI's wording. Otherwise it answers `200 { ok: true, passed, message }`. The hook's own failure is still a 200: the request worked, and `passed` carries the verdict. Add the handler to the file's header comment, re-export it from `src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts` (and update that header's list), and route `"POST /api/notify-test"` in `src/gui/gui-server.ts` beside `"POST /api/config-unset"`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`:
  - In `renderSettings`, only the `notify` row gets `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm rowaction' data-action='notify-test' title='Runs the saved hook once with a synthetic merge_failed event'>Send test</button>` after its Clear button.

Then it calls `postJson("/api/notify-test", {})` and flashes `d.message`, prefixed with `error: ` when `d.passed` is false. A rejected post flashes `"error: " + clientErrorMessage(err)`, which covers the 409's not-configured text.
  - Mention the button in the module's doc comment.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts`: add a delegated click listener beside the `doctor-rerun` one: `if (clickClosest(ev, "button[data-action='notify-test']")) { ev.preventDefault(); testNotify(); }`.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the `notify --test` row, add that the dashboard's Settings view runs the same test from its Notify hook row ("Send test"). `docs/invariants.md` INV-E1: extend the guarantee to the dashboard's `POST /api/notify-test`, which runs under the same bound. Add `testNotifyHook` to **Binds** and `handleNotifyTest` (`src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts`), and add the new endpoint test to **Pinned by**.

### The dashboard's entry drawer offers "Release this entry" on a refused plan or bug, the `plan|bug --release <n>` the CLI already has (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/invariants.md and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A refused plan or bug stays held until a human lifts its **Refused** note. `tumwater plan|bug --release <n>` (`releaseEntry` in `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts` plus `releaseAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`) lifts it, commits it on main, and wakes the kind's role. The dashboard's entry drawer can ask the director, edit, and cancel an entry (`refreshEntry` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts`), but it cannot release one. An operator who sees a refused entry in the dashboard has to switch to a terminal. Add a "Release this entry" button that appears only when the entry carries a Refused note. It posts to a new `POST /api/backlog-release`, which does what `--release` does. No `release` route or action exists under `src/gui` or `src/ui/gui` today (grep `release` there). This plan leaves the TUI and `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` alone.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`: add `export type ReleaseEntryOutcome = { status: "released"; file: string; title: string } | { status: "gone" } | { status: "moved"; title: string } | { status: "not_refused"; title: string }` and `export function tryReleaseEntry(root, kind, n, expectedTitle): ReleaseEntryOutcome`. It is `tryCancelEntry`'s shape with `releaseEntry`'s splice. Inside `withStateLock(primaryWorktreeLockPath(root), …)`, read the file and run `findEntry(md, sectionTitle, n)`. An undefined entry gives `gone`, and a different title gives `moved`. Then slice the entry's lines and apply `withoutRefusalNotes`. When nothing was dropped the result is `not_refused`. Otherwise splice the kept lines in, `writeTextAtomic`, and return `released`. Then make `releaseEntry` share the slice-and-splice step with it: extract a small `liftRefusal(lines, entry): string[] | null` helper (null when there is no note), so the two cannot drift. `releaseEntry`'s CLI wording and its failures stay as they are.
- `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts`: add `handleBacklogRelease(req, res, root)`, a copy of `handleBacklogCancel`'s validation (`readPostBody`, `checkedBacklogKind`, `checkedEntryPositionAndTitle`, and a 400 on a thrown error). On `released`, commit through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit(root, outcome.file, stampedSubject("operator", \`Release ${kind}: ${outcome.title}\`))` with the same `// vocabulary-ok` comment as its siblings. Then call `requestWake(root, [OPERATOR_FILE_KINDS[kind].role])` from `src/operator/operator-intent.ts`, as `releaseAndAnnounce` does: a released entry is newly eligible, so its role should look now. Answer `200 { ok: true, status: "released", file, title, committed }`. `gone` and `moved` answer `okGone(res)`. `not_refused` answers `200 { ok: true, status: "not_refused", title }` and writes and wakes nothing. Update the file's header comment to list backlog-release.
- Re-export it in `src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts`, and route `"POST /api/backlog-release"` in `src/gui/gui-server.ts` beside `"POST /api/backlog-cancel"`.
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` `handleBacklog`: add `refused: refusalNote(entry.body) !== null` (`refusalNote` from `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`) to the JSON it sends, so the drawer knows without parsing markdown. Questions are never refused, so the field is `false` for them, which is harmless.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` `refreshEntry`: for plans and bugs, when `d.refused` is true, add `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm btn-primary' data-act='entry-release' data-arg='<file>:<index>'>Release this entry</button>` before "Edit this entry". Use one click, with no arming: release is undoable and is what the operator came to do.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts` `runAct`: add an `entry-release` branch shaped like `entry-cancel` without the arm step. It uses `entryTitleAt`, then `postAction("/api/backlog-release", { kind, position: Number(index) + 1, title }, …)`, then `closeDrawer()`. The flash is `Released “<title>” in PLANS.md|BUGS.md — <role> will pick it up` plus `uncommittedTail(d)`. For `not_refused` it reads `That entry carries no Refused note — refreshed`. Otherwise it reads `That entry was removed or moved — refreshed`.
- `docs/invariants.md`: in the operator-commit guarantee that lists "Your cancel, edit, and question answer …", add the release (`--release` and the dashboard's Release) as committing `Release <kind>: <title>` and waking the kind's role. Add `handleBacklogRelease` to that section's code list.

**Files touched.** src/backlog/backlog-write.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/invariants.md, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui.test.ts, test/gui-client-boot.test.ts, and new `tryReleaseEntry` cases in `test/backlog-write-cancel.test.ts` (where the `tryCancelEntry` unit tests live).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit (`tryReleaseEntry` against a temp root): an entry whose body starts with a `**Refused 2026-10-16 by feature: x**` line between blank lines gives `released`. The file then holds the entry without the note and with one blank line where the note was, which is the same bytes `releaseEntry` produces on a copy of that file. A stale title gives `moved` and position 9 gives `gone`. An entry with no note gives `not_refused`. All three leave the file byte-identical. The existing CLI test "plan and bug --release lift the Refused note and commit it on main" (`test/backlog-commit.test.ts`) passes unchanged.
- Endpoint (`test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`, modeled on "handleBacklogCancel removes the entry, answers gone for a stale title, 400s bad input, wakes nobody"): releasing a refused plan answers `{ ok: true, status: "released", file: "PLANS.md", title, committed: false }` (the temp root is not a git repo), removes the note, and leaves a wake request naming `feature` at `wakeRequestPath(root)` (`src/paths.ts`). Releasing a refused bug names `bugfix`. A stale title answers `{ ok: true, status: "gone" }`. An unrefused entry answers `status: "not_refused"` with no file change and no wake. The 400 bodies the cancel test lists (bad kind, position 0, missing or empty title) each 400 with the file unchanged.
- `GET /api/backlog` answers `refused: true` for an entry carrying a Refused note and `refused: false` for one without. The `/api/backlog` test in `test/gui.test.ts` deep-equals `{ title, body }`, so add `refused: false` to its expected objects and add one refused entry to its fixture to assert `refused: true`.
- Client (`test/gui-client-boot.test.ts`, modeled on "entry-cancel arms on the first click and posts the cancel on the second"): one `entry-release` act on `plans:1` posts `["/api/backlog-release", { kind: "plan", position: 2, title }]` right away, and `bugs:0` posts `kind: "bug"`. A drawer test, or a grep-level check like those the existing drawer tests use, shows the button renders only when `refused` is true.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Fallback chain, part 4/7: Priced fallback steps with their own daily caps (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/7 landed; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "When a step is available" and "Spend per step"; touches src/config/ src/loop/loop-state.ts src/budget/budget.ts src/tick/tick-usage.ts src/loop/loop-pi.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts docs/backends.md and their tests)

**Goal.** A fallback must be free today, because it only ever runs at the cap. Once a used-up window also moves work (part 1/7), the step after the subscription is often a paid one. For example, "spend up to $5 a day on HF Inference Providers, then go local". This part lets a step be an object with its own daily cap, and lets priced steps sit in a chain. A priced step is usable only while the team is under `maxDailyCostUsd` and the step is under its own cap, so no cap can be passed.

**Approach.**
- Config (src/config/config-schema.ts, config-validation.ts):
  - A chain element may be `{ "model": "<model id>", "maxDailyCostUsd"?: number }`.
  - Add `FALLBACK_STEP_KEYS`. `model` is required, and `maxDailyCostUsd` must be a positive number.
  - A string element is the same as `{ "model": … }`.
- src/loop/loop-state.ts: `LoopState.dayCostByPair?: Record<string, number>`.
  - It holds real USD per `modelPairName` for the local day in `dayStamp`.
  - It is healed on load like `dayCostUsd`: non-numbers and negatives drop, and a `__proto__` key is kept as an own property.
- src/budget/budget.ts:
  - `recordDailyCost(s, usd, now, pair?)` also folds into `dayCostByPair[pair]`, and the day rollover clears it.
  - `pairDailyCost(states, pair, now)` sums it over roles.
- src/tick/tick-usage.ts: `fold` passes the run's pair, built from the run's own resolved config. src/loop/loop-pi.ts already has `opts.config`; pass `modelPairName(opts.config)` beside the hold key. Estimated (subscription) spend never folds into it.
- src/gates/budget-gates.ts: the usable predicate per step becomes:
  - **Free step:** usable when its breaker is serving (today's rule).
  - **Priced step:** usable when `!reached`, the step's pair spend is under its own cap (if it has one), and its breaker is serving.

  At the cap only free steps remain usable, which is today's behavior. Priced steps also join the breaker map.
- **Per-run cap.** `applyFallbackModel` records each moved tier's step cap on the derived config: `fallbackStepCaps?: Record<pairName, number>`, set only on the derived view and never read from tumwater.json.
  - `authoringBudgetCap` (src/loop/loop-pi.ts) lowers an API-billed Claude run's `--max-budget-usd` to the step's remaining budget when its pair has one.
  - Subscription runs still get no per-run cap.
- docs/backends.md: the step-object form, the "priced steps never run past a cap" rule, and an example chain of subscription Claude, then HF capped at $5, then local.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/config/config-fallbacks.ts, src/loop/loop-state.ts, src/budget/budget.ts, src/tick/tick-usage.ts, src/loop/loop-pi.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md.
- Tests: test/config-validation-model.test.ts, test/loop-state.test.ts, test/budget.test.ts, test/tick-usage.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/loop-pi-claude.test.ts. (The chain-resolution and step-cap tests landed in test/budget-gates.test.ts rather than test/orchestrator-fallback.test.ts; the per-run pair key is `seamPairName` in src/config/config-views.ts, threaded through src/loop/loop.ts and src/landing/landing-slot.ts.)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `recordDailyCost` with a pair:
  - It accumulates per pair and resets at local midnight.
  - A run with only estimated cost leaves `dayCostByPair` untouched.
  - A corrupt stored map heals to `{}`.
- Below the cap, with a rejected window and `fallback: [{ model: HF, maxDailyCostUsd: 5 }, LOCAL]`:
  - The tier resolves to HF.
  - Once the HF pair's spend reaches $5 it resolves to LOCAL.
  - At the team cap it resolves to LOCAL, whatever the HF spend.
- An API-billed Claude step with $2 left on its cap gets `--max-budget-usd 2` or less.
- Existing configs with only free fallbacks resolve exactly as before, and `npm test` passes.
