### `tumwater doctor`'s refusal warning says how many planned parts wait on a refused part, so a series stuck behind a refusal is visible (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `checkRefusedEntries` in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, adds one exported function to `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, and adds tests to `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts` and `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts` plus one clause in `docs/cli.md`'s Audit row. The TUI backlog pane plan edits only `src/ui/tui/`, and Plain terms text 18/19 edits role instructions and hold-mark wording, so the tests here match the doctor's own message text, never a hold mark)

**Goal.** No role clears a **Refused** note. When the refused plan is a series part that other plans require (`requires <Series> i/n landed`), every part that requires it, directly or through a chain of parts, stays blocked until a person edits or releases the refused part. The backlog index, `plan --list` and `tumwater backlog` show those parts only as `[blocked: each waits on an earlier part]` or `[blocked: requires …]`, which looks like normal progress. `checkRefusedEntries` warns about the refused entry but does not say that a series waits on it. The warning should give that count, so the operator knows that releasing or cancelling this one entry frees N parts.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: add an exported pure function `plansWaitingOn(planned: readonly BacklogEntry[], index: number): number[]`. It returns the ascending indexes into `planned` of the entries that require `planned[index]`'s own part, directly or transitively. Matching is by `partKey` (series case-insensitive, part verbatim), the same way `entryHoldAgainst` matches. When `seriesPart(planned[index].title)` is null, return `[]`. Build the reverse edges once: for each entry with a `seriesPart`, for each `requiredParts(entry.title)` ref, record that entry index under the ref's key. Then do a breadth-first walk from the root's key with a visited set of indexes, so a dependency cycle (which `checkPlanDependencies` reports) ends the walk. Never include `index` itself. The doc comment says it is the doctor's count of a refusal's stranded dependents.
2. `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `checkRefusedEntries`: for PLANS.md entries, compute `waiting = plansWaitingOn(planned, index).length`. Bugs get 0. Then:
   - The first entry's message adds, after the `stale` clause and before `more`: `; ${waiting} planned part(s) wait on it, directly or through an earlier part`, only when `waiting > 0`.
   - Each `andMore` item adds ` [${waiting} part(s) wait on it]` when `waiting > 0`, after the existing `[prerequisites no longer planned]` suffix.
   - With no waiting parts, the message is the same as today. The ok text is unchanged. Update the doc comment to say the warning counts the parts the refusal holds.
3. `docs/cli.md`, Audit row: after "flagging one whose prerequisites are no longer planned", add ", and counting the planned parts that wait on a refused part".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test `plansWaitingOn follows requires clauses transitively and stops on a cycle`. Use entries `S, part 1/3: a`, `S, part 2/3: b (requires part 1/3 landed)`, `S, part 3/3: c (requires part 2/3 landed)`, `Other`, and `T, part 1/1: d (requires S 1/3 landed)`. Then `plansWaitingOn(planned, 0)` is `[1, 2, 4]`, `plansWaitingOn(planned, 2)` is `[]`, and `plansWaitingOn(planned, 3)` (no series part) is `[]`. A second fixture, where `X, part 1/2` and `X, part 2/2` require each other, returns `[1]` for index 0 and terminates. Before writing the requires clauses in the fixtures, confirm against `requiredParts`'s parsing that they parse, for example by asserting `requiredParts` on one of them.
- New test `checkRefusedEntries counts the planned parts that wait on a refused part`. Its PLANS.md fixture has a refused `S, part 1/3` and parts 2/3 and 3/3 that require the earlier part. The warn detail contains `; 2 planned part(s) wait on it, directly or through an earlier part`. A second refused, non-series plan in the same fixture shows up in the `(and 1 more: …)` tail with no `wait on it` suffix.
- The existing tests `checkRefusedEntries warns naming the first refused entry, the rest, and how to release it` and `checkRefusedEntries reads ok with no notes, with no files, and ignores Done and Fixed` pass unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The TUI backlog pane's list shows each blocked series as one line, so bugs and questions are not pushed off the screen by 100+ waiting parts (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `labeledBacklogEntries` and `backlogLines` in `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts` and the backlog list-mode branch of `paneBody` in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, with tests in `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`. It does not touch `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`, or the selection logic. The dashboard plan edits only `src/ui/status-payload.ts` and `src/ui/gui/`. Plain terms text 8/19 and 18/19 edit help prose and role instructions and hold marks, so the tests here build expected marks from `holdMark` instead of fixed strings; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The TUI's backlog pane (`paneBody`'s `pane.kind === "backlog"` branch in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`) has a list mode. It prints `plans (N):` with one line per planned entry, then the open bugs, then the open questions, and keeps the head of the list when it overflows `eventBudget`. In this repo, more than 80 plan lines are Plain terms parts waiting on an earlier part, so the bugs and questions sections never show. `plan --list`, the prompt's backlog index and `tumwater backlog` already show such a series as one line through `groupBlockedSeries` in `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`. The TUI list should do the same. Each series with two or more blocked parts becomes one line, `<series>, N blocked parts (2/5–5/5) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]`, at the place of its first part. The `plans (N):` count stays the number of planned entries. Entry mode (up/down) is unchanged: the selection still walks the flat entry list, one entry per part, so every part can still be opened, edited, or cancelled.

**Approach.**
1. `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`:
   - `labeledBacklogEntries` also returns, for each row, `hold: EntryHold` and `claimer: string | undefined`. Plans and bugs read them from `backlogHolds(root)` and `backlogInProgress(root)` (both exported from `../../backlog/backlog-eligibility.js`, with the same order as `backlogMarks`). Questions get `hold: null, claimer: undefined`. Keep `mark` as it is today, from `backlogMarks`. Update the doc comment.
   - Add an exported pure function `planListLines(plans: ReadonlyArray<{ title: string; mark: string; hold: EntryHold; claimer: string | undefined }>): string[]`. It maps `groupBlockedSeries(plans)`: a `row` group returns `row.title + row.mark`, and a `series` group returns `` `${g.series}, ${g.rows.length} blocked parts (${partsLabel(g.rows)}) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]` ``. That is the same text `listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` prints after its position prefix. Import `groupBlockedSeries` and `partsLabel` from `../../backlog/backlog-structure.js`, where both are already exported.
   - `backlogLines(plans, bugs, questions, planCount = plans.length)`: the subheader reads `plans (${planCount}):`. The empty checks still use the array lengths. Every current caller and test passes three arguments, so they are unchanged.
2. `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, list mode: build the plan lines with `planListLines(flat.filter((e) => e.label === "plan"))` and pass the plan entry count as `planCount`. Bugs and questions keep `listed(...)`. The bold-subheader and dim-`(` tone rules stay as they are. Entry mode and the stale-selection clamp are not changed.
3. `docs/cli.md`: in the Steer-the-project row, where `plan --list` is said to show a series' blocked parts as one line, add that the TUI's backlog pane list does too, with up/down still opening each part.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test `planListLines collapses a series' blocked parts to one line at its first part`. Its rows are `Ready` (hold null), `S, part 1/3: a` (hold null), `S, part 2/3: b` and `S, part 3/3: c` (each with hold `{ blockedBy: [...] }`, claimer undefined) and `Lone, part 2/2: d` (blocked). **Goal.** The dashboard's Plans tab now lists the entries a role can pick first and gathers the rest under "Blocked (N)". ### `tumwater backlog` prints each blocked series as one heading with no body, so the plans a role can pick are not buried under thousands of lines of blocked parts (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. **Goal.** `tumwater backlog` (`cmdBacklog` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`) prints every `## Planned` entry with its full body. In this repo, more than 80 parts of the Plain terms series are blocked, each waiting on an earlier part, and together they fill thousands of lines. `plan --list` (`listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`) and the prompt's backlog index (`collapseBlockedSeries`) already show such a series as one line through `groupBlockedSeries`. `tumwater backlog` should do the same. Each series with two or more blocked parts becomes one heading with no body, placed where the first of those parts would have been. Every other entry prints as it does today. `--json` is unchanged, so scripts still get every entry.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`: import `groupBlockedSeries` and `partsLabel` from `./backlog-structure.js` (both are already exported). Add a `renderPlannedSection(entries, holds, inProgress)` beside `renderSection`. With no `holds`, it returns `renderSection("Planned features", entries, undefined, inProgress)`, so output is identical to today. With `holds`, it builds rows `{ index: i, title: entry.title, hold: holds[i] ?? null, claimer: inProgress?.[i] ?? undefined }` and maps `groupBlockedSeries(rows)`:
   - A `row` group prints exactly what `renderSection`'s loop prints for entry `index`: the heading with `holdMark` and `inProgressMark`, a blank line, the body indented two spaces, and a blank line. Move that per-entry block into a small `renderEntry(entry, hold, runner)` helper that both functions call, so the two cannot drift.

2. `renderBacklogMarkdown` calls `renderPlannedSection` for the Planned section. The Open bugs and Open questions sections keep `renderSection`. Bugs are not series in practice, and `plan --list` groups only plans too.
3. `cmdBacklog` needs no change. Its view already carries `holds` and `inProgress`. `--ready` removes every held entry through `readyBacklog` before rendering, so nothing can group in that mode, and its "held entries hidden" count is unchanged.
4. Help and docs: in `src/cli/help.ts`, add one clause to the `tumwater backlog [--ready] [--json]` stanza: "a series with two or more blocked parts prints as one heading (--json still lists every entry)". Add the same clause to the `tumwater backlog` text in `docs/cli.md`'s "Check state" row.

### The dashboard's Plans and Bugs tabs list the entries a role can pick first and gather blocked ones under a "Blocked (N)" divider, so the few ready plans are not buried among 100+ blocked parts (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. The `plan --list` grouping plan edits `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` and `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `questions --answered` edits `cmdQuestions` and `question-answer.ts`, and Plain terms text 7/19 rewords backlog command output and the role page; none touches these files. The TUI's backlog list is left alone, because Plain terms text 9/19 owns the TUI tabs and the tui-panes split is refused; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The dashboard's Plans tab paints `## Planned` in file order. Here that is well over 100 rows. The refused tui-panes plan comes first, then text 7/19, then about 100 blocked Plain terms parts, and the newest plans that roles can pick sit at the very bottom. Each row already shows its hold mark (`planHolds`), but an operator still has to scroll past every blocked row to find the plans that will run next. Show the rows a role can pick first, then the blocked rows under one divider. Every row keeps its click address.

**Approach.**
1. `src/ui/status-payload.ts` `statusPayload`: add two boolean arrays beside `planHolds`/`bugHolds`. Name them `planBlocked` and `bugBlocked`, built as `backlogHolds(root).plans.map((h) => h !== null)` (and the same for `.bugs`). Import `backlogHolds` from `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`; it is stat-cached, so the second read beside `backlogMarks` costs a cache hit. They are index-for-index parallel to `plans`/`bugs`, like `planHolds`. Any non-null `EntryHold` counts as blocked: refused, needs review, needs replan, or requires a part. An entry someone is working on but that has no hold stays `false`, so it keeps its `[working on it: …]` mark in the top group. Do not read the mark string to decide this; the Plain terms parts reword those marks.
2. `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts` `renderBacklog`, in the Plans/Bugs branch (not Questions, not the Inbox): read `blocked = key === "plans" ? (d.planBlocked || []) : key === "bugs" ? (d.bugBlocked || []) : []`. Build the row HTML for each index `i` exactly as today, then split it into two lists: rows where `blocked[i]` is false, then rows where it is true, each in file order. When the second list is not empty, put one divider row between the lists: `<div class='list-item list-divider'><span class='li-meta'>Blocked (N)</span></div>`. "Blocked" is the docs/glossary.md word for a held backlog entry. Each row keeps `data-index='i'`, its original position, so the drawer, the Answer button, and the `openEntryKey` highlight still address the right entry. When no row is blocked, or the payload has no `planBlocked`/`bugBlocked` (an older server), the HTML is the same as before. The New plan/File a bug row stays first. The tab badge still counts every entry.
3. `src/ui/gui/gui-styles.ts`: add one rule, `.list-divider { padding: 6px 16px; background: var(--surface-2); }`, plus `.list-divider:hover` holding the same background so the divider does not light up like a row.
4. No toggle and no setting. Ordering by pickability is the one default, which follows the "opinionated defaults" principle. Grouping a series into one row, as `plan --list` will, is left for a later plan once `groupBlockedSeries` lands.

### `tumwater plan --list` shows each blocked series as one line, as the prompt's backlog index does, so an operator's list of 100+ planned entries fits on a screen and the eligible plans stand out (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `collapseBlockedSeries` and its helpers in `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, the plans branch of `listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, the `plan --list` stanza of `src/cli/help.ts`, and the `--list` clause of `docs/cli.md`'s "Steer the project" row. Plain terms text 7/19, in flight, rewords messages in these two backlog files; this plan adds a grouping helper and one list branch and rewords none of the existing messages. The `questions --answered` plan edits `cmdQuestions` and `question-answer.ts` instead) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater plan --list` prints every `## Planned` entry on its own numbered line. Today that is well over 100 lines, and most are blocked parts of the Plain terms series. The prompt's `<backlog-index>` already groups those parts into one line per series (`collapseBlockedSeries`, from "Compact backlog index, part 1/1"). The operator's list should group them the same way. Numbering is unchanged: a grouped line names the positions it covers, so `--show <n>`, `--edit <n>` and `--cancel <n>` still reach every part.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`: split the grouping out of `collapseBlockedSeries` into an exported pure function, `groupBlockedSeries<T extends SeriesRow>(rows: readonly T[]): SeriesGroup<T>[]`.
   - Types: `SeriesRow = { title: string; hold: EntryHold; claimer: string | undefined }` and `SeriesGroup<T> = { kind: "row"; row: T } | { kind: "series"; series: string; rows: T[] }`.
   - Same rules as today: a row is collapsible through `collapsibleSeriesPart`, a series groups only with two or more collapsible parts, and the group sits at its first part's place.
   - Make `IndexRow` extend `SeriesRow`. Widen `collapsibleSeriesPart` and `partsLabel` to take `SeriesRow`, and export `partsLabel`.
   - Rewrite `collapseBlockedSeries` as a map over `groupBlockedSeries`. Its output stays character-for-character the same; the existing `renderBacklogIndexBlock` collapse tests in `test/backlog-structure.test.ts` pin this.
2. `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: only the plan prose branch changes. That means not `bugSection`, not `--json`, and not `--done`.
   - Build one row per entry: `{ position: i + 1, title, hold: entryHolds[i] ?? null, claimer: entryRunners[i] ?? undefined }`, then call `groupBlockedSeries`.
   - A `row` group renders exactly as today: `${position}. ${title}${holdMark}${inProgressMark}${entryAgeSuffix}`.
   - A `series` group renders as `${positions}. ${series}, ${k} blocked parts (${partsLabel(rows)}) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]`. Here `positions` joins runs of consecutive positions with an en dash (`13–17`) and separates runs with commas (`13–15, 18`).
   - Since lines are no longer numbered by index, build them directly instead of through `numberedList`. Keep the `plans in PLANS.md:` header.
   - When at least one series grouped, append one footer line: `(each blocked series is one line; --show <n> prints a part, --json lists every entry)`.
   - The `bug --list` prose, every `--json` payload, and `--done` stay unchanged.
3. `src/cli/help.ts`: add one clause to the `plan --list` stanza: "a series' blocked parts show as one line naming their positions". `docs/cli.md`: add the same clause to the `--list` sentence of the "Steer the project" row.
4. No new flag. `--json` and `--show <n>` already give every part. This follows the "opinionated defaults" principle.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`: a new test calls `groupBlockedSeries` directly on a list with:
  - an eligible part 1/4 and three blocked parts 2/4–4/4 of one series;
  - a lone blocked part of another series;
  - a claimed blocked part.

  It yields a row, one series group of three, then rows for the lone part and the claimed part. The existing collapse tests pass unchanged.
- `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts` adds "plan --list shows a blocked series as one line with its positions". Through the `cli` harness, it uses a PLANS.md with an unrelated plan, series S parts 1/3–3/3 (2/3 requires part 1/3 landed, 3/3 requires part 2/3 landed), and a final plan. `plan --list` prints:
  - `1.` for the unrelated plan;
  - `2.` for S part 1/3;
  - `3–4. S, 2 blocked parts (2/3–3/3) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]`;
  - `5.` for the final plan;
  - the footer line.

  Also: `plan --show 4` prints part 3/3, and `plan --list --json` still has five entries with positions 1–5.
- The existing `plan --list` and `bug --list` tests in `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts` pass unchanged. None of their fixtures has two blocked parts of one series, so their output is the same as before.
- The `help topics name the --list forms` test still passes, and `tumwater help plan` shows the new clause.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater questions --answered [-n <count>]` lists the newest answered questions with their decisions, so an operator sees what they and the director decided lately without opening QUESTIONS.md (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `src/backlog/backlog.ts` (one new reader beside `openQuestionEntries`), `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `cmdQuestions` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, the `questions` stanza of `src/cli/help.ts`, and `docs/cli.md`'s "Answer open questions" row. The `plan/bug --list --done` plan edits `listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` and the "Steer the project" row instead. Plain terms text 6/19, in flight, rewords messages in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`; this plan adds a branch to `cmdQuestions` and changes none of its existing messages except the unknown-flag list, done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater questions` lists only `## Open`. Once a question is answered (from the CLI, the dashboard drawer, the TUI's Ctrl+A, or by the director), the only record of the decision is the `## Answered` section of QUESTIONS.md, and no command shows it. An operator who wants to recall "what did I decide about X last week" — or check that the director recorded a decision they gave it in a prompt — has to open the file. `tryAnswerQuestion` (`src/backlog/question-answer.ts`) appends each answered block at the end of `## Answered`, so the newest answers are the last entries in that section.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog.ts`: add `export function answeredQuestionEntries(root: string): BacklogEntry[]` beside `openQuestionEntries`, returning `sectionEntries(root, "QUESTIONS.md", "Answered")`. A missing file or section yields `[]`, and the `_None yet._` placeholder is not an entry (`sectionEntries` already skips non-heading lines).
- `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`:
  - `export const ANSWER_DATE_RE = /\*\*Answered (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b/`, and `export function answerDate(body: string): string | null` returning the first match's date. It reads the body, not the heading, because the answer stamp is a body paragraph (both the current `**Answered <date> by operator:**` stamp and older hand-written `**Answered <date> by the user: …**` paragraphs match).
  - `function answerPreview(body: string): string`: the first body line that starts with `**Answered `, with every `**` removed, whitespace collapsed, and passed through `truncate(…, BODY_PREVIEW_MAX)`; `""` when no line matches.
  - `export function answeredQuestionsNewestFirst(root: string, count: number): { entries: BacklogEntry[]; older: number }`: `answeredQuestionEntries(root)` reversed (file order is oldest first), the first `count` of them, and `older` = how many were left out.
  - `export function answeredQuestionList(root: string, count: number): string`: `no answered questions` when there are none; otherwise the header `answered questions in QUESTIONS.md, newest first:` followed by one `- <title>` bullet per entry, with ` — <answerPreview>` appended when the preview is non-empty, and a final `(<older> older; -n <count> shows more)` line when `older > 0`. Bullets, not numbers, because `questions answer <n>` positions address only `## Open`.
  - `export function answeredQuestionPayload(root: string, count: number): { questions: { title: string; body: string; answeredOn: string | null }[]; older: number }`, with `answeredOn` from `answerDate(body)`.
- `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdQuestions`: before the question number has been seen (`!numbered`), the arg loop also consumes `--answered` (once, through `rejectRepeatFlag`) and `-n <count>` (once; its value through `parseCountFlag("-n", args[++i])`, which already fails `-n needs a value` on a missing one). The `--`-prefixed unknown-flag branch admits `--answered`, and its message becomes `(valid flags for tumwater questions: --json, --file, --answered)`. After the loop:
  - `-n` without `--answered` fails `-n needs --answered (it limits the answered questions listed)`.
  - `--answered` with any word (a subcommand such as `answer`) fails `--answered lists answered questions; it takes no subcommand`, and with `--file` fails `--file only applies to questions answer <n>` (the existing message).
  - Otherwise `--answered` prints `answeredQuestionList(root, n ?? 10)`, or `sayJson(answeredQuestionPayload(root, n ?? 10))` under `--json`, and returns. Like the bare list, it runs without a repo gate and writes nothing.
  - Without `--answered`, every existing path behaves as today.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: below the `tumwater questions [--json]` stanza add `tumwater questions --answered [-n <count>] [--json]` with the prose "List the newest answered questions, newest first (default 10), each with its answer line; --json prints {questions, older}, each with title, body, answeredOn". `completion.ts` takes its words from the usage lines.
- `docs/cli.md`, "Answer open questions" row: after the `--json prints the list as data` clause add "; `tumwater questions --answered [-n <count>]` lists the newest answered questions with their answer lines, newest first (`--json` carries each one's `answeredOn` date)".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/question-commands.test.ts`, `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/question-commands.test.ts`, in-process: with a QUESTIONS.md whose `## Answered` holds twelve entries in file order Q1…Q12, each body ending `**Answered 2026-10-<day> by operator:** decision <k>`, `answeredQuestionList(root, 10)` starts with `answered questions in QUESTIONS.md, newest first:`, lists Q12 first and Q3 last as `- ` bullets, each carrying ` — Answered 2026-10-… by operator: decision …`, and ends `(2 older; -n <count> shows more)`; with count 12 there is no `older` line. `answeredQuestionPayload(root, 10)` has `questions.length === 10`, `older === 2`, and Q12's `answeredOn` is its stamp date. An entry with no `**Answered` line yields `answeredOn: null` and a bare `- <title>` bullet. An `## Open` entry never appears. A file whose `## Answered` holds only `_None yet._`, and a missing QUESTIONS.md, both render `no answered questions`.
- `test/question-commands.test.ts`: answering an open question through `answerQuestion` and then calling `answeredQuestionList` lists that question first — the newest-first claim checked against the real append path.
- `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`, through the `cli` harness: `questions --answered` exits 0 and prints the header and newest entry; `questions --answered -n 1 --json` parses to one entry and `older` equal to the rest; `questions -n 2` fails with `-n needs --answered`; `questions --answered --answered` fails through the repeat refusal; `questions --answered answer 1 x` fails with `takes no subcommand`; `questions --bogus` names `--answered` in its valid-flag list. The existing `questions` and `questions answer` tests pass unchanged, including the single-dash and `--json`-as-decision-word tests in `test/cli-questions-strictness.test.ts`.
- The help test that checks each command's usage still passes with the new stanza, and `tumwater help questions` shows `--answered`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater plan --list --done` and `bug --list --done` show the newest finished plans and fixed bugs, so an operator sees what the team completed lately without opening PLANS.md or BUGS.md (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`, `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-md.ts`, two lines of `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`'s bug/plan `--list` stanzas, and `docs/cli.md`'s "Steer the project" row. The `backlog --ready` plan edits `cmdBacklog`, the `backlog` help stanza, and the "Check state" row instead. Plain terms text 5/19, which is in flight, rewords `src/report/` messages but not the completion-date scan this plan touches) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `plan --list` and `bug --list` show only the actionable sections (`## Planned`, `## Open`). Nothing on the CLI answers "what did the team finish lately?" in backlog terms. `tumwater history` lists runs and commits, not the plans and bugs they closed. `tumwater report` counts `featuresDone`/`bugsFixed` per day but names no entries. Today an operator has to open PLANS.md (thousands of lines here) and read the top of `## Done`. Landings paste each finished entry first under `## Done`/`## Fixed` (`src/landing/backlog-conflicts.ts` module doc), so the newest entries are the first ones in each section.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-md.ts`: export `lastDate` (today module-private) without changing it, and update its doc comment to name the new caller.
- `src/backlog/backlog.ts`: add `export const DONE_DATE_RE = /done (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/` and `export const FIXED_DATE_RE = /\b(?:re-landed|fixed|closed|resolved) (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/`, moved verbatim from `collectReport`'s two `sectionCompletionDates` calls in `src/report/report-data.ts`. Move the explanation of the completion verbs, now a comment above the call, onto `FIXED_DATE_RE`. `report-data.ts` imports both constants and passes them in place of the literals, so the report's counts stay the same. Add `donePlanEntries(root)` and `fixedBugEntries(root)` beside `plannedPlanEntries`, both `sectionEntries` over `"PLANS.md"`/`"Done"` and `"BUGS.md"`/`"Fixed"`. Add `export function completionDate(title: string, dateRe: RegExp): string | null`, which returns `lastDate(title, dateRe)`. It reads only the heading line, like `filingDate`. A heading that keeps its date on a wrapped continuation line or in its body yields `null`.
- `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: the arg loop also consumes `--done` (once, through `rejectRepeatFlag`) and `-n <count>` (once). The count's value goes through `parseCountFlag("-n", value)`, and a missing value fails with that function's own `-n needs a value` message. When `-n` appears without `--done`, fail with `-n needs --done (it limits the finished entries listed)`. With `--done`, read `fixedBugEntries` (bug) or `donePlanEntries` (plan), take the first `n` entries (default 10), and let `older` be the number of entries left out.
  - Prose: the header line is `fixed bugs in BUGS.md, newest first:` or `done plans in PLANS.md, newest first:`. Each entry follows as a `- <title>` bullet. Bullets, not numbers, because `--edit`/`--cancel` positions address only the actionable section. When `older > 0`, a final line reads `(<older> older; -n <count> shows more)`. An empty or missing section prints `no fixed bugs` or `no done plans`.
  - `--json` prints `{ entries: [{ title, body, completedOn }], older }`. `completedOn` is `completionDate(title, FIXED_DATE_RE | DONE_DATE_RE)`, or `null` when the heading has no date.
  - These lists carry no hold, working-on-it mark, or age suffix: a finished entry has none of them. Without `--done`, the function behaves as it does today. Update its doc comment.
- `src/cli.ts` needs no edit, because `--list` already routes both commands to `listAndAnnounce`. `plan --done` without `--list` reaches `fileAndAnnounce`, and its `rejectUnknownArgs(command, [arg], [JSON_FLAG])` already refuses it.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: below each `--list [--json]` stanza, add a stanza `tumwater bug --list --done [-n <count>] [--json]` / `tumwater plan --list --done [-n <count>] [--json]` with the prose "List the newest entries in BUGS.md ## Fixed (PLANS.md ## Done), newest first (default 10); --json prints {entries, older}, each entry with title, body, completedOn". `completion.ts` takes its words from the usage lines.
- `docs/cli.md`, "Steer the project" row: after the `--list` clause, add "`--list --done [-n <count>]` lists the newest fixed bugs or done plans instead, newest first (`--json` carries each one's `completedOn` date)".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-md.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, `test/backlog.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog.test.ts`, unit: `completionDate("X (planned 2026-10-01 by plan) (done 2026-10-03)", DONE_DATE_RE)` is `"2026-10-03"`. `completionDate("Y (found by bugfix 2026-10-01) — fixed 2026-10-02", FIXED_DATE_RE)` is `"2026-10-02"`. A heading with no date yields `null`. `donePlanEntries` and `fixedBugEntries` return the `## Done` / `## Fixed` entries in file order and never an entry from `## Planned`, `## Open`, or a later `## Verified` section.
- `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, through the `cli` harness: in a PLANS.md with one Planned entry and twelve Done entries, `plan --list --done` prints `done plans in PLANS.md, newest first:`, the first ten Done titles as `- ` bullets in file order, then `(2 older; -n <count> shows more)`, and no Planned title. `-n 12` prints all twelve and no `older` line. `--json` parses to `entries.length === 10` with `older === 2`, and each entry has `completedOn`. `bug --list --done` on a BUGS.md with no `## Fixed` entries prints `no fixed bugs`.
- In the same file: `plan --list -n 3` fails with `-n needs --done`. `plan --list --done --done` fails through the repeat refusal. `plan --done` (no `--list`) still fails as an unknown flag. The existing `plan --list` assertions pass unchanged.
- In `test/report*.test.ts`, the existing `featuresDone`/`bugsFixed` assertions pass unchanged.
- The "help topics name the --list forms" test also finds `--list --done` in `tumwater help plan` and `tumwater help bug`.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/help.test.ts`.

### Plain terms text, part 7/19: Inbox and backlog command output and the role page (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/19, part 6/19, Plain terms groundwork 4/4 and Plain terms commands 6/6 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Glossary" and "Wording rules"; touches src/inbox/ + src/backlog/backlog-write.ts + backlog-cli.ts + question-answer.ts + backlog-structure.ts + src/roles/role-render.ts + role-view.ts + roles.ts + tests; done 2026-10-16)

### `tumwater backlog --ready` shows only the plans and bugs no hold keeps from being picked (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdBacklog`, `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`, `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, and `docs/cli.md`. The in-flight working-on-it-mark plan touches only `docs/cli.md`'s "Steer the project" row, and this one touches only its "Check state" row; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater backlog` prints every planned plan and open bug with its full body. In this repo that is more than 100 plans, nearly all of them `[blocked: requires …]`, so the few entries a role could pick next are buried in thousands of lines. The holds are already computed (`backlogHolds` in `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`) and printed as heading marks. Nothing filters on them. An operator asking "what will feature or bugfix pick up next?" has to page through the whole listing or post-process `--json`.

**Approach.**
- `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`: add `export const READY_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--ready"] };` beside `JSON_FLAG`, with a one-line doc comment in the style of its value-less siblings (`STAT_FLAG`, `SUMMARY_FLAG`).
- `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`: export `BacklogView` (today a local type) and add `export function readyBacklog(view: BacklogView): BacklogView`. It keeps plan `i` and bug `i` only when `view.holds?.plans[i]` / `view.holds?.bugs[i]` is `null`, and filters `holds` and `inProgress` with the same indexes so the arrays stay parallel. `questions` passes through unchanged, because questions carry no holds. An entry a role is working on has no hold, so it stays, together with its `[working on it: …]` mark. This matches how the planner counts eligible entries. A view without `holds` is returned unchanged. The doc comment says all of this.
- `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdBacklog`: `rejectUnknownArgs("backlog", args, [JSON_FLAG, READY_FLAG])`. When `args.includes("--ready")`, the thunk returns `readyBacklog(view)`, so `--json` and the Markdown view filter alike. The JSON shape stays the same: the same keys, with shorter arrays. In the Markdown branch only, and only with `--ready`, append one line after the sections: `_(<n> held entries hidden; run \`tumwater backlog\` to see them)_`, where `<n>` is the number of plans and bugs dropped. Leave the line out when `<n>` is 0. An emptied section still renders `_(none)_` through `renderSection`.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the stanza's usage becomes `tumwater backlog [--ready] [--json]`, and its prose gains: "--ready keeps only the planned plans and open bugs no hold keeps from being picked (entries a role is working on stay)". `completion.ts` derives its words from the usage line, so it needs no edit.
- `docs/cli.md`, the "Check state" row: after the `tumwater backlog --json` clause, add "`tumwater backlog --ready` (only the plans and bugs no hold keeps from being picked, with entries a role is working on kept and a count of the hidden ones; composes with `--json`)".

**Files touched.** `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-render.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-render.test.ts`, unit: `readyBacklog` on a view with three plans (held `"refused"`, `null`, `{ blockedBy: ["Foo 1/2"] }`), two bugs (`null`, `"needs-review"`), `inProgress.plans` `[null, "feature-2", null]`, and one question returns the middle plan with `holds.plans` `[null]` and `inProgress.plans` `["feature-2"]`, the first bug only, and the question untouched. A view without `holds` comes back deep-equal to its input.
- Same file, CLI via `runCli`: a PLANS.md with one refused plan and one eligible plan, and a BUGS.md with one open bug. `tumwater backlog --ready` exits 0, prints the eligible plan's and the bug's headings, does not print the refused plan's heading, and ends with `_(1 held entries hidden; run \`tumwater backlog\` to see them)_`. `tumwater backlog --ready --json` parses to `plans.length === 1`, `holds.plans` `[null]`, and `bugs.length === 1`. On a backlog with no held entries, `--ready` prints no hidden-count line.
- The existing unknown-argument assertion in "tumwater backlog prints the backlog and rejects flags…" is updated to the gate's message listing both `--json` and `--ready`, and its comment no longer says `--json` is the only flag.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/help.test.ts`.

**Approach.**
- Rules for every Plain terms text part:
  - Rewrite each user-visible string literal in the modules below by plans/terminology.md "Glossary" and "Wording rules", and add a `// vocabulary: plain` header line to each module this part converts.

The dashboard model and the stuck alert interpolate that regex, so they follow. Add a test that feeds `inFlightDetail`'s actual output, not a literal, to the browser stall check.

For example, `due` replaces `queued`, `merging` replaces `landing`, `approved, waiting to merge` replaces `vetted, awaiting merge`, `waiting to start` replaces `awaiting slot`, and every hold reads `waiting: <reason>`. The work is mostly mechanical. A few modules match these labels by string, and all of them change together in this part.

**Approach.**
- Rules for every Plain terms text part:
  - Rewrite each user-visible string literal in the modules below by plans/terminology.md "Glossary" and "Wording rules", and add a `// vocabulary: plain` header line to each module this part converts.

The guard's word list starts without `dry` and `telemetry` (the role ids series adds them), so those ids and `--dry-run` need no marker in this series.

  - Strings that name a renamed command or config key use its new name.
  - Rename no identifier, JSON key, event type, config key, command or file.
- Labels returned by `loopPhase` (src/ui/status-model.ts):

  | Today | New |
  | --- | --- |
  | `queued` | `due` |
  | `vetted, awaiting merge` | `approved, waiting to merge` |
  | `landing <t> · <stage> <t>` | `merging <t> · <stage> <t>` |
  | `awaiting slot <t>` | `waiting to start <t>` |
  | `awaiting <key> slot <t>` | `waiting for <key> <t>` |
  | `main red` | `main's check is failing` |
  | `budget paused` | `waiting: budget spent` |
  | `cap paused` | `waiting: daily cap spent` |
  | `disk hold` | `waiting: low disk` |
  | `held: bootstrap` | `waiting: bootstrap` |
  | `held: maintenance quota a/b` (built by `loopRowCells`) | `waiting: maintenance allowance used a/b` |
  | `idle: sibling mid-entry` | `idle: another <base role> instance is working on it` |
  | `waiting for prompts` (idle director) | `ready for messages` |

  These stay: working, reviewing, director working, paused, quiet until, sleeping (for …), failing, stopped, deferred (…), idle: no unclaimed …, and the ` · no change ×N` suffix.
- Update `LOOP_RANK_RULES` and `ACTIVE_PHASE_PREFIXES` so each state keeps its rank:
  - Rank 0 (active): `working`, `reviewing` and `merging`.
  - Rank 1: the prefixes `approved`, `waiting to start` and `waiting for `. The last covers a waiter parked on a provider key. It is also why the idle director's label moves away from "waiting for …".
  - Rank 2: the phases `failing` and `main's check is failing`.
  - Rank 3: the phase `paused` and the prefix `waiting:`.

### Plain terms text, part 1/19: Event messages and the Activity tally speak the glossary (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires Plain terms groundwork 4/4 and Plain terms commands 6/6 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Glossary" and "Wording rules"; touches src/events/event-format.ts + src/text/phrases.ts + sayTally in src/cli/log-commands.ts + tallyChips in src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts + tests; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Every event line that `tumwater logs`, the TUI Activity pane, the dashboard feed and the notify hook show reads in plain terms ("feature #2 run #12 merged", "team paused — roles start no new runs", "waiting: low disk"). The per-type tally (`tumwater logs --count` and the dashboard's Activity chips) shows display labels instead of raw codes like `3 × tick_end`.

**Approach.**
- Rules for every Plain terms text part:
  - Rewrite each user-visible string literal in the modules below by plans/terminology.md "Glossary" and "Wording rules", and add a `// vocabulary: plain` header line to each module this part converts.
  - Machine strings that a later series renames stay as they are, each on a line ending `// vocabulary-ok: <reason>`: event type codes, the `"harness"` event source, persisted state values, `--json` keys, `/api` routes, and the `tumwater(operator):` prefix. The guard's word list starts without `dry` and `telemetry` (the role ids series adds them), so those ids and `--dry-run` need no marker in this series.
  - Print role ids through `roleLabel` and raw event/result codes through `eventTypeLabel` (the groundwork helpers).
  - Strings that name a renamed command or config key use its new name ("Commands and config").
  - Rename no identifier, JSON key, event type, config key, command or file.
- `eventMessage` (src/events/event-format.ts): rewrite every case. Examples of the target wording:
  - Runs: `tick_start` → `run #N started on <model>`. `tick_end` → `run #N <eventTypeLabel(result)> — <summary>`, so `no_change` reads "no change", `changed` reads "merged" and `queued` reads "waiting to merge". `tick_aborted` → "run stopped by you".
  - Merges: `land_queued` → "waiting to merge <sha> — <summary>". `landed` → "merge of <sha> done". `land_failed` → "merge of <sha> failed (<label>)".
  - Pauses: `fleet_paused`, `fleet_resumed` and `role_paused` say "team", "roles" and "runs". `role_streak_paused` → "… N runs failed in a row …".
  - Waits: `disk_low`, `maintenance_quota_hold`, `bootstrap_complete`, `rate_limit_hold` and `claude_window_*` use the Wording rules' "waiting" forms ("waiting: low disk — …", "the maintenance roles wait until the window rolls over"). "claude seams" becomes "claude model jobs".
  - Budget: `budget_fallback` and the fallback clause of `budget_paused` say "over-cap model".
  - Updates and restarts:
    - `build_stale` → "update available (N commits behind) — restarts when idle".
    - `restart_pending` → "… finishing current runs (no new runs start)".
    - `restart` → "restarting onto update <sha> (finished current work in Nm; N run(s) resume after the restart)".
    - `restart_refused` and `restart_blocked` → "staying on version <sha>".
    - `supervisor_exit` → "tumwater is down — restart N …; start it again with `tumwater start`".
    - `orchestrator_start` → "tumwater started (pid N, version <sha>)", and `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED` → "tumwater stopped".
  - Waiting to start: `slot_wait` → "waited 3m to start (<role> run; 5 workspaces, 2 pinned)", with purpose `vet` read as "check". `permit_reserve` → "… reserved for work roles that have work to take".
  - Inbox: `prompt_enqueued`, `prompt_cancelled`, `prompt_edited` and `prompt_taken` → "message added to the inbox: …", "… taken by run #N: …".
  - `resume` causes say "run" and "agent". Only the cut-off cause, which only pi produces, keeps "pi session".
- `deferredReasonText`: "no work landed since last tick" → "nothing merged since the last run".
- `formatEvent`: print the source column as `roleLabel(eventRole(e))`, and as "tumwater" for the `"harness"` source (the event log series renames the stored value later). Widen the padded column from 9 to 10 so `feature #2` fits. `eventFeedItem` keeps shipping the raw id, because it is a JSON value.

Function names stay for the code series.

### The dashboard's Plans/Bugs tabs and the TUI's backlog pane show the `[working on it: …]` mark (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It touches only `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, and two tests, none of which the in-flight commands 4/6 or stale-bugs plans edit; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater backlog` and `plan`/`bug --list` now mark an entry a role is working on with `[working on it: feature #2]` (`backlogInProgress` and `inProgressMark` in `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`). The two live views of the same backlog do not show it yet. The dashboard's Plans and Bugs tabs render `planHolds`/`bugHolds` from `statusPayload` (`src/ui/status-payload.ts`) as a `li-meta` span beside each title (`renderBacklog` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`). The TUI's backlog pane appends `labeledBacklogEntries`' `mark` (`src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, rendered in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`). Both read `backlogMarks(root)`, which today projects only the holds. So an operator watching three feature instances on the dashboard cannot tell which plans are taken.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts` `backlogMarks`: also read `backlogInProgress(root)` once. Entry `i`'s mark becomes `holdMark(holds.plans[i]) + inProgressMark(inProgress.plans[i] ?? null)`, and the same for bugs. The hold mark comes first, then the working mark, the order `listAndAnnounce` prints. Rewrite its doc comment to say the mark carries both the eligibility hold and the working-on-it mark, and is still the empty string for an eligible entry nobody is working on. `backlogHolds` and `claims.ts`'s use of it stay unchanged, because the allocator decides on holds alone.

### `tumwater doctor` names an open bug that has gone unfixed for days: a "stale bugs" check (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It adds one check beside the in-flight plan-dependencies check in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, so whichever lands second extends the same `doctor.ts` list and `test/doctor.test.ts` name list) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The bugfix role fixes an open bug within hours. A bug still in BUGS.md `## Open` days after its `(found by … YYYY-MM-DD)` or `(reported … YYYY-MM-DD)` stamp means no loop is fixing it: the bugfix role is disabled, paused, or failing on it, or keeps passing it over. Doctor already warns about open questions that wait too long (`checkStaleQuestions`) and about refused bugs (`checkRefusedEntries`). Nothing names an unrefused bug that has simply sat. `bug --list` shows each bug's age, but only to an operator who runs it.

**Approach.**
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`: add `const STALE_BUG_DAYS = 3;` beside `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS`. Its doc comment says it is an opinionated default with no knob, the `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS` precedent. Three days is long enough that a bug filed late one evening and fixed the next day never warns.
- Same module: add `export function checkStaleBugs(root: string): CheckOutcome` after `checkStaleQuestions`, in its shape:
  - `readDocChecked(path.join(root, "BUGS.md"), "BUGS.md", "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify")`; return its outcome when the file is missing.

Skip an entry whose `refusalNote(entry.body)` is non-null, because the refusals check already names it. Skip an entry whose `filingDate(entry.title)` (import it from `../backlog/backlog.js`) is null. Keep the entries whose `ageInDays(stamp) >= STALE_BUG_DAYS`.
  - None kept: `okOutcome("no open bug has waited more than 3 days for a fix")`.
  - Otherwise warn on the first kept entry: `BUGS.md bug #<position> "<title truncated to FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX>" has waited <days> d for a fix<more> — no role is fixing it: check that the bugfix role is enabled and not failing, or retract it with \`tumwater bug --cancel <position>\``. `<more>` is `andMore(rest, (b) => \`#${b.position} "${truncate(b.title, FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX)}"\`)`.
  - A warn, never a fail, like every check in the module.
- Update the module's header doc comment, which lists its checks, to include stale bugs.

A missing BUGS.md reads `{ level: "ok", detail: "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify" }`.

### `tumwater doctor` checks the plans' `requires … landed` dependencies: it names a prerequisite that matches no plan, a clause that does not parse, and a dependency cycle (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. The two role-page plans touch `src/roles/` + `gui-client-drawer.ts` and customRoles 3/6 touches `src/config/`; this touches only `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, and their tests. Plain terms text 4/19 later rewords the doctor's check names, and it will pick up this one too) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The claim allocator holds a plan part only while a prerequisite named in its heading's `requires … landed` clause is still under `## Planned` (`entryHoldAgainst` in `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`). Three mistakes in that clause go unnoticed:
- **A dangling ref.** The clause names a series or part that no PLANS.md heading carries, through a typo like `Plain terms command 6/6` or a renumbered split. The ref is then never "still planned", so the dependent part becomes eligible at once and can land before its real prerequisite.
- **An unparseable clause.** The clause has `requires … landed` text that `requiredParts` turns into no refs, such as a bare `requires part 1/2 landed` on a heading with no `<Series>, part i/n:` prefix. That holds nothing either.
- **A cycle.** Two planned parts that require each other directly or through a chain are held forever, and the only sign is a `[blocked: …]` mark that never clears.

`tumwater doctor` has backlog checks for refusals, stalled plans, stranded plans, and duplicate headings (`src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`), but none for dependencies. Grep finds no `cycle` or `dangling` in `src/backlog/` or `src/doctor/` other than an unrelated pid-recycling comment in doctor-orphans.ts. The plan role writes these clauses by hand, and a long series like Plain terms holds dozens of them, so a single typo can quietly reorder the series.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`:
  - Split the clause extraction out of `requiredParts` into a private `requiresClause(title): string | null`. It covers the trailing or open parenthetical and the `/requires\s+(.+?)\s+landed\b/i` match, and returns the captured ref text. `requiredParts` keeps its behavior and existing tests.
  - Add an exported pure `planDependencyProblems(planned: readonly BacklogEntry[], doneTitles: readonly string[]): { cycle: string[] | null; dangling: Array<{ title: string; ref: string }>; unparsed: string[] }`, with a doc comment in the file's style.
  - **Known parts** are the `plannedPartKeys(planned)` keys plus the `partKey` of `seriesPart(t)` for each done title.
  - **`dangling`** lists, in planned order, every ref of every planned entry whose `partKey` is not a known part. `ref` is formatted `${series} ${part}/${of}`, the same form `blockedBy` uses.
  - **`unparsed`** lists the titles of planned entries where `requiresClause` is non-null but `requiredParts` returns [].
  - **`cycle`** is the first cycle found by a depth-first walk over planned entries that have a `seriesPart`. Each entry has an edge to every planned entry its refs name by `partKey`, and a self-reference counts. The cycle is reported as its `Series i/n` names in walk order, starting and ending on the same node (e.g. `["S 1/2", "S 2/2", "S 1/2"]`). It is null when there is none.
  - Refused and needs-review entries are judged the same as the rest, because their clauses still decide when they unblock.
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`: add `checkPlanDependencies(root)`, which reads `plannedPlanEntries(root)` and `donePlans(root)` (src/backlog/backlog.ts) and returns one outcome:
  - It warns on the most serious problem first, never fails: a cycle, then dangling refs, then unparsed clauses.
  - A cycle reads ``plan dependency cycle: S 1/2 → S 2/2 → S 1/2 — every part on it stays blocked forever; edit one heading's `requires … landed` clause to break it``.
  - A dangling ref reads ``PLANS.md plan "<title truncated to FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX>" requires <ref>, which no PLANS.md heading carries — the hold is void, so the plan is claimable now; fix the series name or part number``.
  - An unparsed clause reads ``PLANS.md plan "<title>" has a `requires … landed` clause that names no part the allocator can read — it holds nothing; write each ref as `<Series> i/n` or give the heading a `<Series>, part i/n:` prefix``.
  - Further items of the reported kind are appended through the module's `andMore` helper, and a count of the other kinds follows when non-zero: `(also N dangling ref(s), M unparsed clause(s))`.
  - The ok outcome reads `every planned plan's requires clause names a known part, with no cycle`.
  - Extend the module's header comment to list the new check.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import it and add `{ name: "plan dependencies", ...checkPlanDependencies(root) }` right after the `stalled plans` row.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`. There is no allocator, claim, index, or render change, so eligibility behaves exactly as before.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts` covers `planDependencyProblems` in these cases:
  - Planned `S, part 2/3: …(requires part 1/3 landed)` with `S, part 1/3: …` among the done titles has no problems.
  - The same entry requiring `T 1/3` (no such heading) yields `dangling: [{ title, ref: "T 1/3" }]`.
  - A heading `Plain plan (requires part 1/2 landed)` with no series prefix yields it in `unparsed`.
  - Planned `S, part 1/2: … (requires part 2/2 landed)` and `S, part 2/2: … (requires part 1/2 landed)` yield a non-null `cycle` that names both parts and starts and ends on the same name.
  - A self-reference yields a one-hop cycle.
  - A clause-free heading yields nothing.
  - The existing `requiredParts` tests pass unchanged.
- `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts` covers `checkPlanDependencies` on temp PLANS.md files: ok on a clean `## Planned` + `## Done` pair, ok when PLANS.md is absent, and a warn for each of the three kinds matching the wording above. When a cycle and a dangling ref are both present, the cycle is named and the line carries `(also 1 dangling ref(s), 0 unparsed clause(s))`.
- The row-name list asserted in `test/doctor.test.ts` gains `"plan dependencies"` between `"stalled plans"` and `"stale questions"`.
- Today's tree: the refused `tui-panes` plan heading in `## Planned` carries a bare `requires part 1/2 landed` with no series prefix, so `tumwater doctor` run on this repo warns `unparsed` for it. That warning is expected and correct, not a regression.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater backlog` and `plan`/`bug --list` show which role instance is working on each entry, so an operator sees the plans and bugs in progress without opening the role rows (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. The two waiting plans touch `src/roles/`, `gui-client-drawer.ts`, `src/doctor/` and the end of `backlog-eligibility.ts`; this touches `backlog-eligibility.ts` only beside `backlogMarks`, plus the two backlog CLI shells and the renderer; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A role's live claim on a backlog entry is already read by `allLiveClaims` (`src/loop/loop-state.ts`, `Map<entryKey, runner id>`). The loops' own backlog index prints it as `[in flight by feature-3]` (`renderIndexRow` in `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`). The operator's backlog views do not show it: `tumwater backlog` (`cmdBacklog` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, rendered by `renderBacklogMarkdown` in `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`) and `tumwater plan --list` / `bug --list` (`listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`) mark only holds. As a result an operator with three feature instances cannot tell from the backlog which plans are being worked on and which are waiting. Show it, in plain terms (docs/glossary.md maps "claim" to "working on it" and `feature-2` to `feature #2`).

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: beside `backlogMarks`, add an exported `backlogInProgress(root): { plans: (string | null)[]; bugs: (string | null)[] }`. Its arrays are parallel to `plannedPlanEntries(root)` and `openBugEntries(root)` (the same readers and order as `backlogHolds`). Entry `i` is the runner id whose live claim key equals `entryKey(entry.title)`, or `null`. Build the map with one `allLiveClaims(root)` call. Do not cache: `allLiveClaims` is already stat-cached per role. Also add an exported `inProgressMark(runner: string | null): string`. It returns `""` for null, else `` ` [working on it: ${roleLabel(runner)}]` `` (`roleLabel` from `src/roles/role-labels.ts`, so `feature-2` reads `feature #2` and a bare `feature` reads `feature`). Leave `renderIndexRow`'s prompt text alone, because the Plain terms text series owns prompt wording.
- `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`: `BacklogView` gains an optional `inProgress?: { plans: (string | null)[]; bugs: (string | null)[] }`. `renderSection` takes it as an optional fourth argument and appends `inProgressMark(...)` after the `holdMark(...)` on entry `i`'s `### ` heading. A missing `inProgress` must leave the document byte-identical to today, which the existing "no holds leaves the document unchanged" test pins.
- `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdBacklog`: the payload thunk adds `inProgress: backlogInProgress(root)` next to `holds`. The `--json` document therefore gains a top-level `inProgress` object whose `plans`/`bugs` arrays hold runner ids (raw `feature-2`, not the label) or `null`.
- `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: read `backlogInProgress(root)` once. Each numbered line appends `inProgressMark(...)` after the hold mark and before `entryAgeSuffix`. Each `--json` entry gains `inProgress: <runner id> | null`, always present like `hold`.
- Help and docs: in `src/cli/help.ts`, add one clause to the `tumwater backlog [--json]` stanza and to the `plan`/`bug --list` stanzas naming the `[working on it: …]` mark and the `inProgress` key. In `docs/cli.md`, add the same clause to the "Check state" row's `tumwater backlog` text and to the `--list` sentence in the "Steer the project" row.
- Not in scope: the dashboard's Plans/Bugs tabs and the TUI backlog pane (`backlogMarks` callers). A follow-up plan can carry the mark there once this lands. Keying is by entry key alone, exactly as the index's `claimed.get(key)` does, so a plan and a bug with identical stamp-free titles would share a mark. The index has the same limit, and this plan does not change it.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/backlog-render.test.ts`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

Save a `feature-2` state whose `claim.key` matches the first plan and a `bugfix` state whose claim matches the bug (the `saveLoopState` pattern from the existing "parallel-work instance" test). `backlogInProgress` must then return `{ plans: ["feature-2", null], bugs: ["bugfix"] }`. With no claims saved, every element is `null`. `inProgressMark(null) === ""` and `inProgressMark("feature-2") === " [working on it: feature #2]"`.
- `test/backlog-render.test.ts`: `renderBacklogMarkdown` with `inProgress` puts the mark on the claimed heading after any hold mark, and without `inProgress` the output equals today's. `tumwater backlog` on a root with a saved claim prints the mark on that heading, and `tumwater backlog --json` carries `inProgress.plans`/`inProgress.bugs` arrays parallel to `plans`/`bugs`.
- `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`: `plan --list` on a root with a saved `feature-2` claim prints `1. <title> [working on it: feature #2]` (plus the age suffix the existing tests expect). `plan --list --json` entries carry `inProgress: "feature-2"` on the claimed entry and `inProgress: null` on the other.

### `tumwater role <id>` and the GUI loop drawer show the loop's `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` cap, today's spend against it, and whether it is holding the loop now (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of the plain-terms series. It touches the same three files as the quiet-hours role-page plan above (`src/roles/role-view.ts`, `src/roles/role-render.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts`) but different fields and lines, so either can land first. It reads, and does not edit, `roleCapVerdicts` in src/gates/role-cap-gates.ts) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A loop that has reached its own `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` entry starts no new tick until local midnight. The scheduler applies that through `pollRoleCapGate`, the status snapshot shows it as `capPaused` (`src/status/status-budget.ts`), and `tumwater doctor` names it (`src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts`). The per-loop inspection says nothing about it. `rolePayload` in `src/roles/role-view.ts` carries `usage` (spend over the retained event window) but no cap: grep finds no `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` or `roleCap` in `src/roles/` or in `drawerConfigHtml`. So under `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole: {"feature": 1}`, `tumwater role feature-2` prints `Next tick: due now` for a loop whose group has spent $1.04 today, and gives no hint of the cap.

**Approach.** Get the verdict from `roleCapVerdicts`, the function the gate and the status observer already share, so the role page cannot disagree with the scheduler.
- `src/roles/role-view.ts`: add an optional field to `RoleViewPayload`: `dailyCap?: { capUsd: number; spentUsd: number; over: boolean; roleIds: string[] }`. Give it a doc comment in the file's style.
  - Fill it only when `cfg.maxDailyCostUsdPerRole?.[baseRoleOf(role)]` is a finite number above 0, mirroring `roleCapPaused`'s rule that 0 disables the cap, and the role is not `DIRECTOR_ROLE`.
  - The runners are `loopIds(cfg).filter((id) => baseRoleOf(id) === baseRoleOf(role))`, plus `role` itself when it is missing (a disabled loop is still inspectable). Each is mapped to `{ role: id, state: loadLoopState(root, id) }`. Reuse the `state` already loaded for `role`, not a second read.
  - Pass the runners to `roleCapVerdicts(runners, cfg.maxDailyCostUsdPerRole, now.getTime())` and take the entry for `baseRoleOf(role)`. Copy its `over`, `spentUsd`, and `roleIds`, and add the cap as `capUsd`.
  - `now` is the trailing `now: Date = new Date()` test-seam parameter after `modelsPath`. If the quiet-hours plan has already added it, reuse it; otherwise add it, with that exact name and default.
  - When no cap applies the field is absent, so the JSON of a fleet without per-role caps keeps its current shape.
- `src/roles/role-render.ts`: right after the `- Spend:` line in `renderRoleMarkdown`, print one line when `p.dailyCap` is present: `- Daily cap: <spent> of <cap> spent today (holding now — no new ticks until local midnight)`, or `(not holding)` when `over` is false. Format both amounts with the `usd` helper the Spend line uses. When `roleIds.length > 1`, add ` · shared by <ids joined with ", ">` after the parenthetical, because instances share and sum one cap. A payload without the field renders no new line.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts`: in `drawerConfigHtml`, right after the `Spend` row, add one `kvRow("Daily cap", …)` with the same wording, using `fmtUsd`. Guard it with `view.dailyCap && typeof view.dailyCap === "object"` and coerce the numbers with `Number(x) || 0`, as the Spend row does. Include the shared suffix only when `Array.isArray(dc.roleIds) && dc.roleIds.length > 1`. Do not use backticks, because the script is one `String.raw` template.
- The TUI renders `inspectMarkdownLines`, which holds only the notebook and prompt blocks, so it needs no change.

### Plain terms commands, part 4/6: Rename the agent and agents config keys to backend and backends (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/6 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Commands and config"; touches src/config/ and src/pi/pi-bin.ts and src/agent/agent-backend.ts and src/cli/ and src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts plus tests)

**Goal.** The config names the agent backend `backend` (default for bare model ids) and `backends` (per-backend `bin`/`args`). Old files keep working. The legacy `agentBin`/`piArgs` now chain to `backends.pi.bin`/`.args`.

**Approach.**
- Add the rows `agent` → `backend` and `agents` → `backends`, scope `"top"`, to `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES`. `canonicalConfigKey` already maps `agents.<id>.<field>` → `backends.<id>.<field>` by its first segment (part 1/6).
- Schema (src/config/config-schema.ts):
  - `TumwaterConfig.agent` → `backend` and `agents` → `backends`, with their `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` entries.
  - `AgentConfig`, `AGENT_KEYS` and `AGENT_IDS` keep their names until Plain terms code cleanup.
- `ResolvedModelConfig` (src/config/config-views.ts): today it is `Omit<TumwaterConfig, "model" | "agent"> & {…, agent?}`. Make it `Omit<TumwaterConfig, "model"> & {…, agent?}`.
  - A resolved seam's own `agent` is the backend that seam runs on. It is an internal field and keeps its name.
  - The configured default is now `backend`.
  - `defaultConfig()` (typed as the resolved view) sets `backend: "pi"` and `backends: {}`, and no longer sets `agent`. Every reader already defaults a missing seam `agent` to pi.
  - This matters: whole-config writes serialize the merged defaults. A default `agent` key would put both `agent` and `backend` on disk, and the next load would refuse the file.
- Readers of the configured default and section:
  - src/config/config-views.ts: `routeModel(…, config.backend ?? "pi", …)` in both places, and `resolvedAgentConfig` reading `config.backends?.[id]`;
  - src/config/config-fallbacks.ts: the `config.agent` read;
  - src/config/config.ts: `overlayDefaults`, `cloneConfig`, `collapseAgentAliases` reading `backends.pi`;
  - src/agent/agent-backend.ts: its config view type's `agents?` field;
  - src/pi/pi-bin.ts: the config-key wording becomes `` `backends.${agent}.bin` ``, while pi's is still `agentBin`.
  - Seam-level `.agent` reads (run-agent.ts, review.ts, loop-pi.ts, doctor) are the resolved field and do not change. Let typecheck separate the two.
- Validation (src/config/config-validation.ts):
  - `checkString(r, "", "backend", …)`, the `backends` section check, and the prefix `backends.<id>`;
  - the legacy-alias rule reads `r.backends.pi`, and its messages say `agentBin and backends.pi.bin set the same value — keep one (backends.pi.bin is the current spelling; agentBin is its old name)`, and the same for `piArgs`/`backends.pi.args`.
  - Chaining needs no new code: normalization moves a file's `agents` to `backends` first, so `agentBin` together with `agents.pi.bin` is refused too.
- Keys and writes:
  - src/config/config-keys.ts: `parseConfigKey`'s dotted head becomes `backends`; `DOTTED_KEY_HEADS`; the error reads `unknown backend field "x" for backends.<id> (valid fields: bin, args)`. The parsed kind may stay `"agent"`.
  - src/config/config-write.ts: the set and unset agent branches read and write `backends`.
  - src/cli/config-commands.ts: `config get` reads `record.backends`.
  - src/cli/completion.ts: emits `backends.<id>.<field>`.
- Dashboard: `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` (src/config/config-editable-keys.ts) `"agents"` → `"backends"`, and the browser copy in src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts's `SETTINGS_KEYS` gets the same key change. Its label text belongs to Plain terms text.
- Out of scope: the status payload's `budget.agent` and `role --json`'s `agent` are script keys owned by Plain terms scripting.
- Tests:
  - TypeScript configs that set the top-level `agent`/`agents` (config-views, config-validation, config-write, config-unset-key, config, pi-bin, claude-run, startup-gate, doctor-checks, gui-client-settings, gui-endpoints, completion and the rest typecheck names). Seam/`ResolvedModelConfig` `agent:` values stay.
  - New cases in test/config-aliases.test.ts:
    - `{"agent":"claude"}` loads as `backend`;
    - `agents.pi.bin` loads as `backends.pi.bin`;
    - `agentBin` together with `agents.pi.bin` is refused naming `backends.pi.bin`;
    - `config set agents.claude.args '["--x"]'` writes `backends.claude.args`.

**Files touched.** src/config/config-aliases.ts, config-schema.ts, config.ts, config-views.ts, config-fallbacks.ts, config-validation.ts, config-keys.ts, config-write.ts, config-editable-keys.ts; src/agent/agent-backend.ts; src/pi/pi-bin.ts; src/cli/config-commands.ts, completion.ts; src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts; comments in src/agent/claude/claude-args.ts, claude-backend.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts. Tests as listed.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A file with `"agent": "claude"` and `"agents": {"claude": {"args": ["--x"]}}` loads as `backend`/`backends` and runs claude seams with `--x`. Doctor names both renames.
- `tumwater config set agents.pi.bin /opt/pi` writes `backends.pi.bin`. A file with `agentBin` and `backends.pi.bin` is refused naming both.
- `tumwater config set maxDailyCostUsd 5` on a file holding `"agent": "claude"` writes a file with `backend` and no `agent`, and that file loads again.
- The dashboard Settings view edits `backends`, and `/api/config` serves it. `tumwater completion --config-keys` lists `backend`, `backends.pi.bin` and `backends.claude.args`, and no `agents.` key.
- `npm run test` passes.
